Later, a style of pleated skirt became fashionable called the "fairy-retaining skirt." See Unofficial Biography of Empress Zhao. After Emperor Cheng's death, Zhao Feiyan committed suicide fearing punishment. See Book of Han, Vol. 97, "Biographies of Imperial Relatives". The whole line seems to combine the two stories, saying Zhao Feiyan died for playing with flowers.

C: 一个海棠丝剪不断香事宜怪：疑是杨贵妃的故事。安史之乱平定之后，唐明皇回到长安。他叫人把贵妃的骸骨重新安葬。墓开，只见锦香囊一个。见《顾氏文房小说.杨太真外传》。元代关汉卿有《唐明皇哭香囊》杂剧。今佚。据《录鬼簿》。又据《事类统编》卷七十八引《太真外传》："明皇登沉香亭，如太真（杨贵妃）。宿酒未醒，钗横鬟乱。不能再拜。上笑曰：'岂海棠春睡未足耶！'"
E: One, the begonia silk cannot be cut, the fragrant affair is strange indeed.Suspected to be the story of Consort Yang. After the An Lushan Rebellion was pacified, Emperor Ming of Tang returned to Chang'an. He had the consort's remains reburied. When the tomb was opened, only a brocade incense pouch was found. See Mr. Gu's Library of Stories, "Unofficial Biography of Yang Taizhen". The Yuan playwright Guan Hanqing had a zaju Emperor Ming of Tang Cries Over the Incense Pouch, now lost. According to Register of Ghosts. Also, according to Classified Compendium of Matters and Things, Vol. 78, quoting "Unofficial Biography of Taizhen": "Emperor Ming ascended the Aloeswood Pavilion to see Taizhen (Consort Yang). Her overnight wine not yet sober, hairpins askew, locks disheveled. She could not perform the bow. The Emperor laughed and said: 'Is it that the begonia's spring slumber is not enough?'"

C: 一个瑞香风、赶不上非烟在：唐人传奇故事：武公业的爱妾步非烟，和赵象偷偷地爱上了。赵旬送给她的诗中有两句说："瑞香风引思深夜，知是蕊宫仙驭来。"后来事泄，非烟被武公业独打而死。见《太平广记》卷四九一《非烟传》。
E: One, the auspicious fragrance breeze, could not catch up with Feiyan's presence.A Tang chuanqi tale: Wu Gongye's beloved concubine Bu Feiyan secretly fell in love with Zhao Xiang. Two lines in a poem Zhao Xiang sent her said: "Auspicious fragrance breeze leads thoughts deep into the night, I know it is the immortal carriage from the Stamen Palace coming." Later the affair was exposed; Feiyan was beaten to death by Wu Gongye. See Extensive Records of the Taiping Era, Vol. 491, "Biography of Feiyan".

C: 望梅止渴：喻可望不可即。曹操行军，路上没水。他说到前面大梅林去可以吃梅子解渴。士兵听了，口水也流出来了。见《世说新语.解谲》。这里指杜丽娘题诗"不在梅边在柳边"所表示的对爱情的徒然渴望。
E: Quench thirst by gazing at plums.Metaphor for something that can be seen but not reached. Cao Cao was marching; there was no water on the road. He said that ahead was a large plum grove where they could eat plums to quench their thirst. The soldiers heard this and salivated. See A New Account of the Tales of the World, "Jiejue" (Release from Trickery). Here it refers to the vain longing for love expressed in Du Liniang's poem "Not by the plum tree, but by the willow."

C: 道场：进行超度亡灵的一种宗教仪式的场地。
E: Daoist or Buddhist ritual (often for the dead).A place where a religious ritual is performed to exonerate the dead

C: 窈娘：唐代乔知之的宠婢，为武承嗣所夺，投井死。见《本事诗》卷一。窈娘堤，在洛阳。
E: Yaoniang.The favored maid of Qiao Zhiyi of the Tang dynasty; taken by Wu Chengsi, she threw herself into a well and died. See Ben Shi Poetry, Vol. 1. Yaoniang Embankment is in Luoyang.

C: 黄梁境：梦境。唐人传奇故事：卢生在邯郸的诱店里，借道士吕翁的枕头小睡。梦幻中功名成就，官高极品。醒来，旅店主人的黄梁饭还没有炊熟。见《太平广记》卷八十二引《异闻集.吕翁》。后来一般用黄粱作梦的代称。
E: Millet dream realm (illusion).Dream realm. A Tang chuanqi tale: Lu Sheng at an inn in Handan borrowed the pillow of the Daoist Lü Weng for a nap. In his dream, he achieved fame and rank, rising to the highest office. Waking, the millet porridge of the innkeeper was not yet cooked. See Extensive Records of the Taiping Era, Vol. 82, quoting Collection of Strange Hearsay, "Lü Weng". Later, yellow millet was commonly used as a synonym for a dream.

C: 落韦与孤莺莺齐飞，秋水共长天一色：唐王勃《滕王阁序》中的句子。这里引用，着重在后一句"秋水"与"秋波"一词的关联。
E: Falling reeds and lonely warblers fly together, autumn waters merge with the vast sky's one hue. (A variation of Wang Bo's famous line)A line from Wang Bo's Tang "Preface to the Prince of Teng's Pavilion". Quoted here, emphasizing the connection between the latter phrase "autumn waters" and the term "autumn waves" (meaning a beautiful woman's eyes).

C: 飞上烟绡萼绿华：萼绿华，神话中女仙名，相传是九嶷山得道女罗郁。见《太平广记》卷五十七引《真诰.萼绿华》。全句意思说：好象仙女飞上了绢幅，化成画像。
E: Flew onto the misty silk, E Lühua.E Lühua, name of a mythical female immortal, said to be Luo Yu, a woman who attained the Dao on Jiuyi Mountain. See Extensive Records of the Taiping Era, Vol. 57, quoting Declarations of the Perfected, "E Lühua". The whole line means: As if an immortal maiden flew onto the silk scroll, becoming a painted image.

C: 做个画屏中倚玉蒹葭：《世说新语.容光焕发止》："魏明帝使后北毛曾与夏侯泰初共坐。时人谓：'蒹葭倚玉树'。"蒹葭，荻，同物，喻毛曾，这里是柳梦梅自喻。全句意思说：恨不得自己也化成画中人物，和她一起。
E: A New Account of the Tales of the World, "Grace and Mien": "Emperor Ming of Wei had Mao Zeng, his empress's relative, sit together with Xiahou Taichu. People of the time said: 'Reeds leaning against a jade tree.'" Jianjia, reeds, same thing,biyu  (metaphorically referring to) Mao Zeng; here Liu Mengmei uses it for himself. The whole line means: How I wish I could also transform into a figure in the painting to be with her.

C: 石也要点头：佛家传说：梁高僧竺道生在苏州虎丘讲法。立石为徒，石皆点头。见《事类统编》卷六十三。
E: Stones would also nod their heads.Buddhist legend: The Liang dynasty eminent monk Zhu Daosheng preached the Dharma at Tiger Hill in Suzhou. He set up stones as disciples, and the stones all nodded. See Classified Compendium of Matters and Things, Vol. 63.

C: 彩凤暗随鸦：杜大中当兵出身。他的爱妾才色俱美，抱怨嫁不到好丈夫。作《临江仙》一首，说自己是彩凤随鸦。见《事文类聚》卷十六《武人置妾》条。
E: A colorful phoenix secretly follows a crow.Du Dazhong came from a military background. His beloved concubine was talented and beautiful; she complained about not marrying a good husband. She composed a ci poem to the tune "Immortal by the River," saying she was a colorful phoenix following a crow. See Classified Collection of Matters and Literature, Vol. 16, entry "Military Men Taking Concubines".

C: 梁清：神话中女仙名，或即织女侍儿梁玉清。相传她和太白星逃往下界，生一子。见《太平广记》卷五十九引《独异志.梁玉清》。
E: Liang Qing.Name of a mythical female immortal, perhaps the Weaver Girl's attendant Liang Yuqing. Legend says she and the Great White Star (Venus) fled to the mortal world and had a son. See Extensive Records of the Taiping Era, Vol. 59, quoting Records of Unique Strange Things, "Liang Yuqing".

C: 张骞犯了你星汉槎：神话传说：汉张骞乘水上浮木（槎）到银河边牵牛、织女那里。见《荆楚岁时记》。你，以织女比杜丽娘。
E: Zhang Qian trespassed on your Starry River raft.Myth: Han dynasty Zhang Qian rode a floating log (raft) on water to the Starry River (Milky Way) to visit the Cowherd and Weaver Girl. See Record of the Seasons of Jing and Chu. "You" compares the Weaver Girl to Du Liniang.

C: 认陶潜眼挫的花：陶潜，晋代大诗人，《桃花源记》的作者。桃花源和刘晨、阮肇的故事附会在一起以后，陶潜有时也和刘、阮一样，被用作情郎的代称。眼挫的花，眼花错看。全句意思说：找情郎看错了人。
E: Mistakenly recognizing Tao Qian, the eyes failed (were dazzled).Tao Qian (Tao Yuanming), great Jin dynasty poet, author of "Peach Blossom Spring remembering". After the Peach Blossom Spring was conflated with the story of Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao, Tao Qian was sometimes also used, like Liu and Ruan, as a term for a lover. "Eyes failed" means eyes were dazzled, mistaken. The whole line means: Looking for a lover, she mistook the person.

C: 走临邛道数儿差：走临邛，指私奔。卓文君，四川临邛卓王孙的女儿，寡居在家。一天，听司马相如奏琴，爱上了他。偷偷地离家，和相如同居。见《史记.司马相如列传》。全句意思说：私奔走错了路。
E: Took the road to Linqiong, the fate was wrong."Going to Linqiong" refers to eloping. Zhuo Wenjun, daughter of Zhuo Wangsun of Linqiong in Sichuan, was widowed at home. One day, hearing Sima Xiangru play the qin, she fell in love with him. She secretly left home and lived with Xiangru. See Records of the Grand Historian, "Biography of Sima Xiangru". The whole line means: Eloping took the wrong path.

C: 度仙香空散花：佛家传说：文殊到维摩诘那里问病，天女以天花散到菩萨身上，花从菩萨身上落下。散在大弟子身止的却没有落下。天女说，这是因为大弟子结习还没有尽。见《维摩诘经.问疾品》。
E: Bestowing immortal incense, vainly scattering flowers.Buddhist legend: Manjushri went to Vimalakirti to inquire about his illness; a deva girl scattered heavenly flowers on the bodhisattva, and the flowers fell off him. Those scattered on the great disciples did not fall off. The deva girl said this was because the great disciples' habitual tendencies were not yet exhausted. See Vimalakirti Nirdesa Sutra, "Chapter on Inquiring about the Illness".

C: 夜行无烛：《礼.内则》："女子出门......夜行以烛，无烛则止。"古代礼制规定，女子夜间出行必须持烛照明，若无烛火则不应夜行。
E: Book of Rites, "Neize": "When a woman goes out... at night she should travel with a candle; if she has no candle, she should stop." Ancient ritual rules stipulated that women must carry a candle for illumination when going out at night; if they had no candlelight, they should not travel at night.

C: 赵飞卿旧有瑕：赵飞卿，或指汉成帝的皇后赵飞燕。相传贫贱时，曾和射鸟者私通。见《赵飞燕外传》。旧有瑕，当指此。
E: Zhao Feiqing had flaws in the past.Zhao Feiqing probably refers to Zhao Feiyan, empress of Emperor Cheng of Han. Legend says that in her poor and lowly days, she had an affair with a bird shooter. See Unofficial Biography of Zhao Feiyan. "Had flaws in the past" likely refers to this.

C: 弄莺簧赴柳衙簧，乐器名。一般常用簧声来形容莺啼。柳衙，柳成行。衙，排衙，原指长官排列仪仗，接受属官的参谒。清周亮工《书影》卷十引《中朝故事》："曲江池畔多柳，亦号柳衙。"这里指柳梦梅住房。
E: Playing oriole-pipe, going to Willow Yamen. Huang is an instrument name. The sound of the reed is often used to describe oriole songs. "Willow Yamen" means willows planted in rows. Yamen originally meant an official arranging his retinue to receive subordinates' visits. Zhou Lianggong's Qing work Shuying, Vol. 10, quotes Stories from the Central Court: "By the Qujiang Pond there were many willows, also called Willow Yamen." Here it refers to Liu Mengmei's residence.

C: 清风明月知无价：句本李白《襄阳歌》："清风郎月不用一钱买。"这里用意不同。"无价"，极言珍贵。
E: Clear breeze, bright moon, know they are priceless.Line based on Li Bai's "Song of Xiangyang": "Clear breeze, bright moon, need not a penny to buy." The meaning here is different. "Priceless" emphasizes extreme preciousness.

C: 巫峡：此指巫山，男女欢会。《元曲选.两世姻缘》第三折《调笑令》："莫不是梦儿中云雨巫峡。"参看第出注十三。
E: Wu Gorge: here refers to Wushan Mountain, place of romantic encounter. From the third act, "Song of Flirtation," of Love Across Two Lifetimes in Selection of Yuan Plays: "Is it not clouds and rain in Wu Gorge in a dream?" See note 13 of the previous act.

C: 吹笙：神话传说：西王母侍女董双成，本在杭州西湖妙庭观修炼，后来吹笙骑鹤飞上天去。见《浙江通志》卷一九八。
E: Playing the sheng panpipe.Myth: Dong Shuangcheng, attendant of the Queen Mother of the West, originally cultivated at the Miaoting Temple by West Lake in Hangzhou; later she played the sheng and rode a crane to fly up to heaven. See General Gazetteer of Zhejiang, Vol. 198.

C: 女冠儿生来出家相：女冠即女道士，唐代以来女子出家为道士的称呼（《唐六典》载："女道士曰女冠"）。出家相，佛教术语，指出家人的威仪（《释氏要览》），此处借指道姑身份。
E: The Taoist nun is born with the appearance of leaving home.Nüguan means female Daoist priest, a term for women who become Daoist priests since the Tang dynasty (Tang Liu Dian records: "Female Daoist priests are called nüguan"). "Appearance of leaving home" is a Buddhist term for the dignified manner of those who have left home (Essentials of the Śākya Clan); here borrowed to refer to the identity of a Daoist nun.

C: 守著三清像，三清，道教最高神------玉清元始天尊、上清灵宝天尊、太清道德天尊（《云笈七签》）。换水添香，道教供奉仪式，每日更换净水、添香火（《道门科范》）。
E: Guarding the image of the Three Pure Ones. The Three Pure Ones are the highest Daoist deities: the Jade Pure Original Celestial Worthy, the Upper Pure Numinous Treasure Celestial Worthy, and the Great Pure Dao and Virtue Celestial Worthy (Seven Slips from a Cloudy Satchel). Changing water and adding incense: Daoist offering rituals, changing pure water and adding incense daily (Daoist Ritual Codes).

C: 常无欲以观其妙，常有欲以观其窍：《道德经》第一章：常无欲以观其妙，常有欲以观其徼。老道姑断章取义，用"窍"（谐音"俏"）调侃小道姑与柳秀才私会。反映明代道教世俗化，经典被戏谑解读。
E: Daodejing, Chapter 1: "Constantly without desire, thereby observe its subtlety; constantly with desire, thereby observe its manifestations." The old nun takes the phrase out of context, using "qiao" (manifestations, homophone for "pretty") to tease the young nun about her secret meeting with Scholar Liu. Reflects the secularization of Daoism in the Ming dynasty, with classics being playfully interpreted.

C: 洗凡心冰壶月朗：冰壶，喻高洁（王昌龄《芙蓉楼送辛渐》"一片冰心在玉壶"）。月朗，佛教常用喻清净心（《楞严经》"净若琉璃，内含宝月"）。
E: Wash the worldly heart, ice pot, moon bright.Ice pot metaphorically means noble and unsullied (Wang Changling's "Seeing Off Xin Jian at Lotus Tower": "A heart of ice in a vase of jade"). Bright moon is commonly used in Buddhism to metaphorically mean a pure mind (Śūraṅgama Sūtra: "Pure like lapis lazuli, containing a precious moon within").

C: 韫椟而藏姑待姑：典出《论语·子罕》"韫椟而藏诸"，指怀才不露。"姑待姑"表面劝道姑安分，实则暗指"姑娘等待姑娘"（同性暧昧）。
E: Tucked away in a cabinet, waiting for the maiden.Alludes to Analects, "Zihan": "Concealed in a cabinet, waiting," meaning to hide one's talent and not reveal it. "Gu dai gu superficially advises the nun to be content, but actually hints at "maiden waiting for maiden" (homosexual ambiguity).

C: 嫁的个彭郎港口无：彭郎，江西彭泽县江边有彭郎矶，民间附会为小姑（山）之夫（《方舆胜览》）。陈最良用此典讽刺二道姑争风吃醋
E: Marry a Penglang, but there's no port.Penglang: by the river in Pengze County, Jiangxi, there is Penglang Rock, which folk etymology associated as the husband of Little Gu (Hill) (General Geography). Chen Zuiliang uses this allusion to satirize the two nuns for being jealous.

C: 裂了这仙衣四五铢：四五铢，极言仙衣轻薄（《太真外传》载天衣"重不过一铢"）。劝道姑撕破道袍还俗。
E: Tear this immortal robe of four or five zhu.Four or five zhu (a very small weight unit) emphasizes the extreme lightness of the immortal robe (Unofficial Biography of Taizhen records celestial clothes "weigh no more than one zhu"). Advises the nun to tear her Daoist robe and return to secular life.

C: 杜鹃花下雨：杜鹃啼血（《华阳国志》蜀帝化鹃传说）。白居易《琵琶行》"杜鹃啼血猿哀鸣"。陈最良泪洒杜丽娘坟前，呼应"春寒""穷泪"。
E: Under the azalea flowers, rain (tears).Cuckoo cries blood (legend of the Shu emperor transforming into a cuckoo in Chronicles of Huayang). Bai Juyi's "Song of the Pipa": "Cuckoos cry blood, apes wail mournfully." Chen Zuiliang sheds tears before Du Liniang's grave, echoing "spring chill" and "poor tears".

C: 幽辉半床：句见元稹《会真记》。本用来形容崔莺莺到张生那里幽会时的月景。这里暗示道姑到柳梦梅那边去幽会。
E: Dim light fills half the bed.Line seen in Yuan Zhen'sStory of Yingying. Originally used to describe the moonlight when Cui Yingying went to Zhang Sheng's place for a tryst. Here it hints that the nun went to Liu Mengmei's place for a tryst.

C: 柳下先生君子儒：春秋鲁国的儒者展禽，居柳下，死后私谥为惠。这是借指柳梦梅。君子儒，见《论语.雍也》。这里指规规矩矩的读书人。
E: The gentleman scholar beneath the willows.Zhan Qin, a Ru scholar of the state of Lu during the Spring and Autumn period, lived beneath the willows; posthumously given the private title Hui. This is used to refer to Liu Mengmei. "Gentleman scholar" see Analects, "Yong Ye". Here it means a proper, well-behaved scholar.

C: 金莲：三寸金莲，形容女人的脚小。
E: Golden lotus (bound feet).Three-inch golden lotus, describes a woman's small (bound) feet.

C: 银烛先教刻五分：南朝梁竟陵王萧子良与友人夜集，刻烛为诗。做四韵的刻一寸。见《南史.王僧孺传》。《全唐诗》卷二十三皮日休《奉和再招》："红蜡先教刻五分。"
E: The silver candle first taught marking five fen.Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling of the Southern Dynasties Liang, gathered with friends at night, notching candles to time poetry composition. One inch for a four-line stanza. See History of the Southern Dynasties, Biography of Wang Sengru. Pi Rixiu's "In Response to Another Invitation" in Quan Tangshi, Vol. 23: "The red candle first taught marking five fen."

C: 还则怕夜深花睡么：苏轼《苏文忠公诗》卷二十二《海棠》："只恐夜深花睡去，故烧高烛照红妆。"诗人只担心深夜时分花儿会进入梦乡沉沉睡去，所以特意点燃了高高的蜡烛，照耀着如同美人红妆般娇艳的海棠花。
E: Still fear that late at night the flowers will sleep?Su Shi's Collected Poems of Su Wenzhong, Vol. 22, "The Crab apple": "Only fear that late at night the flowers will fall asleep, so I burn a tall candle to shine on their red makeup." The poet only feared that late at night the flowers would enter dreamland and fall deeply asleep, so he specially lit a tall candle to illuminate the crabapple flowers, delicate and beautiful like a beauty's red makeup.

C: 画屏人踏歌：唐人传奇故事：有一士人醉卧醒来，看见画屏上的妇人，都来到他的床前歌舞，他一声惊叫，妇人就回到画屏上去了。见《酉阳杂俚.诺臬记》。
E: People from the painted screen step and sing.A Tang tale: A scholar was drunk and asleep; waking, he saw the women from the painted screen all come to his bedside to sing and dance; he cried out in surprise, and the women returned to the screen. See Youyang Zazu, "Records of Nuogao".

C: 北门卧护要耆英：《新唐书.裴度传》：唐宪宗以中书令裴度兼洒东节度使，差官向他宣谕说："为朕卧护北门可也。"耆英，老年的贤者。全者，凭藉老将的威名，就是卧着不动，也能收到防守北方的实效。
E: New Book of Tang, Biography of Pei Du: Emperor Xianzong of Tang appointed Pei Du, Secretariat Director, to concurrently command the Eastern Army. An official sent to inform him said: "For me, lying down and guarding the northern gate will suffice." Qiying means elderly worthies. The whole meaning: Relying on the old general's fearsome reputation, even lying down motionless, he could effectively defend the north.

C: 三千客：战国时代齐国孟尝君田文有食客三千人。见《史记.孟尝君列传》。这里是杜宝表示自己爱贤好客。
E: Three thousand guests.Tian Wen, Lord Mengchang of the state of Qi during the Warring States period, had three thousand retainers. See Records of the Grand Historian, "Biography of Lord Mengchang". Here Du Bao indicates his love for worthies and hospitality.

C: 百二：《史记.高祖本纪》："秦形胜之国，带河山之险，县隔千里，持戈百万，秦得百二焉。"形势险要，利于扼守，一百万人可以胜过一倍的敌人。
E: Records of the Grand Historian, "Basic Annals of Gaozu": "Qin is a country of strategic advantage, girdled by the perils of rivers and mountains; separated by a thousand li, holding a million spears, Qin gets one hundred and two." Meaning the terrain is strategically advantageous, easy to defend; one million men can overcome twice their number of enemies.

C: 按三韬把六出旗门放：《六韬》、《三略》都是古代的兵书。这里三韬，指阵图。六出旗门，指这个阵势有六个出入口。
E: According to the Three Strategies(or Six Secret Teachings), deploy the six-exit banner gates. The Six Secret Teaching sand Three Strategies are ancient military texts. Here "three strategies" likely refers to battle formations. "Six-exit banner gates" means this formation has six inlet and outlet .

C: 竹影寺：元代谚语："竹林寺有影无形。"元曲习用此语，如《汉宫秋》三折《醉春风》："想娘娘似竹林寺，不见半分形，只留下这个影、影。"这里是反用，既有影，人们捕风捉影，就免不了有闲话。
E: Zhuying Temple: A Yuan Dynasty proverb stated: "The Bamboo Grove Temple has a shadow but no form." This phrase was commonly used in Yuan drama (Zaju), such as in the aria "Drunk in the Spring Breeze" from Act III of The Sorrow of Han Palace: "I think of my lady like the Bamboo Grove Temple, not a trace of her form is seen, only this shadow, this shadow remains." Here it is used in reverse; since there is a shadow, people are prone to catching at shadows, which inevitably leads to gossip.

C: 那有个相如在客，肯驾香车？萧史无家，便用瑶阙：意思说：谁肯像卓文君私奔司马相如一样来爱一个异乡人？萧史不碰上秦弄玉，哪能上天？这两句都说自己未婚。
E: Where is there a Sima Xiangru living as a guest, willing to ride in a perfumed carriage? Xiao Shi had no home, yet he dwelt in a jade palace. The meaning is: Who would be willing to love a stranger like Zhuo Wenjun who eloped with Sima Xiangru? If Xiao Shi had not encountered Qin Nongyu, how could he have ascended to heaven? Both lines indicate that the speaker is unmarried.

C: 飞环：神话中女仙名，姓许。唐许浑梦登昆仑山，看见有人饮酒。他写了一首诗，诗中提到许飞环的名字。后来又梦到昆仑山，许飞环对他说："你为甚么把我的名字传出去？"许浑就把原句"座中唯有许飞环"改为"天风吹下步虚声。"见《本事诗》卷二。
E: Feihuan: The name of a female celestial in mythology, surnamed Xu. The Tang poet Xu Hun dreamt of ascending Mount Kunlun and saw people drinking wine. He wrote a poem mentioning the name Xu Feihuan. Later, he dreamt of Mount Kunlun again, and Xu Feihuan said to him: "Why did you spread my name abroad?" Xu Hun then changed the original line "Among the company, only Xu Feihuan was present" to "The heavenly wind blew down the sound of pacing the void." See Ben Shi Shi (The Origins of Poetry), Volume 2.

C: 七魄三魂：道家认为人有三魂七魄。这里就是魂魄、灵魂。
E: Seven Po and Three Hun: Daoism holds that a person has three Hun (ethereal souls) and seven Po (corporeal souls). Here it simply means soul or spirit.

C: 梦回远塞荒鸡呖：南唐李景词《摊破浣溪沙》："细雨梦回鸡塞远。"在一场淅淅沥沥的细雨中，主人公从梦乡中缓缓苏醒过来，恍惚间才惊觉，梦中与自己相会的远在鸡塞的那个人，实际上依旧远隔千山万水，鸡塞的距离还是那么的遥远。
E: Dreaming back to the distant frontier, a wild cock crows: From the lyric poem "Silk-Washing Stream" (expanded form) by Li Jing of the Southern Tang: "In the fine rain, waking from a dream, the fowl-frontier is far." In a continuous, drizzling rain, the protagonist slowly awakens from a dream and, in a daze, realizes with a start that the person who met them in the dream, far away at the Fowl-Frontier, is in reality still separated by countless mountains and rivers; the distance to the Fowl-Frontier remains vast.

C: 麻姑：神话中女仙名。他曾三次看见东海变为桑田。见《类说》卷三引《王氏神仙传》。
E: Magū: The name of a female celestial in mythology. She witnessed the Eastern Sea change into mulberry fields three times. See Lei Shuo (Classified Stories), Volume 3, quoting Wangshi Shenxian Zhuan (The Biographies of Immortals, Wang Clan).

C: 掉书子：掉书袋，引经据典自炫博学的人。这里指读书人。
E: Pedant: A "bookbag-dropper," one who shows off their learning by quoting classics and canons. Here it refers to a scholar or learned person.

C: 鼓盆歌、庐墓三年礼：鼓盆歌，悼亡。庄子的妻子死了，他没有哭泣，敲着盆子在唱歌。见《庄子.至乐》。庐墓，信在坟旁。妻丧不行庐墓三年礼，这里是调笑。
E: Drumming on a bowl and singing, observing the three-year mourning ritual by living in a hut by the grave: Drumming on a bowl and singing signifies mourning the deceased. When Zhuangzi's wife died, he did not weep but drummed on a bowl and sang. See Zhuangzi, Chapter "Ultimate Happiness". "Living in a hut by the grave" means dwelling beside the tomb. The three-year mourning ritual by the grave was not observed for a wife's death; here it is used jokingly.

C: 七级浮屠：救人命。谚语："救人一命，胜造七级浮屠。"浮屠，梵语的音译，即佛塔，本为安放骨殖之所。造浮屠，就是行功德、做善事。
E: Seven-storied pagoda: Saves a life. The proverb says: "Saving one life surpasses the merit of building a seven-storied pagoda." "Futu" is a transliteration of the Sanskrit word stūpa, meaning a Buddhist pagoda, originally a reliquary for housing bones. Building a pagoda is performing a meritorious deed, doing good.

C: 挡了凶煞：迷信的说法，冲撞（挡）了凶神（凶煞），就会害病。
E: Offending a baleful spirit: According to superstitious belief, if one offends or obstructs a malignant deity (a baleful spirit), they will fall ill.

C: 李少君：汉武帝时的方士名。自称有神妙的法术。见《史记.封禅书》。后来他渐渐成为传说中的人物。
E: Li Shaojun: The name of a Fangshi (magician/alchemist) during the reign of Emperor Wu of Han. He claimed to possess miraculous arts. See Records of the Grand Historian, "Feng Shan Shu" (Treatise on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices). Later he gradually became a legendary figure.

C: 地官符：指活埋。道家为人骗病夫作天、地、水三官手书（符），地官符埋入土内。见《三国志.魏志.张鲁传》注。
E: Di Guan Fu (Earth Official Talisman): Refers to live burial. Daoist masters prepared talismans (fu) for the Three Officials (Heaven, Earth, Water) to cure people's illnesses; the Earth Official Talisman was buried in the ground. See the commentary in Records of the Three Kingdoms, Book of Wei, "Biography of Zhang Lu".

C: 青台：这里疑作泉台、黄泉解。汤显祖在诗里用到青台，都是指歌楼酒馆。《玉茗堂诗》卷五《送安卿》："五陵年少宿青台，一岁烟花几度开？"同书卷七《送刘贻哲出饷宣府》："锦帐青台醉欲曛。"
E: Qingtai: Here it is likely interpreted as "Spring Terrace" or "Yellow Springs" (i.e., the underworld). When Tang Xianzu used "Qingtai" in his poems, it referred to singing towers and taverns. From Poems from the Jade Tea Hall, Volume 5, "Seeing An Qing Off": "The young gallants of the Five Mausoleums lodge at the Qingtai; how many times a year do the fireworks bloom?" From the same book, Volume 7, "Seeing Liu Yizhe Off on a Mission to Supply Xuanfu": "In brocade tents and blue towers, drunk until dusk."

C: 今夕何夕：《诗.唐风.绸缪》："今夕何夕，见此良人。子兮子兮，如此良人何？"这是一首爱人在晚上相会的诗。
E: What night is this night?: From the Book of Songs, "Airs of Tang", "Chou Mou": "What night is this night? That I see this good man. You, oh you, what shall I do with this good man?" This is a poem about lovers meeting at night.

C: 眠一柳，当了三槐：眠一柳，《三转旧事》："汉苑中有柳，状如人，号曰人柳。一日三眠三起。"三槐，三公。这里指春试第。全句意思说：一夜欢爱，就如取了功名一样。
E: Sleeping by a willow, equates to attaining the Three Dukes: "Sleeping by a willow" comes from Sanzhuan Jiushi (Old Tales in Three Volumes): "In the Han park there was a willow whose shape resembled a person; it was called the Human Willow. It slept and rose three times a day." The "Three Huai" refer to the Three Dukes (highest ministers). Here it means passing the spring examinations. The whole line means: A night of love is like attaining an official rank.

C: 柳耆卿：宋代著名的词作家柳永，字耆卿。许多小说、戏曲都写到他的风流故事。上句杜兰香和此句柳耆卿，和丽娘、梦梅的姓相合。
E: Liu Qi Qing: The famous Song Dynasty lyricist (Ci writer) Liu Yong, courtesy name Qi Qing. Many novels and plays wrote about his romantic stories. The previous line's Du Lanxiang and this line's Liu Qi Qing correspond with the surnames of Li Niang and Mengmei.

C: 春娘爱上酒家子楼：唐李昌符《婢仆诗》五十首中的二首："春娘爱上酒家楼，不怕归迟总不留。推道那家娘子卧，且留教住待梳头。""不论秋菊与春花，个个能嗵空肚茶。无事莫教频入库，一名闲物要些些。"见《北梦琐言》卷十。这是无聊文人侮辱劳动者的东西，剧作者引用它们，见出他自己的阶级局限性。
E: Chunniang falls in love and goes up to the tavern boy's loft: From two of the fifty "Poems about Maidservants" by Li Changfu of the Tang Dynasty: "Chunniang fell in love and went up to the tavern loft, not fearing to return late, she was never kept. Pushing aside the lady of that house who was lying down, she was asked to stay and wait to have her hair done." "Regardless of autumn chrysanthemums or spring flowers, each can drink tea on an empty stomach. Don't let them frequently enter the storehouse for no reason, a mere idle thing requires a little something." See Beimeng Suoyan (Trifling Words of the Northern Dream), Volume 10. This is something written by idle literati to insult laborers; the playwright's use of them reveals his own class limitations.

C: 如笑如呆，欢情丝不断，梦境重开：化用李商隐《无题》中"春心莫共花争发，一寸相思一寸灰"的意境，描写杜丽娘还魂后似梦似醒的情态。"欢情丝"暗指《牡丹亭》核心主题"情不知所起，一往而深。"
E: Like laughing, like dazed, threads of joyous feeling unbroken, the dream scene reopens: Evokes the conception and mood of Li Shangyin's "Untitled" poem: "Do not let your spring heart strive to bloom with the flowers, for every inch of longing turns to ashes." It describes Du Liniang's dreamlike, trance-like state after her soul returns. "Threads of joyous feeling" alludes to the core theme of The Peony Pavilion: "Love comes from whence none knows, yet once come, it goes deep."

C: 惊香辞地府，舆梓出天台："舆梓"出自《后汉书·方术传》费长房故事，指载着棺木离开阴间；"天台"典出刘晨阮肇入天台山遇仙传说，此处反其意而用，指从阴间重返人世。
E: Startled fragrance takes leave of the underworld; bearing the coffin, she emerges from Tiantai. "Bearing the coffin" comes from the story of Fei Changfang in the "Biographies of Magical Technicians" chapter of the Book of the Later Han, meaning carrying the coffin out of the netherworld. "Tiantai" alludes to the legend of Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao entering Tiantai Mountain and encountering immortals; here the meaning is reversed, indicating a return from the underworld to the world of the living.

C: 怕如烟入抱，似影投怀：源自《庄子·齐物论》"方其梦也，不知其梦也"与《列子·周穆王》"形所假者，性所托者"，表现虚实难辨的恍惚状态。
E: Fearing like smoke entering the embrace, like a shadow throwing itself into her bosom: Derived from Zhuangzi, "Discussion on Making All Things Equal": "While he is dreaming he does not know it is a dream," and from Liezi, "King Mu of Zhou": "What the form borrows, what the nature entrusts itself to." It expresses a trance-like state where reality and illusion are hard to distinguish.

C: 蛾眉秋恨满三霜：汤显祖自创词句。"三霜"出自《诗经·豳风·七月》"九月肃霜"，借指三年时光，呼应杜丽娘死去三年的情节。
E: Moth-eyebrows filled with autumn resentment for three frosts: A phrase coined by Tang Xianzu. "Three frosts" comes from the Book of Songs, "Airs of Bin", "Seventh Month": "In the ninth month, harsh frosts fall," borrowed here to mean three years' time, echoing the plot point of Du Liniang being dead for three years.

C: 土花零落旧罗裳，睡损红妆："土花"出自李贺《金铜仙人辞汉歌》"三十六宫土花碧"，指苔藓；"睡损红妆"化用温庭筠《菩萨蛮》"懒起画蛾眉，弄妆梳洗迟"，描写墓中容颜凋零。
E: Earth-flowers (moss) scatter over the old silk robes; sleep has damaged the rouge and powder. "Earth-flowers" comes from Li He's "Song of the Bronze Immortal Bidding Farewell to Han": "In the thirty-six palaces, the earth-flowers are green," meaning moss. "Sleep has damaged the rouge and powder" adapts Wen Tingyun's "Buddhist Dancers": "Lazily rising to paint moth-eyebrows, slowly adorning, washing, and combing." It describes the fading of her appearance in the tomb.

C: 风定彩云独怯，火传金拖重梨："彩云独怯"化用李白《宫中行乐词》"只愁歌舞散，化作彩云飞"，表现杜丽娘还魂后的脆弱；"火传金拖"或为"火传金柝"之误，典出《晋书·天文志》夜间更柝声，比喻阴阳界限模糊。
E: The wind settles, the colored clouds alone are timid; the fire passes the golden watchman's clapper, heavy and pear-shaped. "The colored clouds alone are timid" adapts Li Bai's "Palace Poem of Merry-Making": "Only fearing the song and dance will scatter, turning into colored clouds and flying away," expressing Du Liniang's fragility after her soul's return. "The fire passes the golden watchman's clapper" might be an error for "the fire passes the golden watchman's clapper" （jintuo), alluding to the sound of the night watchman's clapper in the Book of Jin, "Treatise on Astronomy," metaphorically suggesting the blurring of the boundary between Yin (netherworld) and Yang (living world).

C: 除是高唐：出自宋玉《高唐赋》楚王梦神女典故，原句"妾在巫山之阳，高丘之阻，旦为朝云，暮为行雨"，此处形容杜丽娘还魂如神女入梦般虚幻。
E: Unless it is the Gaotang Shrine: Comes from the story of King Xiang of Chu dreaming of the goddess in Song Yu's "Rhapsody on the Gaotang Shrine." The original line is: "I dwell on the sunny side of Mount Wu, amid the high hills' obstacles. At dawn I am the morning clouds, at dusk I am the passing rain." Here it describes Du Liniang's return from death as being as illusory as the goddess entering a dream.

C: 死淋侵走上阳台，活森沙走出这泉台："阳台"出自《高唐赋》"朝朝暮暮，阳台之下"，指男女相会之处；"泉台"出自《左传·僖公二十五年》，指阴间。两句形成生死对比。
E: Drenched in death, she walks up to the Sunny Terrace (lover's rendezvous); vividly alive, she walks out of this Spring Terrace (underworld). "Sunny Terrace" comes from the "Rhapsody on the Gaotang Shrine": "Morning after morning, evening after evening, beneath the Sunny Terrace," meaning a place for lovers to meet. "Spring Terrace" comes from the Zuo Zhuan, 25th Year of Duke Xi, meaning the underworld. The two lines form a contrast between death and life.

C: 艳质久尘埋，又挣出这烟花界："尘埋"出自《搜神记》谈生故事中鬼妻复生情节；"烟花界"化用张若虚《春江花月夜》"昨夜闲潭梦落花"，指人间红尘。
E: Her beautiful form long buried in dust, she struggles free again from this realm of mist and flowers (mortal world). "Buried in dust" comes from the story of Tan Sheng in In Search of the Supernatural, where the ghost wife returns to life. "Realm of mist and flowers" adapts Zhang Ruoxu's "Spring, River, Flowers, Moon, Night": "Last night in the idle pool I dreamed of falling flowers," meaning the mortal world of red dust.

C: 地窟里扶卿做玉真："地窟"出自《搜神记》人鬼相恋故事；"玉真"出自唐代《逸史》玉真娘子传说，或源自曹植《洛神赋》"凌波微步"的洛神形象，比喻重生如仙。
E: From the earthen vault (tomb) I help you become a Jade Perfected (immortal). "Earthen vault" comes from stories of love between humans and ghosts in In Search of the Supernatural. "Jade Perfected" comes from the legend of the Lady Jade Perfected in the Tang Unofficial History, or perhaps from the image of the Luo River Goddess in Cao Zhi's "Rhapsody on the Goddess of the Luo": "Treading the waves with light steps," metaphorically comparing rebirth to becoming an immortal.

C: 风吹不动顶垂丝：唐雍陶《咏双白鹭》："双鹭应怜水满池，风飘不动顶丝垂"。雍陶任简州刺史时，在成都浣花溪观察白鹭，见其头顶羽毛（垂丝）在风中纹丝不动，遂作此诗咏其静立之姿。
E: The wind blows, yet it does not stir the silken threads hanging from its crown.From Yong Tao's (Tang Dynasty) "Ode to a Pair of White Egrets": "The pair of egrets must pity the pool filled with water; the wind blows, yet the silken threads on their crowns hang motionless." While serving as Prefect of Jianzhou, Yong Tao observed egrets at Huanhua Stream in Chengdu and noticed the feathers on their heads (the hanging threads) remained perfectly still in the wind, so he wrote this poem praising their serene posture.

C: 吟背春城出草迟：唐郑谷《中年》："苔色满墙寻故第，雨声一夜忆春城"。郑谷晚年回忆往事的诗作，描写暮春时节寻访旧居所见苔藓满墙、夜雨怀城的萧瑟景象。
E:
Chanting, back turned to the spring city, the grass emerges late.
From Zheng Gu's (Tang Dynasty) "Middle Age": "The color of moss fills the walls as I search for my old residence; the sound of rain all night makes me remember the spring city." A poem by Zheng Gu recalling past events in his later years, describing the bleak scene of visiting an old residence in late spring, seeing moss-covered walls, and thinking of the city on a rainy night.

C: 毕竟百年浑是梦：唐李涉《题鹤林寺僧舍》："终日昏昏醉梦间，忽闻春尽强登山"。李涉在镇江遇盗，盗匪闻其诗名而释之，遂于鹤林寺题壁抒发人生虚幻之感。
E: After all, a hundred years are utterly like a dream.From Li She's (Tang Dynasty) "Inscribed on the Monk's Abode at Helin Temple": "All day in a daze between drunkenness and dreams, suddenly I hear that spring is ending and force myself to climb the mountain." Li She encountered bandits in Zhenjiang who, upon hearing his fame as a poet, released him. He then inscribed this poem on the wall of Helin Temple expressing the illusory nature of life.

C: 夜来风雨葬西施：唐韩偓《哭花》："若是有情争不哭，夜来风雨葬西施"。韩偓以春秋越国美女西施沉江的传说为喻，描写风雨摧花的凄凉景象。
E: Last night's wind and rain buried Xi Shi.From Han Wo's (Tang Dynasty) "Mourning the Flowers": "If they had feeling, could they contend not to weep? Last night's wind and rain buried Xi Shi." Han Wo uses the legend of the beautiful Xi Shi of the Spring and Autumn period Yue state drowning in a river as a metaphor to describe the bleak scene of wind and rain destroying flowers.

C: 严扉不掩云长在：《列子·汤问》："云气不待族而雨"。殷汤问夏革自然之理，夏革解释云雾不需积聚即可降雨的自然现象。
E: The stern gate unbarred, clouds perpetually dwell.From Liezi, "Questions of Tang": "Cloud vapor does not wait to gather before it rains." King Tang of Yin asked Xia Ge about the principles of nature; Xia Ge explained the natural phenomenon where clouds and mist can produce rain without needing to accumulate first.

C: 院径无媒草自深：《诗经·召南·野有死麕》："野有死麕，白茅包之"。描写青年猎人用白茅包裹猎物，向怀春少女示爱的古老婚恋习俗。
E: The courtyard path without a go-between, the grass grows deep of itself. From the Book of Songs, "Airs of Zhao and South", "In the Wilds Lies a Dead Roe": "In the wilds lies a dead roe, wrapped with white rushes." Describes the ancient courtship custom where a young hunter wraps his game in white rushes to present to a lovesick maiden.

C: 当时曾此葬金钗：《晋书·吴猛传》："猛乃密将金钗置棺中"。吴猛家贫，无力置办陪葬品，遂将亡妻金钗偷偷放入棺中，后感动天神使金钗复现。
E: Here, in those times, a gold hairpin was buried. From the Book of Jin, "Biography of Wu Meng": "Wu Meng secretly placed a gold hairpin inside the coffin." Wu Meng's family was poor and could not afford burial goods, so he secretly placed his deceased wife's gold hairpin in her coffin; later, he moved the heavenly gods, and the hairpin reappeared.

C: 玉镜台无分照泉台：《世说新语·假谲》载温峤以玉镜台为聘，诈称代人说媒，实则自娶表妹刘氏的故事。
E: The jade mirror-stand has no part in illuminating the Spring Terrace (underworld). The Shishuo Xinyu (A New Account of the Tales of the World), chapter "False and Cunning," records the story of Wen Jiao using a jade mirror-stand as a betrothal gift, falsely claiming to be arranging a match for someone else, but actually marrying his cousin Miss Liu himself.

C: 昆池碎劫无余在：《搜神记》卷十三载汉武帝开凿昆明池得黑灰，西域胡僧识为"天地劫灰之余"，乃上古劫火焚烧后的残留物。
E: Of the shattered kalpa at Kunming Pool, nothing remains. In Search of the Supernatural, Volume 13, records that when Emperor Wu of Han excavated the Kunming Pool, he found black ashes. A Western Regions monk identified them as "the remnants of the kalpa ashes of heaven and earth," leftover from the burning of the primordial kalpa fire.

C: 观音锁骨连环债：《太平广记》卷一百一记延州妇人死后，胡僧发现其骨节如锁链相连，曰："此锁骨菩萨，慈悲喜舍之所致也"
E: Guanyin's Locked-Bone Karmic Debt: The Extensive Records of the Taiping Era, Volume 101, records that after a woman from Yanzhou died, a foreign monk found her bone joints interlinked like a chain, saying: "This is the Bodhisattva of the Interlocking Bones, resulting from her compassion, kindness, joy, and relinquishment."

C: 乱红衣暗泣莲腮：唐李贺《黄头郎》："红衣落尽暗莲愁"。描写秋塘中残荷凋零，如含愁哭泣的拟人化景象。
E: Disordered red garments secretly weep on lotus cheeks. From Li He's (Tang Dynasty) "The Yellow-Head Bailiff": "The red garments all fallen, the hidden lotus grieves." Describes the personified image of withered lotus blossoms fading in an autumn pond, as if weeping with sorrow.

C: 虎儿出于柙，龟玉毁于椟中：《论语·季氏》："虎兕出于柙，龟玉毁于椟中，是谁之过与？"孔子以猛兽出笼、宝玉毁匣比喻官员失职。
E: The tiger cub escapes from its cage; the tortoise-shell and jade are destroyed within their casket. From the Analects of Confucius, "Ji Shi": "When a tiger or rhinoceros escapes from its cage, when tortoise-shell or jade is destroyed in its casket—whose fault is it?" Confucius uses the metaphors of a wild beast escaping its pen and precious jade being destroyed in its box to criticize official negligence.

C: 石虔婆他古弄里金珠曾见来：《晋书·石崇传》记石崇婢女翔风能辨玉声、金色，尝言："西方、北方玉声沉重而性温润"
E: Stone Fierce Grandma, in that old lane, has seen gold and pearls before. The Book of Jin, "Biography of Shi Chong," records that Shi Chong's maidservant, Xiangfeng, could discern the sound of jade and the quality of gold. She once said: "Jade from the west and north has a heavy sound and a warm, moist nature."

C: 破周书汲冢才：《晋书·束皙传》："太康二年，汲郡人不准盗发魏襄王墓，得竹书数十车"。记载西晋盗墓者发现汲冢竹简的史实。
E: The talent that recovered the lost Zhou texts from the Ji Tomb. The Book of Jin, "Biography of Shu Xi": "In the second year of the Taikang era, a man from Ji Commandery named Bu Zhuo illicitly opened the tomb of King Xiang of Wei and obtained several cartloads of bamboo texts." Records the historical fact of the discovery of the Ji Tomb bamboo slips by a tomb raider during the Western Jin Dynasty.

C: 金盍银墙做打家贼：汉乐府《陌上桑》："青丝系马尾，黄金络马头"。描写罗敷夫婿"腰中鹿卢剑，可值千万余"的富贵形象。
E: Gold caps and silver walls make a house-breaking thief. From the Han Dynasty Music Bureau poem "Mulberries by the Path": "Blue threads tied to the horse's tail, yellow gold bridling the horse's head." Describes the wealthy image of Luofu's husband: "At his waist a deer-stalker sword, worth more than ten million."

C: 靴尖踢倒长天堑：南宁末投降蒙古的叛将吕文焕答宋太皇太后书："孤城其如弹丸，谓靴尖之踢倒；长江虽曰堑固，欲提鞭而断流。"见《说郛》卷七引《钱唐遣事》。
E: The tip of a boot could kick over the long Heavenly Moat (Yangtze River). From the letter of the traitorous general Lü Wenhuan (who surrendered to the Mongols at the end of the Southern Song) in reply to the Grand Empress Dowager of Song: "An isolated city is like a pellet, said to be kicked over by a boot tip; although the Yangtze River is called a solid moat, I wish to lift my whip and cut its flow." See Shuo Fu (The Story Net), Volume 7, quoting Qiantaang Yishi (Forgotten Events of Qiantang).

C: 七步才：形容人才思很快。曹植被他的哥哥魏文帝曹丕所迫，在七步内写成一首诗："煮豆持作羹，漉豉以为汁。箕在釜下燃，豉在釜中泣。本自同根生，相煎何太急！"见《世说新语.文学》。
E: Seven-Paces Talent: Describes someone whose literary thoughts are very swift. Cao Zhi was pressured by his brother, Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), to compose a poem within seven paces: "They boiled beans to make a broth, / They filtered the beans to extract the juice. / The beanstalks burned beneath the cauldron, / The beans in the cauldron wept. / Since we sprang from the selfsame root, / Why should you torment me so urgently!" See Shishuo Xinyu, "Literature".

C: 沈醉了九重春色：九重，天子信处。《楚辞.九辩》："君之门以九重。"春，喻酒。杜甫《草堂诗笺》卷十二《奉和贾至舍人早朝大明宫》诗："九重春色醉仙桃。"
E: Deeply intoxicated by the ninefold spring hues. "Ninefold" refers to the imperial palace, the abode of the Son of Heaven. From the Chu Ci, "Nine Arguments": "The lord's gates are of ninefold depth." "Spring" here metaphorically means wine. From Du Fu's poem in Cottage Poetry Notes, Volume 12, "In Response to Secretary Jia Zhi's 'Early Audience at the Daming Palace'": "The ninefold spring hues intoxicate the immortal peaches."

C: 看花：《全唐诗》卷十四孟郊《登科后》诗："春风得意马蹄疾，一日看遍长安花。"
E: Viewing the Flowers: From Meng Jiao's poem "After Passing the Imperial Examinations" in the Complete Tang Poems, Volume 14: "The spring wind is pleased with my success, my horse's hooves move swiftly; in one day I have seen all the flowers of Chang'an."

C: 论四德、似你那三从结愿谐：四德：妇德、妇言、妇容、妇工。三从，女人"未嫁从你、既嫁从夫，夫死后从子"。三从、四德都是用来束缚妇女的封建教条。
E: Discussing the Four Virtues, hoping your Three Obediences will lead to a harmonious union. The Four Virtues are: womanly virtue, womanly speech, womanly appearance, and womanly work. The Three Obediences are: a woman obeys her father before marriage, her husband after marriage, and her son after her husband's death. The Three Obediences and Four Virtues were feudal doctrines used to restrict women.

C: 尺水：《意林》引桓谭《新论》："龙无尺水，无以升天；圣人无尺土，无以王天下。"
E: A foot of water: The Forest of Ideas quotes Huan Tan's New Discussions: "A dragon without a foot of water has no means to ascend to heaven; a sage without a foot of earth has no means to rule the world."

C: 笔尖花：指有才学的人。诗人"李白少诗，梦所用之笔头上生花。后天才赡逸，名闻天下"。见《开元天宝遗事》。
E: Flowers at the brush tip: Refers to a person of talent and learning. The poet "Li Bai, when young, dreamt that the brush he was using sprouted flowers at its tip. Later, his innate talent was abundant and free, and his fame spread throughout the world." See Anecdotes from the Kaiyuan and Tianbao Eras.

C: 浪桃花当一科：黄河春汛叫桃花汛，这时鱼可以乘浪登龙门，比喻在奏举行的进士度登第。一科，一次、一届考试。全句意思说：虽然没有好文章，也只好算考了一科。
E: Rogue peach blossoms count as one examination session. The Yellow River's spring flood is called the Peach Blossom Flood; at this time, fish can ride the waves to leap the Dragon Gate (metaphor for passing the imperial exams). It metaphorically means passing the Jinshi examination held in the capital. "One session" means one sitting, one round of the exams. The whole line means: Even without good examination essays, one might as well consider it as having sat for one session.

C: 当今呵，宝驾迟留，则道西湖书锦游：当今、宝驾，都指皇帝。书锦，衣锦还乡。项羽说："宝贵不归故乡，如衣锦夜行。"见《史记.项羽本纪》。宋韩琦以宰相衔回家乡做官，造书归堂。欧阳修为他写了一篇《书锦堂记》。全句意思指，皇帝在杭州逗留，错把这个地方当作自己的故乡了。有如南宋当时人的诗句所说："错把杭州作汴州。"
E: Now, the precious carriage lingers, mistakenly thinking West Lake is a brocade-clad homecoming tour. "Now" and "precious carriage" both refer to the emperor. "Brocade-clad homecoming" means returning home in glory. Xiang Yu said: "To attain wealth and honor and not return to one's hometown is like wearing embroidered clothes at night." See Records of the Grand Historian, "Basic Annals of Xiang Yu". Han Qi of the Song Dynasty returned to his hometown as a high official (with the title of Chancellor) and built a "Hall of Brocade Return." Ouyang Xiu wrote an essay for him titled "Record of the Hall of Brocade Return." The whole line means the emperor, lingering in Hangzhou, mistakes this place for his homeland. It is like the line from a Southern Song poet: "Mistakenly taking Hangzhou for Bianzhou (the old capital)."

C: 西风扬子津头树：化用唐孟浩然《早寒江上有怀》"木落雁南渡，北风江上寒"。原诗描写秋日思乡之情。扬子津为古渡口，在今扬州南，此处借秋景烘托杜宝忧国之情。
E: West wind at the trees of Yangzi Ford. Adapts Meng Haoran's (Tang Dynasty) "Thoughts on the River in Early Cold": "Leaves fall, wild geese cross south; the north wind chills the river." The original poem describes autumn homesickness. Yangzi Ford was an ancient ferry crossing south of present-day Yangzhou; here the autumn scene is used to highlight Du Bao's anxiety for the nation.

C: 望长淮渺渺愁予：典出《楚辞·九歌·湘夫人》"帝子降兮北渚，目眇眇兮愁予"。原句描写湘君望穿秋水的愁思，此处杜宝借以表达对淮河战事的忧虑。
E: Gazing at the vast Long Huai (Huai River), sorrow fills me. Alludes to the Chu Ci, "Nine Songs", "The Lady of the Xiang River": "The princess descends on the northern isle; my eyes gaze afar, sorrow fills me." The original line describes the Lord of the Xiang's sorrowful longing, gazing until his eyes grew dim. Here, Du Bao uses it to express his anxiety about the military situation on the Huai River.

C: 砧声又报一年秋：出自南宋陆游《秋思》"砧声敲残深巷月，井梧摇落故园秋"。原诗通过捣衣声表现岁月流逝，此处暗示杜宝在扬州已驻守三年。
E: The sound of fulling blocks announces another autumn. From Lu You's (Southern Song) "Autumn Thoughts": "The sound of fulling blocks chipping away the moon in the deep lane; the well-side parasol tree shakes loose, autumn in my old garden." The original poem uses the sound of clothes-pounding to convey the passage of time; here it hints that Du Bao has been stationed in Yangzhou for three years.

C: 塞草中原何处：化用唐王维《使至塞上》"征蓬出汉塞，归雁入胡天"。原诗描写边塞景象，此处反用，表达对中原沦陷区的牵挂。
E: Where in the Central Plains are the frontier grasses? Adapts Wang Wei's (Tang Dynasty) "On Mission to the Frontier": "A lone tumbleweed leaves the Han frontier; returning geese enter the Hu sky." The original poem describes the frontier scene; here it is used inversely to express concern for the occupied Central Plains.

C: 一雁过淮楼：典出《汉书·苏武传》雁足传书故事。原指鸿雁传递书信，此处暗指战报传递，同时象征杜宝孤独的守将形象。
E: A lone goose passes the Huai River tower. Alludes to the story of the goose-foot messenger from the Book of Han, "Biography of Su Wu". Originally referring to a wild goose carrying a letter, here it subtly refers to the transmission of military dispatches and also symbolizes Du Bao's lonely image as a defending general.

C: 天下事，鬓边愁，付东流：化用宋辛弃疾《水龙吟》"倩何人唤取，红巾翠袖，揾英雄泪"。原词抒发壮志难酬之悲，此处表现杜宝将家国忧虑强自压抑。
E: The affairs of the world, the sorrows at my temples, I consign to the east-flowing stream. Adapts Xin Qiji's (Song Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Water Dragon Chant": "But who is there to call, with red handkerchief and green sleeve, to wipe a hero's tears?" The original lyric expresses the sadness of unfulfilled ambition; here it shows Du Bao forcibly suppressing his worries about family and country.

C: 不分吾家小杜：典出《新唐书·杜牧传》。杜牧人称"小杜"以别于杜甫，此处杜宝自比杜牧，暗含对文官领兵的自嘲。
E: Unexpectedly, our family's Little Du. Alludes to the New Book of Tang, "Biography of Du Mu". Du Mu was called "Little Du" to distinguish him from Du Fu. Here, Du Bao compares himself to Du Mu, implying self-mockery about a scholar leading troops.

C: 清时醉梦扬州：化用唐杜牧《遣怀》"十年一觉扬州梦，赢得青楼薄幸名"。原诗反思扬州放浪生活，此处反其意，表现乱世中难得的平静时光。
E: In peaceful times, drunken dreams in Yangzhou. Adapts Du Mu's (Tang Dynasty) "Expressing My Feelings": "Ten years, I woke from a Yangzhou dream, having won, in the blue houses, a name for fickleness." The original poem reflects on a dissolute life in Yangzhou; here the meaning is reversed to express a rare period of calm in turbulent times.

C: 画屏风外秦淮树：典出五代顾闳中《韩熙载夜宴图》。画屏象征富贵生活，秦淮树暗示南京风物，表现夫人对江南安稳生活的怀念。
E: Beyond the painted screen, the trees of Qinhuai. Alludes to Gu Hongzhong's (Five Dynasties) painting "The Night Revels of Han Xizai". The painted screen symbolizes a life of luxury; the Qinhuai trees evoke the scenery of Nanjing (Jiankang), expressing the lady's nostalgia for a stable life in Jiangnan.

C: 两点金焦：指镇江金山、焦山。典出宋陆游《入蜀记》对两山的记载，此处借江南名胜反衬战乱阴影。
E: The two dots of Jin and Jiao: Refer to Mount Jin and Mount Jiao in Zhenjiang. Alludes to Lu You's (Song Dynasty)Diary of a Journey to Shu which records these two mountains. Here, the famous Jiangnan landmarks are used to contrast with the shadow of war.

C: 忘忧恨自少宜男：典出《诗经·卫风·伯兮》"焉得谖草，言树之背"。谖草即忘忧草，原诗写思妇之愁，此处双关杜家无子之憾。
E: Forgetting sorrow, regretting the lack of a son. Alludes to the Book of Songs, "Airs of Wei", "My Lord": "Where can I get the grass of forgetfulness? I would plant it behind the house." The grass of forgetfulness is the daylily. The original poem writes of a pining woman's sorrow; here it puns on the Du family's regret at having no son.

C: 羽檄从参赞：典出《汉书·高帝纪》"吾以羽檄征天下兵"。羽檄指插羽毛的紧急文书，此处表现军情紧急。
E: Feather dispatches follow the advisor. Alludes to the Book of Han, "Annals of Emperor Gaozu": "I used feather dispatches to summon troops from across the land." "Feather dispatches" refer to urgent documents with feathers attached, indicating the urgency of the military situation here.

C: 牙几报驿程：典出《周礼·夏官》"牙璋以起军旅"。牙几指将帅符信，此处描写驿站传递军令的场景。
E: The tally-tablet reports the courier station's distance. Alludes to the Rites of Zhou, "Offices of Summer": "The tooth-shaped scepter (yazhang) is used to raise the army." The "tally-tablet" (yaji) refers to the general's tally or credentials. Here it describes the scene of military orders being transmitted via courier stations.

C: 参军杜甫：典出《旧唐书·杜甫传》"甫往来梓、夔间，漂泊西南天地间"。安史之乱中杜甫与妻子离散，此处比喻杜宝夫妻乱世分离。
E: (Military Advisor like Du Fu. Alludes to the Old Book of Tang, "Biography of Du Fu": "Du Fu traveled between Zizhou and Kuizhou, drifting between heaven and earth in the southwest." During the An Lushan Rebellion, Du Fu was separated from his wife; here it serves as a metaphor for the separation of Du Bao and his wife in times of turmoil.

C: 山妻泣向天隅：化用杜甫《述怀》"去年潼关破，妻子隔绝久...寄书问三川，不知家在否"。原诗描写战乱中夫妻离散之苦，与此处情境直接呼应。
E: My mountain wife weeps, facing the corner of the sky. Adapts Du Fu's "Expressing My Feelings": "Last year Tong Pass fell, my wife and children were cut off for a long time... I sent a letter inquiring of Sanchuan, not knowing if my home still stood." The original poem describes the suffering of family separation during war, directly echoing the situation here.

C: 鳏寡孤独：典出《孟子·梁惠王下》"老而无妻曰鳏，老而无夫曰寡..."。原指四种弱势群体，此处形容战乱造成的家庭破碎。
E: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless. Alludes to Mencius, "King Hui of Liang, Part II": "Those old without wives are called widowers; those old without husbands are called widows..." Originally referring to four disadvantaged groups, here it describes the family fragmentation caused by war.

C: 满眼兵戈一腐儒：化用杜甫《江汉》"江汉思归客，乾坤一腐儒"。原诗自嘲书生无用，此处杜宝夫人感叹文官在乱世的无力感。
E: My eyes filled with weapons of war, I am but a pedantic scholar. Adapts Du Fu's "River Han": "A traveler on the River Han longing for home, between heaven and earth, a pedantic scholar." The original poem is self-mocking about the uselessness of a scholar; here, Du Bao's wife laments the powerlessness of a civil official in chaotic times.

C: 猿啼鹤怨：官、兵的怨声。神话传说：周穆王南征，军官化为猿、鹤，士兵化为虫、沙。见《太平御览》七十四。
E: Apes cry, cranes lament: The complaints of officers and soldiers. A mythological legend says: King Mu of Zhou campaigned south; his officers turned into apes and cranes, his soldiers turned into insects and sand. See Taiping Yulan (Imperial Readings of the Taiping Era), Volume

C: 追风腻旗儿：追风，形容旗子迎风飘展。腻旗，小旗。《词林摘艳》无名氏《门鹌鹑.骠骑.秃厮儿》："追风腻旗手内揉。"又《盛世新声.集贤宾.元和令》："急穰穰追风小腻旗。"
E: Chasing-the-wind, sleek-flag: "Chasing-the-wind" describes a flag fluttering in the wind. "Sleek-flag" means a small flag. From the anonymous aria in Cilin Zhaiyan (Gems from the Forest of Lyrics): "The chasing-the-wind sleek-flag is kneaded in the hand." Also from Shengshi Xinsheng (New Sounds of a Prosperous Age): "Hastily, hastily, the chasing-the-wind little sleek-flag."

C: 开府弄丸，来赴两家之难：开府，开设幕府，主管一方军政大权。此指安抚杜宝。弄丸，一种抛弄弹子的杂技。春秋时代楚国与宋国打仗，楚国勇士熊宜僚在军前弄丸，宋兵停战看他，因而失败。全句意思说：安抚取胜很容易。语本《庄.徐无鬼》："市南宜僚，弄丸而两家之难解。"原指宜僚的另一件事：楚国白公胜要杀子西、子期，派人去请宜僚帮助，宜僚在弄丸不答应，但也不把白公的阴谋泄露。
E: The Commandery Governor juggles balls, coming to resolve the conflict between the two families. "Opening a commandery" means establishing a headquarters, taking charge of military and administrative power in a region. Here it refers to the Pacification Commissioner Du Bao. "Juggling balls" is a kind of juggling trick. During the Spring and Autumn period, when Chu and Song were at war, the Chu warrior Xiong Yiliao juggled balls in front of the army; the Song soldiers stopped fighting to watch him, and thus were defeated. The whole line means: The Pacification Commissioner's victory was easily achieved. The phrasing originates from Zhuangzi, "Xu Wugui": "Shinan Yiliao juggled balls and the conflict between the two families was resolved." This originally referred to another incident involving Yiliao: Bai Gong Sheng of Chu wanted to kill Zixi and Zigi and sent someone to ask Yiliao for help; Yiliao, while juggling balls, refused but also did not reveal Bai Gong's plot.

C: 晓妆台圆梦鹊声高：典出《开元天宝遗事》"时人之家，闻鹊声皆以为喜兆，故谓灵鹊报喜"。原故事记载唐代宫女七夕捉蜘蛛闭于小盒，次日观网密疏卜巧，此处化用为喜鹊报科举喜讯。
E: At the morning dressing table, interpreting a dream, magpie cries sound loud. Alludes to Anecdotes from the Kaiyuan and Tianbao Eras: "In those days, people's households considered the sound of magpies an omen of joy, hence they were called 'prophetic magpies announcing good news'." The original story records Tang palace ladies catching spiders on the Double Seventh Festival and shutting them in small boxes, observing the density of their webs the next day to divine skill; here it is adapted to mean magpies announcing success in the imperial examinations.

C: 博山秋影摇：典出《西京杂记》"长安巧工丁缓作九层博山香炉"。博山炉为汉代名器，形似海上仙山，此处借指闺阁梳妆场景，暗含仙境意象。
E: The autumn shadow of the Boshan censer sways. Alludes to the Miscellaneous Records of the Western Capital: "The skilled craftsman Ding Huan of Chang'an made a nine-tiered Boshan censer." The Boshan censer was a famous Han Dynasty artifact, shaped like the mythical mountains of the immortals in the sea. Here it refers to the boudoir dressing scene, implying an immortal realm imagery.

C: 盼泥金俺明香暗焦：泥金典出《卢氏杂说》唐代进士及第用泥金帖报喜。原指用金粉书写的榜帖，此处双关，既指科举喜报，又暗喻杜丽娘复活后对世俗认可的渴望。
E: Longing for the gilt-paper announcement, I burn incense openly yet fret secretly. "Gilt-paper" alludes to the Lushi Zashuo (Miscellaneous Sayings of Mr. Lu): in the Tang Dynasty, gilt-paper notices were used to announce success in the Jinshi examinations. Originally referring to the announcement written in gold powder, here it has a double meaning: both the examination success notice and a metaphor for Du Liniang's desire for worldly acceptance after her resurrection.

C: 鬼魂求出世，贫落望登科：化用唐郑谷《赠下第举公》"见君失意我惆怅，记得当年落第情"。原诗描写科举失意，此处反用，表现鬼魂（杜丽娘）与寒士（柳梦梅）共同的世俗追求。
E: A ghost seeks rebirth into the world; a poor scholar hopes to pass the exams. Adapts Zheng Gu's (Tang Dynasty) "To a Failed Candidate": "Seeing you disappointed makes me melancholy, I remember the feeling of failing in years past." The original poem describes the disappointment of failing the exams; here it is used inversely to show the shared worldly aspirations of the ghost (Du Liniang) and the poor scholar (Liu Mengmei).

C: 长安咫尺如千里：典出《世说新语·夙惠》"举目见日，不见长安"。原指晋明帝幼时对长安距离的认知，此处比喻功名可望不可即。
E: Chang'an is so close yet seems a thousand miles away. Alludes to the Shishuo Xinyu, "Early Intelligence": "Lifting my eyes I see the sun, but I do not see Chang'an." Originally referring to the young Emperor Ming of Jin's perception of the distance to Chang'an, here it metaphorically means that official rank is within sight but unattainable.

C: 夫婿迢遥第一人：化用唐张籍《节妇吟》"还君明珠双泪垂，恨不相逢未嫁时"。原诗表现婚姻与道德的冲突，此处反用，突出杜丽娘对丈夫科举的期待。
E: My husband, far away, is the foremost candidate. Adapts Zhang Ji's (Tang Dynasty) "Song of the Virtuous Wife": "Returning your bright pearls with double tears; I regret we did not meet before I was married." The original poem expresses the conflict between marriage and morality; here it is used inversely to emphasize Du Liniang's expectation for her husband's success in the exams.

C: 满船明月又把去珠淘：典出《新唐书·李绅传》"淘金户每岁淘金，官收其课"。原指沙里淘金，此处比喻科举补考如月夜淘金般艰难而充满希望。
E: A boat full of bright moonlight again sifts for pearls. Alludes to the New Book of Tang, "Biography of Li Shen": "Gold-panning households panned for gold every year; the government collected the tax." Originally referring to panning for gold in sand, here it metaphorically means that the supplementary examination is as arduous yet hopeful as panning for gold by moonlight.

C: 忙喇煞细柳营：典出《史记·绛侯周勃世家》汉文帝劳军细柳营故事。原指周亚夫治军严整，此处借指战事紧急打乱科举。
E: Urgently disrupting the Xi Liu Camp. Alludes to the story of Emperor Wen of Han inspecting the army at Xi Liu Camp from the Records of the Grand Historian, "Hereditary House of Marquis Jiang (Zhou Bo)". Originally referring to Zhou Yafu's strict military discipline, here it borrows the term to mean that urgent military affairs disrupt the examinations.

C: 权将杏苑抛：杏苑典出《云仙杂记》"进士杏园初宴谓之探花宴"。原指唐代新科进士游宴的杏园，此处指因战乱中断科举。
E: For now, I must abandon the Apricot Grove. "Apricot Grove" alludes to the Yunxian Zaji (Miscellaneous Records of the Cloud Immortals): "The first banquet for new Jinshi graduates in the Apricot Garden is called the Flower-Snatching Banquet." Originally referring to the Apricot Garden where new Tang Jinshi feasted, here it means the interruption of the examinations due to war.

C: 刚则迟误了你夫人花诰：花诰典出《宋史·舆服志》命妇诰命用罗帛织花。原指宋代贵妇的织花诰书，此处指因战事延误杜丽娘受封命妇。
E: This has just delayed your lady's flowery patent. "Flowery patent" alludes to the History of Song, "Treatise on Carriages and Clothing": patents of nobility for titled ladies were woven with flowers on silk gauze. Originally referring to the flower-woven patents of Song noblewomen, here it means the delay in Du Liniang receiving her patent due to the war.

C: 白云亲舍：典出《旧唐书·狄仁杰传》"仁杰登太行山，见白云孤飞，谓左右曰：'吾亲舍其下。'"狄仁杰望云思亲故事，此处杜丽娘借以表达对父母的思念。
E: White clouds over my parents' home. Alludes to the Old Book of Tang, "Biography of Di Renjie": "Di Renjie ascended Mount Taihang, saw a lone white cloud flying, and said to his attendants: 'My parents' home lies beneath it.'" The story of Di Renjie gazing at clouds and thinking of his parents. Here, Du Liniang uses it to express her longing for her parents.

C: 怎知魂向我柳枝销：化用唐李商隐《离亭赋得折杨柳》"含烟惹雾每依依，万绪千条拂落晖"。原诗咏柳寄情，此处双关柳梦梅姓氏与招魂柳枝。
E: How could I know my soul would melt towards your willow branch? Adapts Li Shangyin's (Tang Dynasty) "At the Parting Pavilion: On Plucking a Willow Branch": "Holding mist, catching fog, always clinging; ten thousand thoughts, a thousand strands, brushing the setting sun." The original poem uses the willow to convey emotion; here it puns on Liu Mengmei's surname (Willow) and the willow branch used to summon souls.

C: 好似半青天鹊影成桥：典出《岁华纪丽》引《风俗通》织女七夕渡鹊桥传说。此处反用，比喻战乱中夫妻团聚如鹊桥相会般艰难。
E: It seems like magpie shadows form a bridge across half the sky. Alludes to the legend of the Weaving Maid crossing the Magpie Bridge on the Double Seventh Festival, cited in Suihua Jili (Beautiful Record of the Year's Splendors) from Fengsu Tong (Comprehensive Meaning of Customs). Here it is used inversely, comparing the difficulty of a couple reuniting during war to the meeting on the Magpie Bridge.

C: 怕爹爹执古妆乔：典出《后汉书·逸民传》"饰智巧以逐浮利"。妆乔指装模作样，此处担心父亲古板不信还魂之事。
E: I fear Father is stubborn and puts on airs. Alludes to the Book of the Later Han, "Biographies of Hermits": "Adorning oneself with wisdom and cleverness to pursue shallow gain." "Puts on airs" means to affect a pose or pretend. Here it expresses worry that her father is rigid and won't believe the story of her return from death.

C: 满意儿待驷马过门：驷马典出《汉书·于定国传》"始定国父于公，其闾门坏，父老方共治之"。原指于公预言子孙必显，故扩建闾门容驷马高车，此处指期待科举显贵。
E: Fully expecting a four-horse carriage to pass through the gate. "Four-horse carriage" alludes to the Book of Han, "Biography of Yu Dingguo": "Initially, Yu Dingguo's father, Master Yu, had his village gate repaired when it was damaged, and the elders came together to fix it." Originally, Master Yu predicted his descendants would achieve prominence, so he expanded the village gate to accommodate a high carriage with four horses. Here it refers to the expectation of achieving prominence through the examinations.

C: 抵多少驸马还朝：典出《史记·张耳陈余列传》"张敖尚鲁元公主"。驸马为帝王女婿尊称，此处柳梦梅自比中状元如驸马荣归。
E: How much better than a royal son-in-law returning to court. Alludes to the Records of the Grand Historian, "Biographies of Zhang Er and Chen Yu": "Zhang Ao married Princess Luyuan." "Royal son-in-law" (Fuma) is an honorific title for the emperor's son-in-law. Here, Liu Mengmei compares himself passing the top examination to the glorious return of a royal son-in-law.

C: 报重生这欢声不小：呼应前文《牡丹亭》核心情节，杜丽娘复活与柳梦梅中状元双喜临门，化用《周易·系辞》"生生之谓易"的哲学内涵。
E: Announcing this rebirth, the joyful cries are not small. Echoes the core plot of The Peony Pavilion: Du Liniang's resurrection and Liu Mengmei coming first in the exams, a double celebration. It adapts the philosophical concept from the Book of Changes, "Appended Judgments": "Production and reproduction is what is called (the process of) change."

C: 月明桥上听吹箫：这里指在扬州享乐。《全唐诗》卷十九杜牧《寄扬州韩绰判官》："二十四桥明月夜，玉人何处教吹箫？"
E: Listening to flutes on the moonlit bridge: Here it refers to enjoying pleasure in Yangzhou. From Du Mu's poem "To Judge Han Chuo in Yangzhou" in the Complete Tang Poems, Volume 19: "On the Twenty-Four Bridges in a moonlit night, where is the jade lady teaching the flute?"

C: 大王原是小喽罗：典出《水浒传》第八十三回"原来这伙强人，都是草寇出身"。反映明代通俗文学中"盗贼出身卑微"的常见设定，此处用来讽刺李全夫妇的草莽发迹史。
E: The great king was originally a petty bandit. Alludes to Water Margin, Chapter 83: "It turns out this bunch of robbers all started as rustic bandits." Reflects the common trope in Ming popular literature of "bandits having humble origins," used here to satirize the rise of Li Quan and his wife from banditry.

C: 立下个草朝忒快活：草朝典出《新五代史·南汉世家》"（刘䶮）自立为帝，国号大越，改元乾亨"。原指五代十国时期的草莽政权，此处双关李全建立的伪政权和"草台班子"的戏谑意味。
E: Establishing a makeshift court is far too pleasurable. "Makeshift court" alludes to the New History of the Five Dynasties, "Noble Family of Southern Han": "(Liu Yan) proclaimed himself emperor, named his state Great Yue, and changed the era name to Qianheng." Originally referring to the rustic regimes of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period, here it puns on the puppet regime established by Li Quan and the playful meaning of a "makeshift troupe" or shoddy operation.

C: 腰缠十万：典出南朝梁殷芸《小说》"有客相从，各言所志...其一人曰：'腰缠十万贯，骑鹤上扬州'"。原为夸富之语，此处反讽陈最良穷困潦倒仍怀发财梦。
E: A hundred thousand [strings of cash] tied at the waist. Alludes to Yin Yun's (Liang Dynasty) Xiaoshuo (Fiction): "Some guests were traveling together, each stating their ambition... One of them said: 'With a hundred thousand strings tied at my waist, I'll ride a crane to Yangzhou.'" Originally an expression of wealth, here it ironically describes Chen Zuiliang's poverty-stricken state while still harboring dreams of getting rich.

C: 学先师传食走胡旋：先师指孔子，典出《孟子·滕文公下》"传食于诸侯"。原记孔子周游列国时接受各国供养，此处反用，描写陈最良在乱世中狼狈逃窜。
E: Learning from the ancient master, receiving food while performing the Hu whirl. "Ancient master" refers to Confucius, alluding to Mencius, "Duke Wen of Teng, Part II": "He received food from one prince after another." Originally recording Confucius receiving support from various states during his travels, here it is used inversely to describe Chen Zuiliang's wretched flight amidst the chaos.

C: 明知山有虎，故向虎边行：典出元杂剧《赵氏孤儿》"明知山有虎，偏向虎行"。原表现壮士赴险的勇气，此处反衬陈最良被迫遇寇的无奈。
E: Knowing full well there are tigers in the mountains, yet deliberately walking towards the tiger's side. Alludes to the Yuan Zaju The Orphan of Zhao: "Knowing full well there are tigers in the mountains, yet defiantly walking towards the tiger." Originally showing a hero's courage in facing danger, here it contrasts with Chen Zuiliang's helplessness in being forced to encounter bandits.

C: 乌鸦喜鹊同行，吉凶全然未保：典出《诗经·小雅·正月》"瞻乌爰止，于谁之屋"。古人以乌鸦主凶、喜鹊主吉，此处表现陈最良对命运的忐忑。
E: Crows and magpies travel together; good or ill fortune is entirely uncertain. Alludes to the Book of Songs, "Minor Odes", "First Month": "Look where the crow alights; on whose house will it rest?" The ancients considered crows an omen of ill fortune and magpies an omen of good fortune. Here it shows Chen Zuiliang's apprehension about his fate.

C: 南朝俺不蛮，北朝俺不番：化用《南史·贼臣传》"非蛮非貊，无主无家"。原指侯景之乱时的叛军身份模糊，此处表现李全集团在宋金之间的骑墙立场。
E: To the Southern Court, I am not a southern barbarian; to the Northern Court, I am not a foreigner. Adapts the History of the Southern Dynasties, "Biographies of Treacherous Ministers": "Neither southern barbarian nor northern tribesman, without a lord, without a home." Originally referring to the ambiguous identity of the rebel forces during the Hou Jing rebellion, here it shows Li Quan's group's fence-sitting stance between the Song and Jin.

C: 没路走羊肠：典出《汉书·王莽传》"羊肠九折，路无坦途"。原形容太行山险道，此处比喻陈最良陷入绝境。
E: No road to take but the goat's gut path. Alludes to the Book of Han, "Biography of Wang Mang": "The goat's gut path twists nine times; the road has no level stretches." Originally describing the dangerous paths of the Taihang Mountains, here it metaphorically means Chen Zuiliang is in a desperate situation.

C: 卫灵公问陈于孔子：典出《论语·卫灵公》"卫灵公问陈于孔子。孔子对曰：'俎豆之事，则尝闻之矣；军旅之事，未之学也。'"原表现孔子反对战争的态度，此处陈最良借以推脱讲解兵法的要求。
E: Duke Ling of Wei asked Confucius about battle arrays. Alludes to the Analects of Confucius, "Duke Ling of Wei": "Duke Ling of Wei asked Confucius about battle arrays. Confucius replied, 'I have heard about the matters of ritual vessels and stands, but I have not studied matters of warfare and armies.'" Originally showing Confucius's opposition to war, here Chen Zuiliang uses it to evade the request to explain military tactics.

C: 吾未见好德如好色者也：出自《论语·子罕》原句。孔子感叹世人重色轻德，此处被陈最良曲解为因南子美色而不敢言兵，体现其迂腐性格。
E: I have never seen one who loves virtue as much as he loves beauty. A direct quote from the Analects of Confucius, "Zi Han". Confucius laments that people value beauty over virtue. Here, Chen Zuiliang misinterprets it as being unable to speak of warfare due to the beauty of Nanzi (Duke Ling's wife), revealing his pedantic character.

C: 献首级讨赏：典出《史记·项羽本纪》"持项王头视鲁，鲁父兄乃降"。原指刘邦用项羽首级招降楚地，此处反用为李全集团伪造证据的心理战术。
E: Presenting a severed head to claim a reward. Alludes to the Records of the Grand Historian, "Basic Annals of Xiang Yu": "Holding King Xiang's head, they showed it to Lu; the elders and brothers of Lu then surrendered." Originally referring to Liu Bang using Xiang Yu's head to induce surrender in Chu territories, here it is used inversely as a psychological tactic by Li Quan's group to fabricate evidence.

C: 著什么耀武扬威早纳降：化用《旧唐书·李密传》"耀武扬威，以胁东都"。原指瓦岗军震慑隋军，此处表现贼寇逼迫杜宝投降的嚣张气焰。
E: Why flaunt your military prowess and demand early surrender? Adapts the Old Book of Tang, "Biography of Li Mi": "Flaunting military prowess to intimidate the Eastern Capital." Originally referring to the Wagang Army intimidating the Sui forces, here it shows the bandits' arrogance in pressuring Du Bao to surrender.

C: 非是谎：典出元杂剧《窦娥冤》"天也，你错勘贤愚枉做天"。反映元代戏曲中常见的赌咒发誓模式，此处表现贼寇虚张声势。
E: It is no lie. Alludes to the Yuan Zaju The Injustice to Dou E: "Heaven! You wrongly judge the worthy and foolish, vainly acting as Heaven!" Reflects the common pattern of swearing oaths in Yuan drama, used here to show the bandits' bluster.

C: 豹子妻：《诚齐乐府.伏义疏财》三折《滚绣球》："本是个梁山寨生成的豹子妻。"豹子妻原指剧中男扮女装的黑旋风李逵。这里指李全妻。豹子，借来形容凶猛。
E: Leopard's Wife: From the aria "Gun Xiu Qiu" in Act III of Chengqi Yuefu. Fuyi Shucai: "Originally was a leopard's wife born of the Liangshan stronghold." "Leopard's Wife" originally referred to the Black Whirlwind Li Kui disguised as a woman in the play. Here it refers to Li Quan's wife. "Leopard" is borrowed to describe fierceness.

C: 大北里宣差传站马：大北里，指金朝。宣差，差官、使命。这里指番将自己。女真"出使者必带牌，有金、银、木这别。上有女真书'准敕急达'字及阿骨打花押。宣差者所至视三品，朝旨差者视五品。"。见《说郛》卷四十一范成大《搅辔录》。站马，驿马，一名馆马。
E: From the Great North (Jin), the envoy transmits post horses. "Great North" refers to the Jin Dynasty. "Envoy" means an official messenger or emissary. Here it refers to the foreign general himself. The Jurchen: "Envoys sent out must carry a tally, differentiated by gold, silver, or wood. On it are Jurchen script characters for 'Authorized by Decree, Urgent Dispatch' and the signature of Aguda. Envoys are treated as third rank; those sent by court decree are treated as fifth rank." See Shuo Fu, Volume 41, Fan Chengda's Jiao Pei Lu (Record of Gathering the Reins). "Post horses" are courier station horses, also called relay horses.

C: 虎头牌滴溜的分花：虎头牌，当指万户金虎符，金人军队中用来证明长官身份的一种证件。参看前注。滴溜，明滴溜的省词，明晃晃的意思。《盛世新声.中吕粉喋儿》："怎敢道小觑俺这腰间明滴溜的虎头牌。"
E: The tiger-head tally glistens brightly, divided by a floral pattern. "Tiger-head tally" likely refers to the Myriarch's gold tiger tally, a credential used in the Jin army to prove an officer's identity. See previous note. "di liu" is an abbreviation of "ming diliu" , meaning shiny or glistening. From Shengshi Xinsheng, the tune "Zhonglü Fen Die'er": "How dare you belittle this bright-glistening tiger-head tally at my waist!"

C: 锁陀八：没陀八及下文哈散、倒剌、孛知，和《诚齐乐府.桃源景》第四折《倘秀才》："他道哈撒呵，原来是问你。......他道锁陀八，原来是酒醉矣。他道倒喇是歌一曲，他道孛知是舞一回。"用法意义相近。下文力娄吉丁母剌失也和《桃源景.滚绣雨衣》"得娄吉邻母剌失"音近，但意义不同。
E: Suotuo ba: "Mei tuo ba" and the following "Ha san", "Dao la", "Bo zhi" have similar usage and meaning to those in the aria "Tang Xiucai" from Act IV of Chengqi Yuefu. Taoyuan Jing (Peach Spring Scene): "He says 'Ha sa he', which originally means 'ask you'... He says 'Suo tuo ba', which originally means 'drunk'. He says 'Dao la' is singing a song, he says 'Bo zhi' is dancing once." The following "Li lou ji ding mu la shi" also sounds similar to "De lou ji lin mu la shi" in Taoyuan Jing, "Gun Xiu Yu Yi", but the meaning is different.

C: 凭陆贾，说庄桥：庄桥，战国楚庄王的后裔。他率兵为楚国平定今四川西部、云南东部地方。后来归路被秦国切断，自立为滇王。到他的后代，才是顺汉朝。见《史记.西南夷列传》。全句意思说，凭着自己具有和陆贾说服赵佗一样的辩才，去说服那个倔强的庄桥。庄桥，这里喻李全。
E: Relying on Lu Jia's [skill] to persuade Zhuang Qiao. Zhuang Qiao was a descendant of King Zhuang of Chu during the Warring States period. He led troops to pacify the areas of present-day western Sichuan and eastern Yunnan for Chu. Later, his return route was cut off by Qin, so he proclaimed himself King of Dian. His descendants later submitted to the Han Dynasty. See Records of the Grand Historian, "Biographies of the Southwestern Yi". The whole line means: Relying on his own eloquence, comparable to Lu Jia's who persuaded Zhao Tuo, to convince that stubborn Zhuang Qiao. Here, Zhuang Qiao metaphorically represents Li Quan.

C: 黑海岸回头星宿高：意思说：只要及早回头，重归祖国，你一定会交好运。古代谚语："若海无边，回头是岸。"
E: On the black sea's shore, turn your head back, the constellations are high. The meaning is: If you just turn back early and return to your homeland, you will certainly have good fortune. An ancient proverb says: "The sea of suffering has no bounds, turn back and there is the shore."

C: 齐肩一字王：唐宋以后皇子封五，以一个字为国名，如齐王；其次，皇子的儿子封王，以二字为国名，如汝南王。这里指平肩一刀，斩首。
E: A single-character king of equal rank. After the Tang and Song dynasties, imperial sons were enfeoffed as kings, using a single character for the state name, e.g., King of Qi. Next, the sons of imperial princes were enfeoffed as kings, using two characters for the state name, e.g., King of Runan. Here it means a level-shouldered cut with a knife, i.e., beheading.

C: 范蠡载西施：春秋时代，越王勾践为吴国所败，退守会稽。历史传说，越王曾令范蠡献美女西施于吴王，吴王大悦，从此，沉湎酒色，朝政尽废。吴亡后，西施复归范蠡，同泛五湖（太湖）而去。，见《越绝书》。明梁辰鱼采取这一故事，写作《浣纱记》传奇。
E: Fan Li carried away Xi Shi. During the Spring and Autumn period, King Goujian of Yue was defeated by Wu and retreated to Kuaiji. Historical legend says that the King of Yue ordered Fan Li to present the beautiful Xi Shi to the King of Wu. The King of Wu was delighted and from then on indulged in wine and women, neglecting all state affairs. After Wu's destruction, Xi Shi returned to Fan Li, and they floated away together on the Five Lakes (Tai Lake). See Yue Jue Shu (Records of Yue's Destruction). Liang Chenyu of the Ming Dynasty adopted this story to write the chuangi play The Silk-Washing Stream.

C: 你真是个楚霸王，不到乌江不止：楚霸王项羽兵败，和他的宠姬虞美人诀别，在乌江自刎。见《史记.项羽本纪》。明沈采取这一故事，写作传奇《千金记》中的第三十七出《别姬》，发展成为后来的京剧《霸王别姬》。
E: You truly are the Hegemon King of Chu, who would not stop until reaching the Wu River. The Hegemon King of Chu, Xiang Yu, was defeated, bid farewell to his beloved concubine Consort Yu, and committed suicide by the Wu River. See Records of the Grand Historian, "Basic Annals of Xiang Yu". Shen of the Ming Dynasty adopted this story to write the 37th scene "Farewell My Concubine" in the chuangi play The Thousand Pieces of Gold, which later developed into the Peking opera Farewell My Concubine.

C: 桃树巧逢前度客：唐诗人刘禹锡曾游玄都观看桃花题诗一首。若干年后到那里重游，桃花都不见。他又题了一首诗，有两句说："种桃道士归何处？前度刘郎今又来。"见《全唐诗》卷十三。前度刘郎，也是双关语，借指在天台山桃源洞与仙女相爱的刘晨。这里喻柳梦梅。
E: The peach tree cleverly meets the guest of times past. The Tang poet Liu Yuxi once visited the Xuandu Temple, saw peach blossoms, and inscribed a poem. Several years later, he revisited the place; the peach blossoms were gone. He inscribed another poem, which included the lines: "Where has the peach-planting Daoist gone? The Liu Lang of times past has come again today." See Complete Tang Poems, Volume 13. "Liu Lang of times past" is also a pun, alluding to Liu Chen who loved an immortal maiden in the Peach Blossom Cave of Tiantai Mountain. Here it metaphorically refers to Liu Mengmei.

C: 漆灯无焰：《佩文韵府》引《江南野史》："沈彬居有一大树。尝曰：'吾死可葬于是。'及葬，穴之，乃古冢。期间一古灯台，上有漆灯一盏。圹头铜牌篆文曰：'佳城今已开，虽开不葬埋。漆灯犹未热，留待沈彬来。'"
E: The lacquered lamp has no flame. The Peiwen Yunfu (Rhyme Treasury of the Peiwen Studio) quotes Jiangnan Yeshi (Unofficial History of Jiangnan): "Shen Bin's dwelling had a large tree. He once said: 'When I die, I can be buried here.' When he was buried and the grave was dug, it turned out to be an ancient tomb. Inside was an ancient lamp stand with a lacquered lamp upon it. A bronze plaque at the head of the grave had seal script characters saying: 'The fine city is now opened; though opened, it is not for burial. The lacquered lamp is not yet warm; it awaits Shen Bin's coming.'"

C: 坠海明珠去复旋：旋，还、回来。全顺意思指女儿死而复活。神话传说：广东合浦本产珠。由于官吏贪残，珠不不生在这里，而生到交趾（越南）去了。东汉孟尝任合浦太守不满一年，政治办得好，珠才重新回来。见《后汉书》卷一百六本传。
E: The pearl that fell into the sea goes away and returns again. "xuan" means to return, come back. The whole meaning indicates the daughter's death and revival. A mythological legend: Hepu in Guangdong originally produced pearls. Due to the greed and cruelty of the officials, the pearls no longer grew there but moved to Jiaozhi (Vietnam). Meng Chang of the Eastern Han served as Governor of Hepu for less than a year; his administration was good, and the pearls returned. See the Book of the Later Han, Volume 106, his biography.

C: 落花流水叶知秋：《淮南子.说山》："见一叶落而知岁之将春。"唐庚《文录》："唐人有诗云：'山僧不解数甲子，一叶落知天下秋。'"
E: Falling flowers, flowing water, a leaf knows autumn. From Huainanzi, "Discourse on Mountains": "See one leaf fall and know that the year is about to turn to spring." Tang Geng's Wen Lu (Record of Literature): "A Tang poet wrote: 'The mountain monk does not understand counting the cycles; one leaf falls and he knows autumn under heaven.'"

C: 漂母：汉代名将韩信，少年贫困，曾在淮阴城边钓鱼，遇见漂母。依靠漂母给他吃的东西，才不致挨饿。后来韩信做了大官，找到漂母，送她千金作报答。见《史记.淮阴侯列传》。
E: The laundress: The famous Han Dynasty general Han Xin was poor in his youth and once fished by the Huaiyin city wall, where he met a laundress. Relying on the food she gave him, he avoided starvation. Later, when Han Xin became a high official, he found the laundress and gave her a thousand pieces of gold in repayment. See Records of the Grand Historian, "Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin (Han Xin)".

C: 瘦王孙：指韩信。他不是贵族出身，《史记》记载漂母称他为王孙（公子），仅是表示对他客气。
E: The thin prince's grandson: Refers to Han Xin. He was not of noble birth; the Records of the Grand Historian records that the laundress called him "prince's grandson" (young nobleman) merely as a polite form of address.

C: 假齐王：秦末，韩信攻下山东一带地方，请刘邦封他做齐假王。刘邦只得正式封他为齐王。见《史记.淮阴侯列传》。
E: Acting King of Qi: At the end of the Qin Dynasty, Han Xin captured the Shandong region and asked Liu Bang to appoint him Acting King of Qi. Liu Bang had no choice but to formally enfeoff him as King of Qi. See Records of the Grand Historian, "Biography of the Marquis of Huaiyin".

C: 文公乞食，僖妻礼他：晋公子重耳亡命到外国。有一次，向一个农夫讨东西吃，人家丢给他一块泥土。到了曹国，曹共公又欺侮他。曹国大臣僖钡羁的妻子却知道他是有前途的人，叫丈夫暗中送东西给他。后来重耳回到晋国执政，就是文公。见《左传》僖公廿三年。
E: Duke Wen begged for food, and Xi's wife treated him with courtesy. Prince Chong'er of Jin fled to foreign states. Once, he begged a farmer for food, and the man threw him a clod of earth. When he reached Cao, Duke Gong of Cao also insulted him. However, the wife of the Cao minister Xi Bieji knew he was a man with a future and told her husband to secretly send him provisions. Later, Chong'er returned to Jin and became its ruler, Duke Wen. See Zuo Zhuan, 23rd Year of Duke Xi.

C: 昭关乞食，相逢浣纱：伍子胥，春秋楚国人。他的父兄被平王害死。他逃走后，在路上乘车向一浣纱女乞食。浣纱女为了使他去得安心，决不汇漏他的行踪，竟抱石投江而死。见《吴越春秋》，元人据这一段故事，写作《伍员吹箫》杂剧。昭关，在安徽含县西北，春秋时代楚国和吴国的交通要道。全子胥逃往吴国，经过这里。
E: Begging for food at Zhaoguan, he met a silk-washer. Wu Zixu was a man of Chu during the Spring and Autumn period. His father and brother were killed by King Ping. After he fled, on the road, he rode in a carriage and begged for food from a silk-washing girl. To set his mind at ease so he could go on, and to absolutely prevent any leak of his whereabouts, she embraced a stone and threw herself into the river to die. See Wu Yue Chunqiu (Spring and Autumn Annals of Wu and Yue). Yuan Dynasty playwrights based the Zaju Wu Yuan Blows the Flute on this story. Zhaoguan, northwest of present-day Han County in Anhui, was a key communication route between Chu and Wu during the Spring and Autumn period. Wu Zixu passed here on his escape to Wu.

C: 长淮千骑雁行秋，浪卷云浮：句本辛弃疾词《声声慢》："指点占牙高处，浪涌云浮。......罢长淮，千骑临秋。"
E: A thousand riders on the Long Huai (Huai River) like wild geese in autumn formation, waves roll, clouds float. The line is based on Xin Qiji's lyric to the tune "Slow, Slow Song": "Pointing to the place where the commander's standard is high, waves surge, clouds float... Finished with the Long Huai, a thousand riders face the autumn."

C: 功名富贵草头露：杜甫《送孔巢你谢病归游江东蒹李白》诗："富贵何如草头露。"见《草堂诗笺》卷二。
E: Merit, fame, wealth, and honor are but dew on the grass. From Du Fu's poem "Seeing Off Kong Chaofu Who, Pleading Illness, Returns to Roam East of the River, and Also Li Bai": "How are wealth and honor like dew on the grass?" See Thatched Cottage Poetry Notes, Volume 2.

C: 未分明：指夫妇关系尚未正式建立。杜甫《新婚别》诗："妾身未分明，何以见姑嫜。"见《草堂诗笺》卷十三。
E: Not yet clarified: Means the marital relationship is not yet formally established. From Du Fu's poem "The Newlywed's Parting": "My person is not yet clarified; how can I face my father- and mother-in-law?" See Thatched Cottage Poetry Notes, Volume 13.

C: 万里筹边第一楼：元赵孟兆诗："春风闲苑三千客，明月扬州第一楼。"万里筹边，南宋时扬州曾为边境地区。又唐代李德裕曾在西川建筹边楼。见《唐书》本传。
E: The First Tower for Planning Defense Across Ten Thousand Li. From a poem by Zhao Mengfu (Yuan Dynasty): "The spring wind in the idle garden, three thousand guests; the bright moon over Yangzhou, the First Tower." "Planning defense across ten thousand li": During the Southern Song, Yangzhou was a border region. Also, Li Deyu of the Tang Dynasty once built a "Planning Defense Tower" in Xichuan. See his biography in the Tang History.

C: 燕支却虏：汉高祖被匈奴围困在平城（今山西大同东）。相传陈平去游说阏氏，说汉高祖献美女求和。阏氏怕美女来了，自己失宠，就劝单于退兵。瘀氏，匈奴酋长的妻子称号。见《史记.陈丞相世家》注。燕支，即姻脂，指美女。这里喻李全妻。
E: Rouge repels the enemy: Emperor Gaozu of Han was besieged by the Xiongnu at Pingcheng (east of present-day Datong, Shanxi). Legend says Chen Ping went to persuade the “e shi “(Yanzhi, consort of the Xiongnu ruler), saying Emperor Gaozu would offer beautiful women to seek peace. The e shi, fearing that if beautiful women came she would lose favor, advised the Chanyu to withdraw his troops. "e shi" is the title for the wife of a Xiongnu chieftain. See the commentary in Records of the Grand Historian, "Hereditary House of Chancellor Chen (Ping)". Yanzhi means rouge, referring to beautiful women. Here it metaphorically refers to Li Quan's wife.

C: 兵洗河汉：用银河（河汉）里的水把兵器洗耳恭听了，藏起来不用。意思说天下太平。杜甫《洗兵马》诗："安得壮士挽天河，净洗甲兵长不用。"见《草堂诗笺》卷十一。
E: Washing weapons in the River Han (Milky Way): Using the water of the Silver River (Milky Way) to wash the weapons clean and put them away unused. It means the world is at peace. From Du Fu's poem "Washing the Horses and Weapons": "How can we get a strong man to pull down the Heavenly River and wash the armor and weapons clean, never to be used again?" See Thatched Cottage Poetry Notes, Volume 11.

C: 明月同谁啸瘐楼：晋征南将军庾亮出镇武昌。一天晚上，他到南楼去玩，遇见僚属就和他们一起坐下来谈笑。见《晋书》本传。
E: With whom shall I whistle under the bright moon on the Yu Tower? Yu Liang, the Jin Dynasty General Who Conquers the South, was stationed in Wuchang. One night, he went to the South Tower for amusement, met his subordinates, and sat down with them to talk and laugh. See his biography in the Book of Jin.

C: 猛把吴钩看了，阑干拍遍：吴钩，刀。句本辛弃疾词《水龙吟》："落日楼头，断鸿声里，江南游子、把吴钩看了，栏干拍遍，无人会，登临意。"
E: Fiercely I look at my Wu hook, slap the balustrade all over. "Wu hook" is a curved sword/knife. The line is based on Xin Qiji's lyric to the tune "Water Dragon Chant": "On the tower in the setting sun, amid the cries of a lone swan, the wanderer south of the River—looks at his Wu hook, slaps the balustrade all over, no one understands his feelings upon climbing high."

C: 借淮阳寇：东汉寇恂由颖川太守调到京都做官。后来他跟随皇帝到颖川，地方上人对皇帝说："请再借您的寇恂在这里做一年事。"见《后汉书.寇恂传》。这里借指挽留杜宝，再在淮阳坐镇。
E: Borrowing the kou (bandit) of Huaiyang: Kou Xun of the Eastern Han was transferred from Governor of Yingchuan to an official post in the capital. Later, he accompanied the emperor to Yingchuan, and the local people said to the emperor: "Please lend us your Kou Xun to work here for another year." See the Book of the Later Han, "Biography of Kou Xun". Here it metaphorically means asking Du Bao to stay and remain in charge at Huaiyang.

C: 楚囚：泛指囚犯。历史故事：春秋时，楚人钟仪，被郑国俘递，郑国把他送到晋国。他戴着南方的冠子（南冠），奏着南方的音乐，表示不忘故国。后被释放。
E: A Chu captive: Generally refers to a prisoner. Historical story: During the Spring and Autumn period, Zhong Yi of Chu was captured by Zheng and sent by Zheng to Jin. He wore a southern hat (nanguan) and played southern music, showing he had not forgotten his native state. He was later released.

C: 蘧龙：喻贤才。《书.舜典》："帝曰，蘧，命汝典乐教胄子......帝曰龙......命汝作纳言。"蘧、龙二臣是舜的贤臣。
E: Qu and Long: Metaphor for worthy talent. From the Book of Documents, "Canon of Shun": "The Emperor said, 'Qu, I charge you to direct music and teach the sons of the nobility.'... The Emperor said, 'Long,... I charge you to be the minister of communications.'" The two ministers Qu and Long were worthy officials of Shun.

C: 天九万，路三千。月余程，抵半年：《庄子.逍遥游》："鹏之徒于南冥也，水声三千时，抟扶摇而上著九万里，去以六月息者也。"这里借用，形容路远。
E: Ninety thousand in heaven, three thousand on the road. A journey of over a month equals half a year.
