From Zhuangzi, "Free and Easy Wandering": "When the roc journeys to the Southern Darkness, the waters are smitten for three thousand li. He beats the whirlwind and rises ninety thousand li, for a flight of six months' duration." Borrowed here to describe the long distance.

C: 黄巢下第题诗讪：黄巢，唐末农民起义军的领袖之一。做事传说：黄巢考进士没有取，就题了一首诗走了。见《新编五代史平话》。
E: Huang Chao, having failed the exams, inscribed a mocking poem. Huang Chao was one of the leaders of the peasant uprising at the end of the Tang Dynasty. A popular legend says: Huang Chao took the Jinshi examination but was not accepted, so he inscribed a poem and left. See Xinbian Wudai Shi Pinghua (New Compiled Plain Tales of the History of the Five Dynasties).

C: 踏的菜园穿：这里有苦出头的意思。有一穷措大常吃蔬菜，忽然吃了一次羊肉，梦见藏神说："羊把菜园踏破了。"见《笑林》。
E: Trampling through the vegetable garden: Here it has the meaning of hardship leading to success. There was a poor scholar who usually ate vegetables; suddenly he ate some mutton once and dreamt that the guardian spirit of the storeroom said: "The sheep have trampled through the vegetable garden." See Xiao Lin (Forest of Laughter).

C: 孔雀屏风：许婚。隋宝毅不肯轻易把女儿许人。他在屏风上画两只孔雀，叫求婚人去身箭。李渊射了两次，都中雀目。宝毅就把女儿许给他。见《唐书.宝后传》。
E: Peacock screen: Betrothal. Dou Yi of the Sui Dynasty would not easily promise his daughter in marriage. He painted two peacocks on a screen and had suitors shoot arrows at them. Li Yuan shot twice and hit the peacocks' eyes both times. Dou Yi then promised his daughter to him. See the Tang History, "Biography of Empress Dou".

C: 定昏店赤绳羁凤：唐人传奇故事：韦固在旅店（定昏店）遇见一老人。天下的婚姻都由这老人主管。凡是夫妻，他就暗中用赤绳系他们的足，这样就不管天南地北，都会聚在一起。见《续玄怪录》。凤，这里是柳梦梅自喻。
E: At the inn of fixed marriages, a red rope tethers the phoenix. A Tang Dynasty tale story: Wei Gu met an old man at an inn (the inn of fixed marriages). This old man controlled all marriages under heaven. For every couple destined to be husband and wife, he secretly tied their feet with a red cord, so that regardless of distance, they would eventually come together. See Xu Xuan Guai Lu (Sequel to Records of the Mysterious and Strange). "Phoenix" here is Liu Mengmei's metaphor for himself.

C: 耿秋光长剑倚崆峒：倚着崆峒山，拔出寒光闪闪的长剑。杜甫诗《投哥舒翰开府二十韵》："防身一长剑，将欲倚崆峒。"见《草堂诗笺》卷三。倚崆峒，夸张地形容剑之长。
E: Gleaming autumn light, a long sword leans against Kongtong. Leaning against Mount Kongtong, he draws his long sword gleaming with cold light. From Du Fu's poem "Presented to General Geshu Han: Twenty Couplets": "A single long sword for self-defense, about to lean against Kongtong." See Thatched Cottage Poetry Notes, Volume 3. "Leaning against Kongtong" is an exaggeration describing the sword's great length.

C: 黑头公：壮年人做大官。见《晋书.诸葛恢传》。
E: Black-Head Duke: A man achieving high office while still young (with black hair). See the Book of Jin, "Biography of Zhuge Hui".

C: 入掌银台护紫微：银台，指唐代的翰林、学士院。紫微，唐开元元年改吕收省为紫微省，中书令为紫微令（宰相）。
E: Entering to take charge of the Silver Terrace, guarding the Purple Tenuity. "Silver Terrace" refers to the Hanlin Academy and the College of Scholars in the Tang Dynasty. "Purple Tenuity": in the first year of the Kaiyuan era, the Department of Affairs of State was renamed the Purple Tenuity Department, and the Zhongshu Ling became the Purple Tenuity Ling (Chancellor).

C: 吃敲才：该死的贼骨头。元杂剧《青衫泪》第三折《沽美酒》："则被你殃煞我吃敲贼。"《元典章》新集刑部内延右新定例，凡处死罪杖杀者皆曰"敲"。据《西雁记》王季思先生注转引。
E: Worthy of a beating: Damnable thief/rascal. From the aria "Gu Mei Jiu" in Act III of the Yuan Zaju Tears on the Blue Gown: "You have nearly been the death of me, a thief worthy of a beating." According to the Yuan Dianzhang (Yuan Statutes), New Collection, Ministry of Justice, a newly established regulation stated that all executions by beating were called "qiao" Cited from Wang Jisi's commentary on The West Swan Romance.

C: 要的门无鬼，先教园有桃：门无鬼，《庄子.天地》篇中人名。园有桃，《诗.魏风》篇名古代迷信说法：桃枝可以打鬼，有桃树的地方就没有鬼。
E: If you want your gate to have no ghosts, first teach your garden to have peach trees. "Gate Without Ghosts" is a person's name in the Zhuangzi, chapter "Heaven and Earth". "Garden Has Peaches" is the title of a poem in the Book of Songs, "Airs of Wei". Ancient superstitious belief: Peach branches can beat ghosts; where there are peach trees, there are no ghosts.

C: 不刮目破窑中吕蒙：刮目，不以旧的眼光看人。《三国志.吴志.吕蒙传》注引《江表传》："士别三日，即更刮目相待。"破窑，吕蒙正事。这里作者有意将吕蒙、吕蒙正两人的故事搅在一起。
E: Not scraping one's eyes to see Lü Meng in the broken kiln: "Scraping one's eyes" means not judging someone by their past. The commentary to the Records of the Three Kingdoms, Book of Wu, "Biography of Lü Meng" quotes the Jiang Biao Zhuan: "After three days' absence, one should look at a gentleman with scraped eyes (i.e., with new respect)." "Broken kiln" refers to the story of Lü Mengzheng. Here the author intentionally mixes up the stories of Lü Meng and Lü Mengzheng.

C: 公冶长陷缧拽中：《论语.公冶长》："子（孔丘）谓，公冶长可妻也。虽在缧拽之中，非其罪也。以其子妻之（把女儿嫁他）。"公冶长原是孔丘弟子。缧拽，用绳索缚起来。缧拽之中，指关在监狱之中。
E: Gongye Chang fell into bonds and fetters. From the Analects of Confucius, "Gongye Chang": "The Master said that Gongye Chang was fit to be given a wife. Although he was in bonds and fetters, it was through no fault of his own. He gave him his own daughter to wife." Gongye Chang was a disciple of Confucius. "Bonds and fetters" means tied up with ropes. "In bonds and fetters" means imprisoned.

C: 柳盗跖：跖，古代奴隶起义的领袖。《庄子.盗跖》把他和柳下惠说成兄弟关系。这是寓言，不足凭信。柳，关合柳梦梅。
E: Liu the Robber Zhi: Zhi was the leader of an ancient slave rebellion. The Zhuangzi chapter "Robber Zhi" makes him and Liu Xiahui brothers. This is a fable and not credible. "Liu" connects with Liu Mengmei.

C: 把一个有对付的玉洁冰清烈火烘：有对付的，有才能的。玉洁冰清，这里指女婿。卫价，同神秀异。他的岳父乐广，也很有名望。当时有人称称赞他们说："妇公冰清，女婿玉润。"见《晋书》卷三十六本传。烈火烘，指前文所写的那些虐待。
E: Subjecting a talented, jade-pure, ice-clear [son-in-law] to fierce fire's baking. "Talented" means having ability. "Jade-pure, ice-clear" here refers to the son-in-law. Wei Jie was exceptionally gifted. His father-in-law, Yue Guang, was also very famous. At that time, people praised them saying: "The wife's father is ice-clear; the son-in-law is jade-moist." See the Book of Jin, Volume 36, his biography. "Baked by fierce fire" refers to the mistreatment described earlier.

C: 把亲娘肠断了影中蛇：有人在乐广家喝酒，看见杯中有蛇而害病。其实，这是墙上的弓影。见《晋书.乐广传》。全句：杜丽娘没有真地死了，而他母亲却信以为真。
E: Breaking her dear mother's heart with the shadow-snake in the cup. Someone was drinking at Yue Guang's house, saw a snake in his cup, and fell ill. Actually, it was the shadow of a bow on the wall. See the Book of Jin, "Biography of Yue Guang". The whole sentence: Du Liniang did not truly die, but her mother believed it to be true.

C: 燕冢：南朝宋末，娼女姚玉京从良，丈夫死了不现嫁人。有一只燕子在他家里的梁上做窝。后来雄燕被莺鸟害了。玉京用红线系在雌燕足上，秋去春来，年年都一样。玉京死后，燕子哀鸣不停。家人告诉它玉京的坟墓所在。燕子飞到玉京坟上，就死了。见《事文类聚》后集卷四十五《燕女坟》条。唐李公佐有《燕女坟记》。这里指丽娘墓。
E: Swallow's Grave: At the end of the Liu Song Dynasty, the courtesan Yao Yujing reformed and married. Her husband died, and she did not remarry. A swallow made a nest on the beam of her house. Later, the male swallow was killed by a shrike. Yujing tied a red thread to the female swallow's foot. It went away in autumn and returned in spring, the same every year. After Yujing died, the swallow cried mournfully without cease. The family told it where Yujing's grave was. The swallow flew to Yujing's grave and died. See the Shiwen Leiju (Classified Anthology of Literary and Narrative Sources), Later Collection, Volume 45, entry "Swallow Maiden's Grave". Li Gongzuo of the Tang wrote a "Record of the Swallow Maiden's Grave". Here it refers to Liniang's grave.

C: 头带魁罡：古时迷信说法：状元受到魁星的护佑。罡，天罡，北斗星。魁，北斗的第一颗到第四颗星。
E: Head wearing Kui and Gang: Ancient superstitious belief: The Zhuangyuan (top graduate) receives the protection of the Kui star. "Gang" is Tiangang, stars of the Big Dipper. "Kui" refers to the first to fourth stars of the Big Dipper.

C: 要问龟鳌窟，还过鸟鹊桥：杜甫诗《玉台观》："江光隐现龟鳖窟，石势参差鸟鹊桥。"见《杜少陵集详注》卷十三。龟鳖窟，原指江海的深处，这里指钱超高频江边；鸟鹊桥，原指七夕鸟鹊驾桥，让牛郎织女渡银河而相会。
E: If you want to ask the tortoise's cave, you must still cross the Magpie Bridge. From Du Fu's poem "Jade Tower Temple": "River light faintly reveals the tortoise's cave; the rock formations suggest the Magpie Bridge." See Detailed Commentary on the Collected Works of Du Shaoling, Volume 13. "Tortoise's cave" originally meant the depths of rivers and seas; here it refers to the Qiantang River bank. "Magpie Bridge" originally referred to the bridge formed by magpies on the Double Seventh Festival, allowing the Cowherd and Weaving Maid to cross the Milky Way and meet.

C: 梅雪争春未肯降，骚人阁笔费平章：宋虔梅坡诗《雪梅》的前二名。后二句是"梅须逊雪三分白，雪却输梅一段香。"平章，原作评章，评论的意思，这里兼指官名平章。
E: Plum and snow contend for spring, neither willing to yield; the poet lays down his brush, laboring to judge. The first two lines of the poem "Snow and Plum" by Lu Meipo (Song Dynasty). The last two lines are: "The plum must yield to the snow by three parts whiteness; the snow loses to the plum by a stretch of fragrance." "Pingzhang" originally meant "to judge" or "comment"; here it also refers to the official title of Pingzhang (a high minister).

C: 有恨妆排，无明耽带：妆排，犹如说播弄。无明，原是佛家说法，这里无明耽带，是无缘无故、有了这样的遭遇的意思。
E: Arranged with resentment, borne through ignorance. "Arranged" is like saying manipulated. "Ignorance" is originally a Buddhist term; here "borne through ignorance" means having such an experience for no reason.

C: 槟榔：药名，从前闽、广人所嗜食，据说下气、消食，多吃则使牙齿变黑。见宋周去非《岭外代答》。上文"萤见一点红嘴"，就是指常吃槟榔，唇齿变色。下文附子、贝母都是药名，这里只是子、母的意思。曲中嵌药名（或曲名），带有文字游戏的性质。
E: Betel nut: A medicinal substance, formerly enjoyed by people in Fujian and Guangdong; it is said to relieve gas and aid digestion, but eating too much blackens the teeth. See Zhou Qufei's (Song Dynasty) Lingwai Daida (Answers about the Region beyond the Passes). The previous line "A glowworm sees a little red mouth" refers to the discoloration of lips and teeth from frequent betel nut chewing. The following terms, "aconite" and "fritillary bulb", are also medicine names, but here they simply mean "son" and "mother". Embedding medicine names (or tune names) in the song has the nature of a word game.

C: 撇道儿：足。这里指嗓子。王骥德《曲律》卷三《论讹字》云："汤海若《还魂记》末折：'把那撇道儿喀，长舌喳。'是以撇道认作嗓子也，误甚。"
E: Instep: Foot. Here it means throat. Wang Jide's Qu Lü (Rules of Song), Volume 3, "On Incorrect Characters", says: "In the final act of Tang Haoruo's Return of the Soul: 'That instep of yours goes "ka", the long tongue goes "zha".' This mistakes 'instep' for 'throat' and is very erroneous."

C:
东窗事发：民间传说：秦桧夫妇在东窗下设计陷害岳飞。秦桧死后，他的鬼魂叫方士告诉其妻王氏："东窗事发矣。"见《通俗编》卷三十七。今传元刊本杂剧《东窗事犯》。
The affair under the east window is exposed: A folk legend: Qin Hui and his wife plotted under the east window to frame Yue Fei. After Qin Hui died, his ghost told a medium to inform his wife, Lady Wang: "The affair under the east window is exposed." See Tong Su Bian (Compilation of Common Sayings), Volume 37. A Yuan printed edition of the Zaju The Crime Committed under the East Window survives.
《紫钗记》
E: The Purple Hairpin

C: 【西江月】堂上敎成燕子：典出《开元天宝遗事》"长安富家子刘逸、李闲喜养燕子，每于堂上教其学语"。原记唐代贵族驯养燕子的雅趣，此处比喻精心培养歌伎。
E:
[Xijiang Moon] In the hall, she teaches the swallows to form [words]:
Alludes to Anecdotes from the Kaiyuan and Tianbao Eras: "The wealthy youths Liu Yi and Li Xian of Chang'an enjoyed keeping swallows and often taught them to speak in the hall." Originally recording the Tang nobility's elegant pastime of training swallows, here it metaphorically means carefully training singing girls.

C:
窗前学画蛾儿：蛾儿指蛾眉，典出《诗经·卫风·硕人》"螓首蛾眉"。原形容女子美眉如蛾触须，此处指歌伎学习妆容。
Before the window, she learns to paint moth-eyebrows."Moth-eyebrows" refers to delicate eyebrows, alluding to the Book of Songs, "Airs of Wei", "The Beautiful Lady": "Forehead like a cicada's, eyebrows like (silkworm) moths' antennae." Originally describing a woman's beautiful eyebrows like moth antennae, here it means the singing girl learning makeup.

淸歌妙舞驻游丝：游丝典出《文选·陆机<文赋>》"浮藻联翩，若翰鸟缨缴，而坠曾云之峻"。原喻诗文飘渺，此处形容歌舞如空中游丝般轻盈缠绵。
Clear songs and wonderful dances halt the floating gossamer."Floating gossamer" alludes to the Selections of Refined Literature, Lu Ji's "Rhapsody on Literature": "Floating phrases flutter past, like a penned bird entangled by a cord, falling from the steepness of layered clouds." Originally a metaphor for the ethereal quality of poetry and prose, here it describes the song and dance as light and lingering like gossamer in the air.

一段烟花佐使：烟花典出《全唐诗》李峤《烛》"烟花不称我，尘土自怜君"。原指春景，此处双关风月场所与戏曲表演。
A section of mist and flowers assists the performance."Mist and flowers" alludes to the Complete Tang Poems, Li Jiao's "Candle": "Mist and flowers do not suit me; dust and earth naturally pity you." Originally referring to spring scenery, here it has a double meaning: the world of pleasure (courtesans) and theatrical performance.

点缀红泉旧本：红泉典出《述异记》"红泉之水，饮之不死"。原为仙境意象，此处指改编前人戏曲剧本。
Embellishing the old text of the Red Spring."Red Spring" alludes to the Shu Yi Ji (Records of Strange Things): "The water of the Red Spring, drinking it confers immortality." Originally an image of an immortal realm, here it means adapting previous dramatic texts.

标题玉茗新词：玉茗典出陆羽《茶经》"茗茶如玉"。明代汤显祖书斋名"玉茗堂"，此处自指其新作《紫钗记》。
Titling the new lyrics of Jade Tea."Jade Tea" alludes to Lu Yu's Classic of Tea: "Fine tea is like jade." Tang Xianzu's study in the Ming Dynasty was named "Jade Tea Hall"; here it refers to his new work The Purple Hairpin.

【沁园春】李子君虞：李益字君虞，典出《旧唐书·李益传》"少有痴病，而多猜忌"。此处指《紫钗记》男主角原型。
[Qinyuan Chun] Master Li, named Junyu:Li Yi, courtesy name Junyu, alludes to the Old Book of Tang, "Biography of Li Yi": "In his youth he had a foolish sickness and was very suspicious." Here it refers to the prototype of the male lead in The Purple Hairpin.

霍家小玉：典出唐蒋防《霍小玉传》。原为唐代传奇中妓女形象，此处指剧中女主角，突出"才貌双奇"特质。
The Huo family's Xiaoyu.Alludes to Jiang Fang's (Tang Dynasty) The Tale of Huo Xiaoyu. Originally the image of a courtesan in a Tang Dynasty tale, here it refers to the female lead in the play, emphasizing her "double rarity of talent and beauty".

堕钗留意：典出《霍小玉传》"生忽见小玉自门隙窥之，掷钗于地"。原为李益、霍小玉定情关键情节。
Dropping the hairpin, she leaves an intention.Alludes to The Tale of Huo Xiaoyu: "The student (Li Yi) suddenly saw Xiaoyu peeping through a crack in the door; she threw a hairpin to the ground." Originally the key scene where Li Yi and Huo Xiaoyu pledge their love.

鲍娘媒妁：典出《战国策》"鲍焦之媒"。原指诚信媒人，此处特指剧中鲍四娘做媒情节。
Aunt Bao acts as matchmaker.Alludes to the Strategies of the Warring States: "Bao Jiao the Matchmaker." Originally referring to an honest matchmaker, here it specifically refers to the plot where Bao Siniang acts as matchmaker in the play.

参军远去：典出《旧唐书·职官志》"参军，掌出使赞导"。指李益中举后赴边关任参军职，导致三年分离。
The Military Advisor goes far away.Alludes to the Old Book of Tang, "Treatise on Officials": "Joining the army is in charge of missions and assisting guidance." Refers to Li Yi, after passing the exams, going to the frontier to serve as joining the army, leading to a three-year separation.

卢太尉设谋招赘：典出《霍小玉传》"卢氏者，甲族也"。剧中将原著卢氏改为卢太尉，强化戏剧冲突。
Grand Marshal Lu schemes to recruit a son-in-law.Alludes to The Tale of Huo Xiaoyu: "The Lu clan was a leading family." In the play, the original character Lu is changed to Grand Marshal Lu to strengthen the dramatic conflict.

别馆禁持：典出《史记·吕不韦列传》"别馆待之"。指剧中卢太尉软禁李益的别馆场景。
Confined and controlled in a separate residence.Alludes to the Records of the Grand Historian, "Biography of Lü Buwei": "Entertained him in a separate residence." Refers to the scene in the play where Grand Marshal Lu detains Li Yi under house arrest in a separate residence.

卖钗卢府：典出原著霍小玉典卖紫钗情节。剧中发展为"穷卖燕花钗"的关键戏剧动作。
Selling the hairpin at the Lu residence.Alludes to the original plot where Huo Xiaoyu pawns and sells the purple hairpin. In the play, it develops into the key dramatic action of "selling the swallow-flower hairpin in poverty".

黄衣客回生起死：黄衣客典出唐传奇《李娃传》"忽有黄衣使者"。此处指剧中黄衫客促成团圆的神奇角色。
The yellow-clad guest restores life and raises the dead."Yellow-clad guest" alludes to the Tang tale The Tale of Li Wa: "Suddenly there was a yellow-clad messenger." Here it refers to the miraculous character of the Man in Yellow in the play who facilitates the reunion.

鞋儿梦：典出《太平广记·梦游上清》"梦中得鞋"。剧中指黄衫客强使二人梦中相会的关键道具。
The shoe dream.Alludes to the Extensive Records of the Taiping Era, "Dream Journey to Shangqing": "Obtaining a shoe in a dream." In the play, it refers to the key prop the Man in Yellow uses to force the two to meet in a dream.

望夫台：典出《幽明录》"武昌山有望夫石"。此处指霍小玉苦等李益的戏剧化场景。
The Gazing-at-Husband Terrace.Alludes to the You Ming Lu (Records of the Hidden and Visible Worlds): "On Wuchang Mountain there is the Gazing-at-Husband Stone." Here it refers to the dramatized scene of Huo Xiaoyu waiting bitterly for Li Yi.

十年映雪图南运：
"映雪"典出《晋书·孙康传》。孙康家贫无灯油，冬夜借雪光读书，后官至御史大夫。"图南"典出《庄子·逍遥游》大鹏鸟飞往南冥的故事，比喻远大志向。此处李益用这两个典故表达自己虽处困境仍怀壮志。
Ten years reflecting snow, planning a southern destiny. "Reflecting snow" alludes to the Book of Jin, "Biography of Sun Kang". Sun Kang's family was poor and had no lamp oil; he read by the light reflected from snow on winter nights, later rising to the post of Censor-in-Chief. "Planning a southern destiny" alludes to the story of the great roc flying to the Southern Darkness in Zhuangzi, "Free and Easy Wandering", metaphor for lofty ambition. Here, Li Yi uses these two allusions to express that despite his difficult situation, he still harbors great ambitions.

咳唾风云：典出《后汉书·赵壹传》。赵壹在《刺世疾邪赋》中写道："咳唾自成珠玉"，形容言辞珍贵如珠宝。此处用来形容李益对自己文章的自信。
Coughed-up spittle becomes wind and clouds.Alludes to the Book of the Later Han, "Biography of Zhao Yi". Zhao Yi wrote in his "Rhapsody on Stabbing the Age's Vices": "My coughed-up spittle naturally becomes pearls and jade," describing his words as precious as jewels. Here it is used to describe Li Yi's confidence in his own writing.

【青玉案】盛世为儒观览遍：化用宋代辛弃疾《青玉案·元夕》词。原词描写元宵夜满城灯火如花开，此处反衬李益空有才学却未遇明主。
[Qingyu An] In this prosperous age, as a scholar, I have observed everything:Adapts Xin Qiji's (Song Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Green Jade Cup" for the Lantern Festival. The original lyric describes the city full of lanterns on the Lantern Festival night like blooming flowers; here it contrasts with Li Yi's possession of talent but lack of meeting an enlightened ruler.

等闲识得东风面：直接引用朱熹《春日》诗。原诗写诗人在泗水边感悟春光的哲理，此处双关李益等待科举机遇。
Casually I recognize the east wind's face.Directly quotes Zhu Xi's poem "Spring Day". The original poem writes of the poet perceiving the philosophy of spring light by the Si River; here it has a double meaning for Li Yi waiting for the opportunity of the imperial examinations.

梦随彩笔绽千花："彩笔"典出《南史·江淹传》。江淹少时梦人授五色笔，文思大进；晚年又梦郭璞索回笔后，才思减退。此即"江郎才尽"典故。
Dreams follow the colorful brush, bursting into a thousand flowers."Colored brush" alludes to the History of the Southern Dynasties, "Biography of Jiang Yan". Jiang Yan dreamed in his youth that someone gave him a five-colored brush, and his literary talent greatly improved; in his old age, he dreamed that Guo Pu asked for the brush back, and his talent declined. This is the story of "Jiang Lang's talent exhausted".

待漏东华：典出唐代官制。百官上朝前需在东华门外"待漏"（等待报晓鼓声）。漏指漏壶，古代计时器。此处表现李益求仕心态。
Awaiting the water clock at Donghua [Gate].Alludes to Tang Dynasty official system. Officials waited outside the Donghua Gate before court, "awaiting the water clock" (waiting for the dawn drum). The "water clock" is the clepsydra, an ancient timekeeping device. Here it shows Li Yi's mindset of seeking office.

红香艺苑，紫臭时流："红紫"典出《论语·阳货》"恶紫之夺朱也"。孔子厌恶紫色混淆正红色。此处"红香"喻高雅文坛，"紫臭"指庸俗权贵。
Red fragrance in the garden of arts, purple stench among the current trend."Red and purple" alludes to the Analects of Confucius, "Yang Huo": "[I] hate purple for displacing vermilion." Confucius hated purple for confusing the true red. Here "red fragrance" metaphorically means the elegant literary world, "purple stench" refers to vulgar powerful officials.

王子敬家藏赐书：王子敬即王献之，王羲之之子。《晋书》记载他获皇帝赐书皆珍藏。此处喻李家藏书丰富。
Wang Zijing's family collected bestowed books.Wang Zijing is Wang Xianzhi, son of Wang Xizhi. The Book of Jin records that he treasured books bestowed by the emperor. Here it metaphorically means the Li family has a rich collection of books.

梁太祖府充名画：梁太祖朱温虽为武将，但好收藏书画。《五代史》记载其府中藏书万卷、名画千轴。此处渲染李家艺术底蕴。
Emperor Taizu of Liang's mansion was filled with famous paintings.Although Emperor Taizu of Liang (Zhu Wen) was a military man, he enjoyed collecting calligraphy and paintings. The History of the Five Dynasties records that his mansion contained ten thousand volumes of books and a thousand scrolls of famous paintings. Here it embellishes the Li family's artistic foundation.

弱冠：典出《礼记·曲礼》。古代男子二十岁行冠礼，称"弱冠"，表示成年。此处强调李益已过二十却未婚。
Weak capping ceremony.Alludes to the Book of Rites, "Summary of the Rules of Propriety Part 1". Ancient men underwent the capping ceremony at twenty, called "weak capping", signifying adulthood. Here it emphasizes that Li Yi is past twenty but still unmarried.

柏叶传芳酝：典出《荆楚岁时记》。汉代元旦有饮椒柏酒习俗，柏叶象征长青。此处用于立春宴饮场景。
Cypress leaves transmit fragrant wine.Alludes to the Jing Chu Sui Shi Ji (Record of the Year and Seasons in Jing and Chu). In the Han Dynasty, there was a custom of drinking pepper and cypress wine on New Year's Day; cypress leaves symbolize everlasting green. Here it is used for a banquet scene at the beginning of spring.

灵池冻释浮鱼阵："灵池"典出《诗经·大雅·灵台》周文王灵沼。原诗描写文王与民同乐，鱼鸟欢跃。此处写春景。
The numinous pool thaws, revealing floating fish formations."Numinous pool" alludes to the Book of Songs, "Greater Odes", "Numinous Tower", King Wen of Zhou's Numinous Pond. The original poem describes King Wen sharing joy with the people, fish and birds leaping happily. Here it describes a spring scene.

屠苏偏让少年人："屠苏"典出《荆楚岁时记》。元旦饮屠苏酒时，按年少者先饮的独特习俗，寓含迎新之意。
The Tusu wine is especially offered to the young man."Tusu wine" alludes to the Jing Chu Sui Shi Ji. When drinking Tusu wine on New Year's Day, there was a unique custom of the youngest drinking first, implying welcoming the new.

岁寒交无二人：化用《论语·子罕》"岁寒知松柏"。孔子说经过严寒才知松柏长青，比喻患难见真情。此处强调三人友谊。
Friendship in years of cold has no second person.Adapts the Analects of Confucius, "Zi Han": "Only when the year grows cold do we see the qualities of the pine and the cypress." Confucius said that only through severe cold do we know the pine and cypress are evergreen, metaphorically meaning adversity reveals true friendship. Here it emphasizes the friendship of the three men.

鲍四娘：剧中重要媒人角色。"鲍"姓可能典出《战国策》记载的诚信媒人鲍焦，与剧中保媒情节呼应。
Aunt Bao the Fourth.An important matchmaker character in the play. The surname "Bao" may allude to the honest matchmaker Bao Jiao recorded in the Strategies of the Warring States, echoing the matchmaking plot in the play.

无媒雪向头中出：化用汉代谚语"白头如新"，指交友不遇。此处双关李益既无媒人说亲，又无贵人提携的困境。
Without a matchmaker, snow appears amidst the hair.Adapts the Han Dynasty proverb "White hair like new," meaning failing to meet a true friend. Here it has a double meaning for Li Yi's predicament: having no matchmaker for marriage and no patron for advancement.

得路云从足下生：典出《史记·范雎传》贾谊语"云蒸龙变"。原指时运到来如云气升腾。此处表现对功名的期待。
Finding a path, clouds follow from beneath his feet.Alludes to Jia Yi's words in the Records of the Grand Historian, "Biography of Fan Ju": "Clouds rise, the dragon transforms." Originally meaning the arrival of fortune is like clouds rising. Here it expresses anticipation of official rank.

满宫花】春正娇：典出《花间集》毛熙震《满宫花》"春正娇，愁似老"。原词描写宫怨，此处借用来表现郑六娘虽值新春却心怀忧愁的复杂心境。
[Man Gong Hua] Spring is truly charming:Alludes to the Collection Among the Flowers, Mao Xizhen's lyric to the tune "Flowers Fill the Palace": "Spring is truly charming, yet sorrow seems old." The original lyric describes palace lament; here it is borrowed to express Zheng Liuniang's complex state of mind, being in early spring yet harboring sorrow.

眉黛不忺重扫：典出《赵飞燕外传》"女弟合德入宫，为薄眉，号远山黛"。汉代流行远山眉，此处用"不忺（不想）重扫"表现郑六娘无心妆扮的慵懒情态。
Moth-eyebrow ink, unwilling to sweep again.Alludes to the Unofficial Biography of Zhao Feiyan: "Her younger sister Hede entered the palace, wore thin eyebrows, called 'distant mountain brows'." Distant mountain brows were popular in the Han Dynasty; here "unwilling to sweep again" shows Zheng Liuniang's lazy mood of having no heart for adornment.

【蝶恋花】谁翦宫花簪彩胜：彩胜典出《荆楚岁时记》"正月七日为人日，剪彩为人，或镂金箔为人，以贴屏风，亦戴之头鬓"。古代立春有剪彩为饰的习俗，此处借问谁来为霍小玉妆扮。
[Die Lian Hua] Who cuts palace flowers to adorn the colored victory garlands?"Colored victory garlands" alludes to the Jing Chu Sui Shi Ji: "The seventh day of the first month is Human Day; colored silk is cut into human shapes, or gold foil is carved into human shapes, to paste on screens, and also to wear in the hair." There was a custom of cutting colored silk for adornment at the beginning of spring; here it asks who will adorn Huo Xiaoyu.

往事不堪重记省：化用李煜《虞美人》"小楼昨夜又东风，故国不堪回首月明中"。原词写亡国之痛，此处表现郑六娘回忆往事的伤感。
Past events cannot bear to be remembered again.Adapts Li Yu's lyric to the tune "The Beautiful Lady Yu": "Last night small towers again had an east wind; my native land cannot bear looking back in the moonlight." The original lyric writes the pain of losing a country; here it shows Zheng Liuniang's sadness in recalling the past.

还恨开迟，冷落梅花信：典出《荆州记》陆凯寄范晔诗"折梅逢驿使，寄与陇头人"。梅花常作报春信使，此处反用，埋怨春信来迟。
Still regret blooming late, neglecting the plum blossom's message.Alludes to the Jingzhou Ji (Records of Jingzhou), the poem Lu Kai sent to Fan Ye: "Breaking off a plum branch, I met a courier; I send it to the man at Longtou." Plum blossoms often serve as messengers of spring; here it is used inversely, complaining that the spring message is late.

靑帝无凭准：青帝典出《尚书纬》"春为东帝，又为青帝"。五方天帝中的春神，此处埋怨春神不守信用，表现盼春焦虑。
The Green Emperor is unreliable."Green Emperor" alludes to the Shangshu Wei (Apocrypha of the Book of Documents): "Spring is the Eastern Emperor, also the Green Emperor." The god of spring among the five directional emperors; here it complains that the spring god is untrustworthy, showing anxiety for spring's arrival.

小家推碧玉之容：碧玉典出《乐府诗集·碧玉歌》"碧玉小家女"。原指平民美女，此处郑六娘自谦出身。
A humble family produces a green jade's beauty."Green jade" alludes to the Music Bureau Poetry Collection, "Song of Green Jade": "Green Jade, daughter of a humble family." Originally referring to a beautiful girl from a common family; here Zheng Liuniang modestly refers to her own background.

大国荐涂金之席：涂金席典出《西京杂记》"赵飞燕为皇后，其女弟上襚三十五条，中有金错绣裆"。此处指郑六娘曾为霍王侍妾的富贵经历。
A great state recommended a gold-lacquered mat."Gold-lacquered mat" alludes to the Miscellaneous Records of the Western Capital: "When Zhao Feiyan became empress, her younger sister presented thirty-five burial garments, among them an embroidered waistband inlaid with gold." Here it refers to Zheng Liuniang's past experience of wealth as a concubine of Prince Huo.

阳城妬尽：典出《汉书·外戚传》"孝成赵皇后，本长安宫人...属阳阿主家"。阳阿主为汉代公主，此处暗指郑六娘曾受王府其他姬妾排挤。
Yangcheng's jealousy was exhausted.Alludes to the Book of Han, "Biographies of the Empresses and Imperial Kinsmen": "Empress Zhao of Emperor Chengxiao was originally a palace maid of Chang'an... attached to the household of the Princess of Yang'a." The Princess of Yang'a was a Han Dynasty princess; here it subtly indicates that Zheng Liuniang was once ostracized by other concubines in the prince's household.

冰井才多：冰井典出《邺中记》"石虎于冰井台藏冰"。此处指霍王府中才女众多，郑六娘以才艺见长。
The ice well had many talents."Ice well" alludes to the Ye Zhong Ji (Records of Ye): "Shi Hu stored ice in the Ice Well Tower." Here it means there were many talented women in Prince Huo's household, and Zheng Liuniang excelled in talent and skill.

惊鸾冶袖，谁偷得韩掾之香：韩掾典出《世说新语》"韩寿美姿容，贾充辟以为掾...充女窥见寿，悦之"。指韩寿偷香典故，此处反用，表现小玉尚未有恋人。
Startling the simurgh with alluring sleeves, who stole the fragrance of Aide Han?"Aide Han" alludes to the Shishuo Xinyu: "Han Shou had handsome features; Jia Chong appointed him as an aide... Jia Chong's daughter peeped at Shou and liked him." Refers to the story of Han Shou stealing the fragrance; here it is used inversely to show that Xiaoyu does not yet have a lover.

绣蝶长裙，未结下汉姝之佩：汉姝典出《列仙传》郑交甫遇汉水神女解佩相赠故事。此处说小玉还未定亲。
Embroidered butterfly long skirt, has not yet tied the pendant of the Han beauty."Han beauty" alludes to the Biographies of Exemplary Immortals, the story of Zheng Jiaofu meeting the goddess of the Han River who untied her pendant and gave it to him. Here it says Xiaoyu is not yet betrothed.

紫玉燕钗：典出《洞冥记》"神女留玉钗与帝，后化为白燕飞去"。此处特制宝钗成为重要剧情道具。
The purple jade swallow hairpin.Alludes to the Dong Ming Ji (Records of the Hidden and Visible Realms): "A goddess left a jade hairpin with the emperor; later it transformed into a white swallow and flew away." Here the specially made precious hairpin becomes an important plot prop.

【绵搭絮】梅额映轻貂：梅额典出《太平御览》引《宋书》"武帝女寿阳公主人日卧含章殿，梅花落额上"。指梅花妆，此处写小玉额饰。
[Mian Da Xu] The plum [decoration] on her forehead shines against light sable."Plum forehead" alludes to the Taiping Yulan quoting the Book of Song: "Princess Shouyang, daughter of Emperor Wu, was lying in the Hanzhang Palace on Human Day; a plum blossom fell on her forehead." Refers to the plum blossom makeup; here it describes Xiaoyu's forehead ornament.

宝鸭熏炉：典出《西京杂记》"长安巧工丁缓作被中香炉...为机环转运四周"。此处描写贵族女子闺阁陈设。
Precious duck censer.Alludes to the Miscellaneous Records of the Western Capital: "The skilled craftsman Ding Huan of Chang'an made an incense burner for under the quilts... with a mechanism that rotated it all around." Here it describes the furnishings of a noblewoman's boudoir.

暗换年华：化用李煜《虞美人》"雕栏玉砌应犹在，只是朱颜改"。原词写物是人非，此处感叹春光悄逝。
Years and months stealthily change.Adapts Li Yu's lyric to the tune "The Beautiful Lady Yu": "The carved balustrades and jade steps must still be there, only the rosy faces have changed." The original lyric writes that things remain but people change; here it laments the stealthy passing of spring light.

【前腔】微酒晕红潮：典出《开元天宝遗事》"杨贵妃每至夏月...红潮生脸"。原写杨贵妃醉态，此处表现小玉微醺娇态。
[Same tune] A little wine brings a red flush.Alludes to Anecdotes from the Kaiyuan and Tianbao Eras: "Whenever Yang Guifei reached summer... a red flush arose on her face." Originally describing Yang Guifei's drunken state; here it shows Xiaoyu's charming manner when slightly tipsy.

宜春胜欲飘：宜春胜典出《荆楚岁时记》"立春之日，悉剪彩为燕戴之"。立春佩戴的彩胜，此处随风欲飘，充满动感。
The suitable spring victory garland seems about to flutter."Suitable spring victory garland" alludes to the Jing Chu Sui Shi Ji: "On the day of the beginning of spring, everyone cuts colored silk into swallows to wear." The colored victory garland worn at the beginning of spring; here it seems about to flutter in the wind, full of movement.

【前腔】长是索春饶：化用李商隐《早起》"莺花啼又笑，毕竟是谁春"。原诗写惜春，此处表现少女对春天的渴望。
[Same tune] Always demanding spring's abundance.Adapts Li Shangyin's "Early Rising": "Orioles and flowers cry and laugh again; after all, whose spring is it?" The original poem writes of cherishing spring; here it shows a young girl's longing for spring.

拾翠闲行：典出曹植《洛神赋》"或采明珠，或拾翠羽"。原写洛水女神，此处写小玉春日游玩的雅致。
Leisurely walking, picking up kingfisher feathers.Alludes to Cao Zhi's "Rhapsody on the Goddess of the Luo River": "Some gather bright pearls, some pick up kingfisher feathers." Originally describing the goddess of the Luo River; here it describes Xiaoyu's elegant spring outing.

【前腔】金步摇：典出《后汉书·舆服志》"皇后步摇，以黄金为山题，贯白珠为桂枝"。汉代贵妇首饰，此处描写玉钗精美。
[Same tune] Golden step-shaker.Alludes to the Book of the Later Han, "Treatise on Carriages and Clothing": "The empress's buyao had a gold mountain base, pierced with white pearls to form cassia branches." A Han Dynasty noblewoman's headdress; here it describes the exquisite jade hairpin.

蜂蝶晴遥：化用杜甫《曲江》"穿花蛱蝶深深见"。原写春景，此处以蜂蝶远飞来衬托玉钗吸引目光。
Bees and butterflies in the clear distance.Adapts Du Fu's "Qujiang River": "Butterflies piercing flowers are seen deep within." Originally describing a spring scene; here the bees and butterflies flying from afar set off the hairpin's power to attract attention.

试拂菱花韵转标：菱花指菱花镜，典出《飞燕外传》"婕妤上七尺菱花镜一奁"。此处描写小玉对镜理妆的优美姿态。
Trying to wipe the water-chestnut-flower [mirror], her grace becomes more striking."Water-chestnut-flower" refers to a water-chestnut-flower mirror, alluding to the Unofficial Biography of Zhao Feiyan: "The Lady Jieyu presented a case containing a seven-foot water-chestnut-flower mirror." Here it describes Xiaoyu's graceful posture while dressing before the mirror.

翠屛闲：宋辛弃疾《祝英台近·晚春》"宝钗分，桃叶渡"。辛弃疾借梁祝词牌写闺怨，描写女子暮春与情人分别的愁绪。
The green screen stands idle.From Xin Qiji's (Song Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Zhu Ying Tai Near" for late spring: "The precious hairpin divided, at the Peach Leaf Ferry." Xin Qiji used the Liang-Zhu tune to write boudoir lament, describing a woman's sorrow at parting with her lover in late spring.

行云梦老巫山下：战国宋玉《高唐赋》"妾在巫山之阳"。楚襄王梦巫山神女自荐枕席，神女化云降雨，后以"云雨"喻男女欢爱。
The moving clouds dream of growing old beneath Mount Wu.From Song Yu's (Warring States period) "Rhapsody on the Gaotang Shrine": "I dwell on the sunny side of Mount Wu." King Xiang of Chu dreamed of the goddess of Mount Wu offering herself; the goddess transformed into clouds and rain, later "clouds and rain" became a metaphor for sexual love.

红泪覆鲛绡：晋王嘉《拾遗记》"以玉唾壶承泪，壶则红色"。魏文帝美人薛灵芸离别时泪凝如血；南朝《述异记》载鲛人所织名贵龙纱。
Red tears soak the mermaid silk.From Wang Jia's (Jin Dynasty) Shi Yi Ji (Records of Neglected Matters): "She caught her tears in a jade spittoon; the spittoon turned red." The beauty Xue Lingyun of Emperor Wen of Wei shed tears like blood at parting; the Southern Dynasties Shu Yi Ji records the precious dragon silk woven by mermaids.

帘垂深院冷萧萧：宋晏几道《少年游》"帘垂深院冷萧萧"。晏几道写贵族女子独守深闺，听更漏声声的寂寞情景。
Curtains hang deep in the courtyard, cold and soughing.From Yan Jidao's (Song Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Wandering in Youth": "Curtains hang deep in the courtyard, cold and soughing." Yan Jidao writes of a noblewoman alone in her secluded chamber, listening to the sound of the water clock, a scene of loneliness.

玉筝弦索：《晋书·陶侃传》"丝竹并奏"。东晋陶侃宴客时筝琶合奏的热闹场面，反衬独奏凄凉。
Jade zheng's strings.From the Book of Jin, "Biography of Tao Kan": "Strings and bamboo instruments played together." The lively scene of zheng and pipa playing together at Tao Kan's banquet during the Eastern Jin contrasts with the desolation of a solo.

鸳鸯被半香销：唐温庭筠《更漏子》"香作穗，蜡成泪"。描写女子独对香烛燃尽，怀念远方情人的孤寂。
The mandarin duck quilt, half its fragrance gone.From Wen Tingyun's (Tang Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Geng Lou Zi": "Incense forms ears, candles become tears." Describes a woman alone facing burnt-out incense and candles, yearning for a distant lover, a scene of solitude.

客思绕无涯：宋吴文英《唐多令》"离人心上秋"。将"愁"字拆解为"心上秋"，写游子秋日离愁。
Traveler's thoughts wind boundlessly.From Wu Wenying's (Song Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Tang Duo Ling": "Autumn in the parting one's heart." The character for "sorrow" is disassembled into "autumn" "on the heart", writing a traveler's autumn sorrow.

青门近狭斜：《三辅黄图》"长安城东出南头第一门曰霸城门"。汉代长安青门乃冶游之地，狭斜指妓院聚集的曲巷。
The Green Gate is near the narrow alleys.From the San Fu Huang Tu (Plan of the Capital): "The first gate on the southern end of the eastern wall of Chang'an city was called the Ba City Gate." The Green Gate of Han Dynasty Chang'an was a place for pleasure-seeking; "narrow alleys" refers to the winding lanes where brothels gathered.

一笑千金：唐崔令钦《教坊记》"千金买笑"。汉武帝为博李夫人一笑，命乐工特制《千金笑》新曲。
A single smile is worth a thousand gold.From Cui Lingqin's (Tang Dynasty) Jiao Fang Ji (Record of the Music Academy): "A thousand gold to buy a smile." Emperor Wu of Han, to win a smile from Lady Li, ordered musicians to specially compose the new tune "A Thousand Gold for a Smile".

一曲红绡：《唐书·李晟传》"一曲红绡不知数"。唐代名将李晟宴客时，歌女一曲终了获赏无数红绡。
One song [earns] red silk.From the Tang History, "Biography of Li Sheng": "For one song, the red silk was beyond counting." When the famous Tang general Li Sheng entertained guests, singing girls received countless red silk as reward after one song.

苏姑子作好梦：唐《太平广记》引《苏姑子传》。书生梦苏姑子预言姻缘，次日果遇佳偶成婚。
The Su maiden had a good dream.The Extensive Records of the Taiping Era (Tang compilation) quotes the Tale of the Su Maiden. A scholar dreamed that the Su maiden predicted his marriage; the next day he indeed met a good match and married.

一缕红丝：唐李复言《续玄怪录》"以赤绳系夫妇之足"。月下老人用红丝系夫妻足，注定姻缘天定。
A single strand of red thread.From Li Fuyan's (Tang Dynasty) Xu Xuan Guai Lu (Sequel to Records of the Mysterious and Strange): "Tying the feet of husband and wife with a red cord." The Old Man under the Moon ties the feet of destined couples with a red thread, signifying marriage decreed by heaven.

紫陌花灯：唐苏味道《正月十五夜》"暗尘随马去"。描写长安元宵夜车马喧阗、明月逐人的灯会盛况。
Flower lanterns on the purple road.From Su Weidao's (Tang Dynasty) poem "The Night of the Fifteenth of the First Month": "Hidden dust follows the horses away." Describes the bustling lantern festival scene in Chang'an on the Lantern Festival night, with noisy carriages and horses, and the bright moon chasing people.

金吾不禁夜：唐苏味道《正月十五夜》"金吾不禁夜，玉漏莫相催"。金吾指唐代禁卫军，负责京城宵禁，而元宵节特许解除宵禁三天，允许百姓彻夜游乐，诗中以此句描写长安元宵夜取消宵禁的盛况。
The Golden Guards do not prohibit the night.From Su Weidao's (Tang Dynasty) poem "The Night of the Fifteenth of the First Month": "The Golden Guards do not prohibit the night; the jade water clock, do not urge us on." "Golden Guards" refers to the Tang Dynasty imperial guards responsible for the capital's curfew; during the Lantern Festival, the curfew was specially

玉漏莫相催：同上苏味道诗。玉漏是古代计时用的铜壶滴漏，由玉石装饰，元宵佳节特许通宵欢庆，故说不必计较时间早晚，原句表现了唐代元宵节全民狂欢的场景。
The jade water clock, do not urge us on.Same Su Weidao poem above. The "jade water clock" is the bronze clepsydra used for timekeeping in ancient times, decorated with jade. During the Lantern Festival, all-night celebration was specially permitted, hence the line says not to worry about the time. The original line expresses the scene of whole populace revelry during the Tang Dynasty Lantern Festival.

禁漏花迟：唐冯延巳《采桑子》"画堂灯暖帘栊卷，禁漏丁丁"。禁漏指宫中的更漏声，花迟指初春花朵尚未盛开，皇宫计时漏声与街边迟开的花树形成对比，描写出宫廷内外元宵时节的特殊氛围。
The palace water clock [sounds], the flowers are late.From Feng Yansi's (Tang Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Cai Sang Zi": "Painted hall, warm lamps, curtains and lattices rolled up; the palace water clock goes 'ding ding'." "Palace water clock" refers to the sound of the water clock in the palace; "flowers are late" means the flowers of early spring have not yet bloomed. The contrast between the palace timekeeping and the late-blooming trees on the streets describes the special atmosphere inside and outside the palace during the Lantern Festival season.

玉街春早：《长安志》"朱雀街广百步，谓之玉街"。朱雀街是唐代长安城的南北中轴线，铺着玉石般的石板，这条主干道在元宵节最早呈现春意。
Jade Street has an early spring.From the Chang'an Zhi (Records of Chang'an): "Zhuque Street was one hundred paces wide and was called Jade Street." Zhuque Street was the north-south central axis of Tang Dynasty Chang'an, paved with jade-like stone slabs. This main thoroughfare showed signs of spring earliest during the Lantern Festival.

王母夜烧灯：《汉武帝内传》"王母遣使乘白鹿告帝当来"。传说西王母出行时有仙童执火炬仪仗，此处以此比喻元宵节的灯火辉煌如同神仙降临，形容元宵灯火之盛。
The Queen Mother burns lanterns at night.From the Nei Zhuan of Emperor Wu of Han (Unofficial Biography of Emperor Wu of Han): "The Queen Mother sent a messenger riding a white deer to inform the emperor she would come." Legend says that when the Queen Mother of the West traveled, immortal boys carried torchbearers in her procession. Here this is used as a metaphor for the Lantern Festival's brilliant lights being like the arrival of immortals, describing the abundance of Lantern Festival lights.

长春阆苑：《拾遗记》"昆仑山有阆风之苑，神仙所居"。阆苑是西王母居住的仙境，四季如春，此处用这一传说形容元宵节的长安街景美如仙境。
Eternal Spring Lang Garden.From the Shi Yi Ji (Records of Neglected Matters): "On Kunlun Mountain there is the Lang Garden, where immortals dwell." Lang Garden is the immortal realm where the Queen Mother of the West resides, with eternal spring. Here this legend is used to describe the Lantern Festival street scenes in Chang'an as beautiful as an immortal realm.

星桥畔长明仙院：《三辅黄图》"渭水贯都，以象天汉，横桥南渡，以法牵牛"。渭水上的桥梁点缀灯火如银河，道观（仙院）彻夜灯火通明，描写出长安元宵夜水陆交辉的盛景。
By the Star Bridge, the Ever-Bright Immortal Court.From the San Fu Huang Tu (Plan of the Capital): "The Wei River traversed the capital, representing the Heavenly River (Milky Way); the horizontal bridge crossed south, imitating the Herd Boy." The bridges over the Wei River were dotted with lights like the Milky Way; Daoist temples (immortal courts) were brightly lit all night, describing the magnificent scene of water and land intermingling in Chang'an on the Lantern Festival night.

红云拥翠华偏：《西京杂记》"贾佩兰说在宫时，正月十五作酒池肉林，灯树高数十丈"。红云指无数红灯，翠华是贵族出行的翠绿华盖，此句形容灯火如云簇拥着贵族车驾的场面。
Red clouds embrace the green-canopied carriage.From the Miscellaneous Records of the Western Capital: "Jia Peilan said that when she was in the palace, on the fifteenth of the first month they made pools of wine and forests of meat, with lantern trees tens of zhang high." "Red clouds" refers to countless red lanterns; "green canopy" is the emerald green canopy used by nobility when traveling. This line describes the scene of lights like clouds crowding around the noble carriages.

十二楼阑干春浅：《史记·孝武本纪》"黄帝时为五城十二楼"。十二楼本是传说中黄帝建造用于迎仙的楼阁，后来泛指高大华丽的楼阁，此处指长安高楼，元宵时节，高楼上的栏杆边已能感受到淡淡春意。
On the twelve towers, by the railings, spring is faint.From the Records of the Grand Historian, "Basic Annals of Emperor Xiaowu": "In the time of the Yellow Emperor, there were five cities and twelve towers." The twelve towers were originally legendary towers built by the Yellow Emperor to receive immortals; later they generally referred to tall, magnificent towers. Here they refer to the high towers of Chang'an; during the Lantern Festival season, a faint sense of spring could already be felt by the railings of these high towers.

三千界芙蓉妆艳：《法华经》"三千大千世界"。三千界是佛教语，指一个世界由三千大千世界组成，此处用这一说法形容满城仕女盛装出游，容貌如芙蓉花开般艳丽的壮观景象。
In the three-thousand worlds, lotus blossoms are adorned with gorgeous makeup.From the Lotus Sutra: "Three thousand great thousand worlds." "Three-thousand worlds" is a Buddhist term meaning a world system composed of three thousand great chiliocosms. Here this concept is used to describe the spectacular sight of the city filled with ladies in splendid attire going on an outing, their beauty as gorgeous as blooming lotus flowers.

星球乱点：宋周密《武林旧事》"一入新正，灯火日盛，皆用琉璃球灯"。当时流行琉璃球灯，悬挂在街头如星辰散布，此句描写各式球形灯笼点缀街市的场景。
Star-spheres scatter randomly.From Zhou Mi's (Song Dynasty) Old Events of Wulin: "Once the new year began, the lanterns daily increased; all used glass ball lanterns." Glass ball lanterns were popular at the time, hung in the streets like scattered stars. This line describes the scene of various spherical lanterns dotting the streets.

银汉斜通宛转桥：《三辅黄图》"渭水贯都，以象天汉"。长安渭水被比喻为银河（银汉），渭水上的拱桥灯火辉煌，宛如连接天人的鹊桥，描写出元宵夜桥梁的美丽景致。
The Silver River (Milky Way) slantly connects to the winding bridge.From the San Fu Huang Tu (Plan of the Capital): "The Wei River traversed the capital, representing the Heavenly River." The Wei River in Chang'an was compared to the Heavenly River (Milky Way); the arched bridges over the Wei River were brilliantly lit, just like the Magpie Bridge connecting heaven and earth, describing the beautiful scenery of the bridges on the Lantern Festival night.

严城不禁葳蕤锁：《汉书·元后传》"曲阳侯根骄奢僭上，赤墀青琐"。葳蕤锁指宫门上的雕花金锁，平时森严的城门在元宵节特许开放，任由百姓出入游玩。
The strict city does not prohibit the luxuriant locks.From the Book of Han, "Biography of the Yuan Empress": "The Marquis of Quyang, Gen, was arrogant, extravagant, and usurped imperial prerogatives; he had red steps and blue locks." "Luxuriant locks" refers to the carved golden locks on palace gates. The normally strict city gates were specially opened during the Lantern Festival, allowing the common people to enter and exit freely for amusement.

成团打队向灯宵：《东京梦华录》"正月十五日元宵，游人已集御街两廊下，奇术异能，歌舞百戏"。描写宋代元宵节时，各种表演团体列队游行，在灯会上展示才艺的团体游赏盛况。
Forming groups and bands towards the lantern night.From Dreams of Splendor of the Eastern Capital (Dongjing Menghua Lu): "On the fifteenth day of the first month, the Lantern Festival, visitors already gathered under the corridors of the Imperial Street; there were extraordinary skills and abilities, song, dance, and hundred entertainments." Describes the grand occasion during the Song Dynasty Lantern Festival when various performance troupes paraded in formation, displaying their talents at the lantern festival in a group tour.

金屋何能闭阿娇：汉班固《汉武故事》"若得阿娇作妇，当作金屋贮之"。此句反用汉武帝"金屋藏娇"的典故，平时深居闺阁的贵族女子，在元宵节也都结伴出游观灯，表现出节日的特殊性。
How can the Golden House confine A'jiao?From Ban Gu's (Han Dynasty) The Story of Emperor Wu of Han: "If I can get A'jiao as my wife, I will build a golden house to store her in." This line inversely uses the story of Emperor Wu of Han "storing A'jiao in a golden house." Noblewomen usually secluded in their chambers would also go out in groups to view the lanterns during the Lantern Festival, showing the special nature of the holiday.

绛台：指华丽的高台，常用来描绘月夜或春日的景致，此处"绛台春夜"描绘春夜高台的景象。
Crimson Tower: Refers to a magnificent high tower, often used to depict moonlit nights or spring scenery. Here, "Crimson Tower on a Spring Night" describes the scene of a high tower on a spring night.

素娥：即嫦娥，神话中月宫中的女神，代指月亮。见《文选·谢庄〈月赋〉》"引玄兔于帝台，集素娥于后庭"。此处"冉冉素娥欲下"形容月亮缓缓升起的样子。
White Lady: That is, Chang'e, the goddess of the moon in mythology, representing the moon. See the Selections of Refined Literature, Xie Zhuang's "Rhapsody on the Moon": "Leading the Dark Hare to the Imperial Terrace, gathering the White Ladies in the rear courtyard." Here, "Slowly, slowly, the White Lady wishes to descend" describes the moon slowly rising.

严城：指戒备森严的城郭，常出现在诗词中描绘城市夜景。此处"月浸严城如画"描绘月光笼罩下的城池如画卷般美丽。
Strict City: Refers to a heavily guarded city wall, often appearing in poetry to depict city night scenes. Here, "The moon soaks the strict city like a painting" describes the city under moonlight as beautiful as a painted scroll.

钿车罗帕：钿车指装饰华丽的马车，罗帕指丝织的手帕，均为古代贵族女子出行或交际的常见物品，常用来代指男女相逢的场景。此处"钿车罗帕相逢处"描绘男女在花灯夜相逢的情景。
Inlaid carriage, gauze handkerchief: "Inlaid carriage" refers to ornately decorated carriages; "gauze handkerchief" refers to silk handkerchiefs. Both were common items for noblewomen traveling or socializing in ancient times, often used to represent scenes of men and women meeting. Here, "The place where inlaid carriages and gauze handkerchiefs meet" describes a scene of men and women meeting on the lantern festival night.

暗尘随马：源自唐代苏味道《正月十五夜》"暗尘随马去，明月逐人来"。原句句意：昏暗的尘土随着马队而去，明亮的月光追逐着人群而来。此处引用描绘花灯夜车马喧嚣、尘土飞扬的热闹场景。
Hidden dust follows the horses: Originates from Su Weidao's (Tang Dynasty) "The Night of the Fifteenth of the First Month": "Hidden dust follows the horses away, the bright moon pursues the people coming." The original meaning: The dim dust follows the horses away, the bright moonlight chases the people coming. Here it is quoted to depict the lively scene of noisy carriages, horses, and dust flying on the lantern festival night.

笙歌世界酒楼台：化用唐代诗句中常见的笙歌、酒楼意象，描绘元宵夜歌舞升平、酒楼林立的繁华景象。
A world of flute songs,wine taverns and towers: Uses the common imagery of flute songs and wine taverns from Tang poetry to depict the prosperous scene of music, dance, peace, and numerous wine taverns on the Lantern Festival night.

鸡踏莲花万树开：化用唐代元宵节俗中"踏莲灯"的场景，莲花灯绽放如万树花开，此处形容花灯繁盛的景象。
Chickens tread on lotuses, ten thousand trees bloom: Uses the scene of "treading on lotus lanterns" from Tang Dynasty Lantern Festival customs; the lotus lanterns bloom like ten thousand trees flowering, here describing the abundant scene of lanterns.

谁家见月能端坐，何处闻灯不看来：源自唐代崔液《上元夜二首·其一》"谁家见月能闲坐，何处闻灯不看来"。原句句意：哪家看到这样的明月能安然端坐，何处听到花灯的消息会不来观赏。此处引用表现人们元宵赏灯的急切心情。
What household seeing the moon can sit properly? What place hearing of lanterns will not come to see? Originates from Cui Ye's (Tang Dynasty) "Two Poems for the First Night of the First Month, No. 1": "What household seeing the moon can sit idle? What place hearing of lanterns will not come to see?" The original meaning: Which household seeing such a bright moon can sit calmly? Where hearing the news of lanterns would not come to see? Here it is quoted to show people's eagerness to view the lanterns on the Lantern Festival.

黄衫豪客：源自唐代传奇《霍小玉传》中帮助李益与霍小玉相见的黄衫客形象，后泛指侠义豪放的男子。此处"黄衫豪客是也"直接化用这一形象。
Yellow-clad heroic guest: Originates from the image of the Man in Yellow who helps Li Yi meet Huo Xiaoyu in the Tang Dynasty tale The Tale of Huo Xiaoyu, later generally referring to chivalrous and heroic men. Here, "It is I, the yellow-clad heroic guest" directly uses this image.

狭邪：原指小巷，后常代指妓院等游乐场所，此处"趁灯宵遨游狭邪"指在元宵夜游览热闹的游乐之处。
Narrow and crooked: Originally meant small alleys, later often referred to pleasure quarters like brothels. Here, "taking advantage of the lantern night to wander the narrow and crooked" means visiting lively pleasure spots on the Lantern Festival night.

蓬阆苑：蓬指蓬莱，阆苑指阆风之苑，均为神话中的仙境，常用来代指美好的境地。此处"等的个蓬阆苑放星槎"中以蓬阆苑喻指与意中人相逢的美好场景。
Penglai and Lang Garden: "Penglai" refers to Penglai, "Lang Garden" refers to the Lang Garden, both are mythical immortal realms, often used to represent beautiful places. Here, "waiting for Penglai and Lang Garden to release the star raft" uses Penglai and Lang Garden to metaphorically represent the beautiful scene of meeting one's beloved.

星槎：神话传说中往来于天河的木筏，见《博物志》卷十"天河与海通，近世有人居海渚者，年年八月有浮槎去来，不失期"。此处"放星槎"喻指期待如乘槎入仙境般遇到意中人。
Star raft: A wooden raft that travels on the Heavenly River in myth and legend, see the Bowu Zhi (Records of Diverse Matters), Volume 10: "The Heavenly River connects with the sea; in recent times, someone living on a sea islet had a floating raft come and go every year in the eighth month, never missing the date." Here, "releasing the star raft" metaphorically means hoping to meet one's beloved as if riding a raft into an immortal realm.

檀郎：原指晋代潘岳，因其小字檀奴，容貌俊美，后成为对美男子或女子所爱男子的美称。见《世说新语·容止》等记载。此处"怪檀郎转眼偷相撇"中，旦以檀郎代指生。
Sandalwood Lord: Originally referred to Pan Yue of the Jin Dynasty, because his childhood name was Tan Nu and he was handsome; later it became a complimentary term for a handsome man or a woman's beloved. See records in the Shishuo Xinyu, "Appearance and Behavior" etc. Here, in "Blaming the Sandalwood Lord for stealthily turning his eyes away in an instant," the female lead uses Sandalwood Lord to refer to the male lead.

小玉姐：指霍小玉，唐代传奇《霍小玉传》中的女主角，为霍王庶女，与李益相恋。此处明确提及"霍王小姐""小玉姐"，呼应这一人物设定。
Sister Xiaoyu: Refers to Huo Xiaoyu, the female lead in the Tang Dynasty tale The Tale of Huo Xiaoyu, the illegitimate daughter of Prince Huo, who fell in love with Li Yi. Here, explicitly mentioning "Prince Huo's young lady" and "Sister Xiaoyu" echoes this character setup.

陇西李益：李益为唐代诗人，字君虞，陇西姑臧（今甘肃武威）人，此处生自报姓名"陇西李益，表字君虞，排号十郎"，化用历史人物身份。
Longxi Li Yi: Li Yi was a Tang Dynasty poet, courtesy name Junyu, from Guzang, Longxi (present-day Wuwei, Gansu). Here, the male lead announces his name: "Li Yi of Longxi, styled Junyu, ranked as the Tenth Lad," using the identity of the historical figure.

蓝桥：神话传说中裴航遇云英处，见唐代裴铏《传奇·裴航》。裴航在蓝桥驿遇仙女云英，历经考验后结为夫妻。此处"似近蓝桥那般欢惬"用蓝桥典故喻指与小玉相逢的喜悦。
Blue Bridge: The place where Pei Hang met Yunying in myth and legend, see Pei Xing's (Tang Dynasty)Chuanqi, "Pei Hang". Pei Hang met the immortal maiden Yunying at the Blue Bridge post station; after undergoing trials, they married. Here, "seeming as joyful as nearing the Blue Bridge" uses the Blue Bridge story to metaphorically represent the joy of meeting Xiaoyu.

飞琼：指神话中的仙女许飞琼，为西王母侍女，后常代指美女或珍贵的玉佩等。此处"便当宝此飞琼"中以飞琼代指所拾玉钗。
Flying Qiong: Refers to the mythical immortal maiden Xu Feiqiong, an attendant of the Queen Mother of the West, later often representing a beautiful woman or a precious jade pendant. Here, "I shall then treasure this Flying Qiong" uses Flying Qiong to represent the picked-up jade hairpin.

燕钗：指形状如燕的玉钗，为古代女子常见饰物，常出现在诗词中代指男女情事。此处"钗，你插新妆宝镜中燕尾斜"描绘玉钗的形状。
Swallow hairpin: Refers to a jade hairpin shaped like a swallow, a common ornament for ancient women, often appearing in poetry to represent romantic affairs. Here, "Hairpin, you are inserted askew like a swallow's tail in the precious mirror of new makeup" describes the shape of the jade hairpin.

堕珥遗簪：源自汉代张衡《西京赋》"堕珥遗簪，稽首请罪"，形容女子游玩时饰物散落的情景。此处"堕珥遗簪幽恨结"描绘元宵夜男女相逢别离的情态。
Dropped earrings, lost hairpins: Originates from Zhang Heng's (Han Dynasty) "Rhapsody on the Western Capital": "Dropped earrings, lost hairpins, kowtowing to apologize," describing the scene of a woman's ornaments scattering while playing. Here, "Dropped earrings, lost hairpins, secret resentment forms" describes the manner of men and women meeting and parting on the Lantern Festival night.

千金一刻：源自宋代苏轼《春夜》"春宵一刻值千金，花有清香月有阴"。原句句意：春天的夜晚，每一刻都价值千金，花儿散发着清香，月亮也有朦胧的阴影。此处"千金一刻，天教钗挂寒枝"强调元宵夜相逢的珍贵。
A thousand gold for one moment: Originates from Su Shi's (Song Dynasty) "Spring Night": "A spring night's moment is worth a thousand gold; flowers have a clear fragrance, the moon has shadows." The original meaning: A spring night's moment is worth a thousand pieces of gold; the flowers emit a light fragrance, the moon also has a hazy shadow. Here, "A thousand gold for one moment, heaven made the hairpin hang on a cold branch" emphasizes the preciousness of the meeting on the Lantern Festival night.

纱笼映月歌浓李：化用唐代元稹《连昌宫词》"楼下公孙昔擅场，空教女子爱风流。开元歌舞古草头，一曲霓裳四海秋。今来独倚西楼望，月照章台柳色愁。纱笼犹记当时影，香径空留旧藓痕"中纱笼映月的意象，此处指歌女在月下歌唱的情景。
Gauze lanterns reflect the moon, singing of lush plum: Uses the imagery of gauze lanterns reflecting the moon from Yuan Zhen's (Tang Dynasty) "Song of the Lianchang Palace": "Below the tower, Gongsun once dominated the scene, vainly teaching women to love romance. Kaiyuan songs and dances, ancient grass heads; one song of rainbow skirts, autumn in the four seas. Now I come alone, leaning on the west tower gazing; moonlight shines on the Zhang Terrace, willow colors sorrowful. Gauze lanterns still remember the shadows of that time; the fragrant path emptily retains old moss traces." Here it refers to the scene of singing girls singing under the moonlight.

翠袖迎风糁落梅：化用宋代李清照《清平乐》"看取晚来风势，故应难看梅花"等诗词中翠袖、落梅的意象，此处形容女子在风中的娇态如梅花飘落。
Green sleeves welcome the wind, scattered falling plum blossoms: Uses the imagery of green sleeves and falling plum blossoms from Li Qingzhao's (Song Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Qing Ping Le" "Observing the wind's force in the evening, surely the plum blossoms will be hard to see" and other poems. Here it describes a woman's charming manner in the wind like drifting plum blossoms.

玉漏：古代计时仪器，以玉为饰，常用来代指时间。此处"和催归玉漏彻"指玉漏显示夜已深沉，催人归去。
Jade water clock: An ancient timekeeping instrument decorated with jade, often used to represent time. Here, "harmonizing with the urging-to-return jade water clock's completion" means the jade water clock shows the night is deep, urging people to return home.

鸾影：原指鸾鸟的影子，常用来代指女子的身影或美好的仪态。此处"鸾影催归"指女子的身影远去，催人离别。
Luan shadow: Originally meant the shadow of a luan bird, often used to represent a woman's figure or graceful bearing. Here, "Luan shadow urges return" means the woman's figure is moving away, urging separation.

婵娟：原指姿态美好的女子，后常代指月亮或美女。此处"婵娟此会真奇绝"指与美女的相逢极为奇妙。
Lovely: Originally meant a woman with a beautiful posture, later often representing the moon or a beautiful woman. Here, "This meeting with the lovely one is truly extraordinary" means the meeting with the beautiful woman is extremely wonderful.

玉天仙：对美女的美称，喻指女子如天仙般美丽。此处"玉天仙罩住得梅梢月"形容女子的美丽如同笼罩着梅梢的月光。
Jade heavenly immortal: A complimentary term for a beautiful woman,metaphorically meaning a woman as beautiful as a heavenly immortal. Here, "The jade heavenly immortal captures the moon on the plum tips" describes the woman's beauty as like moonlight enveloping the plum tips.

春消息：指春天的讯息，常用来代指爱情的萌芽或美好的机遇。此处"春消息漏泄在花灯节"指爱情的讯息在元宵花灯节显露。
Spring news: Refers to news of spring, often used to represent the budding of love or a good opportunity. Here, "Spring news leaked out at the flower lantern festival" means the news of love was revealed during the Lantern Festival.

花淡澹，月婵娟："婵娟"指月亮皎洁美好的样子，常用来形容月色或女子姿态。此处"月婵娟"描绘月光柔和美丽的景象。
Flowers pale, moon lovely: "Lovely" refers to the moon's bright and beautiful appearance, often used to describe moonlight or a woman's posture. Here, "moon lovely" depicts the soft and beautiful moonlight.

星桥：神话传说中七夕喜鹊搭桥使牛郎织女相会，称星桥，后常代指花灯节的灯桥或热闹的桥梁。此处"透万点星桥情半点"指花灯如星桥般璀璨，传递着朦胧情意。
Star bridge: In myth and legend, the magpies form a bridge on the Double Seventh Festival for the Cowherd and Weaving Maid to meet, called the star bridge; later it often represented the lantern bridges of the Lantern Festival or lively bridges. Here, "Penetrating ten thousand points of the star bridge, half a point of feeling" means the lanterns are as brilliant as the star bridge, conveying vague feelings.

广寒：指广寒宫，神话中嫦娥居住的月宫，常代指月亮或清冷的仙境。此处"似广寒低蹑飞鸾"形容小玉姐的姿态如从月宫下凡的仙女轻踏鸾鸟而来。
Vast Cold: Refers to the Vast Cold Palace, the moon palace where Chang'e resides in mythology, often representing the moon or a cold, clear immortal realm. Here, "Like the Vast Cold Palace, lightly treading a flying luan" describes Sister Xiaoyu's posture as like an immortal maiden descending from the moon palace, lightly stepping on a luan bird.

东风病酒：源自宋代李清照《如梦令》"昨夜雨疏风骤，浓睡不消残酒"等诗词中"病酒"意象，指因饮酒过量或离愁而感到不适。此处"觉东风病酒"指清晨醒来因离愁和饮酒而身心慵懒。
East wind, sick with wine: Originates from the imagery of "sick with wine" in Li Qingzhao's (Song Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Ru Meng Ling" "Last night rain was sparse, wind sudden; deep sleep did not dispel the remaining wine" and other poems, meaning feeling unwell due to excessive drinking or the sorrow of parting. Here, "Feeling the east wind, sick with wine" means waking in the morning feeling physically and mentally sluggish due to parting sorrow and drinking.

红鸾：神话中象征爱情的神鸟，"红鸾凑成"指姻缘巧合、爱情到来。此处"恁般红鸾凑成"指与小玉姐的相逢是天赐姻缘。
Red luan: A mythical bird symbolizing love; "red luan comes together" means a coincidental match, the arrival of love. Here, "Such a red luan comes together" means the meeting with Sister Xiaoyu is a heaven-sent match.

玉镜台：源自晋代温峤以玉镜台为聘礼娶表妹刘倩之的典故，见《世说新语·假谲》，后常代指聘礼或姻缘信物。此处"你嫦娥亲许，玉镜台前会得清"以玉镜台喻指姻缘已定。
Jade mirror stand: Originates from the story of Wen Jiao using a jade mirror stand as a betrothal gift to marry his cousin Liu Qianzhi, see the Shishuo Xinyu, "False and Cunning"; later it often represented betrothal gifts or tokens of marriage. Here, "You, Chang'e, personally promised; before the jade mirror stand we will meet clearly" uses the jade mirror stand to metaphorically mean the marriage is settled.

玉京：指道教传说中的天上京城，为神仙所居，常代指仙境或京城。此处"何用崎岖上玉京"意为相逢如入仙境，无需再求赴仙境。
Jade Capital: Refers to the heavenly capital in Daoist legend, where immortals dwell, often representing an immortal realm or the capital city. Here, "Why need I arduously ascend to the Jade Capital?" means meeting is like entering an immortal realm, no need to seek the immortal realm further.

云英：源自唐代裴铏《传奇·裴航》中仙女云英，与裴航在蓝桥相逢结为夫妻，后常代指美女或意中人。此处"知他是云英许琼"以云英喻指小玉姐，期待她应允情意。
Yunying: Originates from the immortal maiden Yunying in Pei Xing's (Tang Dynasty) Chuanqi, "Pei Hang", who met Pei Hang at the Blue Bridge and married him; later often represented a beautiful woman or one's beloved. Here, "Knowing she is Yunying promising Qiong" uses Yunying to metaphorically refer to Sister Xiaoyu, hoping she will consent to the affection.

瑶池：神话中西王母所居的仙境，常有蟠桃宴等传说，常代指仙境或美好的聚会场所。此处"肯向瑶池月下行"形容小玉姐如瑶池仙女般在月下行走。
Jade Pool: The immortal realm where the Queen Mother of the West resides in mythology, often associated with legends like the Peach Banquet; often represents an immortal realm or a beautiful gathering place. Here, "Willing to walk beneath the moon towards the Jade Pool" describes Sister Xiaoyu walking under the moonlight like an immortal maiden of the Jade Pool.

灯花：古代认为灯花爆落是吉兆，常预示喜事或远人归来。此处"昨夜灯花两人照证明"指灯花为两人的缘分作证，是吉祥之兆。
Lantern flower: In ancient times, the sputtering of a lantern wick was considered an auspicious omen, often foretelling happy events or the return of a distant person. Here, "Last night the lantern flower witnessed for both of us" means the lantern flower testifies to the fate of the two, an auspicious sign.

薄妆凝态，试暖弄寒天色："试暖弄寒"描绘初春天气冷暖不定的状态，常用来烘托人物细腻的心境。此处刻画旦在阴晴不定的天色中，带着淡妆凝视的情态。
Light makeup,frozen posture, testing warmth, playing with the cold sky. "Testing warmth, playing with cold" describes the changeable warm and cold weather of early spring, often used to set off a character's delicate state of mind. Here it depicts the female lead in changeable weather, with light makeup, in a gazing posture.

残灯澹月："残灯"指将灭的灯火，"澹月"指朦胧的月光，常组合用于营造清幽或孤寂的氛围。此处"是谁向残灯澹月，仔细端详无奈"以残灯淡月烘托旦对拾钗人的思念与无奈。
Faint lamp, pale moon: "Faint lamp" refers to a dying lamp flame; "pale moon" refers to hazy moonlight; often combined to create a quiet or lonely atmosphere. Here, "Who is it, towards the faint lamp and pale moon, carefully scrutinizing helplessly?" uses the faint lamp and pale moon to set off the female role's longing and helplessness towards the person who picked up the hairpin.

坠钗飞燕："飞燕"指形状如燕的玉钗，"坠钗"即掉落的玉钗，常关联男女相逢的情事。此处"凭坠钗飞燕徘徊"指旦对着掉落的燕钗思绪徘徊，牵挂拾钗之人。
Fallen hairpin, flying swallow: "Flying swallow" refers to the swallow-shaped jade hairpin; "fallen hairpin" is the dropped hairpin, often associated with romantic meetings. Here, "Leaning on the fallen hairpin, the flying swallow lingers" means the female role's thoughts linger over the fallen swallow hairpin, concerned about the person who picked it up.

中酒心情："中酒"指饮酒过量或因酒而感不适，"中酒心情"常用来形容因离愁或慵懒而产生的倦怠情绪。此处"似中酒心情，羞花意绪"形容旦因思念而如饮酒微醺般的慵懒与娇羞。
Sick-with-wine mood: "Sick with wine" means feeling unwell due to excessive drinking or alcohol; "sick-with-wine mood" often describes a weary emotion caused by parting sorrow or laziness. Here, "Like a sick-with-wine mood, shy-flower feelings" describes the female role's laziness and shyness due to longing, as if slightly intoxicated.

灯轮细转，月影平分："灯轮"指元宵节的灯轮，"月影平分"指月光均匀洒落，描绘元宵夜灯月交辉的景象。此处"灯轮细转，月影平分"再现元宵夜与书生相逢时的场景。
Lantern wheels turn finely, moonlight shadows divide equally. "Lantern wheels" refer to the lantern wheels of the Lantern Festival; "moonlight shadows divide equally" means the moonlight falls evenly, depicting the scene of lanterns and moonlight intermingling on the Lantern Festival night. Here, "Lantern wheels turn finely, moonlight shadows divide equally" recreates the scene of meeting the scholar on the Lantern Festival night.

纱笼：指蒙着纱的灯笼，古代女子出行常持纱笼，常作为女子的象征意象。此处"曾半倚纱笼，手捻坠钗闲借问"回忆元宵夜倚着纱笼、借问钗事的情景。
Gauze lantern: Refers to a lantern covered with gauze; ancient women often carried them when going out, often serving as a symbolic image of women. Here, "Once half-leaning on the gauze lantern, hand twirling the fallen hairpin, idly inquiring" recalls the scene on the Lantern Festival night of leaning on the gauze lantern and inquiring about the hairpin.

春从绣户排，月向梅花白：化用传统诗词中"绣户""梅花""月色"的意象，"绣户"代指闺房，"月向梅花白"描绘月光洒在梅花上的洁白景象。此处勾勒春日闺中月夜的景致，烘托情思。
Spring enters through the embroidered door, the moon shines white on the plum blossoms. Uses the imagery of "embroidered door" (boudoir), "plum blossoms", and "moonlight" from traditional poetry; "embroidered door" represents the boudoir; "the moon shines white on the plum blossoms" depicts the white scene of moonlight on plum blossoms. Here it outlines the scene of a spring night in the boudoir, setting off emotional thoughts.

花随玉漏催，人赴金钗会："玉漏"指古代计时的漏壶，"金钗会"代指因钗结缘的相逢。此处"花随玉漏催，人赴金钗会"意为时光流逝，因玉钗促成了相逢之会。
Flowers follow the jade water clock's urging, people go to the golden hairpin meeting. "Jade water clock" refers to the ancient clepsydra for timekeeping; "golden hairpin meeting" represents the meeting facilitated by the hairpin. Here, "Flowers follow the jade water clock's urging, people go to the golden hairpin meeting" means time passes, and the jade hairpin causes the meeting to happen.

疎影横斜：源自宋代林逋《山园小梅》"疏影横斜水清浅，暗香浮动月黄昏"，原句描绘梅花稀疏的影子横斜在水中的姿态。此处"为着疎影横斜，把咱燕钗儿黏带"借用梅花疏影的意象，说明钗因梅枝而掉落。
Sparse shadows slanting: Originates from Lin Bu's (Song Dynasty) "Small Plum Blossoms in the Mountain Garden": "Sparse shadows slant across clear shallow water; hidden fragrance floats in the moonlit dusk." The original line depicts the posture of sparse plum blossom shadows slanting on water. Here, "Because of the sparse shadows slanting, my swallow hairpin got caught" borrows the imagery of sparse plum shadows to explain that the hairpin fell because of the plum branch.

踏靑挑菜："踏靑"指春日郊游，"挑菜"为古代立春习俗，采摘野菜以迎新春，均为春日活动。此处"准望着踏靑挑菜"指鲍四娘本盼着春日郊游，却为婚事而来。
Treading the green, picking vegetables: "Treading the green" means spring outing; "picking vegetables" was an ancient custom at the beginning of spring, picking wild vegetables to welcome spring; both are spring activities. Here, "Exactly expecting to tread the green and pick vegetables" means Aunt Bao the Fourth was originally looking forward to a spring outing but came for the marriage matter.

鹦哥报客来：古代常有养鹦哥报客的习俗，鹦哥成为传递来客讯息的象征。此处"鹦哥报客来"通过鹦哥叫声引出鲍四娘到访。
The parrot announces a guest's arrival: In ancient times, there was often the custom of keeping parrots to announce guests; parrots became symbols of conveying news of visitors. Here, "The parrot announces a guest's arrival" uses the parrot's call to introduce Aunt Bao the Fourth's visit.

玉镜妆台："玉镜"指梳妆用的铜镜，"妆台"为女子梳妆之处，常关联女子情思或姻缘。此处"可似绕帘春色，还上我玉镜妆台"以玉镜妆台代指闺中，盼燕钗回归如春色重回妆台。
Jade mirror dressing table: "Jade mirror" refers to the bronze mirror for dressing; "dressing table" is where women dress, often associated with women's emotions or marriage. Here, "Can it be like spring colors winding around the blinds, returning to my jade mirror dressing table?" uses the jade mirror dressing table to represent the boudoir, hoping the swallow hairpin will return like spring colors returning to the dressing table.

玉镜台：源自晋代温峤以玉镜台为聘礼娶表妹刘倩之的典故，见《世说新语·假谲》，后常代指聘礼或姻缘信物。此处"你说着玉镜台，那酸倈怎就把咱头上钗儿来插钗"借玉镜台典故暗指婚事。
Jade mirror stand: Originates from the story of Wen Jiao using a jade mirror stand as a betrothal gift to marry his cousin Liu Qianzhi, see the Shishuo Xinyu, "False and Cunning"; later often represented betrothal gifts or tokens of marriage. Here, "You speak of the jade mirror stand; how did that sour fellow then come to insert the hairpin in my hair?" uses the jade mirror stand story to subtly refer to the marriage matter.

武陵春色：源自东晋陶渊明《桃花源记》中"武陵人捕鱼为业"发现桃花源的典故，后常代指美好的春景或理想中的境遇。此处"只怕老娘呵识不出武陵春色"以武陵春色喻指与书生的情缘。
Wuling spring colors: Originates from the story in Tao Yuanming's (Eastern Jin) "Peach Blossom Spring" where "a man of Wuling fished for a living" discovered the Peach Blossom Spring; later often represented beautiful spring scenery or an ideal situation. Here, "I only fear, old mother, you won't recognize the Wuling spring colors" uses Wuling spring colors to metaphorically refer to the romantic fate with the scholar.

鸳雏常依膝下："鸳雏"原指鸳鸯幼鸟，常比喻年幼的子女，"依膝下"指子女在父母身边。此处"似鸳雏常依膝下"形容老夫人视女儿如幼雏般疼爱，不舍其出嫁。
Mandarin duck chicks always nestle under the knee: "Mandarin duck chicks" originally referred to young mandarin ducks, often metaphorically young children; "nestle under the knee" means children are by their parents' side. Here, "Like mandarin duck chicks always nestling under the knee" describes the old lady viewing her daughter as a young chick, dearly loving her and reluctant to let her marry.

漏春心："春心"指男女情爱之心，"漏春心"指流露爱慕之情。此处"漏春心何曾得到他"指老夫人认为女儿未曾流露情爱之心。
Leaking spring heart: "Spring heart" means the heart of romantic love; "leaking spring heart" means revealing admiration. Here, "Leaking spring heart, when did it ever reach him?" means the old lady thinks her daughter has never revealed feelings of love.

乘龙娇客："乘龙"源自《太平广记》载萧史乘龙引凤的传说，后以"乘龙快婿"称称心的女婿，"娇客"也指女婿。此处"稳倩个乘龙娇客来招嫁"指老夫人盼女儿嫁得如意女婿。
Riding-dragon pampered guest: "Riding-dragon" originates from the legend of Xiao Shi riding a dragon and attracting a phoenix recorded in the Extensive Records of the Taiping Era; later "riding-dragon son-in-law" meant an ideal son-in-law; "pampered guest" also refers to a son-in-law. Here, "Securely asking for a riding-dragon pampered guest to come and marry" means the old lady hopes her daughter will marry an ideal son-in-law.

起西楼备着吹箫：源自春秋时萧史善吹箫，秦穆公以女弄玉妻之，后二人吹箫引凤成龙飞升的典故，见《列仙传》，"吹箫"常代指婚嫁或夫妻和美。此处"起西楼备着吹箫"喻指为女儿婚嫁做准备。
Raising the west tower, preparing to play the flute: Originates from the story of Xiao Shi being skilled at playing the flute during the Spring and Autumn period; Duke Mu of Qin gave his daughter Nongyu to him as wife; later the two played the flute, attracted a phoenix, became dragons, and ascended to heaven, see the Biographies of Exemplary Immortals; "playing the flute" often represented marriage or marital harmony. Here, "Raising the west tower, preparing to play the flute" metaphorically means preparing for the daughter's marriage.

展东床留敎下榻："东床"源自东晋王羲之坦腹东床被选为女婿的典故，见《世说新语·雅量》，后代指女婿；"下榻"指留客住宿。此处"展东床留敎下榻"指盼女婿上门成婚。
Unfolding the east bed, asking him to stay: "East bed" originates from the story of Wang Xizhi lying uncovered on the east bed and being chosen as a son-in-law, see the Shishuo Xinyu, "Cultivated Tolerance"; later it referred to a son-in-law; "stay" means to lodge a guest. Here, "Unfolding the east bed, asking him to stay" means hoping the son-in-law will come to the house to marry.

李十郞陇西旧家：李益为唐代诗人，字君虞，陇西姑臧（今甘肃武威）人，此处点明其籍贯家世，呼应历史人物背景。
The Tenth Lad Li of an old Longxi family: Li Yi was a Tang Dynasty poet, courtesy name Junyu, from Guzang, Longxi (present-day Wuwei, Gansu). Here it clarifies his native place and family background, echoing the historical figure's context.

碧梧栖老鸾停跨："碧梧"指梧桐，"鸾"为神鸟，传说鸾鸟非梧桐不栖，常以"鸾栖梧"喻指贤才得遇或佳偶相配。此处"管碧梧栖老鸾停跨"喻指李益与小玉姐如鸾鸟栖梧般相配。
Green wutong trees perch old luans stopping their stride. "Green wutong" refers to the wutong tree (Chinese parasol tree); "luan" is a divine bird; legend says luans only perch on wutong trees; often "luan perching on wutong"metaphorically means a worthy talent finding opportunity or a good match. Here, "Surely green wutong trees perch old luans stopping their stride" metaphorically means Li Yi and Sister Xiaoyu are matched like luans perching on wutong.

将雏曲毕竟双飞："将雏"指携带幼雏，"双飞"常喻指夫妻相伴，此处"将雏曲毕竟双飞"祝愿二人婚后如鸟儿双飞，儿女绕膝。
The song of leading the chicks ends with pair flying. "Leading the chicks" means carrying the young; "pair flying" often metaphorically means husband and wife accompanying each other. Here, "The song of leading the chicks ends with pair flying" wishes that after marriage, the two will fly pair like birds, with children around their knees.

求凤操看他驷马："求凤操"指《凤求凰》琴曲，源自司马相如以琴音求卓文君的典故，代指求偶；"驷马"指四匹马拉的车，代指高官厚禄。此处"求凤操看他驷马"赞李益既有才情求偶，又有前程。
Seeking the phoenix tune, watch his four-horse carriage. "Seeking the phoenix tune" refers to the qin tune "Phoenix Seeks Phoenix", originating from the story of Sima Xiangru using qin music to woo Zhuo Wenjun, representing courtship; "four-horse carriage" refers to a carriage with four horses, representing high office and wealth. Here, "Seeking the phoenix tune, watch his four-horse carriage" praises Li Yi for having both the talent to court and the prospect of advancement.

冰淸到底无别话："冰清"形容品行高洁纯净，此处"冰淸到底无别话"指旦自称心性纯净，未涉情爱。
Ice-pure to the end, no other words. "Ice-pure" describes a character pure and unsullied. Here, "Ice-pure to the end, no other words" means the female lead claims her heart is pure and has not involved itself with love.

罗敷早配玄都："罗敷"为汉乐府《陌上桑》中美女，拒斥使君追求，后代指贞洁女子；"玄都"代指佳婿。此处"看罗敷早配玄都"以罗敷喻指女子应早配佳婿。
Luofu early matched with the Mysterious Capital. "Luofu" is the beautiful woman in the Han Music Bureau poem "Mulberries by the Path" who rejected the prefect's advances; later she represented a chaste woman; "Mysterious Capital" represents an ideal husband. Here, "See Luofu early matched with the Mysterious Capital" uses Luofu to metaphorically mean a woman should marry a good husband early.

恨玉兰空孕莲花："玉兰""莲花"均为象征纯洁的花卉，"空孕"指徒然孕育，此处"恨玉兰空孕莲花"感叹女子若不成婚，如花儿徒然绽放而无果。
Resenting the magnolia vainly conceiving the lotus. "Magnolia" and "lotus" are both flowers symbolizing purity; "vainly conceiving" means bearing fruit in vain. Here, "Resenting the magnolia vainly conceiving the lotus" laments that if a woman does not marry, it is like a flower blooming vainly without fruit.

仙查："查"同"槎"，指神话中往来天河的木筏，"仙查"即星槎，源自《博物志》天河浮槎传说。此处"天宫织女犹自嫁，银河畔鹊桥亲踏"以织女乘槎渡银河与牛郎相会的典故，劝女子应如织女般成婚。
Immortal raft: "cha" is the same as "raft", referring to the mythical raft that travels on the Heavenly River; "immortal raft" is the star raft, originating from the legend of the floating raft on the Heavenly River in the Bowu Zhi. Here, "The Weaving Maid of the Heavenly Palace still married herself; by the Silver River's bank, she personally trod the Magpie Bridge" uses the story of the Weaving Maid riding the raft across the Milky Way to meet the Cowherd to persuade a woman to marry like the Weaving Maid.

柘枝儿两头系丝："柘枝"为古代舞曲名，"两头系丝"喻指两头牵挂。此处"只怕柘枝儿两头系丝"指担心老夫人若不舍女儿，会两头牵挂不安。
Zhezhir has threads tied at both ends. "Zhezhi" is the name of an ancient dance tune; "threads tied at both ends"metaphorically means being pulled in two directions. Here, "I only fear Zhezhi has threads tied at both ends" means worrying that if the old lady cannot bear to part with her daughter, she will be anxiously pulled in two directions.

靑春不多也二八："二八"指十六岁，"青春不多也二八"点明女子十六岁青春短暂，劝其珍惜时光成婚。
Youth is not much, only sixteen. "Sixteen" refers to sixteen years old; "youth is not much, only sixteen" points out that a girl's youth at sixteen is brief, urging her to cherish the time and marry.

笼窗动闼："笼窗""动闼"指门窗，代指居家生活，此处"少不得笼窗动闼"指女子终究要成家过日子。
Covering windows, moving doors: "Covering windows" and "moving doors" refer to windows and doors, representing domestic life. Here, "Cannot avoid covering windows and moving doors" means a woman will eventually have to set up a household and live.

破瓜：古代以"破瓜"指女子十六岁（"瓜"字分拆为两个"八"），也指女子成婚。此处"好和歹这些时破瓜"指女子到了成婚的年纪。
Breaking the melon: In ancient times, "breaking the melon" referred to a girl turning sixteen (the character for "melon" can be split into two "eight" characters), and also meant a woman marrying. Here, "For better or worse, around this time she breaks the melon" means the girl has reached marriageable age.

白玉无瑕，靑春有价："白玉无瑕"形容女子纯洁无瑕，"青春有价"指青春宝贵。此处强调女子青春宝贵，应及时成婚。
White jade without flaw, youth has its price. "White jade without flaw" describes a woman's purity and flawlessness; "youth has its price" means youth is precious. Here it emphasizes that a woman's youth is precious and she should marry in time.

丝鞭儿擘打："丝鞭"为古代婚礼中男方送给女方的聘礼，也指媒人提亲，"擘打"指催促。此处"把媒人似丝鞭儿擘打"指鲍四娘催促小姐应允婚事。
Silk whip cracking: "Silk whip" was a betrothal gift from the groom to the bride in ancient weddings, also referred to the matchmaker's proposal; "cracking" means urging. Here, "Treating the matchmaker like cracking a silk whip" means Aunt Bao the Fourth urging the young lady to consent to the marriage.

衬褡人家："衬褡"指匹配、相称，"衬褡人家"指门当户对的配偶。此处"尙没个衬褡人家"指鲍四娘说李益这般才俊尚未婚配。
Matching family: "Matching" means suitable, well-matched; "matching family" means a socially equal spouse. Here, "Still hasn't got a matching family" means Aunt Bao the Fourth says a talented man like Li Yi is still unmarried.

士女愁春没乱煞："愁春"指为青春或情爱烦恼，"没乱煞"指心绪纷乱。此处"士女愁春没乱煞"指青年男女为情爱之事心绪纷乱。
Scholars and ladies worry about spring, utterly confused. "Worrying about spring" means worrying about youth or love; "utterly confused" means emotionally disturbed. Here, "Scholars and ladies worry about spring, utterly confused" means young men and women are emotionally disturbed by matters of love.

母亲行白忙闲话："母亲行"指母亲那边，"白忙闲话"指白费口舌。此处"母亲行白忙闲话"指鲍四娘劝老夫人不必白费口舌，应促成婚事。
Mother's side vainly busies itself with idle talk. "Mother's side" refers to the mother's side; "vainly busying with idle talk" means wasting words. Here, "Mother's side vainly busies itself with idle talk" means Aunt Bao the Fourth advises the old lady not to waste words but should facilitate the marriage.

禁架：指承受、担当，此处"眞和假那些禁架"指无论真假都能担当，劝小姐不必犹豫。
Endure and bear: Means to withstand, bear responsibility. Here, "Truth and falsehood, all those can be endured and borne" means regardless of truth or falsehood, it can be handled, advising the young lady not to hesitate.

玉燕钗头，玉梅花下："玉燕钗"指女子的玉钗，"玉梅花"指洁白的梅花，均为情爱信物或浪漫场景的象征。此处"你不信看玉燕钗头，玉梅花下"指钗与梅可作证姻缘。
On the jade swallow hairpin's head, beneath the jade plum blossoms. "Jade swallow hairpin" refers to the woman's jade hairpin; "jade plum blossoms" refers to pure white plum blossoms; both are symbols of love tokens or romantic scenes. Here, "If you don't believe it, look at the jade swallow hairpin's head, beneath the jade plum blossoms" means the hairpin and plum blossoms can testify to the marriage fate.

元宵夜放了观灯假："观灯假"指元宵节的假期，古代元宵节有赏灯习俗，常为男女相逢提供机会。此处"元宵夜放了观灯假"点明钗掉落的时间背景。
On the Lantern Festival night, the lantern-viewing holiday was given. "Lantern-viewing holiday" refers to the holiday for the Lantern Festival; ancient Lantern Festival had the custom of viewing lanterns, often providing opportunities for men and women to meet. Here, "On the Lantern Festival night, the lantern-viewing holiday was given" clarifies the time background of the hairpin falling.

翠袖笼拿："翠袖"代指女子的衣袖，"笼拿"指用手握住。此处"急寻着被他翠袖笼拿"指书生用衣袖接住掉落的玉钗。
Green sleeves cage and grasp: "Green sleeves" represent a woman's sleeves; "cage and grasp" means to grasp with the hand. Here, "Hastily searching, it was cage by his green sleeves" means the scholar used his sleeve to catch the falling jade hairpin.

禁不得他赚玉留香多霎："赚玉留香"指获取玉钗、留住香气，代指男子对女子的爱慕之举。此处"是禁不得他赚玉留香多霎"指书生难掩对小姐的爱慕之情。
Could not withstand his gaining the jade and retaining the fragrance for a moment. "Gaining the jade and retaining the fragrance" means obtaining the jade hairpin and retaining its fragrance, representing the man's admiration for the woman. Here, "It was that I could not withstand his gaining the jade and retaining the fragrance for a moment" means the scholar could not conceal his admiration for the young lady.

笼灯倚月："笼灯"指持灯笼，"倚月"指倚立月下，描绘浪漫的月夜场景。此处"亏了俺笼灯倚月，听才子佳人打话"回忆元宵夜月下听二人对话的情景。
Holding a lantern, leaning against the moon. "Holding a lantern" means carrying a lantern; "leaning against the moon" means leaning under the moonlight, depicting a romantic moonlit scene. Here, "Thanks to me holding a lantern, leaning against the moon, listening to the talented scholar and beautiful lady converse" recalls the scene of listening to their conversation under the moonlight on the Lantern Festival night.

淡月隐梅花：化用"月"与"梅花"的经典意象，描绘月光朦胧、梅花隐约的清幽景象。此处"俺小姐淡月隐梅花"形容小姐如淡月下的梅花般娇羞含蓄。
Pale moon hides the plum blossoms. Uses the classic imagery of "moon" and "plum blossoms" to depict a quiet scene of hazy moonlight and faint plum blossoms. Here, "My young lady is like the pale moon hiding plum blossoms" describes the young lady as shy and reserved like plum blossoms under a pale moon.

娇波抹："娇波"指女子娇媚的眼神，"抹"指流转。此处"娇波抹，道有心期那些"指小姐以眼神传递心意。
Charming glance wiped: "Charming glance" refers to a woman's charming glance; "wiped" means to flicker. Here, "Charming glance wiped, she spoke of those heart-felt expectations" means the young lady conveyed her intentions with her eyes.

百岁姻缘非笑耍："百岁姻缘"指终身的婚姻，此处"百岁姻缘非笑耍"指老夫人强调婚姻关乎终身，不可儿戏。
A hundred-year marriage is no laughing matter. "Hundred-year marriage" means a lifelong marriage. Here, "A hundred-year marriage is no laughing matter" means the old lady emphasizes that marriage concerns a lifetime and should not be treated lightly.

燕尔翻飞碧海涯："燕尔"指新婚欢乐，"翻飞碧海涯"指远走高飞。此处"怕燕尔翻飞碧海涯"指老夫人担心女儿婚后随女婿远走他乡。
Newlywed joy fluttering to the blue sea's edge. "Newlywed joy" refers to the happiness of newlyweds; "fluttering to the blue sea's edge" means flying far away. Here, "Fearing newlywed joy fluttering to the blue sea's edge" means the old lady worries that after marriage, her daughter will follow her son-in-law far away to another land.

翠气生香春一把：形容女子如春日花草般散发香气与生机。此处"翠气生香春一把"赞小玉姐青春美好。
Jade aura generates fragrance, a handful of spring. Describes a woman emitting fragrance and vitality like spring plants. Here, "Jade aura generates fragrance, a handful of spring" praises Sister Xiaoyu's beautiful youth.

将相根芽：指有成为将相的根基与潜质，此处"那书生也将相根芽"赞李益有前程。
Root and sprout of a general or minister: Means having the foundation and potential to become a general or minister. Here, "That scholar also has the root and sprout of a general or minister" praises Li Yi's prospects.

嵌成宝玉双飞燕：指成对的玉燕钗，象征夫妻成双成对。此处"接了你嵌成宝玉双飞燕"指若成婚，玉钗可成对，象征美满姻缘。
Inlaid to form precious jade pair flying swallows: Refers to the paired jade swallow hairpins, symbolizing husband and wife as a pair. Here, "If I receive you, inlaid to form precious jade pair flying swallows" means if they marry, the jade hairpins can be paired, symbolizing a happy marriage.

飞入寻常百姓家：源自唐代刘禹锡《乌衣巷》"旧时王谢堂前燕，飞入寻常百姓家"，原句感叹世事变迁。此处反用其意，"难道是飞入寻常百姓家"强调李益并非普通百姓，而是良配。
Fly into an ordinary commoner's household. Originates from Liu Yuxi's (Tang Dynasty) "Black Clothes Lane": "Swallows that before the halls of Wang and Xie used to nest, now fly into the homes of common people." The original line laments the changes of the world. Here it is used inversely, "Could it be they fly into an ordinary commoner's household?" emphasizes that Li Yi is not an ordinary commoner but a good match.
