武陵溪蘸出胡麻：源自东晋陶渊明《桃花源记》中武陵人误入桃花源，及汉代刘晨、阮肇入天台山遇仙女食胡麻饭的典故，代指美好姻缘或奇遇。此处"武陵溪蘸出胡麻"喻指此次相逢如武陵遇仙般美好。
The Wuling stream dipped out sesame. Originates from the story in Tao Yuanming's (Eastern Jin) "Peach Blossom Spring" where a man of Wuling mistakenly entered the Peach Blossom Spring, and the Han Dynasty story of Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao entering Tiantai Mountain, meeting immortal maidens and eating sesame meal; represents a wonderful marriage or encounter. Here, "The Wuling stream dipped out sesame" metaphorically means this meeting is as wonderful as meeting immortals in Wuling.

乘龙一骑靑丝马："乘龙"指乘龙快婿，"靑丝马"指俊美的青鬃马，代指佳婿。此处"可有乘龙一骑靑丝马"指盼有如意女婿到来。
Riding a dragon, one rider on a black-maned horse. "Riding a dragon" means the ideal son-in-law (who rides a dragon); "black-maned horse" refers to a handsome horse with a black mane, representing an ideal son-in-law. Here, "Could there be a riding-dragon rider on a black-maned horse?" means hoping for an ideal son-in-law to arrive.

插燕双飞绿鬓鸦："插燕"指插玉燕钗，"绿鬓鸦"形容女子乌黑的鬓发，此处"配上咱插燕双飞绿鬓鸦"指玉钗成对插在女子鬓发上，象征婚姻美满。
Inserting swallows pair flying on raven black hair. "Inserting swallows" means inserting the jade swallow hairpins; "raven black hair" describes a woman's jet-black hair at the temples. Here, "Matching our inserted swallows pair flying on raven black hair" means the jade hairpins are paired and inserted in the woman's hair, symbolizing a happy marriage.

画堂箫鼓安排下："画堂"指华丽的厅堂，"箫鼓"指婚礼中的乐器演奏，此处"俺这裏画堂箫鼓安排下"指老夫人准备好婚礼事宜。
Painted hall, flute and drum, all arranged. "Painted hall" refers to a magnificent hall; "flute and drum" refers to the musical performance at a wedding. Here, "Here in our painted hall, flute and drum are all arranged" means the old lady has prepared the wedding arrangements.

白璧成双锦上花："白璧成双"指成对的白玉，常作为贵重聘礼，"锦上花"比喻美上加美。此处"他还有白璧成双锦上花"指李益将以贵重聘礼促成婚事。
Paired white jades, flowers on brocade. "Paired white jades" refers to a pair of white jades, often used as valuable betrothal gifts; "flowers on brocade"metaphorically means beauty added to beauty. Here, "He also has paired white jades, flowers on brocade" means Li Yi will use valuable betrothal gifts to facilitate the marriage.

月笼灯影袖笼钗：描绘月光笼罩灯影、衣袖笼着玉钗的情景，再现元宵夜相逢的浪漫场景。此处作为结尾诗句，呼应前文钗与月的意象。
Moon envelops lantern shadows, sleeve envelops hairpin. Depicts the scene of moonlight enveloping lantern shadows and a sleeve enveloping the jade hairpin, recreating the romantic scene of the meeting on the Lantern Festival night. Here it serves as a concluding couplet, echoing the earlier imagery of the hairpin and the moon.

飞向温家玉镜台："温家玉镜台"源自晋代温峤以玉镜台为聘礼的典故，此处"飞向温家玉镜台"指玉钗将如聘礼般促成婚事，呼应姻缘主题。
Flying towards the Wen family's jade mirror stand. "Wen family's jade mirror stand" originates from the story of Wen Jiao using a jade mirror stand as a betrothal gift. Here, "Flying towards the Wen family's jade mirror stand" means the jade hairpin will facilitate the marriage like a betrothal gift, echoing the theme of marriage fate.

好是观灯透玉京："玉京"指道教传说中的天上京城，为神仙所居，常代指仙境或京城。此处"好是观灯透玉京"形容元宵观灯的景象如仙境般璀璨。
How fine to view lanterns penetrating the Jade Capital. "Jade Capital" refers to the heavenly capital in Daoist legend, where immortals dwell, often representing an immortal realm or the capital city. Here, "How fine to view lanterns penetrating the Jade Capital" describes the Lantern Festival viewing scene as dazzling as an immortal realm.

如魂如梦见飞琼："飞琼"指神话中的仙女许飞琼，为西王母侍女，后常代指美女。此处"如魂如梦见飞琼"指见到小玉姐如梦中遇见仙女般美好。
Like a soul, like a dream, seeing Flying Qiong. "Flying Qiong" refers to the mythical immortal maiden Xu Feiqiong, an attendant of the Queen Mother of the West, later often representing a beautiful woman. Here, "Like a soul, like a dream, seeing Flying Qiong" means seeing Sister Xiaoyu is as wonderful as meeting an immortal maiden in a dream.

留连步障笙歌隐：描绘元宵夜步障遮护、笙歌隐约的热闹景象。
Lingering,screens conceal flute songs. Depicts the lively scene on the Lantern Festival night with screens providing shelter and the faint sound of flute songs.

彷佛遗钗笑语明：回忆元宵夜拾钗时的欢声笑语。
As if the lost hairpin's laughter and talk were clear. Recalls the clear sound of laughter and talk when picking up the hairpin on the Lantern Festival night.

几时眞个作行云：源自战国宋玉《高唐赋》中"旦为朝云，暮为行雨"的典故，"行云"代指美女或男女情爱。此处"几时眞个作行云"指盼望与小玉姐成就情爱之事。
When will we truly become moving clouds? Originates from the story in Song Yu's (Warring States period) "Rhapsody on the Gaotang Shrine": "At dawn I am the morning clouds, at dusk I am the passing rain." "Moving clouds" represents a beautiful woman or sexual love. Here, "When will we truly become moving clouds?" means hoping to consummate the relationship with Sister Xiaoyu.

盼杀行媒月下人："行媒"指媒人，"月下人"源自"月下老人"的传说，指掌管姻缘的神仙。此处"盼杀行媒月下人"指急切盼望媒人促成姻缘。
Longing to death for the traveling matchmaker, the man under the moon. "Traveling matchmaker" refers to the matchmaker; "man under the moon" originates from the legend of the "Old Man under the Moon", the deity who controls marriage fates. Here, "Longing to death for the traveling matchmaker, the man under the moon" means eagerly hoping the matchmaker will facilitate the marriage.

恰好怕老夫人古撇也："古撇"指性情古板、固执。此处"恰好怕老夫人古撇也"指担心老夫人性情古板，不允婚事。
Just exactly afraid the old lady is stubborn. "Stubborn" means rigid and obstinate in temperament. Here, "Just right afraid the old lady is stubborn" means worrying that the old lady is rigid and will not consent to the marriage.

漏点儿丁东长叹彻："漏点"指漏壶滴漏的声音，常用来表现时间流逝和人物愁绪。此处"漏点儿丁东长叹彻"以漏声衬托长叹，表现思念之切。
The water clock's drops ding-dong, long sighs penetrate. "Water clock's drops" refers to the sound of the clepsydra dripping, often used to show the passage of time and a character's sorrow. Here, "The water clock's drops ding-dong, long sighs penetrate" uses the sound of the water clock to set off the long sighs, showing the intensity of longing.

似悔坠钗轻去瑶阙："瑶阙"指神话中的仙宫，常代指月宫或仙境。此处"似悔坠钗轻去瑶阙"将小玉姐比作从仙宫轻离的仙女，似因坠钗而略带悔意。
As if regretting the fallen hairpin lightly leaving the jade palace. "Jade palace" refers to the mythical immortal palace, often representing the moon palace or an immortal realm. Here, "As if regretting the fallen hairpin lightly leaving the jade palace" compares Sister Xiaoyu to an immortal maiden lightly leaving the immortal palace, seemingly with slight regret because of the fallen hairpin.

自共素娥说：将心事向月亮倾诉。
Personally told the White Lady. Confided her thoughts to the moon (the White Lady, Chang'e).

恍月下闻莺归去也：回忆如月下闻莺般美好的相逢与离别。
Dimly, under the moon, hearing an oriole return home. Recalls the beautiful meeting and parting like hearing an oriole under the moonlight.

天淡晓风明灭：源自宋代柳永《雨霖铃》"杨柳岸，晓风残月"的意境，描绘黎明时分天色朦胧、晓风轻拂的景象。此处"天淡晓风明灭"烘托离别后的怅惘。
Sky pale, dawn wind bright and extinguished. Originates from the conception and mood of Liu Yong's (Song Dynasty) lyric to the tune "Yu Lin Ling": "Willow bank, dawn wind, waning moon." Depicts the scene at dawn of a hazy sky and a light dawn wind. Here, "Sky pale, dawn wind bright and extinguished" sets off the melancholy after parting.

"惺惺"指聪慧、相知的人，"难遇惺惺"指难以遇到心意相通之人。此处"也应他难遇惺惺"指想必小玉姐也因遇到知己而珍惜。
Surely he also finds it hard to meet an understanding soul. "Understanding soul" means an intelligent, kindred spirit; "hard to meet an understanding soul" means difficult to meet someone who understands one's heart. Here, "Surely he also finds it hard to meet an understanding soul" means presumably Sister Xiaoyu also cherishes meeting a kindred spirit.
武陵源：源自东晋陶渊明《桃花源记》中的桃花源，代指理想中的美好境地或情缘所在。此处“比武陵源较直截”指与小玉姐的情缘比桃花源更直接可及。
E: Wulingyuan: derived from the peach blossom source in Tao Yuanming's "Records of the Peach Blossom Spring" of the Eastern Jin Dynasty, it refers to an ideal place or a place where love is located. Here, "more direct than Wulingyuan" means that the love between Xiao Yu and her sister is more direct and accessible than the peach blossom source.

C:
书五车：源自"学富五车"，形容学识渊博。此处"但凭咱书五车"指生以学识自信，不愁无佳人相伴。
Cartloads of Books: Originates from "learned enough to fill five cartloads of books," describing extensive knowledge and learning. Here, "relying solely on my cartloads of books" means the young scholar is confident in his knowledge and does not worry about lacking beautiful companions.

红一捻：指女子纤细的腰肢或娇美的身影，代指美女。此处"甚处少红一捻"指哪里缺少美女，却唯独倾心小玉姐。
A Pinch of Red: Refers to a woman's slender waist or delicate figure, representing a beauty. Here, "where is lacking a pinch of red" means where are beautiful women lacking, yet his heart is set solely on Miss Xiaoyu.

钗头枝叶，和媒人根节："钗头枝叶"指玉钗的装饰，代指情缘的信物；"媒人根节"指媒人促成婚事的关键。此处指玉钗与媒人是姻缘的关键。
The Hairpin's Foliage and the Matchmaker's Crux: "The hairpin's foliage" refers to the adornments on the jade hairpin, representing a token of affection; "the matchmaker's crux" refers to the key element where the matchmaker facilitates the marriage. Here, it means the jade hairpin and the matchmaker are crucial for the marriage alliance.

锦春梭撺定莺儿舌："锦春梭"比喻美好的言辞，"莺儿舌"指媒人的巧舌。此处"锦春梭撺定莺儿舌"指希望媒人用美好言辞促成婚事。
The Brocade Spring Shuttle Urges the Oriole's Tongue: "Brocade spring shuttle" metaphorically means fine words; "oriole's tongue" refers to the matchmaker's eloquent speech. Here, it expresses the hope that the matchmaker will use fine words to successfully arrange the marriage.

望眼夭斜："夭斜"指眼神流转、含情脉脉，"望眼夭斜"形容急切盼望的神情。此处描绘生盼望媒人回音的急切眼神。
Longing Eyes Askance: "Askance" describes a sidelong, amorous glance; "longing eyes askance" depicts an expression of eager anticipation. Here, it portrays the young scholar's anxious look as he awaits the matchmaker's reply.

幽怀喑咽："幽怀"指深藏的心事，"喑咽"指低声哽咽，形容心事难抒的愁苦。此处表现生因等待而心事郁结。
Secret Sorrows, Choked Sobs: "Secret sorrows" means deeply hidden worries; "choked sobs" means low, stifled weeping, describing the anguish of pent-up feelings. Here, it shows the young scholar's distress and bottled-up emotions due to the wait.

碧云天外影晴波："碧云天"源自宋代范仲淹《苏幕遮》"碧云天，黄叶地"，描绘晴空碧云的景象；"晴波"指清澈的水波倒影。此处以景起兴，烘托鲍四娘前来的氛围。
Azure Skies Beyond, Reflecting Sunlit Waves: "Azure skies" originates from Fan Zhongyan's (Song Dynasty) "Su Mu Zhe": "Azure skies above, yellow leaves below," depicting a scene of clear blue skies and clouds; "sunlit waves" refers to the reflection of clear water ripples. Here, the scenery is used to evoke a mood, setting the atmosphere for Bao Siniang's arrival.

晓鬟偷出睡云窝："晓鬟"指清晨的发髻，"睡云窝"指睡卧的闺房。此处"晓鬟偷出睡云窝"形容鲍四娘清晨从闺中赶来的情态。
Morning Hair hastily leaves the slumbering cloud-nest: "Morning hair" refers to the morning hairdo; "slumbering cloud-nest" refers to the bedchamber where one sleeps. Here, it describes Bao Siniang rushing from her chambers early in the morning.

口儿不应心儿可可："可可"指心中认可、愿意。此处"他口儿不应心儿可可"指小玉姐嘴上没应允，心中却已认可。
Mouth says no, but heart says yes: "Yes" means approval, willingness in the heart. Here, "her mouth says no, but her heart says yes" means Miss Xiaoyu hasn't verbally agreed, but inwardly she has already accepted.

题桥彩笔：源自汉代司马相如过升仙桥题字"不乘赤车驷马，不过汝下"的典故，后以"题桥"喻指立志求取功名。此处"道你个题桥彩笔蘸晴波"赞李益有才情且志向高远。
Colored Brush Inscribing the Bridge: Originates from the anecdote of Sima Xiangru (Han Dynasty) writing on the Ascending Immortal Bridge: "Unless I ride in a red carriage drawn by four horses, I will not pass beneath you." Later, "inscribing the bridge" symbolizes aspiring to achieve fame and high office. Here, "I say your colored brush, dipped in sunlit waves, inscribes the bridge" praises Li Yi for his talent and lofty ambitions.

傅粉人才艳绮罗："傅粉人"指容貌俊美的男子，如三国何晏面如傅粉；"艳绮罗"指与美女相配。此处赞李益容貌俊美，与美女相配。
Powdered Talent outshines silks and satins: "Powdered man" refers to a handsome man with a fair complexion, like He Yan of the Three Kingdoms period who had a face like powdered jade; "outshining silks and satins" means matching beautifully with a lovely woman. Here, it praises Li Yi's handsome appearance, worthy of a beauty.

旧家门第识人多：指李益出身世家，见多识广。此处"道是你旧家门第识人多"转述小玉姐对李益家世的认可。
Old distinguished family knows many people: Means Li Yi comes from an established family and is well-connected and experienced. Here, "I say it's your old distinguished family that knows many people" relays Miss Xiaoyu's approval of Li Yi's family background.

钗头玉燕天和合："钗头玉燕"指玉燕钗，"天和合"指天赐缘分相合。此处指玉钗为天赐信物，促成姻缘。
Jade Swallow on the Hairpin, Heaven's Union: "Jade swallow on the hairpin" refers to the jade swallow hairpin; "Heaven's union" means a match made by heaven. Here, it means the jade hairpin is a heaven-sent token that facilitates the marriage.

玉镜台前去画翠蛾："玉镜台"源自晋代温峤以玉镜台为聘礼的典故，"画翠蛾"指女子梳妆画眉。此处指成就婚事后，小玉姐在妆台前梳妆的美好景象。
Before the Jade Mirror Stand, painting dark moth-eyebrows: "Jade mirror stand" originates from the story of Wen Qiao (Jin Dynasty) using a jade mirror stand as betrothal gift; "painting dark moth-eyebrows" refers to a woman applying makeup and drawing her eyebrows. Here, it depicts the lovely scene of Miss Xiaoyu adorning herself before her dressing table after the marriage is settled.

睡觉睡觉娇无那："娇无那"指娇柔无比，此处描绘小玉姐睡醒后的娇柔情态。
Awake, awake, unbearably charming: "Unbearably charming" means extremely delicate and charming. Here, it describes Miss Xiaoyu's delicate and charming state upon waking.

露春纤弹去了粉红涴："春纤"指女子纤细的手指，"粉红涴"指胭脂污渍。此处"露春纤弹去了粉红涴"描绘小玉姐用手指弹去胭脂污渍的娇态。
Revealing slender fingers, flicks away the pink stain: "Slender fingers" refers to a woman's delicate fingers; "pink stain" refers to a smudge of rouge. Here, it depicts Miss Xiaoyu's charming gesture of using her fingers to flick away a rouge smudge.

芙蓉暗笑，碧云偷破："芙蓉"喻指女子面容，"碧云"喻指女子发髻，此处形容小玉姐暗自微笑，发髻微动的娇羞之态。
Hibiscus secretly smiles, azure clouds subtly part: "Hibiscus" metaphorically refers to a woman's face; "azure clouds" metaphorically refers to a woman's hair bun. Here, it describes Miss Xiaoyu's shy demeanor, secretly smiling with her hair bun slightly disheveled.

春心一点眉尖阁："春心"指爱慕之情，"阁"指搁置、凝聚。此处"春心一点眉尖阁"指小玉姐的爱慕之情凝聚在眉梢。
A touch of spring heart rests on the brows' tip: "Spring heart" means feelings of love; "rests" means placed, concentrated. Here, it means Miss Xiaoyu's affection is concentrated in her brows.

阿那：指柔弱美丽的样子，此处"尽阿那"形容小玉姐娇柔的姿态。
Anuo: Refers to a soft, delicate, and beautiful appearance. Here, "utterly anuo" describes Miss Xiaoyu's delicate and graceful posture.

停妥停妥有定夺："停妥"指稳妥，"定夺"指决定。此处生期盼婚事稳妥有定论。
Settled, settled, have a decision: "Settled" means properly arranged; "decision" means a final resolution. Here, the young scholar hopes the marriage matter will be securely settled and decided.

伤春中酒，轻寒自觉："伤春"指因春光而伤感，"中酒"指饮酒不适，此处形容因思念而如伤春中酒般慵懒畏寒。
Heartache of spring, wine-sickness, feeling a slight chill: "Heartache of spring" means melancholy induced by spring scenery; "wine-sickness" means feeling unwell from drinking. Here, it describes feeling languid and sensitive to cold due to longing, akin to spring melancholy or a hangover.

花星捱的孤鸾过："花星"指象征姻缘的星宿，"孤鸾"指独居的人，此处指姻缘星宿终将让独居的自己摆脱孤寂。
The Flower Star endures until the lone simurgh passes: "Flower Star" refers to the star symbolizing marriage destiny; "lone simurgh" refers to a solitary person. Here, it means the matrimonial star will eventually allow the solitary self to escape loneliness.

三日后，五更过，十红拖地送媒婆："十红拖地"指喜庆的红色衣物拖地，代指婚礼相关的喜庆场景，此处生期盼三日后五更天，媒人带来成婚的喜讯。
Three days later, past the fifth watch, ten reds trailing the ground escort the matchmaker: "Ten reds trailing the ground" refers to festive red garments dragging on the ground, representing the celebratory scenes associated with the wedding. Here, the young scholar anticipates that three days later, before dawn, the matchmaker will bring the happy news of the marriage.

一品人才：指才华出众、品行端正的人。此处"论你一品人才眞不弱"赞李益才华出众。
First-rank talent: Refers to a person of outstanding talent and upright character. Here, "judging you, a first-rank talent, truly not weak" praises Li Yi for his exceptional talent.

令阁：指对方的妻子，此处代指小玉姐。"趁风光俊煞你个令阁"指小玉姐趁此春光更显俊美。
Your esteemed lady: Refers to the other party's wife, here representing Miss Xiaoyu. "Taking advantage of the scenery, she beautifies your esteemed lady" means Miss Xiaoyu appears even more beautiful in this spring light.

拭雨黏云半帖罗："拭雨黏云"形容情意缠绵，"半帖罗"指丝罗衣物。此处指还需准备丝罗衣物等聘礼，以表缠绵情意。
Wiping rain, clinging clouds, half a bolt of gauze: "Wiping rain, clinging clouds" describes lingering affection; "half a bolt of gauze" refers to silk gauze garments. Here, it means silk gauze garments and other betrothal gifts still need to be prepared to express the deep affection.

月姊钗头玉："月姊"指月亮，"钗头玉"指玉钗。此处以月与钗呼应前文情缘意象，指玉钗如月光般美好。
Elder Sister Moon's hairpin-head jade: "Elder Sister Moon" refers to the moon; "hairpin-head jade" refers to the jade hairpin. Here, the moon and the hairpin echo the earlier imagery of romantic destiny, meaning the jade hairpin is as beautiful as moonlight.

冰人线脚针："冰人"指媒人，源自《晋书》中令狐策梦冰人断冰为婚的典故，"线脚针"指缝纫的针线，喻指媒人连接姻缘如针线缝合。此处指媒人如针线般促成姻缘。
Matchmaker's thread-end needle: "Matchmaker" (ice person) originates from the anecdote in "Book of Jin" where Linghu Ce dreamed of an ice person breaking ice for a marriage; "thread-end needle" refers to sewing needle and thread, metaphorically meaning the matchmaker connects the marriage like stitching. Here, it means the matchmaker facilitates the union like needle and thread.

传来乌鹊喜："乌鹊"源自七夕喜鹊搭桥的传说，代指喜讯。此处"传来乌鹊喜"指传来姻缘的喜讯。
The magpies' joy is reported: "Magpies" originates from the legend of magpies forming a bridge on the Qixi Festival, representing good news. Here, it means the joyful news of the marriage match is reported.

占得凤凰音："凤凰"象征吉祥和谐，"凤凰音"指吉祥的音讯。此处"占得凤凰音"指占卜得到吉祥的姻缘音讯。
Divined the phoenix's note: "Phoenix" symbolizes auspiciousness and harmony; "phoenix's note" means auspicious news. Here, it means divination has yielded auspicious news regarding the marriage.

人物似相如："相如"指汉代司马相如，以才学和风流著称。此处"人物似相如"指生自比司马相如，有才华风度却缺车马排场。
A figure like Xiangru: "Xiangru" refers to Sima Xiangru of the Han Dynasty, renowned for his literary talent and romantic flair. Here, "a figure like Xiangru" means the young scholar compares himself to Sima Xiangru, having talent and demeanour but lacking the carriages and horses (i.e., wealth and trappings).

画堂车骑："画堂"指华丽厅堂，"车骑"指车马随从，代指富贵排场。此处"少个画堂车骑"指生自叹缺少匹配豪门的车马排场。
Painted hall, carriages and horsemen: "Painted hall" means ornate hall; "carriages and horsemen" means chariots, horses, and attendants, representing wealth and display. Here, "lacking a painted hall, carriages and horsemen" means the young scholar laments his lack of the vehicular display needed to match a powerful family.

终南韦曲，博陵崔氏："终南韦曲"指唐代韦氏家族聚居地（在终南山下），"博陵崔氏"为古代著名士族，均代指名门望族。此处韦崔二人自报家世，显其出身不凡。
Zhongnan Weiqu, Boling Cui Clan: "Zhongnan Weiqu" refers to the area where the Wei family resided (south of Zhongnan Mountain) in the Tang Dynasty; "Boling Cui Clan" was a famous aristocratic family in ancient times; both represent prestigious lineages. Here, Wei and Cui announce their family backgrounds, displaying their distinguished origins.

乘龙快壻：源自《太平广记》载萧史乘龙引凤的传说，后以"乘龙快婿"称称心的女婿。此处"待做这乘龙快壻"指生盼成为配得上豪门的女婿。
Riding-dragon son-in-law: Originates from the legend in "Extensive Records of the Taiping Era" of Xiao Shi riding a dragon and attracting a phoenix; later, "riding-dragon son-in-law" means an ideal, satisfactory son-in-law. Here, "waiting to become this riding-dragon son-in-law" means the young scholar hopes to become a son-in-law worthy of the powerful family.

骐骥才郞："骐骥"指骏马，喻指杰出人才，"才郞"指有才华的男子。此处"骐骥才郞"赞生有才却缺车马。
Steed-talented lad: "Steed" means a fine horse, metaphorically an outstanding talent; "talented lad" means a talented young man. Here, "steed-talented lad" praises the young scholar for his talent but notes his lack of horses and carriage.

驷马高车："驷马"指四匹马拉的车，代指高官厚禄或富贵排场。此处"少的驷马高车"指生感叹缺少彰显身份的车马。
Four-horse high carriage: "Four horses" means a carriage drawn by four horses, representing high office, emolument, or wealthy display. Here, "lacking the four-horse high carriage" means the young scholar sighs over lacking the carriage that signifies status.

巫马期以吿："巫马期"为孔子弟子，此处借用其名谐音"无马期"，戏称无马时可求助。崔氏以此调侃生缺马之事。
Wu Maqi is informed: "Wu Maqi" was a disciple of Confucius; here, his name is used phonetically for "no-horse period," jokingly suggesting he can be asked for help when lacking horses. Cui uses this to tease the young scholar about his lack of horses.

陈成子有马十乘：源自《论语·宪问》"陈成子弑简公。孔子沐浴而朝，告于哀公曰：'陈恒弑其君，请讨之。'公曰：'告夫三子。'孔子曰：'以吾从大夫之后，不敢不告也。君曰"告夫三子"者。'之三子告，不可。孔子曰：'以吾从大夫之后，不敢不告也。'"此处崔氏戏引典故，称自家有马。
Chen Chengzi had ten teams of horses: Originates from "Analects · Xian Wen": "Chen Chengzi assassinated Duke Jian. Confucius bathed and went to court, told Duke Ai: 'Chen Heng has assassinated his ruler, I request to punish him.' The Duke said: 'Tell the three nobles.' Confucius said: 'As I follow behind the senior officials, I dare not not report it. The ruler said "tell the three nobles".' He went and told the three nobles; they refused. Confucius said: 'As I follow behind the senior officials, I dare not not report it.'" Here, Cui playfully cites the story, claiming her family has horses.

鲁韦昌马：源自《百家姓》"鲁韦昌马，苗凤花方"，韦氏借此戏称自家（韦姓）与马相关，有马可借。
Lu, Wei, Chang, Ma: Originates from the "Hundred Family Surnames" list: "Lu, Wei, Chang, Ma, Miao, Feng, Hua, Fang". Wei uses this to jokingly claim her family (surname Wei) is associated with horses (Ma) and has horses to lend.

翩翩豪侠徒："豪侠徒"指豪爽侠义之人，此处指长安养马的豪家。"翩翩"形容其风度洒脱。
Elegant and chivalrous fellows: "Chivalrous fellows" means generous, righteous people; here, it refers to wealthy families in Chang'an who keep horses. "Elegant" describes their graceful and free demeanor.

坐下龙驹："龙驹"指骏马，此处"坐下龙驹"指豪家的骏马，可助生撑场面。
Mounted a dragon steed: "Dragon steed" means a fine horse. Here, "mounted a dragon steed" refers to the fine horses of the wealthy family, which can help the young scholar maintain appearances.

锦屠苏："屠苏"指酒屋或华美的屋舍，"锦屠苏"指华丽的居所，此处代指小玉姐的家门。
Brocade Tusu: "Tusu" refers to a wine shop or a splendid house; "brocade Tusu" means a magnificent residence. Here, it represents Miss Xiaoyu's family home.

步随鞭镫，手捧衣裳，背负琴书：指奴仆侍奉主人的情态，"步随鞭镫"指跟随车马，"手捧衣裳""背负琴书"指携带物品。此处生感叹缺少奴仆侍奉。
Steps follow whip and stirrups, hands hold clothing, back carries lute and books: Refers to the manner of servants attending their master; "steps follow whip and stirrups" means following the carriage and horses; "hands hold clothing," "back carries lute and books" means carrying items. Here, the young scholar laments his lack of servants to attend him.

花星有喜不为孤："花星"指象征姻缘的星宿，"有喜"指姻缘将至，"不为孤"指不再孤单。此处生盼姻缘顺遂，却憾缺奴仆。
The Flower Star has joy, not being alone: "Flower Star" refers to the star symbolizing marriage destiny; "has joy" means marriage is imminent; "not being alone" means no longer solitary. Here, the young scholar hopes for a smooth marriage but regrets lacking servants.

身宫所恨悭奴仆："身宫"指命理中代表自身的宫位，"悭"指缺少，此处指生自叹命里缺少奴仆。
The Body Palace's regret is lacking servants: "Body Palace" refers to the astrological house representing oneself in fortune-telling; "lacking" means deficient. Here, it means the young scholar sighs that his fate lacks servants.

之子于归，先要宜其家人：源自《诗经·周南·桃夭》"之子于归，宜其家人"，原指女子出嫁后使家庭和睦。此处崔氏戏引，调侃生未成婚先求奴仆。
This lady is going to her home, she should first suit her family: Originates from "Classic of Poetry · Zhou Nan · Peach Blossoms": "This lady is going to her home, she will suit her family," originally meaning a woman after marriage should harmonize with her husband's family. Here, Cui playfully quotes this, teasing the young scholar for seeking servants before even getting married.

邦君之妻曰夫人，夫人自称曰小童：源自《礼记·曲礼》，指诸侯之妻的称谓。崔氏借此戏称若带俊童，恐新人（小玉姐）会像"小童"般吃醋。
The wife of a ruler of a state is called Furen, Furen refers to herself as Xiao Tong: Originates from "Book of Rites · Qu Li," referring to the appellation of the wife of a feudal lord. Cui uses this to jokingly say that if he brings handsome attendants, the new wife (Miss Xiaoyu) might become jealous like a "Xiao Tong" (which can mean child/servant, playing on the word).

百家姓要江童颜郭，梅盛林刁：源自《百家姓》"江童颜郭，梅盛林刁"，崔氏戏引，称可用"梅"姓木雕成童仆，调侃生缺奴仆之事。
The Hundred Surnames include Jiang, Tong, Yan, Guo, Mei, Sheng, Lin, Diao: Originates from the "Hundred Family Surnames": "Jiang, Tong, Yan, Guo, Mei, Sheng, Lin, Diao". Cui playfully quotes this, suggesting one could carve a servant from wood with the surname "Mei" (plum), teasing the young scholar about his lack of servants.

秦官冯子都："冯子都"为汉代大将军霍光的宠奴，以美貌受宠，后代指俊奴。此处"不羡秦官冯子都"指豪家奴仆不亚于冯子都，无需羡慕古人。
Qin official Feng Zidu: "Feng Zidu" was a favored servant of the Han general Huo Guang, renowned for his beauty; later refers to handsome servants. Here, "do not envy Qin official Feng Zidu" means the wealthy family's servants are no less than Feng Zidu, so there's no need to envy ancient figures.

吹箫僮约，结柳奴星："吹箫僮"指会吹箫的童仆，"结柳奴"指以柳为名的奴仆，均为古代奴仆常见意象。此处指豪家奴仆无需此类虚名，自有风采。
Flute-playing page contract, Willow-binding slave star: "Flute-playing page" refers to a young servant who plays the flute; "Willow-binding slave" refers to a servant named after willow; both are common images of servants in ancient times. Here, it means the wealthy family's servants don't need such fancy titles; they have their own style.

翦发胡雏："胡雏"指胡人少年，"翦发"指修饰发型，此处指豪家有装扮整齐的胡人奴仆。
Cropped-haired Hu youth: "Hu youth" refers to a non-Han (often Central Asian) youth; "cropped-haired" means having a trimmed hairstyle. Here, it means the wealthy family has neatly attired foreign servants.

垂鞭接马玉童扶："玉童"指俊美的童仆，此处描绘童仆扶生上马的情景，显排场。
Dropping the whip, receiving the horse, a jade lad supports: "Jade lad" refers to a handsome young servant. Here, it depicts a servant helping the young scholar mount the horse, displaying pomp.

衣箱别有平头护："平头"指平头奴，为古代奴仆的一种称谓，此处指有奴仆负责看管衣箱。
The clothing chest separately has a Pingtou guard: "Pingtou" refers to a type of servant in ancient times. Here, it means there are servants specifically responsible for guarding the clothing chest.

坦东床腹：源自东晋王羲之坦腹东床被选为女婿的典故（见《世说新语·雅量》），"坦东床"代指女婿。此处指生可安心做女婿，无需担忧排场。
Baring the east bed belly: Originates from the anecdote of Wang Xizhi (Eastern Jin) lying bare-bellied on an east bed and being chosen as son-in-law (see "A New Account of the Tales of the World · Cultivated Tolerance"); "baring the east bed" represents being a son-in-law. Here, it means the young scholar can comfortably be the son-in-law without worrying about display.

黄金屋：源自汉代刘彻"金屋藏娇"的典故，代指华丽的居所或美妻。此处"稳坐了黄金屋"祝愿生成亲后生活美满。
Golden house: Originates from the story of Liu Che (Emperor Wu of Han) "housing a beauty in a golden house," representing a magnificent residence or a beautiful wife. Here, "securely sitting in the golden house" wishes the young scholar a happy life after marriage.

屛外笼身倚："笼身"指身形被遮挡，此处"屛外笼身倚"描绘旦倚靠在屏风外的情态，显娇羞慵懒。
Outside the screen, shrouded figure leans: "Shrouded figure" means the body is partially concealed. Here, it depicts the female lead (Dan) leaning outside the screen, showing shyness and languor.

睡觉唇红退："睡觉"指睡醒，"唇红退"指唇上胭脂褪去，描绘睡醒后的自然状态。此处刻画旦睡醒后妆容稍褪的模样。
Awake, the lip red fades: "Awake" means waking from sleep; "lip red fades" means the rouge on the lips has worn off, depicting the natural state after waking. Here, it portrays the female lead's appearance upon waking, with makeup slightly faded.

晕纤蛾暗自领佳期："纤蛾"指纤细的眉毛，"晕纤蛾"指眉妆晕染，"领佳期"指知晓成婚日期。此处写旦暗自知晓佳期，眉间含情。
Blurred delicate moths secretly acknowledge the auspicious date: "Delicate moths" refers to slender eyebrows; "blurred delicate moths" means the eyebrow makeup is smudged; "acknowledge the auspicious date" means knowing the wedding date. Here, it writes that the female lead secretly knows the wedding date, with emotion showing between her brows.

珍重花前意："花前意"指花前月下的情意，此处"珍重花前意"指旦珍惜与李生的情缘。
Treasure the feeling before the flowers: "Feeling before the flowers" means the affection shared in romantic settings (lit. before flowers, under the moon). Here, it means the female lead treasures her relationship with Scholar Li.

天穿过了还穿地：形容思绪纷乱，从天上到地下萦绕不绝。此处描绘旦因佳期将近而心神不宁的状态。
Pierced through heaven, still pierces earth: Describes scattered, chaotic thoughts, swirling incessantly from heaven to earth. Here, it depicts the female lead's restless state of mind as the auspicious date approaches.

枕痕一线摇红睡："枕痕"指枕头上的压痕，"摇红"指烛光摇曳，此处描绘旦在烛光下睡醒，枕痕犹存的娇态。
Pillow mark, a single line, swaying red light sleep: "Pillow mark" means the impression left on the face by the pillow; "swaying red light" refers to the flickering candlelight. Here, it depicts the female lead waking by candlelight, the pillow mark still visible, in a charming state.

春色衬儿家："儿家"指女子自称，"春色衬儿家"指春光映衬着自己，显青春美好。此处旦以春色自喻，含娇羞之意。
Spring hues set off my home: "My home" is how a woman refers to herself. "Spring hues set off my home" means the spring scenery enhances her appearance, highlighting youthful beauty. Here, the female lead compares herself to the spring scenery, implying shyness.

羞含荳蔻花："荳蔻"指多年生草本植物，代指少女（如"豆蔻年华"），此处"羞含荳蔻花"形容旦如豆蔻花般娇羞含苞。
Shyly containing cardamom flowers: "Cardamom" refers to a perennial plant, representing a young maiden (e.g., "cardamom years"). Here, "shyly containing cardamom flowers" describes the female lead as shy and budding like a cardamom flower.

裙腰沾蟢子："蟢子"指蜘蛛，古代认为见蟢子是吉兆，象征喜信。此处"裙腰沾蟢子"以蟢子暗喻婚事将至，心生欢喜。
Skirt waist stained by a xi spider: "Xi spider" refers to a spider; anciently, seeing one was considered an auspicious omen, symbolizing happy news. Here, the xi spider metaphorically hints at the imminent marriage, causing joy.

悬愁花烛光："花烛光"指婚礼的烛光，此处"悬愁花烛光"指旦既期盼成婚又因新婚而略带不安。
Suspended worry, wedding candlelight: "Wedding candlelight" refers to the candles used in the wedding ceremony. Here, it means the female lead both anticipates the marriage and feels slightly apprehensive about the new married life.

伤春客：指为春光或情思而伤感的人，此处"他是个伤春客"指李生多愁善感，对情事执着。
Heartache-of-spring guest: Refers to a person who feels melancholy due to spring scenery or lovesickness. Here, "he is a heartache-of-spring guest" means Scholar Li is sentimental and persistent in matters of love.

脉脉此情谁识：源自宋代秦观《迢迢牵牛星》"盈盈一水间，脉脉不得语"，原指情意深厚却无法言说。此处"脉脉此情谁识"指旦与李生的情意深沉，旁人难知。
Wordlessly, who knows this feeling?: Originates from Qin Guan's (Song Dynasty) "Far, Far, the Cowherd Star": "Full, full, the one water between; wordlessly, no words spoken," originally meaning deep affection that cannot be spoken. Here, "wordlessly, who knows this feeling?" means the affection between the female lead and Scholar Li is deep, difficult for others to understand.

人散花灯夕，人盼花朝日："花灯夕"指元宵节，"花朝日"指花朝节（俗传为百花生日），此处对比元宵相逢与花朝佳期，显期盼之情。
People scatter on the Lantern Festival night, people long for the Flower Morning day: "Lantern Festival night" is the Yuanxiao Festival; "Flower Morning day" is the Huazhao Festival (traditionally the birthday of all flowers). Here, contrasting the meeting on Yuanxiao with the auspicious date on Huazhao shows anticipation.

着意东君："东君"指司春之神，此处"着意东君"指期盼春神眷顾，促成好事。
Attentive Lord of the East: "Lord of the East" is the god of spring. Here, "attentive Lord of the East" means hoping for the spring god's favor to facilitate the good event.

邂逅分明还似那回时："邂逅"指偶然相逢，"那回时"指元宵夜相逢，此处写旦梦中重逢如元宵时真切。
Our chance meeting clearly seems like that time again: "Chance meeting" means an accidental encounter; "that time" refers to the meeting on the Lantern Festival night. Here, it writes that the female lead's dream reunion feels as real as the Lantern Festival meeting.

玉钗风不定，为谁闲捻花枝："玉钗风不定"呼应前文坠钗事，"闲捻花枝"描绘娇羞情态，此处写旦梦中不知为谁捻花，暗指心系李生。
Jade hairpin, wind unsettled, for whom idly twirling a flower branch?: "Jade hairpin, wind unsettled" echoes the earlier dropped hairpin incident; "idly twirling a flower branch" depicts a shy, coquettish manner. Here, it writes that in her dream, the female lead doesn't know for whom she twirls the flower, subtly indicating her heart is set on Li.

燕子传消息："燕子"常象征信使，代指传递情信，此处"燕子传消息"指盼燕子般的信使带来佳音。
Swallows convey messages: "Swallows" often symbolize messengers, representing the delivery of love letters. Here, "swallows convey messages" means hoping for a swallow-like messenger to bring good news.

不如嫁与，受他眞个怜惜：直抒胸臆，指旦愿嫁与李生，享受他的真切怜惜。
Might as well marry him, receive his genuine care and affection: A direct expression of feeling; it means the female lead wishes to marry Scholar Li and enjoy his sincere tenderness.

绿枝么凤拍："么凤"指鹦鹉，"拍"指拍打翅膀，此处"绿枝么凤拍"描绘鹦鹉在枝头拍翅的景象，烘托春日氛围。
Green branch, parrot flaps: "Parrot" refers to a parrot; "flaps" means flapping wings. Here, "green branch, parrot flaps" depicts a parrot flapping its wings on a branch, enhancing the spring atmosphere.

香痕暗沁莓苔："香痕"指花香留下的痕迹，"莓苔"指青苔，此处写花香暗渗青苔，显庭院清幽。
Fragrant traces secretly seep into moss and lichen: "Fragrant traces" means the impression left by flower scent; "moss and lichen" refers to moss. Here, it writes that the flower scent subtly permeates the moss, showing the courtyard's serenity.

画堂春暖困金钗："画堂"指华丽厅堂，"困金钗"指女子因春困而慵懒，此处描绘旦在春暖厅堂中慵懒情态。
Painted hall, spring warmth, languid golden hairpin: "Painted hall" means ornate hall; "languid golden hairpin" means a woman feeling languid due to spring lethargy. Here, it depicts the female lead's lazy demeanor in the warm spring hall.

烛花无赖："烛花"指烛火燃烧形成的花形，古代认为烛花爆落是吉兆，"无赖"指调皮可爱。此处"烛花无赖"写洞房烛花摇曳，似通人意。
Candle flame, mischievous: "Candle flame" refers to the flower-like shape formed by a burning candle wick; anciently, a bursting candle flame was considered auspicious; "mischievous" means playful and cute. Here, "candle flame, mischievous" writes of the nuptial chamber candle flickering, as if understanding human sentiment.

背银缸暗擘瑶钗："银缸"指银灯，"瑶钗"指玉钗，"擘瑶钗"指分钗，古代有分钗为盟的习俗。此处写新婚夜暗分玉钗为盟。
Turning from the silver lamp, secretly splitting the jade hairpin: "Silver lamp" means a silver oil lamp; "jade hairpin" refers to the jade hairpin; "splitting the jade hairpin" means breaking the hairpin, an ancient custom symbolizing a pledge (often of love or separation). Here, it writes of secretly splitting the jade hairpin as a pledge on the wedding night.

待玉郞回抱相偎揣："玉郞"指对丈夫的美称，"相偎揣"指相拥依偎，描绘洞房中亲密情态。
Waiting for the jade lord to return, embrace and nestle together: "Jade lord" is a complimentary term for a husband; "nestle together" means to hug and snuggle. Here, it depicts intimate behavior in the nuptial chamber.

颦蛾掩袖低回："颦蛾"指皱眉，此处写旦娇羞皱眉、掩袖低回的情态。
Frowning moth-eyebrows, hiding sleeves, hesitating: "Frowning moth-eyebrows" means frowning; here, it writes of the female lead's shy frowning, sleeve-hiding, and hesitant manner.

春宵一刻千金浼：源自宋代苏轼《春夜》"春宵一刻值千金"，"浼"指珍贵，此处强调新婚夜的珍贵。
A spring night's moment is worth a thousand pieces of gold , precious: Originates from Su Shi's (Song Dynasty) "Spring Night": "A spring night's moment is worth a thousand gold"; "precious" means valuable. Here, it emphasizes the preciousness of the wedding night.

挽流苏罗帏颤开："流苏"指帐幔上的穗子，"罗帏"指丝帐，此处描绘拉开帐幔的情景，显洞房温馨。
Pulling the tasseled silk curtains, trembling open: "Tassels" refers to the fringes on the bed curtains; "silk curtains" means silk bed curtains. Here, it depicts drawing open the curtains, showing the warmth of the nuptial chamber.

结连环红襦懊解："连环"象征姻缘不解，"红襦"指红嫁衣，"懊解"指羞涩地解开，描绘新婚夜娇羞情态。
Fastening the interlocking rings, red jacket annoyingly untied: "Interlocking rings" symbolize the inseparable marriage bond; "red jacket" refers to the red wedding dress; "annoyingly untied" means shyly unfastening. Here, it depicts the shy actions on the wedding night.

鸾惊凤骇："鸾""凤"象征夫妻，"惊""骇"此处指娇羞不安，描绘旦在洞房中的羞涩情态。
Simurgh startled, phoenix alarmed: "Simurgh" and "phoenix" symbolize the husband and wife; "startled" and "alarmed" here refer to shy unease. Here, it depicts the female lead's shy and flustered state in the nuptial chamber.

误春纤搵着檀腮："春纤"指女子手指，"檀腮"指红润的脸颊，"搵"指轻按，此处写旦娇羞中手指轻触脸颊。
Mistakenly, slender fingers press against the sandalwood cheeks: "Slender fingers" refers to a woman's delicate fingers; "sandalwood cheeks" means rosy cheeks; "press" means gently touch. Here, it writes of the female lead's fingers lightly touching her cheeks in shyness.

护丁香怕拆新蓓蕾："丁香"喻指少女，"新蓓蕾"指未绽放的花，喻指少女纯真，此处写旦如护蓓蕾般娇羞矜持。
Protecting the clove, afraid to break the new bud: "Clove" metaphorically refers to a young maiden; "new bud" means an unopened flower, symbolizing a maiden's purity. Here, it writes that the female lead is shy and reserved, like protecting a bud.

道得个荳蔻含胎："荳蔻含胎"指豆蔻含苞，喻指少女娇羞纯真，呼应前文"羞含荳蔻花"。
It is said, the cardamom contains the embryo: "Cardamom contains the embryo" means the cardamom is in bud, metaphorically referring to a young maiden's shyness and innocence, echoing the earlier "shyly containing cardamom flowers."

他犯玉侵香怎放开："犯玉侵香"指亲近美人，此处写李生对旦的爱慕难舍。
He trespasses on jade, invades fragrance, how can he let go?: "Trespasses on jade, invades fragrance" means getting close to the beauty. Here, it writes of Scholar Li's deep admiration for the female lead, unable to part from her.

你凝云觉雨堪潇洒："凝云觉雨"形容情意缠绵，"潇洒"指自在美好，此处写旦在情爱中渐显舒展。
You condense clouds, feel rain, becoming free and easy: "Condense clouds, feel rain" describes lingering affection; "free and easy" means natural and fine. Here, it writes that the female lead gradually becomes more relaxed and expressive in love.

吃紧处花香这回："吃紧处"指关键美好时刻，"花香"喻指美好感受，此处描绘新婚夜的美好体验。
At the crucial moment, the flower's fragrance this time: "Crucial moment" means the key, beautiful moment; "flower's fragrance" metaphorically means beautiful feelings. Here, it depicts the wonderful experience of the wedding night.

断送人腰肢几摆："断送"指撩拨，"腰肢几摆"描绘娇羞扭动的姿态，显新婚娇羞情态。
Ruining person's waist, several sways: "Ruining" means to tease, tantalize; "waist, several sways" depicts a shy, twisting posture, showing the shy demeanor of the new bride.

鸳鸯衬褡儿翦裁："鸳鸯衬褡"指绣有鸳鸯的贴身衣物，象征夫妻恩爱，"翦裁"指缝制，此处指准备新婚衣物。
Mandarin duck lining and padding, cut and sewn: "Mandarin duck lining and padding" refers to undergarments embroidered with mandarin ducks, symbolizing conjugal love; "cut and sewn" means tailored. Here, it refers to preparing wedding garments.

指领上绣缄凭在："绣缄"指绣有标记的衣物，此处指衣物领上的绣记为凭，象征情意。
Pointing to the collar, the embroidered mark is there: "Embroidered mark" refers to clothing with embroidered symbols. Here, it means the embroidery on the collar serves as a token, symbolizing affection.

勾春睡小眠鞋："小眠鞋"指睡鞋，"勾春睡"指助春眠，此处指为新婚准备的睡鞋。
Hooking spring slumber, small sleeping shoes: "Small sleeping shoes" refers to bedtime shoes; "hooking spring slumber" means aiding spring sleep. Here, it refers to sleeping shoes prepared for the wedding.

要一领汗衫儿躭待："汗衫儿"指贴身内衣，"躭待"指留待，此处指准备贴身衣物待新婚使用。
Want one undershirt to wait: "Undershirt" refers to underwear; "to wait" means to keep for later use. Here, it means preparing underwear for use on the wedding night.

那其间半叶轻罗试采："半叶轻罗"指轻薄的丝罗衣物，"试采"指尝试穿着，描绘新婚试穿衣物的娇羞。
At that moment, half a leaf of light gauze tried on: "Half a leaf of light gauze" refers to lightweight silk gauze garments; "tried on" means attempting to wear. Here, it depicts the shyness of trying on wedding garments.

你把羞眸儿半开，斜灯儿半开："羞眸半开"指娇羞睁眼，"斜灯半开"指灯光斜照，营造洞房朦胧娇羞氛围。
You half-open shy eyes, the lamp half-open askance: "Half-open shy eyes" means shyly opening the eyes; "lamp half-open askance" means the lamp light shines obliquely, creating a dim, shy atmosphere in the nuptial chamber.

试显出你做夫妻们料材："料材"指资质、模样，此处指展现做夫妻的情态与资质。
Try to reveal your material as a couple: "Material" means natural endowments, manner. Here, it means displaying the demeanor and qualities of being a married couple.

带朝阳下了楚台："楚台"源自"楚王梦遇巫山神女"的典故，代指男女欢会之处，"下了楚台"指从欢会中醒来。此处写清晨从新婚温存中醒来。
With the morning sun, descended from Chu Terrace: "Chu Terrace" originates from the story "King of Chu dreams of encountering the Goddess of Wu Mountain," representing a place of romantic encounter; "descended from Chu Terrace" means waking from the romantic encounter. Here, it writes of waking from the nuptial intimacy in the morning.

起窥妆照人无奈："窥妆"指照镜梳妆，"无奈"指娇羞难掩，此处写旦清晨梳妆，娇羞模样动人。
Rising, peeking at makeup, mirror reflects person's helplessness: "Peeking at makeup" means looking in the mirror while grooming; "helplessness" means shyness is hard to conceal. Here, it writes of the female lead grooming in the morning, her shy appearance moving.

暗寻思颦眉簇黛："颦眉簇黛"指皱眉攒眉，此处写旦暗自思索，略带娇羞愁绪。
Secretly pondering, frowning brows clustering with kohl: "Frowning brows clustering with kohl" means frowning and knitting the eyebrows. Here, it writes that the female lead ponders secretly, with a slight shy melancholy.

把余红偷觑还猜："余红"指残妆，"偷觑还猜"指偷偷看镜中残妆，暗自猜想。
Stealing a glance at the remaining rouge, still guessing: "Remaining rouge" means leftover makeup; "stealing a glance, still guessing" means secretly looking at the faded makeup in the mirror and wondering.

防人见侍儿们拾在：指怕侍儿看到娇羞情态，此处写旦娇羞避人。
Afraid people will see, the maids pick it up: Means fearing the maids will see her shy state. Here, it writes that the female lead avoids people out of shyness.

贺新人美哉，贺新郞美哉：直接道贺，赞美新婚男女的美好。
Congratulations, new person, beautiful! Congratulations, new groom, beautiful!: Direct congratulations, praising the beauty of the newlyweds.

显的你做夫妻们喜来：指展现出夫妻间的喜悦之情。
It shows you, as a couple, come with joy: Means displaying the joy between husband and wife.

选成亲花朝好在："花朝"指花朝节，"好在"指适宜，此处指选定花朝节成婚正合适。
Choosing to marry on the Flower Morning festival is good: "Flower Morning" is the Huazhao Festival; "is good" means suitable. Here, it means selecting the Huazhao Festival for the wedding is appropriate.

折莫你这几日呵葫芦提较害："折莫"指不管，"葫芦提"指糊里糊涂，"较害"指不适，此处指不管这几日因娇羞而不适，终将成婚。
Never mind these days, confused and somewhat suffering: "Never mind" means regardless; "confused" means muddled; "somewhat suffering" means uncomfortable. Here, it means regardless of these days of discomfort due to shyness, they will eventually marry.

一搦女儿身："一搦"形容身材纤细，"女儿身"指少女之身，此处指旦纤细的少女身姿。
A graspable maiden's body: "Graspable" describes a slender figure; "maiden's body" refers to a young woman's body. Here, it refers to the female lead's slender maidenly figure.

齐眉作妇人："齐眉"源自"举案齐眉"的典故（梁鸿与孟光），指夫妻相敬，"作妇人"指成为已婚女子，此处指旦将成婚为妇，与丈夫相敬。
Raise the tray to the eyebrows, become a wife: "Raise the tray to the eyebrows" originates from the story of Liang Hong and Meng Guang, meaning mutual respect between husband and wife; "become a wife" means to become a married woman. Here, it means the female lead will marry and become a wife, respecting her husband.

人生初见喜：指人生中初次成婚的喜悦，此处点明新婚的喜悦之情。
Life's first meeting joy: Refers to the joy of the first marriage in life. Here, it highlights the joy of the new marriage.

花草一年春：指花草一年一春，喻指青春美好时光，此处以花草春景喻新婚美好如春光。
Flowers and grass, one year's spring: Means flowers and grass have one spring each year, metaphorically referring to the beautiful time of youth. Here, the spring scenery of flowers and grass metaphorically represents the new marriage's beauty, like spring light.

主人性爱秋鸿，身居奴仆同宫："同宫"指命宫、身宫相同，源自命理之说，意为命运相同。此处秋鸿自述身为奴仆，与主人命运相连。
The master naturally loves Qiuhong, my body resides with the servants, same palace: "Same palace" means the Life Palace and Body Palace are the same,and it comes from metaphysics, meaning shared fate. Here, Qiuhong states that as a servant, his fate is linked to his master's.

从今脱了主顾，以前布下了春风："布下春风"指先前铺垫的情意或机缘，此处秋鸿自嘲虽失主顾，却盼借主人婚事得配姻缘。
From now on, freed from the master's employment, previously laid down the spring breeze: "Laid down the spring breeze" means previously the emotional groundwork or opportunity. Here, Qiuhong self-deprecatingly says although he lost his master's employment, he hopes to find a marriage match through his master's wedding.

奴要白饭，马要青刍："青刍"指喂牲口的青草，出自《诗经·小雅·无羊》"尔牧来思，以薪以蒸，以雌以雄。尔羊来思，矜矜兢兢，不骞不崩。麾之以肱，毕来既升。牧人乃梦，众维鱼矣，旐维旟矣。大人占之：众维鱼矣，实维丰年；旐维旟矣，室家溱溱。"此处秋鸿抱怨未备饭食草料，显奴仆处境。
The servant wants white rice, the horse wants green fodder: "Green fodder" refers to green grass for feeding animals,from "Classic of Poetry · Xiao Ya · No Sheep". Here, Qiuhong complains that food and fodder are not prepared, showing the servant's situation.

白面儿郞宜俊马，洞箫才子借髯奴："洞箫才子"指汉代写《洞箫赋》的王褒，代指有才之士；"髯奴"指胡奴（因胡人多须髯）。此处胡奴自嘲为才子借去的奴仆。
Fair-faced lad suits a fine horse, flute-playing talent borrows the bearded servant: "Flute-playing talent" refers to Wang Bao (Han Dynasty) who wrote "Rhapsody on the Panpipes," representing a talented scholar; "bearded servant" refers to a non-Han servant (as non-Han people often had beards). Here, the Hu servant self-deprecatingly says he is a servant borrowed by the talented scholar.

马翦骔，人也翦骔："翦骔"指剪去马颈上的长毛，此处秋鸿调侃胡奴剪发如剪马鬃，暗讽其似马。
Horse's mane trimmed, person's also trimmed: "Mane trimmed" means cutting the long hair on a horse's neck. Here, Qiuhong teases the Hu servant that his haircut is like trimming a horse's mane, subtly mocking his resemblance to a horse.

择吉送鸾书："鸾书"指男女定亲的婚帖，因鸾象征吉祥姻缘，故称。此处指生选定吉日送去婚帖。
Choose an auspicious day to send the simurgh letter: "Simurgh letter" refers to the marriage engagement document, as the simurgh symbolizes an auspicious match. Here, it means the young scholar selects an auspicious day to send the engagement letter.

尽今夜孤眠坦腹："坦腹"源自东晋王羲之坦腹东床的典故（见《世说新语·雅量》），代指女婿。此处生言今夜是婚前最后孤眠，明日便成新郎。
Tonight, spend alone sleeping, baring the belly: "Baring the belly" originates from the story of Wang Xizhi (Eastern Jin), representing the son-in-law. Here, the young scholar says tonight is the last night of sleeping alone before marriage; tomorrow he becomes the groom.

招凤侣，配鸾雏："凤侣""鸾雏"均象征美满夫妻，此处指霍王府招婿，成就美好姻缘。
Summon a phoenix mate, match with a simurgh fledgling: "Phoenix mate" and "simurgh fledgling" both symbolize a blissful couple. Here, it refers to the Huo Prince's mansion seeking a son-in-law, achieving a fine marriage.

借鸳鸯白马光户闾："鸳鸯白马"指象征姻缘的骏马，"光户闾"指光耀门庭。此处指借骏马让婚事更显光彩。
Borrow mandarin duck white horses to glorify the household: "Mandarin duck white horses" means horses symbolizing marriage; "glorify the household" means to bring honor to the family. Here, it means borrowing fine horses to make the wedding more glorious.

闹色紫茸铺，压胯黄金镀："紫茸"指马身上的紫色绒毛，"黄金镀"指马具镀金，描绘骏马装饰华丽。
Lively color, purple velvet spread, pressing the flank, gilded with gold: "Purple velvet" refers to purple velvety hair on the horse; "gilded with gold" means the harness is gold-plated. Here, it depicts the splendid decoration of the fine horse.

飞香红玉：均为古代骏马名，此处代指借来的俊马，赞其神骏。
Flying Aroma, Red Jade: Both are names of famous ancient horses. Here, they represent the borrowed fine horses, praising their divine speed.

阿对前头："阿对"源自汉代杨震家僮名，后泛指家僮。此处指让家僮在前引路护卫。
A Dui in front: "A Dui" originates from the name of a servant of Yang Zhen (Han Dynasty), later making a general reference,household servants. Here, it means having a servant lead the way and guard in front.

要几个人儿护：指需要奴仆在旁护卫，显出行排场。
Need a few people to guard: Means needing servants to guard alongside, displaying the pomp of the procession.

须剔透，要通疏，那人家多礼数："剔透""通疏"指机灵周到，此处生叮嘱奴仆行事机灵，因霍王府礼数繁多。
Must be sharp, must be savvy, that household has many rituals: "Sharp" and "savvy" mean clever and thorough. Here, the young scholar instructs the servants to be clever and thorough because the Huo Prince's mansion has numerous formalities.

名家子，冠世儒："名家子"指出身名门，"冠世儒"指当世杰出的读书人，胡奴赞生出身与才学出众。
Son of a famous family, preeminent scholar of the age: "Son of a famous family" means from a renowned lineage; "preeminent scholar of the age" means an outstanding scholar of the time. Here, the Hu servant praises the young scholar's background and literary talent.

配春风美人堪画图：指生配美女，如骏马配美人，美好如画卷。
Matched with spring breeze beauty, worthy of a painting: Means the young scholar is matched with a beauty, like a fine horse matched with a beauty, fine as a painted picture.

豪门体态殊，风流惯相助：胡奴自称出身豪门，仪态不凡，惯于助人成就风流事。
Wealthy family bearing is exceptional, romantic assistance is customary: The Hu servant claims to come from a wealthy family, have exceptional bearing, and be accustomed to helping people achieve romantic affairs.

跨金鞍骏驹，拥绿鞴苍奴："绿鞴"指绿色臂套（奴仆装饰），"苍奴"指胡奴（肤色较深），描绘生骑骏马、奴仆簇拥的排场。
Straddling a golden saddle on a fine steed, surrounded by green-gauntleted, swarthy servants: "Green gauntlets" refers to green arm covers (servant attire); "swarthy servants" refers to Hu servants (darker complexion). Here, it depicts the young scholar riding a fine horse, surrounded by servants, showing pomp.

到琐窗窥处："琐窗"指镂刻连锁图案的窗棂，代指闺房，此处暗指到女方闺阁前迎亲。
Arrive at the trivial  window peeping place: " trivial  window" refers to windows with interlocking patterns, representing the women's chambers. Here, it subtly means arriving before the bride's chambers for the wedding procession.

坦露了东床腹：再次用王羲之坦腹典故，胡奴调侃生酒后可能如东床坦腹般随性。
Baring the east bed belly: Again using the Wang Xizhi story, the Hu servant teases that the young scholar, after drinking, might be as casual as baring his belly on the east bed.

高控辔，响传呼，显风光赛寻俗："高控辔"指拉紧马缰绳，"响传呼"指随从吆喝，"寻俗"指寻常习俗，此处指要尽显风光，超越一般排场。
High control the reins, loud shouts, display grandeur surpassing the ordinary: "High control the reins" means pulling the reins tight; "loud shouts" means the attendants shouting; "ordinary" means common custom. Here, it means to fully display grandeur, surpassing usual pomp.

雕胡人当酒，莝荐马为刍："雕胡"指茭白，可作粮食，此处指备酒食；"莝荐"指铡碎的草，"刍"指草料，意为备酒食款待奴仆，备草料喂马。
Gujia grain for the men as wine, chopped straw for the horses as fodder: "Gujia grain" refers to wild rice stem, can be used as food, here means preparing wine and food; "chopped straw" means chopped grass; "fodder" means forage. It means prepare food and wine to entertain the servants, and prepare fodder for the horses.

坐凭金騕褭，走置锦流苏："騕褭"指古代骏马名，"锦流苏"指帐幔或马具上的彩色穗子，此处描绘生乘坐骏马，行时马具流苏飘动的景象。
Sitting astride the golden Yaoniao, moving set with brocade tassels: "Yaoniao" is the name of a famous ancient horse; "brocade tassels" refers to colored fringes on canopies or horse trappings. Here, it depicts the young scholar riding a fine horse, the horse's tassels flowing as it moves.

红线结姻缘：源于唐代李复言《续玄怪录·定婚店》中月老以红线系男女之足定姻缘的故事，后世用"红线"象征姻缘天定。
Red thread ties the marriage fate: Originates from the story in Li Fuyan's (Tang Dynasty) "Continued Records of the Mysterious and Strange · The Matchmaking Shop" where the Old Man under the Moon ties a red thread around the ankles of a man and woman to determine their marriage. Later generations use the "red thread" to symbolize a marriage destined by heaven.

探花人到：唐代进士及第后有探花宴，挑选年少英俊进士为"探花使"，文中"探花人"指代新郎，寓意才貌出众。
The Flower Scout arrives: In the Tang Dynasty, after passing the imperial examination, there was a Flower Scout banquet where young, handsome scholars were chosen as "Flower Scouts." Here, "Flower Scout" refers to the groom, implying outstanding talent and appearance.

秦楼：源自秦穆公女儿弄玉与萧史的故事，弄玉所居之楼称秦楼，后泛指女子居所。
Qin Tower: Originates from the story of Duke Mu of Qin's daughter Nongyu and Xiao Shi; the tower where Nongyu lived was called Qin Tower. Later, it generally refers to women's quarters.

风情似柳，有如张绪少年：南朝齐武帝赞灵和殿蜀柳"似张绪当年时"，张绪以风姿俊美著称，此处形容李生风姿如张绪。
Romantic grace like willow, resembling the young Zhang Xu: Emperor Wu of Southern Qi praised the Shu willows at Linghe Hall as "resembling Zhang Xu in his youth." Zhang Xu was renowned for his elegant demeanour . Here, it describes Scholar Li's graceful demeanour  like Zhang Xu.

回策如萦，不减王家叔父："王家叔父"指王羲之，以风度与书法闻名，此句赞李生挥鞭姿态不输王羲之风采。
Turning the whip as if coiling, not inferior to the Wang family uncle: "Wang family uncle" refers to Wang Xizhi, famous for his demeanour  and calligraphy. This line praises Scholar Li's posture wielding the whip as no less impressive than Wang Xizhi's elegant demeanour .

抵多少、宋玉全身，相如半面：宋玉、司马相如均为古代才子，以才貌双全闻名，此处言李生风采胜过二人。
Worth how much? Song Yu's whole body, Xiangru's half face: Song Yu and Sima Xiangru were both ancient talented scholars, renowned for both talent and looks. Here, it says Scholar Li's elegant demeanour surpasses both of them.

齐眉夫妇：出自"举案齐眉"典故，东汉梁鸿与孟光相敬如宾，孟光送饭时托盘举至眉高，祝愿新人夫妻相敬。
Eyebrow-level couple: Originates from the story of Liang Hong and Meng Guang (Eastern Han) who respected each other like guests; Meng Guang raised the tray to eyebrow level when serving food. It wishes the newlyweds mutual respect.

金屏合箭：用唐高祖李渊射屏选婿故事，窦皇后父画屏孔雀，李渊射中眼睛得婚，寓意姻缘美满。
Golden screen combined arrow: Uses the story of Tang Gaozu Li Yuan shooting a screen to choose a son-in-law; Dou Empress's father painted peacocks on a screen, Li Yuan hit the eye and won the marriage. It implies a blissful marriage.

吹箫侣天借云迎，飞琼佩月高风转："吹箫侣"指萧史弄玉吹箫引凤成仙；"飞琼"为仙女许飞琼，将新人比作神仙眷侣。
Flute-playing couple, heaven lends clouds to welcome, Feiqiong's pendant, moon high, wind turns: "Flute-playing couple" refers to Xiao Shi and Nongyu who played the flute to attract phoenixes and became immortals; "Feiqiong" is the fairy Xu Feiqiong. It compares the newlyweds to an immortal couple.

一饮琼浆，蓝桥试结良缘：源于裴航遇云英故事，裴航在蓝桥驿得云英赠浆，后结为夫妻，表达机缘巧合下的良缘。
One drink of jade nectar, at Blue Bridge try to form a good match: Originates from the story of Pei Hang meeting Yunying; Pei Hang received nectar from Yunying at Blue Bridge Post Station, later they married. It expresses a good match formed by chance.

三星在天：出自《诗经·唐风·绸缪》"三星在天，见此良人"，原诗咏新婚，此处指成婚吉时。
Three stars in the sky: Originates from "Classic of Poetry · Tang Feng · Chou Mou": "Three stars in the sky, seeing this good man." The original poem celebrates a new marriage. Here, it refers to the auspicious time for the wedding.

步生莲：源自南朝齐潘妃典故，东昏侯令潘妃行于金箔莲花上，称"步步生莲华"，形容女子步态优美。
Steps birth lotuses: Originates from the story of Consort Pan of Southern Qi; Emperor Donghun ordered Consort Pan to walk on gold foil lotuses, called "each step births a lotus flower," describing a woman's graceful tread.

春花春月两相辉，千里良缘一色丝：化用"千里姻缘一线牵"，以春花春月、红线象征美好姻缘与缘分珍贵。
Spring flowers and spring moon shine on each other, thousand-mile good match, one color thread: Adapts "a thousand-mile marriage is connected by a single thread," using spring flowers, spring moon, and the red thread to symbolize a beautiful marriage and precious destiny.

盼到洞房花烛夜，图他金榜挂名时：化用"洞房花烛夜，金榜题名时"，为人生两大喜事，表达对新人祝福与对新郎科举的期盼。
Longing for the nuptial chamber, flower candle night, hoping for his time of golden list, name displayed: Adapts "nuptial chamber, flower candle night" and "golden list, name displayed," the two great joys of life, expressing blessings for the newlyweds and hope for the groom's success in the imperial exams.

巫山洛浦："巫山"源自楚王梦遇巫山神女的故事，"洛浦"源自曹植遇洛神的典故，均指男女情爱。
Wu Mountain, Luo Riverbank: "Wu Mountain" originates from the story of the King of Chu dreaming of the Goddess of Wu Mountain; "Luo Riverbank" originates from the story of Cao Zhi encountering the Goddess of the Luo River. Both refer to romantic love between men and women.

秦楼箫史凤初飞：化用萧史弄玉吹箫引凤的故事，萧史弄玉居秦楼，吹箫引凤成仙，此处指新人如神仙眷侣成婚。
Qin Tower, Xiao Shi, phoenix first flies: Adapts the story of Xiao Shi and Nongyu playing the flute to attract phoenixes; they lived in Qin Tower, attracted phoenixes and became immortals. Here, it means the newlyweds marry like an immortal couple.

天上忝成银汉匹："银汉匹"指如牛郎织女般的姻缘，牛郎织女隔银河相望，借指两人的美好姻缘。
Heaven deigns to form a Milky Way pair: "Milky Way pair" refers to a marriage like the Cowherd and Weaver Girl, who gaze at each other across the Milky Way. It alludes to the couple's beautiful marriage.

举案齐眉：出自东汉梁鸿与孟光的故事，孟光送饭时将托盘举至眉高，表夫妻相敬，文中祝愿夫妻和睦。
Raise the tray to the eyebrows: Originates from the story of Liang Hong and Meng Guang (Eastern Han); Meng Guang raised the tray to eyebrow level when serving food, showing mutual respect between husband and wife. Here, it wishes the couple harmony.

吹箫楼上一对凤凰飞：再次化用萧史弄玉吹箫引凤的典故，以凤凰齐飞祝愿新人恩爱长久。
Flute-playing tower above, a pair of phoenixes fly: Again adapts the Xiao Shi and Nongyu story, using phoenixes flying together to wish the newlyweds lasting love.

掌朝枢："朝枢"指朝廷中枢要职，代指掌握朝廷大权，"枢"常喻朝廷关键职位。
Hold the court pivot: "Court pivot" refers to a central, vital position in the court, representing holding great power in the court. "Pivot" often metaphorically refers to key court positions.

乘舆：指代皇帝的车驾，亦代指皇帝，出自《孟子·梁惠王下》"今乘舆已驾矣"。
Imperial carriage: Refers to the emperor's carriage, also represents the emperor himself. Originates from "Mencius · King Hui of Liang II": "Now the imperial carriage is already harnessed."

鸾旗：皇帝仪仗中的旗帜，上绘鸾鸟，代指皇帝出行仪仗，出自《汉书·贾山传》"鸾旗在前，属车在后"。
Simurgh banners: Banners in the emperor's procession, painted with simurghs, representing the emperor's travel procession. Originates from "Book of Han · Biography of Jia Shan": "Simurgh banners in front, auxiliary carriages behind."

大比年：指科举考试年份，源于周代每三年大比之制，《周礼·地官·乡大夫》载"三年则大比，考其德行道艺"。
Great Comparison year: Refers to the year of the imperial examinations. Originates from the Zhou Dynasty system of holding a "great comparison" every three years. "Rites of Zhou the Earth God ·Village Chief" records: "Every three years is the great comparison, examining their virtue, conduct, dao, and arts."

攀春月桂：比喻科举登第，"月桂"即月中桂树，科举登第称"折桂"，出自《晋书·郤诜传》"犹桂林之一枝"。
Climb the spring moon cassia: Metaphor for passing the imperial examinations. "Moon cassia" is the cassia tree in the moon; passing the exams was called "breaking off a cassia branch." Originates from "Book of Jin · Biography of Xi Shen": "Like one branch from the cassia forest."

翠华：指皇帝仪仗队，以翠羽为饰，出自《汉书·司马相如传上》"建翠华之旗"。
Kingfisher-feathered canopy: Refers to the emperor's procession, adorned with kingfisher feathers. Originates from "Book of Han · Biography of Sima Xiangru I": "Raise the kingfisher-feathered banners."

近水楼台先得月，向阳花木易为春：出自宋代苏麟《断句》，原指近水楼台先见月、向阳花木早逢春，此处喻借职权优先择婿。
Near-water towers get the moon first; sun-facing flowers and trees easily meet spring: Originates from Su Lin's (Song Dynasty) "Broken Lines." Originally means towers near water see the moon first; flowers and trees facing the sun easily encounter spring. Here, it metaphorically means using one's position to take precedence to choose a son-in-law.

洛下才人贪折桂："折桂"比喻科举登第，源自《晋书·郤诜传》"犹桂林之一枝，昆山之片玉"，"洛下"指洛阳，代指科举之地。
Talented people of Luoyang crave to break the cassia: "Break the cassia" metaphorically means passing the imperial exams,from "Book of Jin · Biography of Xi Shen": "Like one branch from the cassia forest, one piece of jade from Kunlun Mountain." "Luoyang" refers to Luoyang, representing the place of examinations.

女萝无托，秋扇见捐："女萝无托"指像女萝（蔓生植物）失去依附，喻指失去依靠；"秋扇见捐"源自班婕妤《怨歌行》"秋扇见捐"，喻指色衰爱弛被抛弃。
Dodder has nothing to cling to, autumn fan is discarded: "Dodder has nothing to cling to" means like dodder (a creeping plant) losing its support, metaphorically losing reliance; "autumn fan is discarded" originates from Ban Jieyu's "Song of Resentment": "autumn fan is discarded," metaphorically meaning being abandoned when beauty fades and love cools.

水上鸳鸯，云中翡翠：鸳鸯、翡翠均为雌雄相伴的水鸟，常象征夫妻恩爱，文中用作盟约中的喻指。
Water mandarin ducks, cloud kingfishers: Mandarin ducks and kingfishers are waterfowl that pair male and female, often symbolizing conjugal love. Here, they are used metaphorically in the vow.

引喻山河，指诚日月：以山河、日月为誓，源自古代盟誓常用山河日月表诚心，如《史记》中多有以山河为誓的记载。
Cite metaphors of mountains and rivers, point to sincerity of sun and moon: Swearing by mountains, rivers, sun, and moon, originates from ancient oaths often using these to express sincerity, such as records in "Records of the Grand Historian" of swearing by mountains and rivers.

心字香：一种制成心形的香，常象征情意，此处"心字香前酬愿"指在香前许愿表心意。
Heart-character incense: Incense formed into the shape of a heart, often symbolizing affection. Here, "before the heart-character incense, repay a vow" means making a vow before the incense to express feelings.

青帝：古代神话中的司春之神，此处"教青帝长如愿"指愿春神保佑心愿长久。
Green Emperor: The god of spring in ancient mythology. Here, "make the Green Emperor always grant wishes" means wishing the spring god to protect and make wishes last.

海枯石烂：常用作盟誓之语，形容爱情永恒不变，最早可见于宋代司马光等文人作品中的类似表述。
Seas run dry and stones crumble: Commonly used in vows, describing eternal, unchanging love. Earliest similar expressions can be seen in the works of Sima Guang (Song Dynasty) and other literati.

游上苑："上苑"指皇家园林，此处"趁春风游上苑"暗指赴京赶考，如春日游园般充满希望。
Wander the Upper Park: "Upper Park" refers to the imperial gardens. Here, "take advantage of the spring breeze to wander the Upper Park" subtly refers to going to the capital for the exams, full of hope like strolling in a garden in spring.

燕尔欢迟，鸳班赴早："燕尔"源自《诗经·邶风·谷风》"燕尔新婚"，指新婚欢乐；"鸳班"指官员行列，此处指新婚欢聚未久，便要赴科举早行。
Yan'er joy is late, Mandarin Duck rank departs early: "Yan'er" originates from "Classic of Poetry · Bei Feng · Valley Wind": "Yan'er new marriage," referring to the joy of a new marriage; "Mandarin Duck rank" refers to the ranks of officials. Here, it means the joyous new marriage gathering is brief before having to depart early for the examinations.

浪桃香二月春雷早："浪桃香"形容春日桃花盛放，"春雷早"暗喻科举机会早至，如春雷催生万物。
Billowing peach fragrance, second month, spring thunder early: "Billowing peach fragrance" describes peach blossoms blooming profusely in spring; "spring thunder early" metaphorically implies the opportunity of the exams arrives early, like spring thunder hastening the growth of all things.

画眉人去走章台道："画眉人"指夫妻，源自张敞画眉典故；"章台道"原指长安章台街，代指游宦之路，此处指丈夫赴考离去。
Eyebrow-painting person goes, walking the Zhangtai Road: "Eyebrow-painting person" refers to the married couple,from Zhang Chang's eyebrow-painting story; "Zhangtai Road" originally referred to Zhangtai Street in Chang'an, representing the road of official travel. Here, it means the husband leaves for the examinations.

乘龙人试把龙门跳："乘龙人"指女婿，"龙门跳"比喻科举登第，源自"鲤鱼跳龙门"典故，指科举成功如跃过龙门。
Riding-dragon person tries to jump the Dragon Gate: "Riding-dragon person" refers to the son-in-law; "jump the Dragon Gate" metaphorically means passing the imperial exams,from the "carp jumps the Dragon Gate"story, meaning exam success is like leaping over the Dragon Gate.

黄金榜标，披香殿朝："黄金榜"指科举放榜的榜单；"披香殿"为汉代宫殿名，代指朝廷宫殿，此处指科举得中后朝见君王。
Golden list displayed, Pixiang Palace court: "Golden list" refers to the posted list of exam passers; "Pixiang Palace" is the name of a Han Dynasty palace, representing the imperial court. Here, it means attending court and seeing the emperor after passing the exams.

丽春园接受了求贤诏："丽春园"代指春日园林，"求贤诏"指朝廷征召贤才的诏令，此处指接受科举征召。
Lichun Garden receives the seeking-worthies decree: "Lichun Garden" represents spring gardens; "seeking-worthies decree" refers to the imperial decree summoning talented individuals. Here, it means accepting the summons to take the exams.

泥金报：指科举得中后用泥金书写的喜报，古代科举中第后会送泥金喜报回家。
Gold-paste report: Refers to the happy news report written in gold paste after passing the imperial exams. In ancient times, a gold-paste report would be sent home after success in the exams.

诗成夺锦袍：源自唐代武则天令臣下赋诗，宋之问诗成得赐锦袍的故事，比喻科举中第或文才出众获赏。
Poetry finished, seize the brocade robe: Originates from the story of Empress Wu Zetian (Tang) ordering officials to compose poetry, and Song Zhiwen winning a brocade robe for his poem. It metaphorically means passing the exams or being rewarded for outstanding literary talent.

沉香亭捧砚写清平调：源自李白为唐玄宗、杨贵妃作《清平调》的故事，此处想象科举成功后为君王赋诗的荣耀。
Chenxiang Pavilion, holding the inkstone, writing Qingping Melodies: Originates from the story of Li Bai composing the "Qingping Melodies" for Emperor Xuanzong of Tang and Consort Yang. Here, it imagines the glory of composing poetry for the monarch after exam success.

夫人县君，七香车载了："夫人"县君"为古代命妇封号；"七香车"为古代贵族妇女所乘华丽车辆，指科举成功后妻子获封受荣。
Furen, County Lady, carried in the seven-incense carriage: "Furen" and "County Lady" are titles for women granted by the court in ancient times; "seven-incense carriage" is a magnificent carriage ridden by noblewomen. It means the wife receives titles and honors after the husband's exam success.

学一个京兆眉儿向昼锦描："京兆眉"源自张敞为妻画眉典故，"昼锦"指富贵还乡，此处盼丈夫功成名就后如张敞般恩爱如初。
Learn to paint a Capital Governor's eyebrows towards brocade in daylight: "Capital Governor's eyebrows" originates from Zhang Chang's eyebrow-painting story for his wife; "brocade in daylight" means returning home in glory and wealth. Here, it hopes the husband will be as affectionate as Zhang Chang after achieving success and fame.

黄屋去东巡："黄屋"指皇帝的车驾，因车盖以黄缯为里，故称，代指皇帝出行，源自《史记·秦始皇本纪》"乘黄屋左纛"。
Yellow Canopy goes east on tour: "Yellow Canopy" refers to the emperor's carriage, because the canopy was lined with yellow silk, hence the name; it represents the emperor traveling. Originates from "Records of the Grand Historian · Annals of Qin Shi Huang": "Riding the Yellow Canopy with left pennant."

直上龙门峻："龙门峻"比喻科举仕途艰险，"直上龙门"源自"鲤鱼跳龙门"典故，指科举登第如跃过险峻龙门。
Straight up the steep Dragon Gate: "Steep Dragon Gate" metaphorically means the difficulty of the exam and official path; "straight up the Dragon Gate" originates from the "carp jumps the Dragon Gate"story, meaning passing the exams is like leaping over the steep Dragon Gate.

领取上林春信："上林"指汉代上林苑，代指皇家宫苑，"春信"指春天的消息，此处喻指科举成功后获得朝廷赏识的喜讯。
Receive the Upper Forest spring message: "Upper Forest" refers to the Han Dynasty Shanglin Park, representing the imperial gardens; "spring message" means news of spring. Here, it metaphorically means the happy news of gaining the court's appreciation after exam success.

龙蛇砚影笔生花："笔生花"源自李白"梦笔生花"典故，指文思泉涌，此处形容应试时文笔精妙如砚中龙蛇舞动、笔下生花。
Dragon and snake inkstone shadow, pen births flowers: "Pen births flowers" originates from Li Bai's story "dreaming his pen sprouted flowers," meaning literary ideas flow abundantly. Here, it describes the exquisite writing during the exam, like dragons and snakes dancing in the inkstone, flowers blooming under the pen.

状元红浪桃生晕："状元红"指喜庆的红颜色或酒名，"浪桃生晕"形容桃花盛放如红晕，暗喻科举高中的喜庆。
Zhuangyuan red, billowing peaches birth a blush: "Zhuangyuan red" refers to a festive red color or a wine name; "billowing peaches birth a blush" describes peach blossoms blooming like a blush, subtly metaphorizing the joy of top placement in the exams.

乌帽宫花斜插鬓："乌帽宫花"指科举中第后所戴的乌纱帽和簪戴的宫花，是古代科举及第的标志。
Black cap, palace flower slantingly inserted at the temple: "Black cap, palace flower" refers to the black gauze cap worn and the palace flower inserted after passing the imperial exams, a sign of success in ancient times.

翰苑风清，蓬莱天近："翰苑"指翰林院，"蓬莱"指传说中仙山，代指朝廷禁地，此处形容翰林院清雅、靠近朝廷如近蓬莱仙境。
Hanlin courtyard breeze clear, Penglai sky near: "Hanlin courtyard" refers to the Hanlin Academy; "Penglai" refers to the mythical fairy mountain, representing the forbidden precincts of the court. Here, it describes the Hanlin Academy as elegant and close to the court, like being near the Penglai paradise.

视草玉堂人："视草"指为皇帝修改文稿，"玉堂"指翰林院，代指在翰林院任职的官员，源自汉代玉堂殿为文人所居。
Viewing drafts, Jade Hall person: "Viewing drafts" means editing documents for the emperor; "Jade Hall" refers to the Hanlin Academy, representing officials serving there. Originates from the Jade Hall Palace of the Han Dynasty where literati resided.

紫荷囊金鱼佩："紫荷囊""金鱼佩"均为古代官员的服饰或配饰，象征官职身份，此处指官员的风采。
Purple lotus bag, golden fish pendant: Both "purple lotus bag" and "golden fish pendant" were attire or accessories of ancient officials, symbolizing rank and status . Here, they refer to the official's demeanor.

紫薇堂印："紫薇堂"指中书省或宰相官署，因唐代中书省称紫薇省，"掌紫薇堂印"指担任宰相之职。
Ziwei Hall seal: "Ziwei Hall" refers to the Secretariat or the office of the prime minister . Since the Tang Dynasty Secretariat was called the Ziwei Province, "holding the Ziwei Hall seal" means holding the office of prime minister .

凤池头立稳："凤池"指中书省，代指朝廷要职，"立稳凤池头"指在朝廷重要职位上站稳脚跟。
Phoenix Pond head stand firm: "Phoenix Pond" refers to the Secretariat, representing important court positions. "Stand firm at the Phoenix Pond head" means securing a firm footing in a key court position.

上朝班玉笋："玉笋"比喻朝廷官员行列整齐如竹笋，"朝班玉笋"指在朝官员的行列，形容进入仕途。
Ascend court ranks, jade bamboo shoots: "Jade bamboo shoots" metaphorically describe the neat ranks of court officials like bamboo shoots. "Court ranks, jade bamboo shoots" refers to the ranks of officials at court, describing entering officialdom.

画凌云第一人："凌云"指文才高超，如《史记》载司马相如"赋可以凌云"，此处指成为文才出众、仕途得意的顶尖人才。
Paint soaring clouds, number one person: "Soaring clouds" means literary talent so high it reaches the clouds, as in "Records of the Grand Historian" describing Sima Xiangru's "rhapsody can soar to the clouds." Here, it means becoming the top talent with outstanding literary skill and successful official career.

唯有太平方寸血，今朝尽向隗台倾："隗台"即黄金台，源自燕昭王筑台招贤典故，此处指将报国之心倾注于科举，如贤才向黄金台汇聚。
Only the blood of a peaceful square inch, today entirely pours towards Kui Terrace: "Kui Terrace" is the Golden Terrace, originating from the story of King Zhao of Yan building a terrace to recruit worthies. Here, it means pouring one's heart of serving the country into the exams, like worthies gathering at the Golden Terrace.

天可汗：唐代少数民族对唐太宗的尊称，后泛指唐朝皇帝，此处"大唐朝素号天可汗"指唐朝声威远播，受各族拥戴。
Heavenly Kaghan: Title used by minority peoples for Emperor Taizong of Tang, later refer to Tang emperors. Here, "the Great Tang Dynasty is commonly called Heavenly Kaghan" means the Tang's prestige spread far, receiving allegiance from various peoples.

呼韩：指呼韩邪单于，汉代匈奴单于，曾归附汉朝，此处"河西臂断呼韩"以呼韩邪喻指归附的少数民族，指河西地区如断匈奴右臂般稳定。
Hu Han: Refers to Huhanye Chanyu, a Xiongnu chieftain of the Han Dynasty who submitted to the Han. Here, "Hexi arm severed Hu Han" uses Huhanye to represent submitted minority peoples, meaning the Hexi region was stabilized like severing the Xiongnu's right arm.

吐番：即吐蕃，古代藏族政权，此处指吐蕃对河西地区的威胁。
Tufan: i.e., Tibet, the ancient Tibetan political power . Here, it refers to the threat posed by Tibet to the Hexi region.

狮蛮：指绣有狮子、蛮王图案的服饰，多为武将所穿，"怒冲冠带挺狮蛮"形容将领怒发冲冠、身着狮蛮服饰的雄姿。
Lion-barbarian: Refers to clothing embroidered with lions and barbarian kings, often worn by military officers. "Anger rushes crown and sash, stiffen lion-barbarian" describes a general's majestic posture with bristling anger and wearing lion-barbarian attire.

玉关：即玉门关，古代西北重要关隘，"风传玉关"指军情从玉门关传来。
Jade Gate: i.e., Yumen Pass, an important northwestern pass in ancient times. "Wind transmits from Jade Gate" means military news comes from Yumen Pass.

天山：指西域天山山脉，"长剑天山"形容将领镇守边疆的壮志，如长剑直抵天山。
Heavenly Mountains: Refers to the Tianshan mountain range in the Western Regions. "Long sword Heavenly Mountains" describes a general's ambition to guard the frontier, like a long sword reaching to the Heavenly Mountains.

河源：指黄河源头，古代认为河源出西域，"临风把星宿弹"以河源、星宿描绘边疆壮阔，显豪情。
River Source: Refers to the source of the Yellow River, anciently believed to be in the Western Regions. "Facing the wind, pluck the stars" uses the river source and stars to depict the vastness of the frontier, showing lofty spirit.

凌烟：指凌烟阁，唐太宗为表彰功臣建凌烟阁绘其像，"图画凌烟"指渴望建功立业，名留凌烟阁。
Lingyan: Refers to Lingyan Pavilion, built by Emperor Taizong of Tang to honor meritorious officials by painting their portraits. "Painted in Lingyan" means to be wishful to achieve merit and fame, leaving one's name in Lingyan Pavilion.

毛锥：指毛笔，代指文臣，"长枪队里也要毛锥站"指军队中也需要文臣参与军咨、记室等事务。
Hair awl: Refers to a writing brush, representing civil officials. "In the long spear ranks, also need hair awls to stand" means the army also needs civil officials for advisory, clerical, etc., duties.

羽书飞奏檄凯还："羽书"指紧急军信，"檄"指讨伐文书，"凯还"指凯旋，指文臣需草拟军信、檄文，助军队凯旋。
Feather document flies report, proclamation victory return: "Feather document" means urgent military dispatch; "proclamation" means declaration of war; "victory return" means triumphant return. It means civil officials need to draft military dispatches and proclamations to aid the army's victory.

投笔新参：源自班超"投笔从戎"的典故，班超原为书生，后弃笔从军立功封侯，"投笔新参"指新科翰林弃文从武参与军务。
Throw brush, new advisor: Originates from Ban Chao's story "throwing away the brush to join the army." Ban Chao was originally a scholar, later abandoned writing to join the army, achieved merit, and was enfeoffed. "Throw brush, new advisor" means a newly appointed Hanlin scholar abandons literature for military participation.

定远：指班超，封定远侯，"做个定远班"指希望新参参谋能如班超般建功立业。
Dingyuan: Refers to Ban Chao, enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingyuan. "Become a Dingyuan Ban" means hoping the new advisor can achieve merit like Ban Chao.

吐谷浑：古代少数民族政权，此处代指边疆敌军，"定报生擒吐谷浑"表平定边疆的决心。
Tuyuhun: An ancient minority political power , here representing frontier enemies. "Certainly report capturing Tuyuhun alive" expresses the determination to pacify the frontier.

悔教夫婿觅封侯：源自王昌龄《闺怨》"忽见陌头杨柳色，悔教夫婿觅封侯"，此处化用诗句，表达旦因丈夫赴考分离而生的悔意与牵挂。
Regret teaching husband to seek marquisate: Originates from Wang Changling's "Chamber Resentment": "Suddenly seeing willow colors at the road's head, regret teaching husband to seek marquisate." Here, the line is adapted to express the female lead's regret and worry due to her husband leaving for the exams.

杜鹃桥上数归舟："杜鹃桥""数归舟"均为盼归意象，杜鹃常与思归关联，数归舟则直接表现等待丈夫归来的心情。
Cuckoo Bridge, counting returning boats: Both "Cuckoo Bridge" and "counting returning boats" are images of longing for return. Cuckoos are often associated with longing for home; counting returning boats directly shows the feeling of waiting for the husband's return.

洛阳春老，知他逗遛："洛阳春老"指春光将尽，暗喻时光流逝，担忧丈夫在洛阳因春光或事务停留不归。
Luoyang spring ages, know he lingers: "Luoyang spring ages" means spring is ending, metaphorically time passing, worrying that her husband lingers in Luoyang due to the spring scenery or affairs and does not return.

插花筵上，占定酒头筹："插花筵"指科举中第后的宴饮，"酒头筹"指宴席上的首位，祝愿李生科举得中，在庆功宴上拔得头筹。
Flower-inserting feast, secure the wine first place: "Flower-inserting feast" refers to the banquet after passing the exams; "wine first place" means the top position at the feast. It wishes Scholar Li success in the exams and to take the top place at the victory banquet.

锦袍穿上了御街游："锦袍御街游"指科举中第后状元游街的荣耀场景，代指科举成功后的风光。
Brocade robe worn, parading the Imperial Street: "Brocade robe parading the Imperial Street" refers to the glorious scene of the top graduate parading through the streets after exam success, representing the glory after success.

紫骅骝：指骏马，古代科举中第者常乘骏马游街，此处"紫骅骝"代指中第后的出行排场。
Purple Hualiu: Refers to a fine horse. Successful exam candidates often rode fine horses in parades. Here, "purple Hualiu" represents the travel pomp after success.

美人图开在手，央及煞状元收：暗指担心丈夫中第后被其他女子吸引，以"美人图"喻指诱惑，表达旦的忧虑。
Beauty picture opened in hand, urgently beg the Zhuangyuan to accept: Subtly means worrying that after success, her husband might be attracted to other women; "beauty picture" metaphorically represents temptation, expressing the female lead's anxiety.

平康笑留："平康"指唐代长安平康坊，为歌妓聚集处，此处担忧丈夫在游街时流连欢场。
Pingkang laughs and detains: "Pingkang" refers to the Pingkang Ward in Chang'an, Tang Dynasty, where singing girls gathered. Here, it worries that her husband might linger in pleasure quarters during the parade.

秦楼诉休："秦楼"代指自家闺楼，"诉休"指诉说离别之苦，怕丈夫在外流连而不顾家中牵挂。
Qin Tower complains cease: "Qin Tower" represents her own women's quarters; "complains cease" means telling of the pain of separation. She fears her husband lingers outside and neglects the concerns at home.

丝萝契急难丢："丝萝"源自《古诗十九首》"与君为新婚，菟丝附女萝"，以丝萝相依喻指夫妻情意，强调缘分深厚难舍。
Dodder vine pact urgently hard to discard: "Dodder vine" originates from "Nineteen Old Poems": "With you as new marriage, dodder clings to vine," using dodder and vine clinging together to metaphorically represent conjugal affection, emphasizing a deep, hard-to-abandon bond.

夜香不冷花前咒："夜香"指夜间焚香许愿，"花前咒"指在花前祈祷，表达旦默默祈愿丈夫平安归来的心意。
Night incense not cold, before flowers curse: "Night incense" means burning incense and making vows at night; "before flowers curse" means praying before flowers. It expresses the female lead's silent prayer for her husband's safe return.

昼锦还归月下游："昼锦"指富贵还乡，"月下游"指浪漫归来，盼丈夫功成名就后如月光般美好归来。
Daytime brocade return, under moonlight wander: "Daytime brocade" means returning home wealthy and honored; "under moonlight wander" means a romantic return. It hopes the husband will return beautifully like moonlight after achieving success and fame.

泥金喜：指科举得中的泥金喜报，是古代科举中第后传递喜讯的方式，此处盼喜报传来。
Gold-paste joy: Refers to the gold-paste happy news report of exam success, the method of conveying the news in ancient times. Here, it hopes for the report to arrive.

鸾封红耀手："鸾封"指带有鸾鸟图案的封函，代指喜信或朝廷封赠文书，"红耀手"形容喜信到手的喜庆。
Simurgh seal, red dazzling hand: "Simurgh seal" refers to a sealed document with simurgh patterns, representing happy news or court bestowal documents; "red dazzling hand" describes the joy of receiving the happy news.

灯花闲弄玉钗头："灯花"为传统吉兆，象征喜事，"弄玉钗"表现等待时的慵懒情态，暗含对喜讯的期盼。
Lamp flame idly plays with jade hairpin head: "Lamp flame" is a traditional auspicious omen, symbolizing happy events; "plays with jade hairpin" shows a lazy manner while waiting, implicitly containing anticipation for good news.

青云有路透朝元："朝元"指朝见天子，源自道教徒朝见神仙称朝元，后泛指朝见君主，此处指青云之路可通往朝廷面见君王。
Blue clouds have a road penetrating to court the primal: "Court the primal" means having an audience with the emperor, originates from Daoists attending on immortals, later refer to attending on the monarch. Here, it means the road to high position leads to the court and seeing the emperor.

三天日色黄图外："三天"指天宫，代指朝廷；"黄图"指帝都，此处描绘帝都外日光普照，显朝廷气象。
Three Heavens' sun color outside the Yellow Chart: "Three Heavens" refers to the heavenly palace, representing the court; "Yellow Chart" refers to the imperial capital. Here, it depicts sunlight shining outside the capital, showing the court's atmosphere.

八柱擎天："八柱"源自古代神话中支撑天地的八根柱子，喻指宰相辅佐君王如柱擎天，支撑国家。
Eight pillars prop up heaven: "Eight pillars" originates from the eight pillars supporting heaven and earth in ancient mythology, metaphorically meaning the prime minister assists the ruler like pillars propping up heaven, supporting the state.

蓬莱殿：指皇宫大殿，蓬莱为仙山，代指帝王居所，此处"送上蓬莱殿"指进入皇宫面见君王。
Penglai Palace: Refers to the main palace hall; Penglai is a fairy mountain, representing the emperor's residence. Here, "sent up to Penglai Palace" means entering the palace to see the emperor.

身惹御炉烟："御炉"指皇宫中的香炉，"惹御炉烟"形容身处皇宫，沾染御炉香气，显受君王恩宠。
Body attracts imperial stove smoke: "Imperial stove" refers to the incense burners in the palace; "attracts imperial stove smoke" describes being in the palace, imbued with the imperial incense fragrance, showing the emperor's favor.

笙歌上苑："上苑"指皇家园林，此处"笙歌上苑"描绘科举中第后在皇家园林设宴的喜庆场景。
Pipes and songs, Upper Park: "Upper Park" refers to the imperial gardens. Here, "pipes and songs, Upper Park" depicts the celebratory scene of a banquet in the imperial gardens after exam success.

曲江人醉杏花筵："曲江"指长安曲江池，唐代科举放榜后常在曲江设宴，称"曲江宴"；"杏花筵"指科举宴饮，因杏花盛开时举行而得名。
Qujiang people drunk on apricot blossom feast: "Qujiang" refers to the Qujiang Pool in Chang'an; after the exam results were posted in the Tang Dynasty, a banquet was often held at Qujiang, called the "Qujiang Feast"; "apricot blossom feast" refers to the exam celebration banquet, named because it was held when apricot blossoms bloomed.

铃索一声花满院："铃索"指宫殿中的铃铛绳索，用于传呼，此处写铃声响起，庭院花开，烘托喜庆氛围。
Bell rope one sound, flowers fill the courtyard: "Bell rope" refers to the rope connected to bells in the palace used for summoning; here, the bell sounds, the courtyard flowers bloom, enhancing the festive atmosphere.

紫陌万人生喜色，曲江千树发仙桃："紫陌"指帝都道路，"曲江仙桃"喻指科举中第的喜讯，如曲江桃树结果般喜人。
Purple paths, ten thousand people birth joyful expressions; Qujiang, thousand trees produce fairy peaches: "Purple paths" refers to the capital's roads; "Qujiang fairy peaches" metaphorically means the happy news of exam success, as joyful as Qujiang peach trees bearing fruit.

青云已是酬恩处："青云"指高官显位，"酬恩"指报答君王恩宠，此处言科举得中、身居高位已报答恩情。
Blue clouds already are the place to repay kindness: "Blue clouds" means high official positions; "repay kindness" means repaying the ruler's favor. Here, it says passing the exams and holding high office has already repaid the kindness.

剑履下朝堂，平步星辰上："剑履上殿"为古代大臣特权，可带剑穿鞋上殿，此处"剑履下朝堂"指退朝，"平步星辰"形容官位极高，如平步星辰之上，显权势显赫。
Sword and shoes descend the court hall, level step on stars above: "Sword and shoes ascend the hall" was a privilege for high ministers in ancient times, allowing them to wear swords and shoes in court. Here, "sword and shoes descend the court hall" means leaving court after audience; "level step on stars" describes an extremely high official rank, like stepping level with the stars, showing great power and influence.

春风桃李遍门墙：源自杜甫《奉赠韦左丞丈二十二韵》"桃李满天下，何须堂屋深"，以桃李喻门生弟子，此处指卢太尉门生众多，遍布门墙。
Spring breeze, peaches and plums are found everywhere: Originates from Du Fu's "Respectfully Presented to Vice-Director Wei, Twenty-two Rhymes": "Peaches and plums fill the world, why need deep halls?" Using peaches and plums to metaphorically represent disciples. Here, it means Grand Marshal Lu has many disciples, filling his door and wall.

只手擎天势独尊："只手擎天"喻指独力支撑天下，形容权势极大，可独揽朝政，无人能及。
Single hand props up heaven, posture uniquely mister: "Single hand props up heaven" metaphorically means single-handedly supporting the world, describing immense power, able to monopolize court affairs, unmatched by anyone.

玉门关外参军："参军"为古代官职，掌参谋军务，玉门关为西北边关，此处指卢太尉设计将李益派往边关任参军。
Beyond Jade Gate Pass, Army Consultant: "Army Consultant" was an ancient official position responsible for military staff work. Jade Gate Pass was a northwestern frontier pass. Here, it means Grand Marshal Lu schemes to send Li Yi to the frontier to serve as Army Consultant.

编修院无他情况："编修院"指翰林院，为文人任职之所，此处说翰林院没有李益的相关任职记录，为派往边关找借口。
