俏崔氏坐成花烛，蠢卢生梦醒黄粱：崔氏、卢生均出自汤显祖《邯郸记》，崔氏得配卢生，卢生梦醒悟透功名富贵如黄粱一梦。文中借戏曲人物收束，呼应"人生如梦"主旨。
Pretty Cui Shi sits through the wedding candles; foolish Lu Sheng wakes from the millet dream: Cui Shi and Lu Sheng are from Tang Xianzu's "The Handan Dream." Cui Shi marries Lu Sheng; Lu Sheng wakes from the dream realizing official rank and wealth are like a dream of yellow millet. In the text, it uses the play's characters to conclude, echoing the theme "life is like a dream."

极目云霄有路，惊心岁月无涯：化用"云霄有路"喻仕途希望，"岁月无涯"叹时光流逝，文中卢生望仕途却忧年华虚度。
Gazing, clouds and skies have a path; startling the heart, years and months are boundless: Uses "clouds and skies have a path" to metaphorically mean hope for an official career; "years and months are boundless" sighs over the passage of time. In the text, Lu Sheng looks towards an official career but worries about wasting his years.

白屋三间，红尘一榻："白屋"指贫寒之家，"红尘"喻世俗纷扰，文中写卢生家境贫寒却身处世俗烦忧中。
Three rooms of a white hut, one couch in the red dust: "White hut" means a poor household; "red dust" metaphorically means worldly turmoil. In the text, it describes Lu Sheng's poor family circumstances yet his involvement in worldly worries.

展秋窗腐草无萤火，盼古道垂杨有暮鸦：化用秋日萧瑟意象，"腐草无萤火""垂杨有暮鸦"写秋景凄凉，烘托卢生失意心境。
Opening the autumn window, decayed grass has no fireflies; hoping the ancient road's drooping willows have crows at dusk: Uses desolate autumn imagery; "decayed grass has no fireflies" and "drooping willows have crows at dusk" describe a bleak autumn scene, enhancing Lu Sheng's disheartened state of mind.

李赤是李白之兄：李赤为唐代诗人，相传其模仿李白却不及，文中卢生自嘲所谓"才子"名不副实。
Li Chi is Li Bai's elder brother: Li Chi was a Tang Dynasty poet, said to have imitated Li Bai but was inferior. In the text, Lu Sheng self-deprecatingly mocks his so-called "talented scholar" reputation as undeserved.

梁九乃梁八之弟：以虚构的"梁九""梁八"调侃科举中侥幸得中的人，文中卢生叹自己不如那些平庸之辈得志。
Liang Jiu is Liang Ba's younger brother: Uses fictional "Liang Jiu" and "Liang Ba" to mock those who passed the exams by luck. In the text, Lu Sheng sighs that he is less successful than those mediocre people.

稂不稂，莠不莠：稂、莠均为田间杂草，喻不成材，文中卢生自嘲落魄潦倒，不被人看重。
Neither proper grain nor proper weed; " Chinese pennisetum " and " green bristlegrass " are both field weeds, metaphorically meaning good-for-nothing. In the text, Lu Sheng mocks himself as down-and-out and not valued by others.

学老圃，混着老农：化用《论语》"学圃""学稼"典故，指归隐务农，文中卢生感慨怀才不遇，只能暂混农夫之中。
Learning from old gardeners, mixing with old farmers: Alludes to the story "learning gardening" and "learning farming" from the Analects, meaning retiring to farm. In the text, Lu Sheng laments his unrecognized talent,only temporarily among farmers.

驷马高车：指高官显贵的车马，喻仕途得意，文中卢生叹自己骑驴落魄，难望富贵。
Four-horse chariots: Refers to the carriages of high officials and nobles, metaphorically meaning success in an official career. In the text, Lu Sheng sighs that he rides a donkey, and can hardly hope for wealth and honor.

返照入闾巷，忧来共谁语：化用秋日傍晚孤寂景象，"返照""忧来"写卢生日暮独行，愁绪无人可诉。
Returning light enters the village lanes; sorrow comes, with whom to speak?: Uses the lonely scene of an autumn evening; "returning light" and "sorrow comes" describe Lu Sheng walking alone at dusk, his worries with no one to tell.

秋风动禾黍：以秋风中禾黍摇曳的秋景，烘托卢生漂泊无依的凄凉处境。
Autumn wind stirs the millet: Uses the autumn scene of millet swaying in the autumn wind to enhance Lu Sheng's desolate situation of a wanderer having no one to depend upon ..

蓬岛何曾见一人，披星带月斩麒麟：化用仙家典故，"蓬岛"指蓬莱仙境，"斩麒麟"喻修仙斩除心魔，文中吕洞宾以诗句自表仙者身份。
Penglai Isle, when did it ever see a man? Under stars and moon, slaying the qilin: Uses immortal story; "Penglai Isle" refers to the Penglai fairyland; "slaying the qilin" metaphorically means cultivating immortality by slaying inner demons. In the text, Lü Dongbin uses the verse to declare his immortal identity.

无缘邀得乘风去，回向瀛洲看日轮："瀛洲"为传说中仙山，"乘风""看日轮"写求仙不得仍向仙境回望，文中吕洞宾叹度人不易仍坚持寻觅。
Fated not to invite and ride the wind away, turning back towards Yingzhou to watch the sun's wheel: "Yingzhou" is a legendary fairy mountain; "ride the wind" and "watch the sun's wheel" describe failing to achieve immortality but still looking back towards the fairy realm. In the text, Lü Dongbin sighs that saving people is hard but persists in seeking.

翠凤毛翎札帚叉，闲踏天门扫落花：以"翠凤毛帚""扫落花"写仙界日常，文中何仙姑描绘自己在天门扫花的情景。
Jade phoenix feather broom, idly tread the Celestial Gate, sweeping fallen flowers: Uses "jade phoenix feather broom" and "sweeping fallen flowers" to describe daily life in the immortal realm. In the text, He Xiangu describes her task of sweeping flowers at the Celestial Gate.

剑斩黄龙一线差：化用吕洞宾"剑斩黄龙"的传说（因逞强差点犯错），文中何仙姑叮嘱吕洞宾此行勿再鲁莽。
Your sword slashed the Yellow Dragon, barely missing: Alludes to the legend of Lü Dongbin's "sword slashing the Yellow Dragon" (where he almost erred due to flaunt his superiority ). In the text, He Xiangu cautions Lü Dongbin not to be rash on this journey.

向东老贫穷卖酒家：东老为宋代隐士，以善酿酒闻名，文中指吕洞宾曾在贫时借酒家消愁，何仙姑劝其勿再沉溺。
Facing East Old, poor, selling wine: East Old was a Song Dynasty recluse famous for brewing good wine. In the text, it refers to Lü Dongbin once drowning his sorrows in a tavern when poor. He Xiangu urges him not to indulge again.

错教人留恨碧桃花："碧桃花"喻错过的机缘，文中何仙姑提醒吕洞宾若迟误度人，会留遗憾。
Wrongly teaching people to leave regrets under the green peach blossoms: "Green peach blossoms" metaphorically mean missed opportunities. In the text, He Xiangu reminds Lü Dongbin that if he delays saving people, he will leave regrets.

黄鹤楼铁笛吹：化用吕洞宾在黄鹤楼吹笛的传说，喻仙者潇洒行迹，文中吕洞宾自述曾在黄鹤楼行侠。
At Yellow Crane Tower, playing the iron flute: Alludes to the legend of Lü Dongbin playing the flute at Yellow Crane Tower, symbolizing the carefree travels of an immortal. In the text, Lü Dongbin states he once performed chivalrous deeds at Yellow Crane Tower.

平沙落雁呼：化用"平沙落雁"的经典意象，写洞庭秋景，烘托吕洞宾漂泊度人的心境。
Level sands, falling geese call: Uses the classic imagery of "wild geese descending on level sand." It describes the autumn scenery of Dongting Lake, enhancing Lü Dongbin's mood of leading a wandering life while saving people.

使酒的烂了胁肚，使气的腆破胸脯，急财的守着家兄，急色的守着院主：以俚语调侃沉迷酒、气、财、色的人终受其害，文中吕洞宾劝诫世人勿贪世俗欲望。
Those given to wine rot their guts; those given to anger burst their chests; those eager for wealth guard their family elder (money); those eager  for lust guard the brothel keeper: Uses colloquial language to mock thse obsessed with wine, anger, wealth, and lust, who ultimately suffer. In the text, Lü Dongbin admonishes people not to crave worldly desires.

毕月乌、房日兔：均为星宿名，"毕月乌"指月神，"房日兔"指日神，文中吕洞宾以星宿考问世人，显仙者见识。
Net Moon Crow, Chamber Sun Hare: Both are names of asterisms (lunar mansions). "Net Moon Crow" refers to the moon spirit; "Chamber Sun Hare" refers to the sun spirit. In the text, Lü Dongbin quizzes people with asterisms, showing an immortal's knowledge.

黄婆土筑了基，放在偃月炉："黄婆""偃月炉"均为道家炼丹术语，喻修行根基，文中吕洞宾解释磁枕的道家玄机。
Yellow Dame earth built the foundation, placed in the Crescent Moon Furnace: "Yellow Dame" and "Crescent Moon Furnace" are Daoist alchemy terms, metaphorically meaning the foundation of cultivation. In the text, Lü Dongbin explains the Daoist mystery of the magnetic pillow.

按八风，开地户，凭二曜，透天枢："八风""地户""二曜""天枢"均为道家天文地理概念，文中指磁枕蕴含自然之道。
Following the eight winds, opening the earth door, relying on the two luminaries, penetrating the celestial pivot: "Eight winds," "earth door," "two luminaries" (sun and moon), "celestial pivot" are all Daoist astronomical and geographical concepts. In the text, it means the magnetic pillow contains the Dao of nature.

会歌舞邯郸女，几千年出不的个蔺相如："邯郸女""蔺相如"均与邯郸相关，前者指俗艳，后者指贤才，文中吕洞宾疑邯郸难寻可度之人。
Dancing and singing Handan girls, for millennia not producing a single Lin Xiangru: "Handan girls" and "Lin Xiangru" are both associated with Handan; the former refers to vulgar beauty, the latter to worthy talent. In the text, Lü Dongbin doubts that Handan can produce someone worth saving.

芦花明月人何处，流水高山客有无：化用"芦花明月""流水高山"的隐逸与知音意象，文中吕洞宾寻觅有缘人的迷茫。
Reed catkins, bright moon, where is the man? Flowing water, high mountain, is there a guest?: Uses the imagery of "reed catkins, bright moon" and "flowing water, high mountain" associated with reclusion and understanding friends. In the text, it expresses Lü Dongbin's confusion while searching for a predestined person.

欠一个蓬莱洞扫花人，走一片邯郸城寻地主：呼应开篇扫花之任，文中吕洞宾决心在邯郸找到可度之人，完成使命。
Owing one Penglai cave flower sweeper, I walk through Handan city seeking the land's master: Echoes the flower-sweeping task from the beginning. In the text, Lü Dongbin resolves to find someone in Handan worth saving to complete his mission.

一粒粟中藏世界，半升铛里煮乾坤：化用道家"微观见宏观"的哲理，"粟中藏世界""铛里煮乾坤"喻小中见大，文中吕洞宾以诗句暗示仙术玄妙。
A single grain of millet hides a world; half a pint pot boils heaven and earth: Adapts the Daoist philosophy of "seeing the macrocosm in the microcosm." "Grain hides a world" and "pot boils heaven and earth" metaphorically mean seeing the large in the small. In the text, Lü Dongbin uses the verse to hint at the mystery of immortal arts.

夫巴陵胜状......其乐洋洋者矣：引用范仲淹《岳阳楼记》全文，描绘岳阳楼的阴晴之景与登楼心境，文中吕洞宾借名篇向卢生展现世间风光。
Now the superb scenery of Baling... their joy is boundless: Quotes the entire text of Fan Zhongyan's "Record of Yueyang Tower," describing the changing scenes of Yueyang Tower and the mood of ascending it. In the text, Lü Dongbin uses this famous piece to show Lu Sheng the sights of the world.

朝游碧落暮苍梧，袖有青蛇胆气粗：化用吕洞宾的仙游典故，"碧落""苍梧"写仙迹遍布，"青蛇"显侠气，文中吕洞宾自述行迹。
Morning roaming the blue void, evening Cangwu; sleeve holds the green snake, courage is bold: Uses the story of Lü Dongbin's immortal travels; "blue void" and "Cangwu" describe widespread immortal traces; "green snake" shows chivalrous spirit. In the text, Lü Dongbin describes his own travels.

试青紫当年如拾毛："青紫"代指高官印绶，喻科举得志易如拾毛，文中卢生叹自己早年壮志未酬。
Trying for blue and purple (high office) in those years was like picking up hairs: "Blue and purple" refer to the seals and ribbons of high officials, metaphorically meaning achieving success in the exams was as easy as picking up hairs. In the text, Lu Sheng sighs that his early ambitions were unfulfilled.

藤穿刺绣锦编牙，玉切香雕体势佳：描写磁枕材质精美，"藤穿""玉切"显其雅致，文中卢生初见磁枕的好奇。
Rattan pierces embroidery, brocade weaves ivory; jade cuts, fragrance carves, form and posture excellent: Describes the exquisite material of the magnetic pillow; "rattan pierces" and "jade cuts" show its elegance. In the text, it describes Lu Sheng's curiosity upon first seeing the magnetic pillow.

闪铜环呀的转帘牙，满庭花，重重帘幕锁烟霞：以"铜环""帘牙""烟霞"写豪门深院景象，文中卢生入梦后误入崔府的情景。
Gleaming bronze rings creak, turning the curtain hooks; courtyard full of flowers, layer upon layer of curtains lock in mist and haze: Uses "bronze rings," "curtain hooks," "mist and haze" to describe the scene of a wealthy family's deep courtyards. In the text, it describes Lu Sheng mistakenly entering the Cui residence after entering the dream.

如鱼失水旱莲花：以"旱莲花"喻困境中的自己，文中卢生躲藏时的慌张无助。
Like a fish out of water, a dry lotus flower: Uses "dry lotus flower" to metaphorically describe himself in a difficult situation. In the text, it describes Lu Sheng's panic and helplessness while hiding.

阮郎门下：化用刘晨、阮肇入天台遇仙姬的典故，喻误入仙境结缘，文中崔女暗指与卢生相逢如仙缘。
At the gate of Ruan Lang: Alludes to the story of Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao entering Tiantai and meeting immortal maidens. It metaphorically means mistakenly entering a fairyland and forming a bond. In the text, Miss Cui implicitly suggests meeting Lu Sheng is like an immortal fate.

颠倒英雄在绛纱，无财帛，单枪入马："绛纱"指闺阁，文中卢生自嘲穷困却得美人收留，似英雄遇奇缘。
Hero upside down in crimson gauze, without wealth or goods, single spear entering the horse: "Crimson gauze" refers to the women's quarters. In the text, Lu Sheng mocks himself for being poor yet taken in by a beauty, like a hero encountering a strange fate.

崔卢旧世家：崔、卢均为古代望族，文中借"旧世家"强调两人门第匹配，为姻缘添彩。
Cui and Lu, old eminent families: Cui and Lu were both ancient prominent families. In the text, it uses "old eminent families" to emphasize their social match, adding luster to the marriage.

无媒织女容招嫁：化用"牛郎织女"典故，喻无媒而结合的姻缘，文中写崔女不顾礼法收留卢生。
Unwedded Weaving Maid allows recruiting marriage: Alludes to the story of the Cowherd and the Weaving Maid, metaphorically meaning a marriage formed without a matchmaker. In the text, it describes Miss Cui taking in Lu Sheng despite propriety.

五百岁因缘到了家：以"五百年姻缘"喻命中注定的缘分，文中崔女与卢生确认姻缘天定。
A five-hundred-year predestined affinity has come home: Uses "five-hundred-year marriage fate" to metaphorically mean a destiny-ordained fate. In the text, Miss Cui and Lu Sheng confirm their marriage is heaven-ordained.

千秋万古共平原，生事萧条空掩门：化用怀古与穷居意象，"平原"喻历史沧桑，"萧条空门"写家境贫寒，文中萧嵩以诗句自叹身世。
A thousand autumns, ten thousand ages share the plain; life's affairs desolate, vainly closing the gate: Uses imagery of remembering antiquity and impoverished dwelling; "plain" metaphorically means historical vicissitudes; "desolate, empty gate" describes poor family circumstances. In the text, Xiao Song uses the verse to sigh over his own situation.

试问酒旗歌板地，有谁倾盖待王孙："倾盖"指初交相得，"王孙"自指贵族后裔，文中萧嵩叹虽为世家之后却无人礼遇。
I ask the land of wine flags and song clappers: who there would meet a prince's grandson with tilted carriage-cover?: "Tilted carriage-cover" means hitting it off at first meeting; "prince's grandson" refers to himself as a descendant of nobility. In the text, Xiao Song sighs that although from an eminent family, he receives no courtesy.

梁武帝萧衍之苗裔，宋国公萧瑀之曾孙：萧衍为南朝梁武帝，萧瑀为初唐名臣，文中借历史名人彰显萧嵩的世家背景。
Descendant of Emperor Wu of Liang, Xiao Yan; great-grandson of Duke of Song, Xiao Yu: Xiao Yan was Emperor Wu of the Liang Dynasty during the Southern Dynasties; Xiao Yu was a famous minister of the early Tang. In the text, it uses historical figures to highlight Xiao Song's eminent family background.

金牙大总管封闻喜县公裴行俭之晚子：裴行俭为唐代名将，封闻喜县公，文中点明裴光庭的显赫家世。
Late son of the Grand General with the Golden Tally, Enfeoffed Duke of Wenxi, Pei Xingjian: Pei Xingjian was a famous Tang Dynasty general, enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi. In the text, it clarifies Pei Guangting's illustrious family background.

嫦娥所爱，无过两儒："嫦娥"喻科举主考官或朝廷，"两儒"指萧嵩与裴光庭，文中裴光庭怕萧嵩夺走状元之位。
What Chang'e loves is nothing more than two scholars: "Chang'e" metaphorically refers to the chief examiner or the court; "two scholars" refer to Xiao Song and Pei Guangting. In the text, Pei Guangting fears Xiao Song will take the top graduate (zhuangyuan) position.

裴航要闪住你萧郎路：用"裴航遇仙"典故，喻裴光庭想阻碍萧嵩的仕途，文中裴光庭坦言想独占功名。
Pei Hang wants to block your path, Xiao Lang: Uses the story of "Pei Hang meeting an immortal," metaphorically meaning Pei Guangting wants to obstruct Xiao Song's official career. In the text, Pei Guangting openly states his desire to monopolize the success.

笔花高吐，你真难展舒："笔花"喻才华横溢，文中萧嵩调侃自己若全力应试，裴光庭难以施展。
Pen flowers spew high; you truly find it hard to unfold: "Pen flowers" metaphorically mean overflowing talent. In the text, Xiao Song jokes that if he tries his best in the exam, Pei Guangting will find it difficult to compete.

金阶对策也好商量做："金阶对策"指殿试应答，文中萧嵩表示愿在科举中与裴光庭相互照应。
Golden steps policy discussions can also be negotiated: "Golden steps policy discussions" refer to the palace examination responses. In the text, Xiao Song indicates willingness to cooperate with Pei Guangting in the exams.

月宫花谈笑取："月宫花"喻状元头衔，文中两人期许轻松夺取功名，展现对仕途的自信。
Moon palace flowers, taken with talk and laughter: "Moon palace flowers" metaphorically mean the zhuangyuan title. In the text, the two expect to easily seize success, showing confidence in their official careers.

但是学成文武艺，都堪货与帝王家：化用俗语，指才华应献给朝廷换取功名，文末点出两人赴京应试的目的。
But having mastered the arts of both pen and sword, all are fit to be sold to the imperial house: Adapts a common saying, meaning talent should be offered to the court in exchange for rank and fame. At the end of the text, it points out the purpose of the two going to the capital for the exams.

红围粉簇清幽路，那得人游？天与风流，有客窥帘动玉钩：化用"红粉围簇""窥帘"的闺阁意象，写崔女深院遇卢生的情境，文中描绘两人结缘的浪漫氛围。
Red surrounds, powder clusters, a secluded path; how could people wander there? Heaven bestows romance; a guest peeps behind the curtain, moving the jade hook: Uses the imagery of the women's quarters: "red and powder clusters" and "peeping behind the curtain." It describes the situation of Miss Cui meeting Lu Sheng in her deep courtyard. In the text, it depicts the romantic atmosphere of their meeting.

不羡名公乐此身，这风光别似武陵春："武陵春"化用桃花源典故，喻当前生活如仙境，文中卢生叹与崔女相处的惬意胜过功名。
Not envying famous dukes who enjoy this life; this scenery is distinctly like Wuling spring: "Wuling spring" alludes to the Peach Blossom Spring story, metaphorically meaning current life is like a fairyland. In the text, Lu Sheng sighs that the ease of being with Miss Cui surpasses official success.

百花仙醒能留客，一面红妆恼煞人："百花仙"喻崔女，"红妆恼人"写其美貌动人，文中两人以诗句互赞，情意融融。
Hundred Flowers Immortal awake can detain guests; one glimpse of red attire is utterly captivating: "Hundred Flowers Immortal" metaphorically refers to Miss Cui; "red attire captivating" describes her captivating beauty. In the text, the two praise each other with verse, full of affection.

七辈无白衣女壻："白衣"指未做官的人，文中崔女强调家族惯例，激励卢生应试求官。
For seven generations, no white-clothed son-in-law: "White-clothed" means someone without official rank. In the text, Miss Cui emphasizes family tradition, encouraging Lu Sheng to take the exams and seek office.

紫阁金门路渺茫，上天梯有了他气长："紫阁金门"指仕途，"上天梯"喻晋升之路，文中崔女言金钱可助卢生打通官场门路。
Purple towers, golden gates, the road is vast and obscure; the ladder to heaven, with it, his spirit is long: "Purple towers, golden gates" refer to the official career path; "ladder to heaven" metaphorically means the path of promotion. In the text, Miss Cui says money can help Lu Sheng open doors in the official world.

泥金早传唱："泥金"指科举中第的喜报，文中祈盼卢生早日金榜题名，喜讯传来。
Gilt paste early proclaimed: "Gilt paste" refers to the announcement of success in the exams. In the text, it expresses the hope that Lu Sheng will soon pass the exams and the news will come.

指定衣锦还乡似阮郎：用刘晨、阮肇（阮郎）入天台遇仙后返乡的典故，喻卢生功成名就后归来，文中崔女盼卢生高中还乡。
Definitely return home in silks like Ruan Lang: Uses the story of Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao (Ruan Lang) returning home after meeting immortals in Tiantai. It metaphorically means Lu Sheng returning after achieving success and fame. In the text, Miss Cui hopes Lu Sheng will pass highly and return home.

走章台再休似前胡撞："章台"代指官场，文中崔女嘱卢生入仕后谨慎行事，勿再鲁莽。
Walking through Zhang Terrace, never again be reckless like before: "Zhang Terrace" refers to the official world. In the text, Miss Cui advises Lu Sheng to act cautiously after entering officialdom, not recklessly as before.

留着这一对画不了的愁眉待张敞：用"张敞画眉"典故，喻夫妻恩爱，文中崔女盼卢生归来后如张敞般为自己画眉，延续温情。
Keep these pair of unpaintable sorrowful brows waiting for Zhang Chang: Uses the story of "Zhang Chang painting eyebrows," symbolizing conjugal affection. In the text, Miss Cui hopes that after Lu Sheng returns, he will paint her eyebrows like Zhang Chang, continuing their warmth.

开元通宝是钱财："开元通宝"为唐代货币，文中直白点出金钱在求官中的作用，讽刺官场现实。
Kaiyuan Tongbao coins are wealth: "Kaiyuan Tongbao" was Tang Dynasty currency. In the text, it bluntly points out the role of money in seeking office, satirizing the reality of officialdom.

犹得三朝托后车，普将雷雨发萌芽："后车"喻权贵侍从，"雷雨"喻朝廷恩泽，文中宇文融以诗句自表受朝廷重用，掌科举大权。
Still able to rely on the rear carriage for three reigns, widely spreading thunder and rain to sprout buds: "Rear carriage" metaphorically means the attendants of the powerful; "thunder and rain" metaphorically means imperial favor. In the text, Yuwen Rong uses the verse to boast of being favored by the court and holding authority over the exams.

中原骏马搜求尽，谁道门生隔绛纱："骏马"喻人才，"绛纱"指权贵之门，文中宇文融自诩广揽人才，无人能隔其门路。
Central Plain's fine horses searched out exhaustively; who says disciples are separated by crimson gauze?: "Fine horses" metaphorically mean talent; "crimson gauze" refers to the gates of the powerful. In the text, Yuwen Rong boasts of widely gathering talent, and no one can block his access.

棘闱帘外："棘闱"指科举考场，文中高力士到考场附近传达御意，点明场景。
Outside the thorn enclosure's curtains: "Thorn enclosure" refers to the examination hall. In the text, Gao Lishi goes near the exam hall to convey the imperial will, setting the scene.

看上了山东卢秀才，亲看御笔题红在："题红"指皇帝朱笔点状元，文中高力士告知卢生被钦点为状元。
Took a liking to Shandong scholar Lu; personally saw the imperial vermilion brush mark red: "Mark red" means the emperor's vermilion brush designating the zhuangyuan. In the text, Gao Lishi informs Lu Sheng that he has been personally chosen as zhuangyuan by the emperor.

待剪宫袍赐绿来："赐绿"指授予官服（唐代官服以颜色分等级），文中写皇帝将赐卢生官袍，确认其功名。
Await cutting the palace robe, bestowing green coming: "Bestowing green" means granting official robes (Tang official robes were ranked by color). In the text, it writes that the emperor will bestow official robes on Lu Sheng, confirming his success.

卷首定萧、裴，怎到的寒卢那狗才：宇文融原预定萧嵩、裴光庭为状元，文中他惊叹卢生意外中选，流露不满。
The scroll's top predetermined for Xiao and Pei; how did it reach that cold Lu, that dog's offspring?: Yuwen Rong originally predetermined Xiao Song and Pei Guangting for the top spots. In the text, he exclaims in surprise at Lu Sheng's unexpected selection, revealing dissatisfaction.

他的书中有路能分拍，则道俺眼内无珠做总裁："书中有路"暗指卢生靠钻营而非文章得中，文中宇文融自嘲看走眼，实则怨其未钻刺自己。
His books have paths able to split beats; just says my eyes lack pearls, being chief examiner: "Books have paths" subtly means Lu Sheng succeeded through networking rather than essays. In the text, Yuwen Rong mocks himself for misjudging, but actually resents that Lu Sheng didn't network with him.

杏园红你知贡举的须陪待："杏园"指科举放榜后宴请新科进士的场所，文中高力士嘱宇文融主持宴饮。
Apricot Garden red, you Director of Examinations must attend: "Apricot Garden" refers to the place where new and successful candidate in the highest imperial examinations  are banqueted after the results are posted. In the text, Gao Lishi instructs Yuwen Rong to host the banquet.

外面的官儿御道上簪花那一声采："簪花"指新科进士戴花游街的礼仪，文中高力士调侃自己只能旁观助兴，凸显其宦官身份。
The officials outside, on the imperial way, inserting flowers, that one cry of admiration: "Inserting flowers" refers to the ceremony where new and successful candidate in the highest imperial examinations  wear flowers and parade through the streets. In the text, Gao Lishi jokes that he can only watch and cheer, highlighting his eunuch status.

则这黄金买身贵，不用文章中试官：直白点出官场"黄金买官"的腐败，文中宇文融叹卢生靠钻营而非文章得中状元，讽刺科举不公。
Thus, gold buys personal honor; no need for essays to pass the examiners: Bluntly points out the corruption of "buying office with gold" in officialdom. In the text, Yuwen Rong sighs that Lu Sheng became zhuangyuan through networking, not essays, satirizing the unfairness of the exams.

折桂场中开院本，插花筵上唤官身："折桂"典出"蟾宫折桂"，喻科举中第；"插花筵"指为新科进士设的宴席。文中教坊司女妓称奉旨赴宴。
In the cassia-plucking arena, performing plays; at the flower-inserting feast, summoning official courtesans: "Plucking cassia" alludes to "plucking cassia from the Toad Palace," metaphorically meaning passing the exams; "flower-inserting feast" refers to the banquet for new and successful candidate in the highest imperial examinations . In the text, female entertainers from the Music Bureau say they are summoned by decree to attend the feast.

红绫春宴饼："红绫宴"为唐代皇帝赐新科进士的宴席，"春宴饼"指宴中美食。文中宇文融回忆自己曾参与的科举喜宴。
Red silk spring feast cakes: "Red silk feast" was the banquet bestowed by the Tang emperor on new and successful candidate in the highest imperial examinations ; "spring feast cakes" refer to delicacies at the feast. In the text, Yuwen Rong recalls the celebratory exam banquet he once participated in.

走马御街游趁，雁塔标题名姓："走马御街""雁塔题名"均为唐代科举习俗，新科进士骑马游街、在大雁塔题姓名。文中卢生等人及第后依习俗行事。
Riding horses, touring the Imperial Avenue; inscribing names on the Wild Goose Pagoda: "Riding horses on the Imperial Avenue" and "inscribing names on the Wild Goose Pagoda" were both Tang Dynasty exam customs for new and successful candidate in the highest imperial examinations . In the text, Lu Sheng and others follow these customs after passing.

应图求骏马，惊代得麒麟："骏马""麒麟"均喻杰出人才，典出选拔贤才的语境。文中宇文融恭维新科进士为难得人才。
According to the chart, seeking fine horses; astonishing the age, obtaining a qilin: "Fine horses" and "qilin" both metaphorically mean outstanding talent, from the context of selecting worthy people. In the text, Yuwen Rong congratulates the new and successful candidate in the highest imperial examinations  as rare talents.

天上文星，唱好是金殿云程，玉堂风景："文星"指文曲星，喻状元；"金殿""玉堂"指朝廷官署。文中赞卢生等为文星高照，入仕显达。
Heaven's literary star; sung well are the golden hall's cloudy path, jade hall's scenery: "Literary star" refers to the deity of literature, metaphorically the zhuangyuan; "golden hall" and "jade hall" refer to court offices. In the text, it praises Lu Sheng and others as illuminated by the literary star, entering officialdom gloriously.

折桂人来，嫦娥送影："折桂"喻科举中第，"嫦娥"喻月宫仙子，暗合"蟾宫折桂"典故。文中女妓以典故贺卢生及第。
The cassia-plucker comes; Chang'e sends her shadow: "Plucking cassia" metaphorically means passing the exams; "Chang'e" metaphorically refers to the moon fairy, subtly alluding to the "plucking cassia from the Toad Palace"story. In the text, the female entertainers use the story to congratulate Lu Sheng on passing.

香飘醉墨粉红催，天子门生带笑来："天子门生"指皇帝钦点的进士，典出科举由皇帝最终定夺的制度。文中卢生题诗表明自己是皇帝直接录取。
Fragrance drifts, drunk ink, pink urges; Son of the Emperor's gate, comes with a smile: "Son of the Emperor's gate" refers to a successful candidate in the highest imperial examinations  personally chosen by the emperor, from the system where the emperor had the final say. In the text, Lu Sheng inscribes a poem stating he was directly selected by the emperor.

同登学士瀛，满把琼浆领："学士瀛"指翰林院（古称"瀛洲"），文中萧嵩、裴光庭贺卢生同入翰林。
Together ascending the scholars' Ying(isle), fully grasping receive jade nectar: "Scholars' Ying" refers to the Hanlin Academy (anciently called "Yingzhou"). In the text, Xiao Song and Pei Guangting congratulate Lu Sheng on also entering the Hanlin Academy.

御楼高接着帽檐平，撇靴尖走上头厅："御楼"指皇宫高楼，"头厅"指朝廷要职。文中宇文融祝卢生仕途高升，实则暗藏不满。
Imperial tower high meets hat brim level; flicking boot toes, walking up to the head hall: "Imperial tower" refers to the high towers of the palace; "head hall" refers to important court positions. In the text, Yuwen Rong wishes Lu Sheng promotion in his career, but actually conceals dissatisfaction.

书生白面好轻人，只道文章稳立身：暗讽书生凭文章得官却轻视权贵，文中宇文融不满卢生不依附自己，埋下报复伏笔。
Scholar, white face, fond of despising others; only says essays steadily establish oneself: Subtly satirizes scholars who gain office through essays but look down on the powerful. In the text, Yuwen Rong is dissatisfied that Lu Sheng doesn't attach himself to him, planting the seeds for revenge.

沙塞茫茫，天山直上，三千丈："天山"为西域名山，常出现在边塞题材中，喻边疆辽阔险峻。文中描绘吐蕃所处的塞外环境。
Desert frontier vast and obscure; Tianshan Mountains straight up, three thousand zhang: "Tianshan Mountains" are famous western mountains, often appearing in frontier themes, metaphorically meaning the frontier's vastness and peril. In the text, it describes the environment beyond the frontier where Tibet is situated.

龙虎班行，出将还留相："龙虎班"指文武重臣行列，"出将入相"为古代贤臣理想。文中吐蕃将相自比栋梁，显其野心。
Dragon and tiger ranked rows; exiting as general, remaining as minister: "Dragon and tiger ranks" refer to the ranks of important civil and military officials; "exiting as general, entering as minister" was the ideal for worthy ancient officials. In the text, the Tibetan generals and ministers compare themselves to pillars of the state, showing their ambition.

白草黄羊，千庐万帐，归吾掌："白草""黄羊"为塞外典型动植物，"千庐万帐"指游牧部落的营帐。文中赞普宣示对西域的掌控。
White grass, yellow sheep; a thousand huts, ten thousand tents; all return to my palm: "White grass" and "yellow sheep" are typical plants and animals beyond the frontier; "thousand huts, ten thousand tents" refers to the camps of nomadic tribes. In the text, the Tsanpo proclaims his control over the Western Regions.

气不降唐，稳坐在泥金炕："泥金炕"为游牧民族的华贵坐具，文中赞普表露出不服唐朝、自立一方的态度。
Spirit not submitting to Tang; sitting steadily on the gilt kang : "Gilt kang " is a luxurious seating platform used by nomadic peoples. In the text, the Tsanpo reveals an attitude of refusing to obey the Tang and being self-reliance.

青海湾西驾骆驼，白兰山外雪风多："青海湾""白兰山"均为西域地名，写吐蕃地域的苦寒与辽阔。文中赞普自述所处环境。
West of Kokonor Bay driving camels; beyond Bailan Mountain, much snow and wind: "Kokonor Bay" and "Bailan Mountain" are both place names in the Western Regions. It describes the harsh cold and vastness of the Tibetan territory. In the text, the Tsanpo describes his own environment.

一枝金箭催兵马，占断儿家绿玉河："金箭"为游牧民族发兵信物，"绿玉河"指西域河流。文中赞普以金箭传令，欲抢占河西之地。
A single golden arrow urges troops and horses; cutting off the children's family's Green Jade River: "Golden arrow" was a token for mobilizing troops among nomadic peoples; "Green Jade River" refers to a river in the Western Regions. In the text, the Tsanpo uses a golden arrow to issue orders, wanting to seize the Hexi region.

我国始祖秃发乌孤，曾为南凉皇帝：秃发乌孤为十六国时期南凉建立者，文中赞普追溯先祖荣光，强化部落归属感。
Our country's founding ancestor, Tufa Wugu, once was emperor of Southern Liang: Tufa Wugu was the founder of the Southern Liang during the Sixteen Kingdoms period. In the text, the Tsanpo traces back to ancestral glory, strengthening tribal identity.

家母金城公主，来作西番赞婆：金城公主为唐朝和亲吐蕃的公主，"赞婆"为吐蕃对王妃的称呼。文中借和亲背景暗示唐番关系渊源。
My mother, Princess Jincheng, came to be Tsanpo of Tubo: Princess Jincheng was a Tang princess who married into Tubo (Tibet) for peace; "Tsanpo" is the Tibetan title for the king's consort. In the text, it uses the peace marriage background to hint at the historical connection between Tang and Tibet.

先取河西，后图陇右："河西""陇右"为唐代西北边疆地区，文中吐蕃定下逐步攻占唐朝领土的策略。
First take Hexi, later plan for Longyou: "Hexi" and "Longyou" were northwestern border regions of the Tang. In the text, Tibet sets the strategy of gradually capturing Tang territory.

番鼓儿紧紧帮，番铙的点点当，汗呼呼海螺蛳吹的响："番鼓""番铙""海螺蛳"均为西域乐器，文中描绘吐蕃出兵时的军乐场景。
Barbarian drums tightly assisting; barbarian cymbals dotting and clanging; sweaty conch shells blowing loudly: "Barbarian drums," "barbarian cymbals," "conch shells" are all musical instruments from the Western Regions. In the text, it describes the military music scene when Tibetan troops set out.

令旗儿打着羌，刀尖儿点着唐："羌"代指吐蕃部落，"点着唐"直白表露出对唐朝的军事意图。文中凸显吐蕃的进攻野心。
Command flags striking the Qiang; sword points aiming at the Tang: "Qiang" refers to Tibetan tribes; "aiming at the Tang" bluntly reveals military intentions towards the Tang. In the text, it highlights Tibet's offensive ambition.

无路入天门，买断金钱谁说："天门"喻朝廷，"金钱"呼应前文以财物助卢生求官之事。文中崔女叹夫君入仕后难见，暗指当初金钱铺路的无奈。
No way to enter the heavenly gate; who speaks of buying out with money?: "Heavenly gate" metaphorically means the court; "money" echoes the earlier event of using wealth to help Lu Sheng seek office. In the text, Miss Cui sighs that it's hard to see her husband after he entered officialdom, subtly referring to the helplessness of using money to pave the way initially.

一种崔徽情绪，为断鸿愁绝：崔徽为唐代名妓，因思念情人绘像寄情，后成相思代名词；"断鸿"喻离散的夫君。文中崔女以崔徽自比，表思念之苦。
A kind of Cui Hui sentiment, for the severed goose, sorrow extraordinarily: Cui Hui was a famous Tang courtesan who drew her own portrait to send to her distant lover out of longing, later becoming a synonym for love sickness; "severed goose" metaphorically means the separated husband. In the text, Miss Cui compares herself to Cui Hui, expressing the pain of longing.

问章台人去也如天远："章台"代指官场或远行之地，典出汉代长安章台街，后常喻游宦漂泊。文中崔女叹卢生赴京后如隔天涯。
Asking, the person gone to Zhang Terrace is as far as the sky: "Zhang Terrace" refers to the official world or a distant place, from Zhang Terrace Street in Chang'an of the Han Dynasty, later often metaphorically meaning wandering in official service. In the text, Miss Cui sighs that after Lu Sheng went to the capital, he seems as far as the sky.

记当初，伴题桥捧砚亏杀卓文君：用"司马相如题桥立志""卓文君当垆卖酒"典故，喻卢生求学时崔女的资助与陪伴。文中卢生感谢崔女如卓文君般支持自己。
Remembering the beginning, accompanying question Bridge, holding the inkstone, greatly indebted to Zhuo Wenjun: Uses the story of "Sima Xiangru inscribing the bridge to express ambition" and "Zhuo Wenjun selling wine by the wine jars." It metaphorically means Miss Cui's support and companionship during Lu Sheng's studies. In the text, Lu Sheng thanks Miss Cui for supporting him like Zhuo Wenjun.

秋波得似掩花前俊，暗里丝鞭打着人："秋波"写女子柔情，"丝鞭"为古代婚嫁中女方赠男方的信物，喻情意暗许。文中崔女忆初遇时对卢生的倾心。
Autumn waves like hiding handsomeness before flowers; secretly, the silk whip strikes a person: "Autumn waves" describes a woman's tender feelings; "silk whip" was a token given by the woman to the man in ancient marriage customs, metaphorically meaning secretly promising affection. In the text, Miss Cui recalls being smitten with Lu Sheng at their first meeting.

夫人县君："县君"为古代贵族妇女封号，唐代五品官之妻可封县君。文中指崔女因卢生得官获封。
Lady County Mistress: "County Mistress" was a title for noblewomen in ancient times; in the Tang, wives of fifth-rank officials could be granted this title. In the text, it means Miss Cui received the title because of Lu Sheng's office.

则道咱书生禄米几粒太仓陈，要平白地支管着河阳运："太仓"指国家粮仓，"河阳运"指治河漕运事务。文中感叹书生本求安稳俸禄，却意外被派去凿河，暗讽官场无常。
Just thought our scholar's salary grain, a few grains from the Grand Granary's old stock; had to innocently manage the Heyang transport: "Grand Granary" refers to the state granary; "Heyang transport" refers to matters of river control and canal transport. In the text, it sighs that a scholar originally sought a stable salary but was unexpectedly sent to dig canals, subtly satirizing the unpredictability of officialdom.

禹王如在，吏民瞻拜：禹王为上古治水英雄，典出大禹治水的传说。文中卢生率民众祭拜禹王，祈求治水顺利。
If King Yu were present, officials and people would gaze and bow: King Yu was the ancient flood control hero, from the legend of Yu the Great taming the floods. In the text, Lu Sheng leads the people in worshipping King Yu, praying for success in water control.

昔禹凿三门，五行并用："三门"指黄河三门峡，传为大禹治水时凿开；"五行"为金、木、水、火、土，古代认为可助治水。文中卢生借鉴大禹治水之法。
In the past, Yu cut through Three Gates, using the Five Agents together: "Three Gates" refers to the Sanmenxia Gorge on the Yellow River, said to have been cut through by Yu the Great; "Five Agents" are metal, wood, water, fire, earth, anciently believed to aid flood control. In the text, Lu Sheng draws on Yu the Great's methods.

望梅且止三军渴：化用"望梅止渴"典故（曹操以虚指梅林止士兵口渴），文中众人见水初来，暂解干渴之苦。
Gazing at plums stops the three armies' thirst for now: Alludes to the story of "quenching thirst by looking at plums" (where Cao Cao pointed to a non-existent plum grove to stop his soldiers' thirst). In the text, the crowd sees water arriving for the first time, temporarily relieving their thirst.

当铸铁牛于河岸之上："铁牛"为古代镇水信物，唐代常铸铁牛于河边镇水患。文中卢生欲铸铁牛稳固河道，保航运安全。
Should cast iron oxen on the river banks: "Iron oxen" were ancient talismans for controlling water; in the Tang, iron oxen were often cast by rivers to control floods. In the text, Lu Sheng wants to cast iron oxen to stabilize the river course and ensure safe navigation.

插柳沿河，以添胜景："插柳"为古代治河后种柳固堤的习俗，有"柳能固沙护堤"之说。文中民众插柳纪念治水成功。
Plant willows along the river to add to the scenery: "Planting willows" was an ancient custom after river control, to stabilize the banks with willows; there was a saying "willows can fix sand and protect dykes." In the text, the people plant willows to commemorate the success of the water control.

踏破冰凌海浪，撞开积石河梁："积石河梁"指边疆冰封的河流与山梁，写老将征战环境的艰险。文中王君奐描绘自己踏冰破雪的征战生涯。
Treading through icy waves; breaking through Jishi river bridges: "Jishi river bridges" refers to frozen rivers and mountain ridges on the frontier, describing the harsh environment of the veteran general's campaigns. In the text, Wang Junhuan describes his campaigning life of treading ice and breaking snow.

坐拥貔貅胆气豪，玉门关外阵云高："貔貅"喻勇猛士兵，"玉门关"为西北边关要塞。文中凸显边疆驻军的英武与边关局势的紧张。
Sitting possessing pixiu troops, courage bold; beyond Jade Gate Pass, battle clouds are high: "Pixiu" metaphorically means fierce soldiers; "Jade Gate Pass" was a northwestern frontier fortress. In the text, it highlights the bravery of the frontier garrison and the tension of the border situation.

白头未挂封侯印，腰下长悬带血刀："封侯印"典出汉代"李广难封"的遗憾，喻功名未就；"带血刀"显征战惨烈。文中王君奐叹年老未得封侯仍征战沙场。
White head not yet hung with marquis-sealing; long suspended at the waist, a blood-stained sword: "Marquis-sealing" alludes to the regret of "Li Guang was difficult to be ennobled" in the Han, metaphorically meaning unachieved success and fame; "blood-stained sword" shows the fierceness of battle. In the text, Wang Junhuan sighs that he is old, hasn't been enfeoffed as a marquis, and still campaigns on the battlefield.

老河魁福国安邦将："河魁"为星名，主兵事，喻军中主帅。文中赞王君奐为保国安邦的主将。
Old Hekui, general who blessings the state and secures the nation: "Hekui" is a star name, presiding over military affairs, metaphorically meaning the army's commander-in-chief. In the text, it praises Wang Junhuan as the main general protecting and securing the nation.

按星宫顿开旗五方："五方旗"指按东、南、西、北、中五行方位排列的军旗，古代军阵讲究星象方位。文中写军队依星宫布阵。
According to the star palaces, suddenly unfurling flags to the five directions: "Five-direction flags" refers to army flags arranged according to the five directions (east, south, west, north, center) and the Five Agents. Ancient military formations paid attention to astrological position. In the text, it describes the army forming up according to the star palaces.

军儿走的慌，阵儿摆的长。定西番，早擒下先锋热龙莽：直白表露出击退番兵、生擒敌将的决心，文中王君奐战前立誓。
Troops walk hurry and confusingly ; formation put long. Pacifying the Western Barbarians, early capturing the vanguard Relongmang: Bluntly expresses the determination to repel the barbarian troops and capture the enemy general alive. In the text, Wang Junhuan vows before battle.

日前有书教他佯输诈败，唐兵必追，吾以生兵绕出其后：化用"诱敌深入""围魏救赵"的战术思想，文中那逻设伏兵之计破敌。
Days ago had a letter teaching him to pretend to lose and feign defeat; Tang troops will certainly pursue; I use fresh troops to circle behind them: Uses the tactical ideas of "luring the enemy deep" and "besieging Wei to rescue Zhao." In the text, Naluo sets an ambush plan to defeat the enemy.

假饶一国长空阔，尽在吾家掌握中：表露出吐蕃欲吞并唐朝领土的野心，文中番将获胜后气焰嚣张。
Even if a country is long, vast, and wide, it is entirely within my household's grasp: Reveals Tibet's ambition to annex Tang territory. In the text, the Tibetan general acts arrogantly after victory.

鸾驾即时巡幸："鸾驾"指皇帝的车驾，古代帝王出行仪仗以鸾鸟为饰，象征皇权尊贵。文中指唐玄宗东游的车驾即将到来。
The imperial carriage immediately proceeds on tour: "Imperial carriage" refers to the emperor's vehicle; ancient imperial processions were adorned with simurgh birds, symbolizing imperial dignity. In the text, it refers to Emperor Xuanzong of Tang's carriage arriving on his eastern tour soon.

曲柄红罗伞："曲柄红罗伞"是古代帝王专用仪仗之一，用于彰显皇权，文中卢生要求准备此仪仗迎驾。
Curved-handle red gauze umbrella: The "curved-handle red gauze umbrella" was one of the imperial processional items exclusively for the emperor, used to display imperial authority. In the text, Lu Sheng requests this item to be prepared to welcome the emperor.

绣岭宫：唐代行宫名，位于陕州附近，为皇帝巡幸时的驻跸之所，文中指预先备好的皇帝居所。
Xiuling Palace: Name of a Tang Dynasty traveling palace, located near Shanzhou, used as lodging during imperial tours. In the text, it refers to the pre-prepared residence for the emperor.

中貂："中貂"代指宦官，古代宦官常穿貂裘，文中指需小心应对随行的权势宦官。
Zhongdiao: "Zhongdiao" refers to eunuchs , as eunuchs often wore sable furs. In the text, it means one must carefully deal with the powerful eunuchs in the entourage.

地脉三河接，天临万乘通："三河"指黄河、淮河、洛河，"万乘"指帝王。诗句写陕州地势通达，帝王巡幸顺理成章，文末点出迎驾背景。
Earth's veins, three rivers connect; heaven approaches, ten thousand chariots pass: "Three rivers" likely refer to the Yellow, Huai, and Luo Rivers; "ten thousand chariots" refers to the emperor. The verse describes Shanzhou's accessible terrain, making an imperial tour logical. At the end of the text, it points out the background of welcoming the emperor.

雨师洒道，风伯清尘："雨师""风伯"为古代神话中的雨神和风神，典出《山海经》等古籍。文中卢生以神话典故称帝王出行时风雨相助，渲染祥瑞氛围。
Rain Master sprinkles the road; Wind Earl clears the dust: "Rain Master" and "Wind Earl" are the rain and wind deities in ancient mythology, from classics like the Classic of Mountains and Seas. In the text, Lu Sheng uses mythological story to say that wind and rain assist the emperor's journey, creating an auspicious atmosphere.

春日迟迟春草绿，野棠开尽飘香玉。绣岭宫前鹤发翁，犹唱开元太平曲：卢生引用的诗句，描绘绣岭宫春景与太平景象，呼应唐玄宗巡幸，既怀旧又颂扬开元盛世。
Spring days drawn out, spring grass green; wild crabapples bloom fully, drifting fragrant jade. Before Xiuling Palace, a crane-haired old man still sings the Kaiyuan peace tune: Verses quoted by Lu Sheng, describing the spring scenery and peaceful scene at Xiuling Palace, echoing Emperor Xuanzong's tour, both nostalgic and praising the Kaiyuan golden age.

洛浦凌波：化用曹植《洛神赋》"凌波微步，罗袜生尘"，写洛神在洛水轻盈漫步的典故。文中形容棹歌女身姿轻盈美好。
Luo River's wave: Alludes to Cao Zhi's "Rhapsody on the Goddess of the Luo River": "Treading the waves with light steps, silk stockings raising dust," describing the story of the goddess lightly walking on the Luo River. In the text, it describes the boat-song girls' graceful and beautiful figures.

汉女明妆：化用汉水女神的传说（如《诗经·周南·汉广》），指汉水女神妆容明艳。文中与"洛浦凌波"共赞采女娇美。
Han River girl's bright attire: Alludes to the legend of the Han River goddess (e.g., in the Book of Songs, "Odes of Zhou and the South, Han Guang"), meaning the Han River goddess's bright and beautiful attire. In the text, together with "Luo River's wave," it praises the shearer's beauty.

李冰镇蜀，立石兕于江流：李冰为战国时蜀郡太守，治水时立石犀（石兕）镇伏水怪，典出《华阳国志》。文中以李冰治水典故对比卢生铸铁牛镇河，突显其功绩。
Li Bing pacified Shu, erected stone rhinoceroses in the river flow: Li Bing was governor of Shu Commandery in the Warring States period; when controlling water, he erected stone rhinoceroses to subdue water monsters, from the Records of Huayang. In the text, it uses Li Bing's water control story to contrast with Lu Sheng casting iron oxen to control the river, highlighting his achievement.

张骞凿空，饮牵郎于汉渚：张骞通西域被称为"凿空"（《史记》）；"牵郎"传为张骞治水时相关典故。文中借古喻今，赞卢生开河之功堪比张骞通西域。
Zhang Qian forced, drank with Qian Lang at the Han islet: Zhang Qian's opening of the Western Regions was called " forced" (hollowing out, pioneering) in the Records of the Grand Historian; "Qian Lang" is reportedly related to a story of Zhang Qian controlling water. In the text, it uses the past to illustrate the present, praising Lu Sheng's canal-digging achievement as comparable to Zhang Qian's opening of the Western Regions.

甘棠召：典出《诗经·召南·甘棠》，召公曾在甘棠树下理政，后人怀念而护树。文中将卢生修的柳堤比作甘棠，赞其政绩被百姓铭记。
Gan Tang summons: From the Book of Songs, "Odes of Zhao and the South, Gan Tang." Duke of Zhao once administered government under a gan tang tree, and later generations cherished and protected the tree in his memory. In the text, it compares the willow embankment built by Lu Sheng to the gan tang, praising his administrative achievements being remembered by the people.

河清照：化用"河清海晏"（黄河水清喻天下太平），文中赞裴光庭的《铁牛颂》如河清般彰显太平盛世。
River clear shines: Adapts "river clear, sea calm" (the Yellow River running clear symbolizes peace under heaven). In the text, it praises Pei Guangting's "Ode to the Iron Oxen" as shining like a clear river, displaying the peaceful age.

禹凿鸿碑：指大禹治水后立碑记功的传说。文中将卢生开河功绩与大禹相比，突显其功业卓著。
Yu's carving of the great stele: Refers to the legend of Yu the Great erecting a stele to record his achievements after controlling the floods. In the text, it compares Lu Sheng's canal-digging achievement to Yu the Great's, highlighting his outstanding accomplishment.

阳关唱好：化用"阳关三叠"（古送别曲），"阳关"为西域要塞。文中指卢生出征西域，期望其建功立业。
Yang Pass sings well: Alludes to "Three Refrains of Yang Pass" (an ancient farewell song); "Yang Pass" was a fortress in the Western Regions. In the text, it refers to Lu Sheng's expedition to the Western Regions, expecting him to achieve merit and establish himself.

一天明月大刀头："大刀头"为古代隐语，"刀头"有环（"环"谐"还"），暗指还家。文末以诗句表达崔氏盼卢生归来的思念。
One sky bright moon, big knife's head: "Big knife's head" was ancient slang; the knife's head has a ring ("ring" homophonous with "return"), secretly meaning returning home. At the end of the text, it uses the verse to express Lady Cui's longing for Lu Sheng's return.

三十登坛众所尊，红旗半卷出辕门。前军已战交河北，直斩楼兰报国恩："斩楼兰"典出《汉书·傅介子传》，楼兰为古代西域国名，曾反复归附又背叛汉朝，傅介子奉命刺杀楼兰王。后以"斩楼兰"喻杀敌报国、建功立业。文中卢生引诗句表出征报国之志。
Thirty, ascending the altar, respected by all; red flags half-furled, exiting the camp gate. The forward army has already fought north of the Jiao River; straightaway beheading Loulan to repay the state's grace: "Beheading Loulan" alludes to the Biography of Fu Jiezi in the Book of Han. Loulan was an ancient kingdom in the Western Regions that repeatedly submitted to and betrayed the Han. Fu Jiezi was ordered to assassinate the king of Loulan. Later, "beheading Loulan" came to mean killing the enemy to serve the country and achieving merit. In the text, Lu Sheng quotes the verse to express his ambition to campaign and serve the country.

御沟红叶之计：典出唐代传说，宫女在红叶上题诗，顺御沟（皇宫排水沟）流出，被士人拾得，后成传递情意或信息的象征。文中卢生仿此计，以树叶刺字传谣，借流水送入番营，假托"天神所使"离间番王与丞相。
The scheme of the Imperial Ditch's red leaves: From a Tang Dynasty legend where a palace maid wrote a poem on a red leaf which floated down the imperial ditch (palace drain) and was picked up by a scholar, later becoming a symbol for conveying affection or messages. In the text, Lu Sheng imitates this scheme, carving words on leaves to spread rumors, sending them into the barbarian camp via flowing water, falsely claiming to be "sent by the heavenly god" to sow discord between the barbarian king and his minister.

紫塞长驱飞虎豹，拥貔貅万里咆哮："貔貅"为古代传说中猛兽，喻勇猛军队，常用来形容精锐之师。文中指卢生率领的大军勇猛善战，长驱边塞。
Purple Frontier long drive, flying tigers and leopards; possessing pixiu, roaring for ten thousand miles: "Pixiu" are legendary fierce beasts, metaphorically meaning brave armies, often used to describe elite troops. In the text, it refers to the brave and skilled army led by Lu Sheng, driving deep into the frontier.

日落辕门鼓角鸣，千群面缚出番城。洗兵鱼海云迎阵，秣马龙堆月照营："洗兵"典出《旧唐书·高骈传》"洗兵海岛，刷马江洲"，指洗净兵器，准备凯旋；"鱼海""龙堆"均为西域地名，代指边疆战场。诗句描绘大军凯旋、边塞安营的场景。
Sunset, camp gate drums and horns sound; a thousand groups, bound faces, exit the barbarian city. Washing weapons at Fish Sea, clouds greet the array; feeding horses at Dragon Mound, moon illuminates the camp: "Washing weapons" alludes to Gao Pian's biography in the Old Book of Tang: "washing weapons on the sea island, grooming horses on the river isle," meaning cleaning weapons in preparation for triumphant return; "Fish Sea" and "Dragon Mound" are both place names in the Western Regions, representing the frontier battlefield. The verses depict the scene of the army's triumphant return and camping on the frontier.

莫教飞鸟尽，留取报恩环："飞鸟尽，良弓藏"典出《史记·越王勾践世家》，范蠡劝文种功成身退之语，喻功成后功臣遭弃；"报恩环"化用"苏武持节归汉"意象，文中指番将求卢生留其生路，勿赶尽杀绝。
Do not let the flying birds be exhausted; keep the gratitude-repaying ring: "Flying birds exhausted, good bow stored" alludes to the Family of Goujian, King of Yue in the Records of the Grand Historian, where Fan Li advised Wen Zhong to retire after success, metaphorically meaning meritorious officials are discarded after success; "gratitude-repaying ring" adapts the imagery of "Su Wu returning to Han holding his ceremonial staff." In the text, it means the barbarian general begs Lu Sheng to spare his life, not to exterminate them completely.

空留一片石，万古在天山：引用古诗，"天山片石"常为边疆战功纪功碑的象征，文中指自古征战者在天山留碑记功的传统。
Vainly leaving one piece of stone, for ten thousand ages on the Tianshan Mountains: Quotes an ancient poem. "Tianshan piece of stone" often symbolizes frontier victory steles. In the text, it refers to the tradition of campaigners since ancient times leaving steles on the Tianshan to record achievements.

勒石而还："勒石"典出《后汉书·窦宪传》，窦宪破北匈奴后在燕然山刻石记功，后以"勒石燕然"指建立不朽战功。文中卢生在天山刻石记功，效仿古代名将。
Inscribing stone and returning: "Inscribing stone" alludes to the Biography of Dou Xian in the Book of the Later Han. After defeating the Northern Xiongnu, Dou Xian inscribed a stone on Mount Yanran to record his achievement. Later, "inscribing stone at Yanran" came to mean establishing immortal military merits. In the text, Lu Sheng inscribes a stone on the Tianshan to record his achievement, emulating ancient famous generals.

霍飘姚：指霍去病，西汉名将，官至骠骑将军，封冠军侯，以抗击匈奴著称，文中以霍去病喻卢生战功卓著。
Huo Piaoyao: Refers to Huo Qubing, a famous Western Han general who reached the rank of Swift Cavalry General, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Champion, and was renowned for fighting the Xiongnu. In the text, Huo Qubing is used metaphorically for Lu Sheng's outstanding military achievements.

汉班超：指班超，东汉名将，出使西域，平定诸国，封定远侯，文中以班超喻卢生在西域的开拓功绩。
Han Banchao: Refers to Ban Chao, a famous Eastern Han general who was sent to the Western Regions, pacified various states, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingyuan. In the text, Ban Chao is used metaphorically for Lu Sheng's pioneering achievements in the Western Regions.

没字碑：指武则天无字碑，虽无文字却功过留待后人评说。文中指即使碑无文字，卢生的功绩也会被铭记。
Wordless stele: Refers to Wu Zetian's wordless stele, which, though without words, leaves her merits and faults for later generations to judge. In the text, it means even if the stele has no words, Lu Sheng's achievements will be remembered.

昔日崔徽今又徽：崔徽为唐代名妓，因思念情人绘像寄情，后成为相思的代名词。文中崔女以崔徽自比，表对卢生的深切思念。
Formerly Cui Hui, now again Hui: Cui Hui was a famous Tang courtesan who drew her portrait out of longing for her lover, later becoming a synonym for lovesickness. In the text, Lady Cui compares herself to Cui Hui, expressing deep longing for Lu Sheng.

去时儿女悲，归来笳鼓竞：化用离别与凯旋的场景，"儿女悲"写离别之伤感，"笳鼓竞"写归来之喜庆。文中烘托卢生出征时的牵挂与凯旋时的热闹。
Leaving, children sorrow; returning, reed pipes and drums compete: Uses scenes of departure and triumphant return; "children sorrow" describes the sadness of departure; "reed pipes and drums compete" describes the joy of return. In the text, it enhances the concern at Lu Sheng's departure and the excitement at his triumphant return.

何如霍去病：霍去病为西汉名将，多次率军击败匈奴，战功赫赫，封冠军侯。文中以霍去病喻卢生，赞其征战有功，堪比古代名将。
How compared to Huo Qubing?: Huo Qubing was a famous Western Han general who led armies to defeat the Xiongnu multiple times, achieving great military success, enfeoffed as Marquis of Champion. In the text, Huo Qubing is used metaphorically for Lu Sheng, praising his successful campaigning, comparable to ancient famous generals.

四马车才下的这东华路："东华路"指皇宫东华门附近道路，为官员上朝必经之路，文中写宇文融在官场权势显赫，官员纷纷俯伏。
Four-horse carriage just descended this Donghua Road: "Donghua Road" refers to the road near the Donghua Gate of the palace, which officials must take to attend court. In the text, it describes Yuwen Rong's powerful position in officialdom, with officials bowing down to him.

平章两字何如："平章"为古代官名，"同平章事"即宰相，文中萧嵩感叹与卢生同任宰相的处境。
How about the two characters 'Pingzhang'?: "Pingzhang" was an ancient official title; "Tong Pingzhang Shi" meant chancellor. In the text, Xiao Song sighs over the situation of being chancellor alongside Lu Sheng.

千真万真，既不呵，得了番书，合当奏上："番书"指番将热龙莽的书信，宇文融以此为据诬告卢生通番，文中凸显其构陷之心。
A thousand truths, ten thousand truths; if not, then having obtained the barbarian letter, ought to memorialize it: "Barbarian letter" refers to the letter from the barbarian general Relongmang. Yuwen Rong uses this as evidence to falsely accuse Lu Sheng of colluding with the barbarians. In the text, it highlights his intention to frame.

你敢教三声不押花字么："押花字"指在公文上签字画押，文中宇文融以权势逼迫萧嵩在诬告奏折上签字。
Do you dare to say three times you won't affix your flowery signature?: "Affixing flowery signature" means signing and sealing a document. In the text, Yuwen Rong uses his power to force Xiao Song to sign the false accusation memorial.

添你一个'通同卖国'四字：宇文融威胁萧嵩，若不签字便诬陷其同谋，显官场倾轧之狠。
Add four characters for you: 'colluding and selling out the country': Yuwen Rong threatens Xiao Song that if he doesn't sign, he will accuse him of being an accomplice, showing the ruthlessness of officialdom intrigue.

花押上一字之下，加他两点，做个不忠二字：萧嵩以巧妙改花押表"不忠"，暗藏对诬告的不满，为后续翻案留伏笔，体现其隐忍与智术。
Below one character of the flowery signature, add two dots for him, making the two characters 'disloyal': Xiao Song cleverly alters his signature to read "disloyal," secretly expressing dissatisfaction with the false accusation, leaving foreshadowing for later reversal, showing his forbearance and cleverness.

鸳鸯瓦为何而碎："鸳鸯瓦"为古代宫殿或豪宅屋顶的成对瓦片，象征夫妻和睦，文中瓦碎暗喻卢生夫妇即将遭遇变故。
Why did the mandarin duck tiles break?: "Mandarin duck tiles" were paired tiles on ancient palace or mansion roofs, symbolizing marital harmony. In the text, the broken tiles metaphorically hints the Lu couple face misfortune soon.

乌鸦知风，虫蚁知雨：古谚，指动物能感知自然变化，常用来预兆人事吉凶，文中崔氏以碎瓦、金弹等异象预感灾祸。
Crows know the wind; insects and ants know the rain: An old proverb meaning animals can sense natural changes, often used to portend human fortune or misfortune. In the text, Lady Cui uses omens like broken tiles and golden pellets to forecast disaster.

佩玉鸣金宰相家："佩玉鸣金"指官员佩戴的玉器与金饰，行走时发声，喻高官身份，文中写卢生身为宰相的显赫。
Jade pendants chiming, golden ornaments ringing, the chancellor's household: "Jade pendants chiming, golden ornaments ringing" refers to the jade and gold ornaments worn by officials that make sound when walking, metaphorically meaning high official status. In the text, it describes Lu Sheng's prominence as chancellor.

圣旨着擒拿，奏发中书到门下："中书""门下"为唐代三省中的中枢机构，掌政令草拟与审核，文中指宇文融通过中枢机构下发捉拿卢生的圣旨。
Imperial decree orders arrest; memorial sent from the Secretariat to the Chancellery: "Secretariat" and "Chancellery" were central organs among the Three Departments in the Tang, responsible for drafting and reviewing government orders. In the text, it means Yuwen Rong issued the imperial decree for Lu Sheng's arrest through the central organs.

明正典刑：指依照法律公开处决，文中指卢生被判公开处斩，凸显罪名之重。
Openly applying the canonical punishments: Means public execution according to the law. In the text, it means Lu Sheng was sentenced to public beheading, highlighting the severity of the charge.

牵这些业畜，午门前叫冤："午门"为皇宫正门，古代常在此喊冤申诉，文中崔氏领子女到午门鸣冤，求皇帝宽恕。
Leading these karmic beasts, crying injustice before the Meridian Gate: "Meridian Gate" was the main gate of the palace, where people often appealed injustices in ancient times. In the text, Lady Cui leads her children to the Meridian Gate to proclaim their injustice, begging the emperor for mercy.

云阳市风流洒角："云阳市"为古代著名刑场（今河南云阳），常用来代指处决之地，文中指卢生将被押赴刑场。
Yunyang Market, dashing sprinkling corners: "Yunyang Market" was a famous execution ground in ancient times (modern Yunyang, Henan), often used to refer to the place of execution. In the text, it means Lu Sheng will be taken to the execution ground.

鬼门关安置："鬼门关"为古代广南险恶之地（今广西北流），喻极偏远艰苦的流放地，文中指卢生被贬至绝境。
Guimen Pass arranging for: "Guimen Pass" was a perilous place in ancient Guangnan (modern Beiliu, Guangxi), metaphorically meaning an extremely remote and harsh place of exile. In the text, it means Lu Sheng was exiled to a desperate place.

淮阴胯：化用"韩信受胯下之辱"典故，文中卢生感叹自己如韩信般遭冤屈，暗指萧嵩或如萧何般未能相救。
Huaiyin's crotch: Alludes to the story of "Han Xin suffering the humiliation under the crotch." In the text, Lu Sheng laments being wronged like Han Xin, subtly implying that Xiao Song, like Xiao He, failed to save him.

望夫山立着化："望夫山"为传说中女子盼夫不归化而为山的故事，文中卢生怕崔氏过度悲伤。
Awaiting Husband Mountain stands transformed: "Awaiting Husband Mountain" is the story of a woman who waited for her husband until she turned into a mountain. In the text, Lu Sheng fears Lady Cui will be overly grief-stricken.

无雁处海天涯："雁"常喻书信传递，"无雁处"指偏远到无法通信之地，文中写卢生流放之地的隔绝荒凉。
No wild goose place, sea, sky's edge: "Wild goose" often metaphorically means letter delivery; "no wild goose place" means a place so remote communication is impossible. In the text, it describes the isolation and desolation of Lu Sheng's place of exile.

口里蜜，腹中刀：俗语，喻表面和善而内心阴险，文中形容宇文融的奸猾本性。
Honey in the mouth, knife in the belly: A proverb meaning surface is kind but inward is sinister. In the text, it describes Yuwen Rong's treacherous nature.

一万重烟瘴怎生逃："烟瘴"指南方湿热多瘴气的环境，文中宇文融盼卢生在流放地难以存活。
Ten thousand layers of miasma, how to escape?: "Miasma" refers to the damp, hot, miasma-filled environment of the south. In the text, Yuwen Rong hopes Lu Sheng cannot survive in the place of exile.

鬼门关：古代广南险恶之地（今广西北流），喻绝境，文中指宇文融认为卢生流放至此必死。
Guimen Pass: A perilous place in ancient Guangnan (modern Beiliu, Guangxi), metaphorically meaning a desperate situation. In the text, it means Yuwen Rong believes Lu Sheng will certainly die exiled here.

没为官婢：古代法律规定，罪犯家属可被收为官府奴婢，文中指宇文融奏请将崔氏没入官府服役。
Confiscated to become government slaves: Ancient law stipulated that family members of criminals could be confiscated as government slaves. In the text, it means Yuwen Rong memorializes to have Lady Cui confiscated into government service.

外机坊织作："机坊"为古代官办纺织作坊，文中指崔氏被罚到官办作坊织布。
Outer Weaving Workshop weaving: "Weaving Workshop" was a government-run textile workshop in ancient times. In the text, it means Lady Cui is punished to weave in a government workshop.

五城使：唐代负责京城治安的官员，文中指宇文融派京城巡捉使执行抓捕。
Five Cities Commissioner: Official responsible for capital security in the Tang. In the text, it means Yuwen Rong sends the Capital Patrol and Arrest Commissioner to carry out the arrest.

吏部纪录：古代吏部记录官员功绩以备升迁，文中宇文融以"记功"奖赏执行命令的官员。
Ministry of Personnel records: The Ministry of Personnel recorded officials' achievements for potential promotion. In the text, Yuwen Rong uses "recording merit" to reward the officials carrying out the orders.

脸上几根毛，僭号"鬼头刀"："鬼头刀"为古代行刑刀具，因刀头刻鬼形得名，文中贼匪以"鬼头刀"为绰号，显其凶悍。
A few hairs on the face, usurping the name "Ghost-Head Sword": "Ghost-Head Sword" was an ancient executioner's sword, named for the ghost head carved on the pommel. In the text, bandits use "Ghost-Head Sword" as a nickname, showing their fierceness.

混名"下剔上"：贼匪自解绰号意为"从颏下剔到头上"，形容其凶残，遇反抗便下杀手。
Mixed name "Slice Below to Above": The bandits explain the nickname means "slicing from under the chin to the top of the head," describing their cruelty, killing anyone who resists.

瘴母：指南方山林中致人患病的毒瘴气团，文中卢生遇"瘴母"，写流放地环境险恶。
Miasma mother: Refers to toxic miasma clouds in southern forests that cause illness. In the text, Lu Sheng encounters "miasma mother," describing the dangerous environment of the place of exile.

扑赵盾、小神獒：典出《左传》，晋灵公派猛犬（神獒）刺杀赵盾，文中卢生以"神獒"喻猛虎，怕遭伤害。
Pouncing on Zhao Dun, little Divine Ao: From the Zuo Zhuan, where Duke Ling of Jin sent a fierce dog (Divine Ao) to assassinate Zhao Dun. In the text, Lu Sheng uses "Divine Ao" metaphorically for a fierce tiger, fearing harm.

乌艚还是白艚："艚"指载货大船，"乌艚""白艚"为不同船型，文中写卢生遇船求救，显逃亡之险。
Black cargo ship or white cargo ship?: "Cargo ship" refers to large cargo vessels; "black cargo ship" and "white cargo ship" are different types. In the text, it describes Lu Sheng encountering a ship and crying for help , showing the danger of his escape.

鲸鱼晒翅：古代传说鲸鱼常跃出海面"晒翅"，喻海上巨浪或危险，文中写行船遇鲸鱼，突显海难之危。
Whale drying its wings: Ancient legend says whales often leap out of the water to "dry their wings," metaphorically meaning huge waves or danger at sea. In the text, it describes encountering a whale while sailing, highlighting the peril of shipwreck.

鬼门关：古代广南险恶之地（今广西北流），文中指卢生流放的绝境，关口题字"鬼门关"加剧绝望感。
Guimen Pass: A perilous place in ancient Guangnan (modern Beiliu, Guangxi). In the text, it refers to the desperate place of Lu Sheng's exile; the inscription "Guimen Pass" at the pass intensifies the sense of despair.

四德狗子：蛮户对护院狗的戏称，称其"咬贼、咬兽、咬鼠、咬鬼"四德，文中写卢生借狗防鬼，显处境凄凉。
Four-Virtue doggie: A mocking name used by native households for guard dogs, said to have the four virtues of "biting thieves, beasts, rats, and ghosts." In the text, it describes Lu Sheng using a dog to ward off ghosts, showing his wretched situation.

老平章到头的受用了："平章"指宰相，文中自嘲昔日宰相竟落得靠黑鬼抬上碉房的下场，暗含辛酸与讽刺。
Old Pingzhang finally gets to enjoy it: "Pingzhang" means chancellor. In the text, it self-mockingly says the former chancellor ends up being carried up to a watchtower by black ghosts, containing bitterness and satire.

苏妻织锦回文：东晋窦滔妻苏蕙，因丈夫被贬流沙，织《璇玑图》回文诗以寄思念，可从正反、横竖等多角度诵读，表达深情。见《晋书·列女传·窦滔妻苏氏》。文中卢夫人欲学苏妻织回文锦表白冤情。
Su's wife weaving brocade palindrome: Su Hui, wife of Dou Tao of the Eastern Jin, wove the "Xuanji Tu" palindrome poem out of longing when her husband was exiled to Liusha. It could be read from multiple angles (forward, backward, vertically, etc.), expressing deep feeling. See Jin Shu, Biographies of Exemplary Women, Wife of Dou Tao. In the text, Lady Lu wants to learn from Su's wife to weave a palindrome brocade to proclaim her injustice.

"宣威沙漠，臣伏戎羌"：出自《千字文》。原句描述朝廷声威远播沙漠，外族臣服归顺之意。文中指犒赏夷人的锦段字号。
"Displaying power in the desert, submitting the Rong and Qiang": From the Thousand Character Classic. The original line describes the court's prestige spreading far into the desert, and foreign tribes submitting. In the text, it refers to the brocade patterns used to reward the barbarians.

"抛残红泪湿窗纱，织就龟文献内家。但得丝纶天上落，犹如锦上再添花"：未明确见于经典古籍，为剧中结尾诗句。原句大意：洒下的泪水打湿窗纱，织成珍贵的锦缎献给宫中；若能得到朝廷的旨意（赦免或重用），便如同锦缎上再添花朵般美好。
"Scattered remnant red tears wet the window gauze; woven into tortoise-shell patterns presented to the inner court. If only the silken threads from heaven would fall, it would be like adding flowers to brocade": Not clearly found in classical texts; it is a concluding verse from the play. General meaning: Shed tears wet the window gauze; woven into precious brocade presented to the palace; if only an imperial decree (pardon or reuse) could be obtained, it would be like adding flowers to brocade.

南冠君子：指囚犯或战俘。《左传·成公九年》记载，晋侯在军府见到钟仪，问"南冠而絷者，谁也"，钟仪是被俘的楚国官员，他每天戴着楚国的帽子面南而站。后以"南冠君子"泛称囚犯。李白《流夜郎闻酺不预》中有"北阙圣人歌太康，南冠君子窜遐荒"，此处"南冠君子"指被流放的自己。
Southern Cap Gentleman: Refers to a prisoner or prisoner of war. According to Zuo Zhuan, Duke Cheng Year 9, the Marquis of Jin saw Zhong Yi in the army storehouse and asked, "Who is the one wearing a southern cap and bound?" Zhong Yi was a captured Chu official who wore his Chu cap daily and stood facing south. Later, "Southern Cap Gentleman" came to mean prisoner in general. Li Bai's poem contains the line "Northern Que sages sing of Taikang, Southern Cap gentlemen flee to distant wastes." Here, "Southern Cap Gentleman" refers to his exiled self.

汉诏：指汉朝的诏书，这里代指皇帝的命令。原句"忽然汉诏还冠冕"意思是突然收到皇帝的命令，恢复官员的冠冕（即恢复官职）。
Han decree: Refers to a Han Dynasty decree, here standing for the emperor's command. The original line "Suddenly a Han decree returns the cap and crown" means suddenly receiving an imperial command to restore the official's cap and crown (i.e., restore his office).

鸳鹭：原指鸳鸯和鹭鸶，常比喻朝官。"计日应随鸳鹭行"意思是预计不久就会跟随朝官们一起上朝。
Mandarin ducks and egrets: Originally refer to mandarin ducks and egrets, often metaphorically meaning court officials. "Counting the days, should follow the mandarin duck and egret procession" means expecting soon to follow the court officials to audience.

云阳市：古代杀人的刑场，在长安东南。常用来代指死刑。此处"云阳市别了妻男"指卢生流放前与家人分离，如同面临刑场之别。
Yunyang Market: Ancient execution ground, southeast of Chang'an. Often used to refer to execution. Here, "Parting from wife and children at Yunyang Market" means Lu Sheng separating from his family before exile, like facing execution.

凤凰池：原指禁苑中的池沼，后多代指宰相办公的地方。此处"向凤凰池洗净征衫"指卢生重回相位，洗去流放的风尘。
Phoenix Pool: Originally a pond in the imperial park, later often referred to the place where the chancellor worked. Here, "Towards the Phoenix Pool, washing clean the campaign gown" means Lu Sheng returning to his post as chancellor, washing off the dust of exile.

举头红日近，回首白云低：出自寇准《咏华山》。原句为"只有天在上，更无山与齐。举头红日近，回首白云低。"原句意思是抬头看太阳离得很近，回头看白云显得很低，描绘华山之高。此处引用以抒发卢生回京时的心境。
Raising head, red sun near; turning head, white clouds low: From Kou Zhun's "Ode to Mount Hua." Original lines: "Only heaven is above, no mountain is its equal. Raising head, red sun near; turning head, white clouds low." The original meaning is looking up, the sun seems very close; looking back, the clouds seem very low, depicting Mount Hua's height. Here it is quoted to express Lu Sheng's state of mind upon returning to the capital.

夜白飞黄：指良马。"夜白"是唐太宗的名马，"飞黄"是传说中的神马，能乘云而飞。《淮南子·览冥训》有"青龙进驾，飞黄伏皂"。此处指皇帝赏赐给卢府的骏马。
Ye Bai and Fei Huang: Refer to fine horses. "Ye Bai" was a famous horse of Emperor Taizong of Tang; "Fei Huang" is a legendary divine horse that could ride on clouds and fly. The Huainanzi mentions "Green dragon advances the carriage, Fei Huang serves at the trough." Here it refers to the fine horses bestowed by the emperor upon the Lu household.

金谷名园：指西晋石崇的金谷园，以奢华著称，在洛阳西北。石崇曾在此宴客游乐，后常以"金谷园"代指豪华园林。此处"更有金谷名园胜洛阳"指卢府的园林比洛阳的金谷园还要奢华。
Golden Valley famous garden: Refers to Shi Chong's Golden Valley Garden of the Western Jin, famous for its luxury, northwest of Luoyang. Shi Chong entertained guests there. Later, "Golden Valley Garden" often referred to luxurious gardens. Here, "Furthermore, the Golden Valley famous garden surpasses Luoyang" means the Lu household's garden is even more luxurious than the Golden Valley Garden in Luoyang.

人逢开口笑，花插满头归：出自杜牧《九日齐山登高》。原句为"尘世难逢开口笑，菊花须插满头归"。原句意思是人世间难得有开怀大笑的时候，应当把菊花插满头上尽兴而归。此处引用以表现众人的愉悦情态。
People meet, open mouths laugh; flowers inserted fill heads, return: From Du Mu's "Climbing Mount Qi on the Ninth Day." Original lines: "The mortal world seldom sees open-mouthed laughter; chrysanthemums must be inserted to fill the head upon return." The original meaning is that it's rare to have a good laugh in the world, one should insert chrysanthemums all over one's head and return merrily. Here it is quoted to show the joyful mood of the crowd.

压沙堤：唐代长安朱雀门外的道路，为宰相出入的通道。因地势高，每逢下雨，宰相仪仗行过无泥，故称"沙堤"。后常以"压沙堤"代指宰相的荣耀。此处"压沙堤，归软马"指卢生身为宰相，荣耀归府。
Pressing the Sand Dyke: The road outside the Zhuque Gate in Chang'an during the Tang, used by the chancellor. Because of its high elevation, when it rained, the chancellor's procession could pass without mud, hence the name "Sand Dyke." Later, "pressing the Sand Dyke" often referred to the chancellor's glory. Here, "Pressing the Sand Dyke, returning on a soft horse" means Lu Sheng, as chancellor, returns home gloriously.

列桂捧琼觞："列桂"指科举登第者，此处代指卢生的儿子们；"琼觞"指玉杯。全句意为儿子们捧着玉杯向父母敬酒。
Arrayed cassia holders raising jade cups: "Arrayed cassia holders" refers to those who passed the exams, here meaning Lu Sheng's sons; "jade cups" are jade wine cups. The whole line means the sons raise jade cups to toast their parents.

皓齿蛾眉，乃伐性之斧：出自《吕氏春秋·本生》"靡曼皓齿，郑卫之音，务以自乐，命之曰伐性之斧"。原句意思是美丽的容貌和淫靡的音乐，会损害人的本性，如同砍伐生命的斧头。
White teeth and moth eyebrows are axes that hew at nature: From Lüshi Chunqiu, "Ben Sheng": "Luxuriant beauty, white teeth, the music of Zheng and Wei, devoted to self-pleasure, are called axes that hew at nature." The original meaning is that beautiful features and decadent music damage one's nature, like an axe hewing at life.

五色令人目盲，五音令人耳聋：出自《老子》第十二章。原句意思是过多的色彩会让人眼睛失明，过多的声音会让人耳朵失聪，强调摒弃外物诱惑。
The five colors make one's eyes blind; the five notes make one's ears deaf: From Laozi, Chapter 12. The original meaning is that too many colors blind the eyes, too many sounds deafen the ears, emphasizing rejecting external temptations.

却之不恭：出自《孟子·万章下》"却之却之为不恭"。原句意思是拒绝对方的馈赠或邀请，显得不恭敬。此处指卢生不便拒绝皇帝赏赐的女乐。
To decline it would be disrespectful: From Mencius, Wan Zhang Part II: "To decline and decline it is disrespectful." The original meaning is that refusing a gift or invitation from someone appears disrespectful. Here it means Lu Sheng finds it inconvenient to refuse the female musicians bestowed by the emperor.

舞霓裳：指《霓裳羽衣舞》，唐代著名宫廷乐舞，相传为唐玄宗所作。此处指女乐表演的舞蹈。
Dancing Nichang: Refers to the "Rainbow and Feather Garment Dance," a famous Tang court dance, said to be composed by Emperor Xuanzong of Tang. Here it means the dance performed by the female musicians.

残梦到黄粱：化用"黄粱一梦"典故（见《太平广记》卷八十二引《异闻集·吕翁》），原指虚幻的梦境，此处为乐工演唱的误语，后改口"残韵绕虹梁"。
Remnant dream reaches the yellow millet: Alludes to the "yellow millet dream"story (see Taiping Guangji, Vol. 82, quoting Yìwén Jí, Lü Weng), originally meaning an illusory dream. Here it is a slip of the tongue by the musician singing, later corrected to "remnant melody encircles the rainbow beam."

夜夜笙歌归院落，朝朝灯火下楼台：化用白居易《长恨歌》"骊宫高处入青云，仙乐风飘处处闻。缓歌慢舞凝丝竹，尽日君王看不足"意境，原句描绘宫廷享乐场景，此处指卢府日夜宴乐的奢华生活。
Nightly, playing and singing return to the courtyard; morningly, lanterns and torches descend the towers: Adapts the mood from Bai Juyi's "Song of Everlasting Sorrow": "Li Palace high enters the blue clouds; immortal music wind-borne heard everywhere. Slow songs, gentle dances congeal strings and bamboo; all day the monarch cannot see enough." The original describes courtly pleasure; here it refers to the luxurious life of nightly banquets and music at the Lu residence.

黄阁：指宰相办公的官署。汉代丞相、太尉等官署用黄色涂门，故称"黄阁"。后常以"黄阁"代指宰相职位。此处"生意尽凭黄阁下"指卢生身为宰相，政务全凭他决断。
Yellow Chamber: Refers to the chancellor's office. The offices of the Chancellor and Grand Commandant in the Han were painted yellow, hence the name "Yellow Chamber." Later, "Yellow Chamber" often referred to the chancellor's position. Here, "All business depends on beneath the Yellow Chamber" means Lu Sheng, as chancellor, decides all government affairs.

玉堂：指翰林院或宰相办公的地方，因玉堂清贵，常代指高官职位。此处"玉堂风月"指卢生在相位上的风雅生活。
Jade Hall: Refers to the Hanlin Academy or the chancellor's office. Because the Jade Hall was pure and esteemed, it often referred to high official positions. Here, "Jade Hall breeze and moon" refers to Lu Sheng's elegant life in his ministerial position.

彭祖年高八百，也用采女之术：彭祖是传说中的上古大贤，以长寿著称，相传活了八百岁。古代传说彭祖通过"采女之术"（道家房中术）养生延年。此处指卢生效仿彭祖，想借女乐追求长生。
Peng Zu lived eight hundred years, also used the art of the shearer: Peng Zu is a legendary ancient sage famous for longevity, said to have lived 800 years. Ancient legend says Peng Zu prolonged life through the "art of the shearer" (Daoist sexual arts). Here it means Lu Sheng imitates Peng Zu, wanting to use the female musicians to seek longevity.

钟繇法帖：钟繇是三国时期曹魏著名书法家，擅长楷书，被尊为"楷书鼻祖"，其书法作品被后人称为"钟繇法帖"，为历代书法家所推崇。此处指卢生自认为字迹如钟繇法帖般受皇帝喜爱。
Zhong Yao calligraphy models: Zhong Yao was a famous Cao Wei calligrapher of the Three Kingdoms period, skilled in regular script, honored as the "originator of regular script." His calligraphy works were called "Zhong Yao calligraphy models" by later generations and were highly regarded by calligraphers through the ages. Here it means Lu Sheng thinks his handwriting is as beloved by the emperor as Zhong Yao's models.

姜公望：指姜子牙（吕尚），相传姜子牙八十岁时在渭水垂钓，遇周文王重用，后辅佐周武王伐纣建周，成就大业。此处"微臣要挣挫做姜公望"指卢生希望如姜子牙般老当益壮，为国效力。
Jiang Gongwang: Refers to Jiang Ziya (Lü Shang). Legend says Jiang Ziya was fishing at the Wei River at age 80 when he was employed by King Wen of Zhou. He later assisted King Wu of Zhou in defeating Zhou and establishing the Zhou dynasty, achieving great things. Here, "Your humble servant wants to strive to be a Jiang Gongwang" means Lu Sheng hopes to be like Jiang Ziya, old but vigorous, serving the country.

文园病：指汉代司马相如曾为文园令，后因病闲居，故以"文园病"代指文人患病。此处"老得文园病"指卢生年老病重。
Wenyuan illness: Refers to Sima Xiangru of the Han who was once Director of Wenyuan, later lived in retirement due to illness, hence "Wenyuan illness" came to mean a literatus falling ill. Here, "Aged, contracting Wenyuan illness" means Lu Sheng is old and seriously ill.

封禅书：指古代帝王封禅时所写的文书，司马相如曾作《封禅文》。此处"还留封禅书"指卢生临终前仍想留下奏表谢恩。
Fengshan text: Refers to the document written for the imperial Feng and Shan sacrifices. Sima Xiangru once wrote a "Fengshan Text." Here, "Still leaving a Fengshan text" means Lu Sheng, on his deathbed, still wants to leave a memorial thanking the emperor.

黄粱饭：出自唐人传奇《枕中记》（见《太平广记》卷八十二引《异闻集·吕翁》）。卢生在邯郸旅店中枕仙枕入梦，经历富贵一生，醒来时店主的黄粱饭尚未煮熟。此处"煮黄粱饭你吃哩"呼应典故，点出卢生的富贵经历实为一梦。
Yellow millet meal: From the Tang tale "Record of the Pillow" (see Taiping Guangji, Vol. 82, quoting Yìwén Jí, Lü Weng). Lu Sheng dreams of a life of wealth and honor using a magic pillow in a Handan inn; upon waking, the innkeeper's yellow millet meal is not yet cooked. Here, "Cooking the yellow millet meal for you to eat" echoes the story, pointing out that Lu Sheng's experience of wealth was just a dream.

浮生稊米：出自《庄子·秋水》"计中国之在海内，不似稊米之在大仓乎"。原句意思是人生在世，如同小米粒在粮仓中，极其渺小。此处指卢生醒悟后认为富贵如梦幻，人生渺小。
Floating life, a grain of millet: From Zhuangzi, "Autumn Floods": "Consider the Middle Kingdom within the seas – is it not like a grain of millet in a great granary?" The original meaning is that human life is extremely small, like a millet grain in a granary. Here it means Lu Sheng, upon waking, considers wealth and honor illusory and life insignificant.

蓬莱方丈：传说中的海上仙山，与瀛洲并称"三神山"，为神仙所居。此处"有个小庵儿唤做蓬莱方丈"指吕洞宾引导卢生追求仙道之地。
Penglai and Fangzhang: Legendary fairy mountains in the sea, along with Yingzhou called the "Three Divine Mountains," where immortals dwell. Here, "There is a small hermitage called Penglai Fangzhang" means the place where Lü Dongbin guides Lu Sheng to seek the Dao of immortality.

汉钟离：传说中的八仙之一，姓钟离名权，号正阳子，相传为汉代人，道貌仙姿，常梳双丫髻。此处作为证盟仙真之一，点醒卢生对姻亲的痴迷。
Han Zhongli: One of the Eight Immortals, surname Zhongli, given name Quan, style Zhengyangzi, said to be from the Han Dynasty, with immortal demeanor and appearance, often wearing his hair in double buns. Here, as one of the witnessing immortals, he awakens Lu Sheng to his obsession with marital relations.

曹国舅：八仙之一，为宋代曹太后之弟，虽出身国舅，却看淡富贵，后修道成仙，常持象简朝绅。此处责问卢生对功名的执着。
Cao Guojiu: One of the Eight Immortals, brother of Empress Cao of the Song Dynasty. Although born an imperial in-law, he disregarded wealth and honor, later cultivated the Dao and became an immortal, often holding an ivory tablet and court girdle. Here he questions Lu Sheng's attachment to fame and rank.

铁拐李（李孔目）：八仙之一，相传因修道时肉身被毁，只得附于跛足乞丐之身，常拄铁拐。此处数落卢生开疆拓土的所谓"功勋"。
Iron-Crutch Li (Li Kongmu): One of the Eight Immortals. Legend says his physical body was destroyed while cultivating the Dao, so he had to inhabit a lame beggar's body, often leaning on an iron crutch. Here he enumerates Lu Sheng's so-called "merits" of expanding territory.

蓝采和：八仙之一，原为乐户官身，常穿破蓝衫，手持拍板，踏歌而行。此处提及"打院本乐户官身"，呼应其身份，责问卢生对冤屈的执念。
Lan Caihe: One of the Eight Immortals, originally a musician by profession, often wore a tattered blue gown, held clappers, and sang while walking. Here, mentioning "beating court plays, musician official status" corresponds to his identity, questioning Lu Sheng's obsession with his wrongs.

韩湘子：八仙之一，为唐代文学家韩愈之侄，弃举业修道，传说能造逡巡酒、开顷刻花。此处点醒卢生对家园享乐的留恋。
Han Xiangzi: One of the Eight Immortals, nephew of the Tang writer Han Yu. He abandoned the exams to cultivate the Dao, and legend says he could make instant wine and blossom flowers instantly. Here he awakens Lu Sheng to his attachment to home and pleasure.

何仙姑：八仙中唯一女性，常持笊篱，传说能从笊篱中漏泄春光。此处责问卢生对儿孙的过度牵挂。
He Xiangu: The only female among the Eight Immortals, often depicted holding a bamboo strainer; legend says spring scenery could leak from it. Here, she reproaches Lu Sheng for his excessive attachment to his descendants.

张果老：八仙之一，相传为唐代人，常倒骑白驴，有长生之术，在仙班中辈分较高。此处作为证盟仙翁，主持对卢生的点化。
Zhang Guolao: One of the Eight Immortals, traditionally said to be from the Tang Dynasty, often shown riding a white donkey backwards; possessed the art of longevity and held high seniority among the immortals. Here, he acts as the witnessing immortal elder presiding over Lu Sheng's enlightenment.

蟠桃宴：传说中瑶池每年三月初三举办的宴会，西王母以蟠桃宴请众仙，象征长生与仙境盛会。此处"恰好蟠桃宴时节哩"提及仙境盛会。
Peach Banquet: A legendary feast held annually on the third day of the third lunar month at the Jade Pool, where the Queen Mother of the West entertained immortals with peaches of immortality, symbolizing longevity and a celestial gathering. The line "It happens to be the time of the Peach Banquet" here refers to this celestial event.

云阳市：古代杀人刑场，在长安东南，常用以代指死刑。此处"云阳市餐刀吓人"呼应卢生梦中险些被斩的经历。
Yunyang Execution Ground: An ancient execution ground southeast of Chang'an, often used metonymically for capital punishment. The line "facing the blade at Yunyang was terrifying" here echoes Lu Sheng's dream experience of nearly being executed.

鬼门关：古代关名，在今广西北流，地势险要，为古代赴岭南的必经之地，常用以代指险恶之地。此处"鬼门关挣脱了这残生"指卢生梦中从岭南流放地脱身。
Guimen Pass: Name of an ancient pass, located in present-day Beiliu, Guangxi; strategically important and a necessary route to Lingnan in ancient times, often used metaphorically for a perilous place. The line "escaped this wretched life at Guimen Pass" refers to Lu Sheng's dream escape from his place of exile in Lingnan.

三台印：古代三公之印，代指高官职位。此处"苦恋着三台印"指卢生对宰相职位的留恋。
Seal of the Three Dukes: The seal of the Three Dukes (high ministers) in ancient times, representing high office. The line "bitterly clinging to the Seal of the Three Dukes" refers to Lu Sheng's attachment to his position as Chancellor.

《南柯记》
The Tale of Nanke

玉茗：指白色山茶花，也常代指名贵花卉。此处"玉茗新池雨"描绘雨后新池边玉茗花的景致。
Yuming: Refers to white camellias, often used metonymically for precious flowers. The line "Yuming flowers by the new pond in the rain" here depicts the scene of Yuming flowers by a rain-freshened pond.

契玄：指探究玄妙之道，此处"契玄还有讲残经"指探究玄妙义理时仍有未讲完的经书。
Qixuan: Means probing profound mysteries. The line "Qixuan, yet there are unfinished sutras to expound" refers to exploring profound principles while still having sutras left unexpounded.

槐安国土：出自唐代李公佐传奇《南柯太守传》。淳于棼醉后入梦，被槐安国国王招为驸马，任南柯太守，后因权位之争失势，醒来方知槐安国实为庭中槐树下的蚁国。此处"登宝位槐安国土"指梦中登上槐安国的王位。
Land of Huai'an: From the Tang dynasty tale "The Governor of Nanke" by Li Gongzuo. Chunyu Fen, drunk, dreams he enters a kingdom called Huai'an, is made consort to the princess and appointed Governor of Nanke, later loses power due to court intrigues, and upon waking discovers Huai'an is actually an ant kingdom under a locust tree in his courtyard. The line "ascended the treasured throne in the land of Huai'an" refers to his dream of becoming king of Huai'an.

南柯太守：出自《南柯太守传》，淳于棼在梦中担任槐安国南柯郡太守，政绩卓著。此处"有碑记南柯太守"指其太守任期有碑记载。
Governor of Nanke: From "The Governor of Nanke"; Chunyu Fen serves as the Governor of Nanke Prefecture in the dream kingdom of Huai'an, with outstanding administrative achievements. The line "there is a stele recording the Governor of Nanke" refers to his governorship being commemorated by a stele.

甘露禅师：《南柯太守传》中，甘露寺禅师曾点化淳于棼，使其悟透人生虚幻。此处"无虚诳甘露禅师"指禅师的点化真实不虚。
Chan Master Sweet Dew: In "The Governor of Nanke", a Chan master from Sweet Dew Temple enlightens Chunyu Fen, making him realize the illusory nature of life. The line "not falsely deceiving like the Sweet Dew Chan Master" means the master's enlightenment was genuine.

The line "ascended the treasured throne in the land of Huai'an" refers to his dream of becoming king of Huai'an.

The line "there is a stele recording the Governor of Nanke" refers to his governorship being commemorated by a stele.

Chan Master Sweet Dew: In "The Governor of Nanke", a Chan master from Sweet Dew Temple enlightens Chunyu Fen, making him realize the illusory nature of life. The line "not falsely deceiving like the Sweet Dew Chan Master" means the master's enlightenment was genuine.

淳于髠：战国时期齐国学者，以滑稽善辩著称，《史记·滑稽列传》载其"滑稽多辩，数使诸侯，未尝屈辱"，且善饮，有"一斗亦醉，一石亦醉"之说。此处为生自叙先祖。
Chunyu Kun: A scholar of the Warring States period from the state of Qi, famous for his wit and persuasive speech; the "Records of the Grand Historian: Biographies of Witty Figures" records him as "witty and eloquent, frequently sent as an envoy to various states, never suffering disgrace"; also known for his capacity for drink, with the saying "drunk on one dou, drunk on one dan". Here, the male lead (Chunyu Fen) refers to him as an ancestor.

淳于意：即仓公，西汉医学家，精于医术，《史记·扁鹊仓公列传》载其曾为齐太仓长，因医术闻名，后被诬陷入狱，其女缇萦上书救父。此处"一男不生，一女不死"为对其医术的夸张说法。
Chunyu Yi: Also known as Cang Gong, a Western Han medical expert skilled in healing; the "Records of the Grand Historian: Biographies of Bian Que and Cang Gong" records he was Director of the Grand Granary of Qi, famed for his medical skills, later wrongly imprisoned, and saved by a petition from his daughter Tiying. The line "not a single male dies, not a single female dies" is an exaggerated praise of his medical prowess.

高阳酒徒：出自《史记·郦生陆贾列传》，郦食其自称"高阳酒徒"，后指嗜酒豪放之人。此处"惯使酒的高阳吾至友"以高阳酒徒喻淳于棼善饮。
Gaoyang Drunkard: From the "Records of the Grand Historian: Biographies of Li Yiji and Lu Jia"; Li Yiji called himself the "Drunkard of Gaoyang"; later refers to a heavy drinker of unrestrained character. The line "my close friend, the habitual drinker from Gaoyang" uses this term to describe Chunyu Fen's fondness for drink.

三槐：出自《周礼·秋官·朝士》"面三槐，三公位焉"，古代朝廷种植三棵槐树，象征三公之位。此处"三槐如在，可成丰沛之邦"以三槐喻国家根基，期望建立如丰沛般的基业。
Three Locust Trees: From the "Rites of Zhou: Offices of Autumn: Court Officers" "facing three locust trees are the positions of the Three Dukes"; in ancient courts, three locust trees were planted, symbolizing the positions of the Three Dukes. The line "if the Three Locust Trees exist, a realm like Feng and Pei can be established" uses the trees to symbolize the state's foundation, hoping to establish a base like that of the Han founder.

丰沛之邦：丰、沛为汉高祖刘邦的故乡，后常代指帝王龙兴之地。此处"可成丰沛之邦"指期望槐安国成为兴盛的立国之地。
Land of Feng and Pei: Feng and Pei were the hometown of Han Gaozu Liu Bang, later often used to refer to the place of origin of an emperor. The line "a realm like Feng and Pei can be established" expresses the hope that Huai'an will become a prosperous founding domain.

檀萝：出自唐代李公佐《南柯太守传》，檀萝国为槐安国的邻国，曾与槐安国发生战争。此处"便是檀萝无警"指邻国无战事，边境安宁。
Tanluo: From Tang Li Gongzuo's "The Governor of Nanke"; the kingdom of Tanluo was a neighbor of Huai'an and fought a war with it. The line "even Tanluo gives no alarm" means the neighboring state is peaceful, and the border is secure.
