槐棘：古代朝廷在三公位旁种槐树，九卿位旁种棘树，故以"槐棘"代指朝廷高官或官府。此处"足知你槐棘有人"指朝廷有贤能官员。
Locust Trees and Thorns: In ancient courts, locust trees were planted near the positions of the Three Dukes, and thorn trees near those of the Nine Ministers, hence "locusts and thorns" came to mean high court officials or the officialdom. The line "fully know you have men among the locusts and thorns" means the court has worthy and capable officials.

楼桑村：为三国刘备的故乡，因村中有大桑树如车盖，刘备曾言"吾必当乘此羽葆盖车"，后常代指帝王故乡。此处"似楼桑村裏"以楼桑村喻槐安国根基所在。
Lousang Village: The hometown of Liu Bei of the Three Kingdoms period, named for a large mulberry tree resembling a carriage canopy; Liu Bei once said "I shall surely ride in a carriage with such a feather canopy", later often used to refer to an emperor's birthplace. The line "like in Lousang Village" uses the village to metaphorically indicate Huai'an's foundational location.

赤子无知："赤子"原指婴儿，后常喻百姓、子民。此处"赤子无知"指国中百姓质朴单纯，顺应君臣之礼。
The ignorant common people: "Chizi" originally means infant, later often metaphorically refers to the common people, subjects. Here, "the ignorant common people" means the state's populace is simple and naive, conforming to the rites between ruler and subject.

契玄禅师：出自唐代李公佐《南柯太守传》，甘露寺契玄禅师曾点化淳于棼，使其悟透人生虚幻。此处为禅师自述前缘因果。
Chan Master Qixuan: From Tang Li Gongzuo's "The Governor of Nanke"; Chan Master Qixuan of Sweet Dew Temple enlightened Chunyu Fen, making him realize the illusory nature of life. Here, the Chan master explains his own karmic connections from a previous life.

达摩祖师渡江：达摩为佛教禅宗初祖，相传曾一苇渡江，到中原传播佛法。此处"跟随达摩祖师渡江"提及禅宗初祖事迹，表明禅师修行渊源。
Patriarch Bodhidharma crossing the river: Bodhidharma, the First Patriarch of Chan Buddhism, legend says crossed the Yangtze River on a reed to spread Buddhism in the Central Plains. The line "followed Patriarch Bodhidharma across the river" mentions the deeds of the First Patriarch, indicating the Chan master's lineage.

盂兰：即盂兰盆节，农历七月十五日，佛教徒举行法会，超度亡魂，施舍僧众。此处"七月十五日大会盂兰"指扬州僧俗举办盂兰盆会。
Ullambana: The Ullambana Festival, on the 15th day of the 7th lunar month, when Buddhists hold ceremonies to transfer merit to the deceased and make offerings to the monastic community. The line "on the fifteenth of July, a great Ullambana assembly" refers to the monastic and lay communities of Yangzhou holding an Ullambana ceremony.

石人起舞、新妇骑驴：均为禅宗公案用语，石人起舞喻无心而应，新妇骑驴喻执着外相。此处禅师借此感叹宗门说教多流于形式。
Stone man dancing, bride riding a donkey: Both are Chan koan expressions; "stone man dancing" symbolizes responding without conscious mind, "bride riding a donkey" symbolizes attachment to external forms. Here, the Chan master uses them to lament that the sect's teachings often become mere formalism.

笑拈花：指"拈花微笑"典故，世尊拈花，迦叶微笑，禅宗以心传心由此始。此处"那裏有笑拈花吃茘枝"质疑宗门真意失传。
Smiling while holding a flower: Refers to the story of the Buddha holding up a flower and Mahakasyapa smiling, from which the Chan tradition of mind-to-mind transmission began. The line "where is the smiling while holding a flower, eating lychees?" questions whether the true meaning of the tradition has been lost.

单刀直入：禅宗用语，喻直接明了，不绕弯子。此处指宗门应直指本心。
Single sword straight in: A Chan expression, metaphor for being direct and straightforward, not beating around the bush. Here, it means the sect should point directly to the mind.

五十三参：出自《华严经》，善财童子先后参访五十三位善知识求道。此处"挂一轴五十三参听讲图"指准备讲经的图画。
Fifty-three visitations: From the "Avatamsaka Sutra", where the youth Sudhana visited fifty-three spiritual guides in his quest for enlightenment. The line "hanging a scroll painting of the fifty-three visitations listening to lectures" refers to a painting prepared for the sermon.

石点头：传说晋代高僧道生在虎丘山讲经，群石为之点头，喻佛法精妙动人。此处"除了那戒坛上石点头"指超越形式化的讲经效果。
Stones nodding: Legend says that the Jin Dynasty monk Dao Seng preached at Tiger Hill Mountain and the stones nodded in agreement, metaphor for the profound and moving power of the Dharma. The line "apart from those stones nodding on the ordination platform" means transcending the effects of formalized preaching.

普诸天花下雨：佛教传说佛祖说法时，天雨曼陀罗花，喻佛法广被。此处"则待看普诸天花下雨"指期望法会如天雨繁花般感化众生。
Flowers raining down universally from the heavens: Buddhist legend says that when the Buddha preached, mandarava flowers rained from the sky, symbolizing the widespread reach of the Dharma. The line "then wait to see flowers rain down universally from the heavens" expresses the hope that the assembly will transform beings like a shower of celestial flowers.

三从四德：古代女性行为规范，"三从"指在家从父、出嫁从夫、老而从子；"四德"指妇德、妇言、妇容、妇功。此处国母以此教导公主。
Three Obediences and Four Virtues: Traditional norms for women's behavior: "Three Obediences" - obey father before marriage, husband after marriage, and sons in widowhood; "Four Virtues" - morality, proper speech, modest appearance, and diligent work. Here, the Queen Mother uses them to instruct the princess.

弄玉：相传为春秋时秦穆公之女，善吹箫，后与萧史结为夫妻，乘凤而去，常用以代指贤淑的女子。此处"名方弄玉"以弄玉喻公主。
Nongyu: Legendary daughter of Duke Mu of Qin during the Spring and Autumn period, skilled in playing the flute (or xiao), later married Xiao Shi and rode away on a phoenix; often used to refer to a virtuous and talented woman. The line "her name is Nongyu" compares the princess to Nongyu.

选佛场：原指科举考场，因佛教禅宗以"选佛"喻选拔人才，后也指讲经说法之地。此处"选佛场中去选郞"指在讲经场所挑选女婿。
Field for Selecting Buddhas: Originally meant the imperial examination hall; because the Chan school used "selecting Buddhas" as a metaphor for choosing talent, it also came to mean a place for preaching the Dharma. The line "go to the Field for Selecting Buddhas to choose a husband" means selecting a son-in-law at the preaching site.

东床：出自《世说新语·雅量》，王羲之坦腹东床，被郗鉴选中为婿，后以"东床"代指女婿。此处"禅床侧畔看东床"指在禅床旁挑选女婿。
East Bed: From "A New Account of the Tales of the World: Magnanimity"; Wang Xizhi lay sprawled on the eastern bed and was chosen by Xi Jian as his son-in-law; later "east bed" came to mean son-in-law. The line "by the side of the meditation bed, look at the east bed" means selecting a son-in-law beside the Chan master's seat.

灵山会：指佛祖在灵山说法的法会，代指讲经盛会。此处"管敎他灵山会裏直着个有缘人"指期望在讲经会上找到有缘的女婿。
Spirit Peak Assembly: Refers to the assembly where the Buddha preached on Vulture Peak , metaphorically used for a grand preaching event. The line "ensure that right at the Spirit Peak assembly there is a predestined person" expresses the hope of finding a fated son-in-law at the preaching.

打草惊蛇：原指打草时惊动了草里的蛇，比喻做事不密，使对方有所警觉。此处"有那等吊眼子，敲他几下，叫做打草惊蛇"指对付刁钻之人时稍作警示。
Beat the grass to startle the snake: Originally means startling a snake hidden in the grass by beating it, metaphor for acting indiscreetly and alerting the opponent. The line "for those crafty types, knock them a few times; it's called 'beating the grass to startle the snake'" means giving a slight warning when dealing with tricky people.

将虾吊鲤：比喻用小计诱骗他人。此处"无过是脱稍鬼，松他一筹，则是将虾吊鲤"指对滑头之人用小手段应付。
Use a shrimp to catch a carp: Metaphor for using a small trick to lure someone. The line "it's nothing more than those slippery fellows; give them some leeway, it's just 'using a shrimp to catch a carp'" means dealing with slick individuals with minor tactics.

刘伶：西晋文学家，"竹林七贤"之一，以嗜酒闻名，著有《酒德颂》。此处以刘伶喻嗜酒之人，夸张饮酒之多。
Liu Ling: A Western Jin writer, one of the "Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove", famous for his love of wine, author of "In Praise of the Virtue of Wine". Here, he is used to represent a heavy drinker, exaggerating the amount consumed.

杜康祠：杜康为传说中的酿酒始祖，后以"杜康"代指酒，"杜康祠"代指酒肆或饮酒之处。此处"只杜康祠蘸住了这穷三圣"指在酒肆中消磨时光。
Temple of Dukang: Dukang is the legendary originator of brewing; later "Dukang" came to mean wine, and "Temple of Dukang" means a tavern or drinking place. The line "only the Temple of Dukang has detained these poor three sages" means whiling away time in a tavern.

逃禅中圣："中圣"指醉酒，"逃禅"指逃避禅修或尘世，此处"饮中仙也有个逃禅中圣"指嗜酒之人也会在饮酒中寻求超脱。
Fleeing Chan, becoming a sage (drunk): "Becoming a sage" means getting drunk; "fleeing Chan" means escaping Chan practice or the mundane world. The line "even among immortal drinkers there is 'fleeing Chan, becoming a sage'" means that heavy drinkers also seek transcendence through wine.

黄龙喝棒：黄龙指黄龙慧南禅师，宋代禅宗高僧，以"黄龙三关"接引学人，"喝棒"为禅宗接引学人的方式，以喝声或棒打警醒对方。此处"坐听黄龙喝棒声"指听禅师讲经时的警醒之语。
Huanglong's shouts and sticks: Huanglong refers to Chan Master Huanglong Huinan, a Song Dynasty Chan master famous for his "Huanglong's Three Barriers" to guide students; "shouts and sticks" are Chan methods of guidance, using shouts or strikes to awaken the student. The line "sitting and listening to the sounds of Huanglong's shouts and sticks" refers to hearing the master's awakening words during the sermon.

盂兰大会：即盂兰盆会，农历七月十五日佛教徒举行的法会，超度亡魂，施舍僧众。此处"孝感寺中元盂兰大会"指孝感寺举办的盂兰盆会。
Great Ullambana Assembly: The Ullambana Festival, held by Buddhists on the 15th of the 7th lunar month to transfer merit to the deceased and make offerings to the monastic community. The line "the Zhongyuan Great Ullambana Assembly at Xiaogan Temple" refers to the Ullambana ceremony held at Xiaogan Temple.

五戒：佛教基本戒律，即不杀生、不偷盗、不邪淫、不妄语、不饮酒。此处"小僧扬州府禅智寺一个五戒是也"指僧人的法名或持戒身份。
Five Precepts: The basic Buddhist precepts: not killing, not stealing, not engaging in sexual misconduct, not lying, not taking intoxicants. The line "This humble monk is one Wu Jie from the Chanzi Temple of Yangzhou Prefecture" indicates the monk's religious name or his identity as a precept-holder.

胡旋舞：唐代流行的西域舞蹈，以旋转快速著称，出自西域各族。此处"请看俺婆罗门《胡旋舞》一会也"指西域婆罗门表演的胡旋舞。
Whirling Dance (Huxuan Wu): A popular Central Asian dance from the Tang Dynasty, known for its rapid spinning, originating from various Western Regions peoples. The line "Please watch us Brahmins perform a round of the Whirling Dance" refers to Brahmins from the Western Regions performing the dance.

竹径通幽处，禅房花木深：出自常建《题破山寺后禅院》。原句意思是竹林间的小路通向幽静之处，禅房掩映在花木深处。此处引用描绘禅智院的清幽景致。
A path through bamboos leads to a quiet place, The meditation hall deep among flowers and trees: From Chang Jian's poem "Inscribed on the Meditation Retreat Behind Broken Mountain Temple". The original lines mean a bamboo path leads to seclusion, the meditation hall is nestled deep among flora. Quoted here to depict the serene scenery of Chanzi Temple.

色即是空，空即是色：出自《般若波罗蜜多心经》。原句意思是一切物质现象（色）本质上都是虚幻不实的（空），而虚幻的本质（空）也离不开具体的物质现象（色）。此处禅师以诗句阐释这一佛教义理。
Form is emptiness, emptiness is form: From the "Heart Sutra". The original lines mean all material phenomena (form) are essentially illusory and insubstantial (emptiness), and the nature of emptiness cannot be separated from specific material phenomena (form). Here, the Chan master uses the lines to explain this Buddhist principle.

细雨湿衣看不见，闲花落地听无声：出自刘长卿《送严士元》。原句意思是细雨打湿衣裳却看不见痕迹，闲花飘落地面却听不到声音。此处用以解释"色即是空"，喻物质现象的虚幻无形。
Fine rain dampens clothes unseen, Idle flowers fall to earth unheard: From Liu Changqing's poem "Seeing Off Yan Shiyuan". The original lines mean fine rain moistens garments without visible trace, idle blossoms fall silently to the ground. Used here to explain "form is emptiness", illustrating the intangible nature of material phenomena.

归去岂知还向月，梦来何处更为云：出自薛涛《春望词》。原句意思是归去后不知是否还能面向明月，梦中不知何处又化作云彩。此处用以解释"非色非空"，喻超越虚实的境界。
Returning, how could I know I'd still face the moon? Dreaming, where again do I become a cloud?: From Xue Tao's poem "Spring Gazing Lyrics". The original lines express uncertainty after returning, not knowing if one will still face the moon, and in dreams, not knowing where one transforms into a cloud. Used here to explain "neither form nor emptiness", suggesting a state beyond real and unreal.

妙法莲花经观世音菩萨普门品：出自《妙法莲华经》中的一品，主要讲述观世音菩萨的普门示现和救苦救难的功德。此处贴、小旦演唱此经，契合求姻缘的情境。
Lotus Sutra, Chapter on the Universal Gate of Guanyin Bodhisattva: A chapter from the "Lotus Sutra", primarily describing Guanyin Bodhisattva's universal manifestation and merits of saving beings from suffering. Here, the Tie (role) and Xiao Dan (young female role) sing this sutra, fitting the context of seeking marriage.

道在蝼蚁：出自《庄子·知北游》"道在蝼蚁，在稊稗，在瓦甓，在屎溺"。原句意思是道无处不在，即使在微小的蝼蚁身上也存在。此处禅师引用说明佛法不分贵贱高下。
The Dao is in the ants: From the "Zhuangzi: Knowledge Wanders North" "The Dao is in the ants, in the weeds, in tiles and shards, in piss and shit". The original means the Dao is everywhere, even in tiny ants. Here, the Chan master quotes it to show that the Buddhist Dharma makes no distinction between noble and base.

龙女献珠：出自《法华经·提婆达多品》，龙女以价值三千大千世界的宝珠献佛，即时成佛。此处"待把宝珠抽献，比龙女如何"化用此典故，指献上金钗犀盒如龙珠般珍贵。
Dragon Girl offering the pearl: From the "Lotus Sutra: Chapter on Devadatta", the dragon girl offered a pearl worth three thousand great thousand-worlds to the Buddha and instantly attained Buddhahood. The line "wait to offer up this precious pearl, how does it compare to the Dragon Girl?" alludes to this story, meaning offering the gold hairpin and rhinoceros-horn box is as precious as the dragon pearl.

一笑拈花：即"拈花微笑"，世尊拈花，迦叶微笑，禅宗以心传心的典故。此处"一笑拈花奉释迦"化用此典，指以诚心供奉佛祖。
A smile while holding a flower: The story of the Buddha holding up a flower and Mahakasyapa smiling, the beginning of the Chan mind-to-mind transmission. The line "with a smile, holding a flower, offering to Sakyamuni" alludes to this, meaning making a sincere offering to the Buddha.

连理：指连理枝，两棵树的枝干合生在一起，常用来比喻夫妻恩爱或姻缘美满。此处"连理就中开"指淳于棼与瑶芳的姻缘如连理枝般自然成就。
Intertwined branches (Lianli): Refers to branches from two trees growing together, often used as a metaphor for conjugal love or a happy marriage. The line "intertwined branches bloom within" means the marriage between Chunyu Fen and Yaofang naturally comes to fruition like intertwined branches.

前生债：指前世的因缘或未了的情缘，认为今生的相遇相知是前世债务的偿还。此处"这姻缘一种前生债"指淳于棼与瑶芳的姻缘是前世注定的缘分。
Debt from a previous life: Refers to karmic connections or unresolved affections from past lives, suggesting meetings in this life are repayments of past debts. The line "this marriage is a kind of debt from a previous life" means the marriage between Chunyu Fen and Yaofang is a predestined karmic bond.

事大如山醉亦休：化用俗语，指无论事情多么重大，喝醉了就能暂时忘却。此处表现淳于棼借酒消愁的心态。
Matters big as a mountain, drunk, also cease: A variation of a common saying, meaning no matter how important things are, drunkenness allows temporary forgetfulness. Here it shows Chunyu Fen's mindset of drowning sorrows in wine.

不消阮籍穷途哭，但学刘伶死便埋：阮籍驾车出游，途穷则哭，表现失意情怀；刘伶嗜酒，曾言"死便埋我"，尽显放达。此处淳于棼以二人自比，表达失意与颓丧。
No need for Ruan Ji's crying at the road's end, Just learn from Liu Ling 'bury me when I die': Ruan Ji drove his cart and cried when the road ended, expressing frustration; Liu Ling loved wine and famously said "bury me when I die", showing utter uninhibitedness. Here, Chunyu Fen compares himself to both, expressing his own frustration and despondency.

眼似矒瞪脚似槌：形容醉酒后眼神模糊、脚步沉重的状态。"矒瞪"指视物不清，"槌"喻脚步沉重如锤。
Eyes dazed, feet like hammers: Describes the state of being drunk: blurred vision and heavy steps. "Mengdeng" means blurred vision, "chui" (hammer) metaphorically means heavy steps.

倒玉山因一盏倾：化用"玉山倾倒"典故，形容人醉后身体摇晃欲倒。"玉山"常喻男子风姿挺拔，此处反写醉酒失态。
Jade Mountain topples because of one cup tipped: Alludes to the story "Jade Mountain topples", describing a person swaying and about to fall when drunk. "Jade Mountain" often metaphorically describes a man's upright demeanor; here it's used ironically for drunken disgrace.

窦广国、孔安国：使者借谐音戏说，窦广国为汉初人物，孔安国为汉代经学家，此处故意曲解二人名字，称"国土在窦儿里""孔儿里"，调侃槐树穴中可藏国土，增添荒诞感。
Dou Guangguo, Kong Anguo: The envoys playfully use homophones; Dou Guangguo was a historical figure from early Han, Kong Anguo a Han Dynasty Confucian scholar; here their names are deliberately misinterpreted as "the kingdom is in the hole " and "in the aperture (Kong)", joking that a kingdom can be hidden in a locust tree hole, adding absurdity.

大槐安国：出自唐代李公佐《南柯太守传》，指淳于棼梦中所到的蚁国，位于大槐树穴中。此处"城上金牌四个字，大槐安国"点明梦境中的国度。
Great State of Huai'an: From Tang Li Gongzuo's "The Governor of Nanke", refers to the ant kingdom Chunyu Fen dreams of, located in a large locust tree hole. The line "on the city gate, a gold plaque with four characters: Great State of Huai'an" identifies the dream kingdom.

叔孙礼：指叔孙通所制的礼仪。叔孙通为汉初儒生，曾为汉高祖制定朝仪，规范君臣礼仪。此处"殿上初行叔孙礼"指淳于棼在槐安国朝堂行朝见礼仪，如同遵循叔孙通制定的礼法。
Shusun's Rites: Refers to the rituals formulated by Shusun Tong. Shusun Tong was an early Han Confucian scholar who established court ceremonial for Emperor Gaozu of Han, standardizing rites between ruler and ministers. The line "in the hall, first performing Shusun's Rites" means Chunyu Fen performs court rituals in the Huai'an court, as if following Shusun Tong's protocols.

金瓜玉斧：古代宫廷仪仗中的器物，金瓜为瓜形铜锤，玉斧为象征性的玉制斧头，常用于彰显皇权威严。此处"看殿头左右，金瓜玉斧，明晃一周遭"描绘朝堂仪仗的庄严。
Golden melons and jade axes: Objects used in ancient imperial processions; "golden melons" are melon-shaped bronze maces, "jade axes" are symbolic jade axes, often used to display imperial majesty. The line "see left and right of the hall, golden melons and jade axes, gleaming all around" depicts the solemnity of the court regalia.

红鸾：传说中的神鸟，常被视为婚姻的象征，"红鸾星动"喻指姻缘将至。此处"槐殿里根苗。也引的红鸾到"指淳于棼与金枝公主的姻缘到来。
Red Phoenix (Hongluan): A mythical bird often seen as a symbol of marriage; "the Red Phoenix star moves" metaphorically means marriage prospects are imminent. The line "the root and seed within the locust hall. Also attracted the Red Phoenix" refers to the arrival of the marriage between Chunyu Fen and the Golden Bough Princess.

丹墀：指宫殿前的红色台阶及空地，是臣子朝见君王的地方。此处"丹墀下扬尘舞蹈"指淳于棼在殿阶下行跪拜礼。
Vermilion Steps : The red-painted steps and courtyard in front of a palace, where ministers paid homage to the emperor. The line "below the vermilion steps, stirring dust in the dance" refers to Chunyu Fen performing the kowtow and prostration on the palace steps.

天上牛女：指牛郎织女的传说，每年七夕鹊桥相会，常用来象征爱情与姻缘。此处"真个天上牛女，地下蝼蚁也"以牛郎织女喻淳于棼与公主的姻缘，虽身份悬殊却终成眷属。
Heavenly Cowherd and Weaving Maid: Refers to the legend of the Cowherd and Weaver Girl stars, who meet across the Magpie Bridge on the seventh night of the seventh month, often symbolizing love and marriage. The line "truly the heavenly Cowherd and Weaving Maid, and the earthly ants" compares the marriage of Chunyu Fen and the princess to the stellar lovers, suggesting union despite vastly different statuses.

阮郎：出自刘晨、阮肇入天台山遇仙的传说，后以"阮郎"代指与仙女结缘的男子。此处"却是淳郞，做了阮郞"指淳于棼如阮肇般遇上仙缘，成为驸马。
Ruan Lang: From the legend of Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao entering Tiantai Mountain and encountering immortals; later "Ruan Lang" came to mean a man who forms a relationship with a fairy maiden. The line "but it is Chun Lang, who became Ruan Lang" means Chunyu Fen, like Ruan Zhao, encountered an immortal fate and became the princess's consort.

中心藏之，何日忘之：出自《诗经·小雅·隰桑》。原句意思是心中藏着思念，没有一天能够忘记。此处淳于棼回应琼英郡主的提问，表达对过往相遇的铭记。
Hidden in my heart, never forgotten for a day: From the "Classic of Poetry: Minor Odes: Mulberries on the Lowland". The original lines mean keeping something hidden in one's heart, not forgetting it for a single day. Here, Chunyu Fen responds to Princess Qiongying's question, expressing that he remembers their past meeting.

天台：指刘晨、阮肇入天台山遇仙的典故，代指仙境或良缘之地。此处"不向天台向下方"指淳于棼的姻缘不在传说中的天台，而在现实（梦中）的槐安国。
Tiantai: Refers to the story of Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao encountering immortals on Tiantai Mountain, representing an immortal realm or place of good fate. The line "not towards Tiantai but downwards" means Chunyu Fen's marriage fate lies not in the legendary Tiantai but in the (dream) reality of Huai'an.

洞庭哀响隐潇湘：化用屈原《九歌·湘夫人》中洞庭、潇湘的意境，常以洞庭潇湘的凄清声响喻哀怨之情。此处"似洞庭哀响隐潇湘"形容仙音凄清，触动淳于棼内心的感伤。
The mournful sounds of Dongting, hidden in XiaoXiang: Evokes the imagery from Qu Yuan's "Nine Songs: Lady of the Xiang River" of Dongting Lake and the Xiang River, often using their desolate sounds to symbolize sorrowful feelings. The line "like the mournful sounds of Dongting, hidden in XiaoXiang" describes the ethereal music as plaintive, touching Chunyu Fen's inner melancholy.

襄王赴神女：出自宋玉《高唐赋》，楚襄王梦遇巫山神女，后以"襄王神女"喻男女情缘。此处"正是襄王赴神女"指淳于棼前往洞房与公主成亲，如襄王赴巫山之会。
Xiang King going to the Goddess: From Song Yu's "Rhapsody on the Gaotang Shrine", where King Xiang of Chu dreamed of the Goddess of Wu Mountain; later "Xiang King and the Goddess" came to symbolize romantic encounters. The line "it is exactly Xiang King going to the Goddess" means Chunyu Fen going to the bridal chamber to consummate the marriage with the princess, like the King's encounter.

钧天：指天上的音乐，传说中上帝所居之处的音乐，后常用来形容美妙的仙乐或宫廷音乐。此处"仙乐奏钧天"指迎接驸马的音乐如天上仙乐般美妙。
Music of the Jun Tian: The music of heaven, it is said the music from the dwelling place of the Lord of Heaven; later often used to describe beautiful celestial or court music. The line "immortal music plays the Music of the Jun Tian" means the music greeting the consort is as magnificent as heavenly music.

合卺：古代婚礼仪式之一，将一个瓠瓜剖成两个瓢，新郎新娘各执一瓢饮酒，象征夫妻恩爱、甘苦与共。此处"饮合欢之酒""合卺介"指淳于棼与公主行婚礼饮酒之礼。
Drink the Nuptial Wine (Hejin): An ancient wedding ritual where a gourd was split into two ladles, the bride and groom each drank from one, symbolizing shared joy and hardship. The lines "drink the wine of conjugal joy" and "perform the Hejin ritual" refer to Chunyu Fen and the princess performing the wedding wine ceremony.

金蝉：古代官员帽上的装饰，常以金蝉为饰，象征身份尊贵。此处"帽插金蝉"指淳于棼身为驸马，头戴饰有金蝉的礼帽，尽显华贵。
Golden Cicada: A decoration on ancient officials' hats, often made of gold, symbolizing high status. The line "hat adorned with a golden cicada" means Chunyu Fen, as consort, wears a ceremonial hat with the golden cicada, displaying grandeur.

寿阳妆：出自南朝宋武帝女寿阳公主的典故，传说公主卧于含章殿檐下，梅花落于额上，成五出之花，拂之不去，后人仿为"梅花妆"，也称"寿阳妆"。此处"试学寿阳妆面"指公主梳妆效仿寿阳公主的妆容。
Shouyang Makeup: From the story of Princess Shouyang, daughter of Emperor Wu of the Liu Song Dynasty; legend says she napped under the eaves of Hanzhang Hall, a plum blossom fell on her forehead leaving a five-petaled mark that wouldn't brush off, later imitated as "plum blossom makeup" or "Shouyang makeup". The line "trying to learn the Shouyang makeup" means the princess adorns herself imitating Princess Shouyang's style.

灵根：原指草木的根，后常用来比喻事物的根本或仙缘根基。此处"旧种灵根"指公主身为金枝玉叶，有着尊贵的出身根基。
Numinous Root: Originally means the root of a plant, later often metaphorically refers to the foundation of something or the basis of an immortal connection. The line "long-planted numinous root" refers to the princess's noble birth as a "golden bough and jade leaf".

戚畹：指外戚，因帝王的外戚多居住在畹（古代面积单位）地附近，故称"戚畹"。此处"新连戚畹"指淳于棼成为驸马后，与王室联姻，成为外戚。
Imperial In-Laws (Qiwan): Refers to the imperial relatives by marriage, as they often resided near the emperor's lands (wan was an ancient unit of area). The line "newly connected to the imperial in-laws" means Chunyu Fen, after becoming consort, is related to the royal family through marriage.

桃源：指陶渊明《桃花源记》中的理想境界，后常用来比喻与世隔绝的美好地方或美满姻缘。此处"妆成一曲桃源"指婚礼场景如桃花源般美好幽静。
Peach Blossom Spring: Refers to the ideal land in Tao Yuanming's "Record of the Peach Blossom Spring", later often used as a metaphor for an isolated utopia or a blissful marriage. The line "adorned into a Peach Blossom Spring" means the wedding scene is as beautiful and serene as the utopia.

弄玉临风，笑拈箫管：弄玉为春秋时秦穆公之女，善吹箫，后与萧史结为夫妻，乘凤而去。此处"把弄玉临风，笑拈箫管"以弄玉吹箫喻公主的娴雅，也暗指姻缘美满。
Nongyu facing the wind, smilingly holding flute pipes: Nongyu, daughter of Duke Mu of Qin, skilled in playing the flute (or xiao), married Xiao Shi and rode away on a phoenix. The line "holding Nongyu facing the wind, smilingly holding flute pipes" uses Nongyu playing the flute to describe the princess's elegance, also hinting at the happy marriage.

二十四桥：出自唐代扬州胜景，杜牧有"二十四桥明月夜"之句，常与扬州的繁华、风月相关。此处"想二十四桥，玉人天远"指淳于棼回忆扬州的过往，感叹今昔变化。
Twenty-four Bridges: A famous scenic spot in Yangzhou from the Tang Dynasty; Du Mu's line "the moonlit night on the Twenty-four Bridges" often associates it with Yangzhou's prosperity and romance. The line "thinking of the Twenty-four Bridges, the beautiful one is far away under heaven" refers to Chunyu Fen recalling his past in Yangzhou, lamenting the changes.

红鸾：传说中的神鸟，主婚姻喜庆，后常用来代指姻缘。此处"尽今宵略把红鸾蘸"指今夜成就美满姻缘。
Red Phoenix : A mythical bird presiding over marriage celebrations, later often used to refer to marriage fate. The line "tonight, just briefly dip into the Red Phoenix" means achieving the blissful marriage union tonight.

鸳鹭班：鸳鹭飞行时行列整齐，古代常用来比喻朝官的行列，此处"去鸳鹭班"指次日清晨要去朝堂参加朝会。
Rows of Ducks and Herons (Yuanlu Ban): Ducks and herons fly in orderly rows, anciently often used to metaphorically refer to the ranks of court officials. The line "go to the rows of ducks and herons" means going to the morning court audience the next day.

牛斗看成两下：牛斗指牵牛星和斗宿，此处喻两国如星辰般分立对峙，各占一方。
See the Ox and Dipper as two sides: "Ox and Dipper" refer to the stars Altair and the Dipper constellation; here it metaphorically means the two states stand opposed like stars, each occupying their own side.

草昧成中国：草昧指天地初开时的混沌状态，也指国家初创未开化阶段；中国此处指建立的国家。意为在原始状态中建立起自己的国度。
From chaos, a Middle Kingdom was formed: "Chaos" (Caomei) refers to the primordial state at the beginning of heaven and earth, or the initial, uncivilized stage of a state; "Middle Kingdom" here means the established state. It means establishing one's own kingdom from a primitive state.

刀画地：用刀划地为界，指划分疆土，确立势力范围。
Draw boundaries with a knife: Means demarcating territory with a knife, i.e., dividing land and establishing spheres of influence.

玄驹：指蚂蚁，古代常以玄驹代指蚁类。此处指槐安国的蚁民。
Dark Colts (Xuanju): Refers to ants; anciently often used to mean ants. Here it refers to the ant people of Huai'an.

赤驳：指毛色红白相间的兽类，此处代指檀萝国的部族，与槐安国的"玄驹"形成区别。
Red Dappled (Chibo): Refers to beasts with red and white mottled fur; here it represents the tribes of Tanluo, contrasting with Huai'an's "Dark Colts".

赤象之雄：像赤色大象一样雄壮，形容槐安国自恃强大。
Mighty as red elephants: Describes Huai'an's self-perception of being as powerful and imposing as red elephants.

黍米之细：像黍米一样细小，形容檀萝国被槐安国轻视，视为弱小。
Tiny as millet grains: Describes Tanluo being despised by Huai'an as insignificant and weak, like millet grains.

穿营蓦涧走如梭：穿越营地、跨越山涧，行动像梭子一样迅速，形容檀萝部落行动敏捷。
Pierce camps, leap ravines, swift as a shuttle: Describes the Tanluo tribes moving swiftly through camps and across ravines.

罗施鬼：古代对西南少数民族的称呼，此处借指偏远的部族。
Luoshi ghosts: An ancient term for southwestern minority peoples; here used to refer to remote tribes.

藤甲兵：传说中以藤甲为铠甲的士兵，坚韧灵活，此处喻檀萝国士兵的作战特点。
Rattan-armored soldiers: It is said soldiers armored in rattan, tough and agile; here it describes the fighting characteristics of Tanluo soldiers.

一苇：出自《诗经·卫风·河广》"一苇杭之"，指用一根芦苇就能渡河，喻南柯郡与檀萝国相距甚近，轻易可至。
A single reed: From the "Classic of Poetry: Odes of Wei: The Wide River" "cross it with a single reed"; means a river can be crossed on a single reed, metaphorically indicating Nanke Prefecture and Tanluo are very close, easily reached.

膻腥：原指牛羊等的腥气，此处代指南柯郡的粮草物资，为檀萝国抢掠的目标。
The smell of meat: Originally means the smell of mutton or beef; here it stands for the provisions and supplies of Nanke Prefecture, the target of Tanluo's plunder.

绿槐风小，正绛台清暇，日华低照：出自场景描写，描绘槐安国宫廷的清幽环境，"绛台"指宫殿高台，"日华"指阳光。
Green locust trees, light breeze, just when the crimson tower is serene, the sun's rays shine low: From a scene description, depicting the tranquil environment of the Huai'an court; "crimson tower" refers to the palace tower, "sun's rays" to sunlight.

草昧暗凭天道：草昧指国家初创阶段，意为在国家建立初期，暗中依靠天道运行。
In chaos, secretly relying on the Way of Heaven: "Chaos" refers to the state's initial stage; means in the early days of the state, secretly relying on the operation of the Way of Heaven.

汉干封元年征战故事：右相提及的槐安国先祖征战典故，借历史传说强调国家征战传统。
Tales of campaigns from the first year of Han Ganfeng: Campaign stories of Huai'an's ancestors mentioned by the Right Minister, using historical legends to emphasize the state's martial tradition.

晋太原中桓谦之家典故：引用晋代桓谦家蚂蚁征战的传说，佐证槐安国的军事渊源。
Tale from the Taiyuan era of Jin concerning Huan Qian's household: References the legend of ants battling in Huan Qian's house during the Jin Dynasty, supporting Huai'an's military origins.

元魏天安元年赤黑相斗：北魏时期蚂蚁红黑两派相斗的传说，赤者战败，为槐安国征伐史添例。
In the first year of Yuan Wei Tian'an, red and black fought: Legend from the Northern Wei period about red and black factions of ants fighting, the red side losing; adds another example to Huai'an's history of conquest.

东魏武定四年黄黑交战：东魏时期黄黑蚂蚁交战，黄者获胜班师，进一步丰富征战故事。
In the fourth year of Eastern Wei Wuding, yellow and black battled: Battle between yellow and black ants during the Eastern Wei, the yellow side victorious and returning in triumph; further enriches the campaign stories.

南齐徐玄之家畋猎典故：南齐时徐玄家蚂蚁在花毡上狩猎、砚池钓鱼的传说，体现槐安国的畋猎传统。
Tale from Southern Qi concerning Xu Xuan's household hunting: Legend from Southern Qi about ants hunting on a flowery felt and fishing in an inkstone pool at Xu Xuan's house, reflecting Huai'an's hunting tradition.

龟为玄武：玄武为古代四象之一，象征北方，龟山因对应玄武星宿，成为国家讲武之地。
The tortoise represents the Dark Warrior: The Dark Warrior (Xuanwu) is one of the Four Symbols, representing the north; Tortoise Mountain, corresponding to the Dark Warrior constellation, becomes the state's place for military discussions.

九月登龟伐鼋：古代习俗，九月登上龟山捕猎大鳖，此处呼应传统，说明猎龟山的合理性。
In the ninth month, ascend Tortoise Mountain to hunt great turtles: An ancient custom of ascending Tortoise Mountain in the ninth month to hunt large softshell turtles; here it echoes tradition, justifying the hunt on Tortoise Mountain.

长杨上林，可以方矣：长杨宫、上林苑为汉代皇家猎苑，此处喻龟山猎场可与皇家苑囿相比。
Changyang Park and Shanglin Park can be matched: Changyang Palace and Shanglin Park were Han Dynasty imperial hunting parks; here it means the Tortoise Mountain hunting grounds can compare to imperial parks.

拿倒穿山甲，此俺国世仇也：穿山甲常破坏蚁穴，被槐安国（蚁国）视为世仇，体现蚁国视角的恩怨。
Capture the pangolin, this is our state's generational enemy: Pangolins often destroy ant nests, so they are considered a generational enemy by Huai'an (an ant kingdom), reflecting the ant perspective on grievances.

《大槐安国龟山大猎赋》：田子华所作赋文，铺陈龟山狩猎盛况，仿汉代辞赋风格，彰显文治。
"Rhapsody on the Great Hunt on Tortoise Mountain in the Great State of Huai'an": A rhapsody written by Tian Zihua, elaborately describing the grandeur of the hunt on Tortoise Mountain, imitating the Han Dynasty fu style, showcasing cultural achievement.

玄武之精：指龟山为玄武星宿的精灵所化，赋予龟山神圣色彩。
Essence of the Dark Warrior: Means Tortoise Mountain is transformed from the essence of the Dark Warrior constellation, giving it a sacred aura.

西王母之龟峰、东诸侯之龟蒙：借传说中的龟形山峰，衬托龟山的不凡。
The Queen Mother of the West's Tortoise Peak, the Eastern Feudal Lords' Tortoise Mount: Uses legendary turtle-shaped mountain peaks to highlight Tortoise Mountain's extraordinariness.

形如巴丘之蜕骨，势似鳌山之顶蓬：形容龟山形态，巴丘蜕骨喻其古老，鳌山项蓬喻其高耸。
Shape like the sloughed shell of Ba Hill, posture like the summit of Ao Mountain: Describes Tortoise Mountain's form; "sloughed shell of Ba Hill" suggests antiquity, "summit of Ao Mountain" suggests loftiness.

河、洛之数：指河图洛书的数理，喻龟山纹理蕴含天地之道。
Numbers of the River [Chart] and Luo : Refers to the numerological principles of the Hetu and Luoshu, suggesting Tortoise Mountain's patterns contain the principles of heaven and earth.

介胄之容：形容龟山岩石如铠甲般的外观，显威武之气。
Visage of armor: Describes Tortoise Mountain's rock formations as resembling armor, displaying a martial air.

虎兕出于匣外，龟玉毁于椟中：化用《论语》"虎兕出于柙，龟玉毁于椟中"，强调君王游猎讲武的必要性。
Tigers and rhinos escape their cages, tortoise shells and jade are destroyed in their cases: Adapts the "Analects" quote "When tigers and rhinoceroses escape from their cages... When tortoise shell and jade are destroyed in their cases...", emphasizing the necessity for the ruler to tour, hunt, and discuss military affairs.

通天之冠，玄衮之袍：古代帝王礼帽与礼服，此处指槐安国王的仪仗服饰。
Cap that reaches heaven, robe of dark dragon embroidery: Ancient imperial ceremonial cap and robes; here they refer to the King of Huai'an's regalia.

干将：古代名剑，代指兵器，显狩猎的威武。
Ganjiang: Ancient famous sword, represents weaponry, displaying the hunt's majesty.

雨师洒道，风伯清尘：神话中雨神、风神开路，渲染狩猎的神圣氛围。
The Rain Master sprinkles the road, the Wind Earl clears the dust: Mythological rain and wind deities preparing the way, enhancing the hunt's sacred atmosphere.

蚁附之属：形容随从众多如蚂蚁聚集，贴合槐安国的蚁国设定。
Those who cling like ants: Describes the numerous attendants gathering like ants, fitting the ant kingdom setting of Huai'an.

雷炮霜刀，风矰雨毕：指武器精良、箭矢如雨，描绘狩猎的激烈场面。
Thunderous cannons, frosty blades, wind-borne arrows, rain of Bi arrows: Refers to excellent weapons and arrows falling like rain, depicting the hunt's intensity.

鲮鲤：即穿山甲，被视为蚁国世仇，捕获后象征消除祸患。
Lingli: I.e., pangolin, considered the ant kingdom's generational enemy; its capture symbolizes eliminating a scourge.

《上林》：指司马相如《上林赋》，田子华赋文仿其风格，王以汉武帝赞司马相如事类比，赞田子华之才。
"Shanglin": Refers to Sima Xiangru's "Rhapsody on the Shanglin Park"; Tian Zihua's fu imitates its style; the King compares praising Tian Zihua to Emperor Wu of Han praising Sima Xiangru, commending Tian's talent.

金镶玉板：珍贵的刻载体，王命将赋文刻于其上，彰显对文才的重视。
Gold-inlaid jade tablets: Precious material for inscription; the King orders the fu engraved on them, showing esteem for literary talent.

《龙韬》：古代兵书《六韬》之一，代指兵法，此处指狩猎中演练军事谋略。
"Dragon's Strategies": One of the ancient military texts "Six Strategies", represents military strategy; here it means practicing military tactics during the hunt.

间着匹喇喇笛声儿哜嘹：形容狩猎归途中的乐声，"哜嘹"指声音清脆。
Interspersed with the piping sound of flutes, clear and shrill: Describes the music on the return from the hunt; "jiliao" means clear and shrill sound.

毛赤剥，肉生烧：描写狩猎后分食猎物的场景，显丰收之喜。
Fur red and stripped, flesh roasted fresh: Depicts the scene of dividing and eating the game after the hunt, showing the joy of plenty.

槐角楼：槐安国王赐宴商议国事之处，因临槐树而名，贴合环境设定。
Locust Corner Tower: Where the King of Huai'an holds banquets to discuss state affairs, named for its location near locust trees, fitting the environmental setting.

春色锦桃源：化用陶渊明《桃花源记》的意境，以桃花源的美好比喻槐安国的仙境般生活，此处指宫廷中的春日美景如桃源般绚烂。
Spring scenery brocaded like Peach Blossom Spring: Evokes the imagery of Tao Yuanming's "Peach Blossom Spring", using the utopia's beauty to metaphorically describe Huai'an's idyllic life; here it means the palace's spring scenery is as gorgeous as the utopia.

细腰轻展，渐觉水游鱼：形容公主身姿纤细柔美，如水中游鱼般灵动，"细腰"常喻女子体态轻盈。
Slender waist lightly extends, gradually feeling like a fish swimming in water: Describes the princess's slender and graceful posture, as agile as a fish in water; "slender waist" often metaphorically indicates a woman's graceful figure.

缕金香穗归：指衣物上的金丝香穗随人而归，描绘服饰的华贵精致。
Threads of gold, fragrant tassels, return: Refers to the gold threads and fragrant tassels on clothing returning with the person, depicting the luxurious and exquisite attire.

绿窗槐影翠依微：写窗外槐树的翠影朦胧，"依微"指隐约不清，营造清幽的宫廷氛围。
Green window, locust shadows, emerald and faint: Describes the faint green shadows of the locust tree outside the window; "yiwei" means faint and indistinct, creating a serene palace atmosphere.

出花宫漏迟："宫漏"指古代宫廷计时器，"迟"表现时光悠长，形容在花宫中悠闲度日，感觉时间缓慢。
Leaving the floral palace, the water clock is slow: "Palace water clock" refers to the ancient palace timekeeper; "slow" suggests the passage of time feels long, describing a leisurely life in the flowery palace where time seems to move slowly.

遇贵主有天生之乐，想亡亲有地下之悲：淳于棼感叹虽得公主宠爱享受荣华，却因思念亡亲而心生悲伤，体现喜中带忧的心境。
Meeting the noble princess brings innate joy, thinking of deceased relatives brings subterranean sorrow: Chunyu Fen laments that while he enjoys the princess's favor and splendor, thoughts of his dead parents bring sadness, reflecting a state of joy mixed with sorrow.

禅智桥边好墓田：指淳于棼母亲葬于禅智桥边，"墓田"即墓地，点出亲人安葬之处。
Good grave fields by Chan Wisdom Bridge: Means Chunyu Fen's mother is buried by Chan Wisdom Bridge; "grave fields" means burial ground, indicating where his relative is interred.

身殁在胡：指淳于棼父亲死于胡人之地，"胡"古代对北方少数民族的称呼，此处指边疆战乱之地。
Died in Hu lands: Means Chunyu Fen's father died in the lands of the Hu people (ancient term for northern ethnic groups); here it refers to the border regions of conflict.

亲家翁职守北土，音问不绝：槐安国王称淳于棼父亲在北方任职，常有音信，为后续情节埋下伏笔。
Your esteemed father holds a post in the northern territories, news never ceases: The King of Huai'an claims Chunyu Fen's father is stationed in the north and correspondence is constant, setting up a later plot point.

阳春寸草无：化用"谁言寸草心，报得三春晖"，此处指淳于棼想报答亲恩却无以为报，"阳春"喻父母之恩，"寸草"自喻微小。
The inch-long grass has no [way to repay] the bright spring: Adapts the line "Who says the heart of inch-long grass / Could repay the radiance of full spring?"; here it means Chunyu Fen wishes to repay his parents' kindness but has no means; "bright spring" metaphorically means parental kindness, "inch-long grass" means himself, insignificant.

长生袜、福寿鞋：公主为淳于棼父亲准备的礼物，以鞋袜寄托长寿、福运的祝愿，体现古代儿媳对公婆的礼节。
Longevity socks, fortune and longevity shoes: Gifts prepared by the princess for Chunyu Fen's father, with the socks and shoes conveying wishes for long life and good fortune, reflecting the traditional etiquette of a daughter-in-law towards her parents-in-law.

系书胡雁：化用"鸿雁传书"的典故，指托鸿雁传递书信，此处指请人将家书和礼物送去北方。
Tie the letter to a northern goose: Alludes to the story of wild geese carrying letters; means entrusting a letter to a messenger (like a goose), here referring to asking someone to deliver the letter and gifts north.

不报慈乌："慈乌"指乌鸦反哺，喻子女对父母的孝顺，此处指不能尽孝心中不安，希望通过书信礼物稍尽心意。
Not repaying the pious crow: "Pious crow" refers to crows who feed their parents, symbolizing filial piety; here it means feeling uneasy about not being able to fulfill filial duties fully, hoping the letter and gifts will slightly convey his heart's intention.

老婆官：指依靠妻子关系得到的官职，淳于棼调侃自己若因公主求官便是"老婆官"，带自嘲意味。
Wife's official: Means an official position obtained through one's wife's connections; Chunyu Fen jokes that if he sought office through the princess, it would be a "wife's official", with self-mocking tone.

于家七代祖：淳于棼自嘲家族出身，回应公主"辱没祖先"的玩笑，显夫妻间的轻松互动。
Seven generations of ancestors of the Yu family: Chunyu Fen self-deprecatingly refers to his family lineage, responding to the princess's joke about "disgracing his ancestors", showing light-hearted interaction between the couple.

金章紫绶：指高级官员的金印和紫色绶带，代指高官厚禄。此处"金章紫绶"形容右相段功身居高位，身份尊贵。
Golden seal and purple ribbon: Refers to the gold seal and purple ribbon of high officials, representing high rank and emolument. Here, "golden seal and purple ribbon" describes Right Minister Duan Gong's high position and honourable status.

独步三台宿："三台"指古代中央最高行政机构，代指朝廷要职。意为在朝廷要职中独当一面，常居高位处理政务。
Unrivaled among the stars of the Three Terraces: "Three Terraces" refers to the highest central administrative bodies in ancient times, representing key court positions. Means being peerless among high court officials, constantly handling affairs from a lofty position.

日移花甃："花甃"指砌有花纹的井壁或花坛，"日移"表现时间推移，形容从早朝到日暮，在宫中忙碌多时。
The sun moves across the flowery well curb: "Flowery well curb" refers to a patterned well curb or flower bed; "sun moves" indicates passage of time, describing being busy in the palace from morning court until dusk.

为国机谋：指为国家大事筹划谋略，体现右相心系国事的职责。
Planning strategies for the state: Means devising plans and strategies for important state matters, reflecting the Right Minister's duty of being concerned with state affairs.

南柯跨踞雄州：指南柯郡地理位置重要，是军事要地。"雄州"指地势险要、地位重要的州郡。
Nanke straddles a strategic prefecture: Means Nanke Prefecture is geographically important, a military stronghold. "Strategic prefecture" means a prefecture with strategically important terrain and status.

近檀萝要习边筹：南柯郡靠近檀萝国，需要熟悉边防谋略。"边筹"指边防的筹划、谋略。
Close to Tanluo, one must be versed in border strategies: Nanke Prefecture is near Tanluo, requiring familiarity with border defense strategies. "Border strategies" means the planning and strategy for border defense.

性豪杯酒：形容淳于棼性格豪放，喜好饮酒，右相担心其不适合担任边郡太守。
His nature is bold with cup and wine: Describes Chunyu Fen's unrestrained character and fondness for drink; the Right Minister worries this makes him unsuitable for governing a border prefecture.

君侯疎不间亲："疏不间亲"指关系疏远者不参与关系亲近者的事，紫衣官暗示右相与国王关系疏远，不便干预国王对驸马的任用。
Noble Lord, the distant do not come between the close: "The distant do not come between the close" means those with distant relationships should not interfere in matters between those with close relationships; the purple-robed official hints that the Right Minister's relationship with the King is distant, making it inappropriate to interfere in the King's appointment of the Consort.

玉人金屋：化用"金屋藏娇"典故，指淳于棼与公主的亲密关系，"玉人"代指公主，"金屋"喻宫廷的富贵生活。
Jade beauty in a golden house: Alludes to the story "keeping a beautiful woman in a golden house"; refers to the intimate relationship between Chunyu Fen and the princess; "jade beauty" represents the princess, "golden house" symbolizes the luxurious palace life.

黄金如斗：形容官印或财富极多，代指高官厚禄，此处指南柯太守的重要职位。
Gold like a peck measure: Describes an abundance of official seals or wealth, representing high office and emolument; here it refers to the important position of Governor of Nanke.

疎不间亲：即"疏不间亲"，指关系疏远的人不宜介入关系亲近者之间的事，此处指右相不便反对国王任用驸马。
The distant do not come between the close: Means those with a distant relationship should not interfere in matters between those with a close relationship; here it means the Right Minister finds it inconvenient to oppose the King's appointment of the Consort.

儿女曹：指年轻人或晚辈，此处右相无奈接受国王任用驸马的决定，称其为晚辈间的安排。
The children's generation: Refers to young people or the younger generation; here the Right Minister reluctantly accepts the King's decision to appoint the Consort, calling it an arrangement among the younger generation.

集唐：指汇集唐诗诗句，此处引用四句唐诗，描绘宫廷生活与公主归来的情境，增添文学色彩。
Assembled Tang: Means collecting lines from Tang poetry; here four lines from Tang poems are quoted, depicting palace life and the princess's return, adding literary flavor.

玉胞肚：公主向淳于棼讲述寄书过程，"礼仪合当"体现宫廷规矩，"叮咛停当"表现对家书的重视。
Jade Belly : The princess tells Chunyu Fen about the letter-sending process; "rites and etiquette are proper" reflects palace protocol, "repeated instructions are settled" shows the importance placed on the family letter.

黄堂：古代太守的厅堂，代指太守职位。此处"诏选黄堂"指朝廷任命淳于棼为南柯太守。
Yellow Hall: The hall of an ancient prefect, representing the prefect's position. The line "edict selects for the Yellow Hall" means the court appoints Chunyu Fen as Governor of Nanke.

秦楼：原指传说中秦穆公为女儿弄玉所建之楼，后代指公主居所。此处"捧到秦楼开放"指将任命诏书送到公主宫中。
Qin Tower: Originally refers to the tower built by Duke Mu of Qin for his daughter Nongyu; later refers to a princess's residence. The line "presented to the Qin Tower to be opened" means the appointment edict was delivered to the princess's palace.

温衾扇枕：古代孝道故事，指子女为父母暖被、扇枕，此处淳于棼感叹无法在父亲身边尽孝，体现思念之情。
Warming the quilt, fanning the pillow: Stories from ancient filial piety, where children warm the bedclothes and fan the pillow for their parents; here Chunyu Fen laments not being able to perform these duties for his father, showing his longing.

左戚右贤：指帝王身边的外戚与贤臣，"左戚"指外戚，"右贤"指贤臣，诏书中以此说明任用淳于棼的合理性。
Relatives on the left, worthies on the right: Refers to the imperial relatives by marriage and worthy ministers around the emperor; "relatives on the left" means imperial in-laws, "worthies on the right" means worthy ministers; the edict uses this to justify appointing Chunyu Fen.

政事不理，太守废黜：指南柯郡前任太守治理不善被罢免，为淳于棼任职提供背景。
Affairs of government not attended to, the Prefect is dismissed: Means the previous Governor of Nanke was dismissed for poor governance, providing background for Chunyu Fen's appointment.

离珠：传说中黄帝时期的明目者，此处代指宫中女官或侍从，"掌离珠感动娘娘"指女官传达公主心意，得到国王认可。
Lizhu:It is said that a clear-sighted person from the time of the Yellow Emperor; here represents a palace lady official or attendant; "handling Lizhu moved the Queen Mother" means the lady official conveyed the princess's wishes and gained the King's approval.

倾宫锦绣奁房："倾宫"指奢华的宫殿，"奁房"指女子梳妆的房间，此处指国王和公主拿出宫中财物为淳于棼准备行装。
Palace of splendor, brocaded dressing room: "Palace of splendor" means a luxurious palace, "dressing room" means a woman's dressing room; here it means the King and princess took out palace treasures to prepare luggage for Chunyu Fen.

东床：代指女婿，此处"普人间没俺东床"淳于棼自夸身为驸马的尊贵，无人能及。
East Bed: Represents son-in-law. The line "throughout the mortal world, there is no East Bed like me" is Chunyu Fen boasting about his honourable status as Consort, unmatched by anyone.

琼浆：指美酒，此处"凑南柯饮着琼浆"形容在南柯郡享受富贵生活。
Qiongjiang: Refers to fine wine. The line "happily in Nanke, drinking Qiongjiang" describes enjoying a life of wealth and luxury in Nanke Prefecture.

五鼓朝廊：指清晨五更到朝堂，"整朝衣五鼓朝廊"指淳于棼需清晨准备朝服去朝堂谢恩。
Fifth watch morning corridor: Means going to the court corridor at the fifth watch (early morning). The line "adjust court robes at the fifth watch morning corridor" means Chunyu Fen needs to prepare his court robes early morning to go to court to express gratitude.

女萝：一种依附树木生长的植物，常比喻依附他人而存，此处"恩光附女萝"指淳于棼借助公主的恩宠获得职位。
Dodder (Nvluo): A plant that grows dependent on trees, often metaphorically means relying on others for existence. The line "favor's light clings to the dodder" means Chunyu Fen obtained his position through the princess's favor.

封事：古代大臣上给皇帝的密封奏章，此处"明朝有封事"指淳于棼准备上奏请求任用田子华、周弁。
Sealed memorial: Sealed memorials presented by ministers to the emperor in ancient times. The line "tomorrow morning there is a sealed memorial" means Chunyu Fen prepares to submit a memorial requesting the appointment of Tian Zihua and Zhou Bian.

一掌瞰宫墀：形容站在高处俯瞰宫殿台阶，"宫墀"指宫殿的台阶，体现宫廷的威严与壮阔。
A single palm overlooking the palace steps: Describes standing high and overlooking the palace steps; "palace steps" are the steps of the palace, reflecting its majesty and grandeur.

五马更踟蹰："五马"代指太守，古代太守出行驾车用五匹马，此处指淳于棼以太守身份辞朝，内心既有荣升的喜悦，又有离别的不舍。
Five horses still hesitate: "Five horses" represents a prefect (who used a five-horse carriage); here it means Chunyu Fen, in his capacity as Prefect, takes leave of the court, feeling both the joy of promotion and the reluctance to leave.

将门余子：指出身将门的后代，淳于棼自称将门之子，体现其家族背景。
Scion of a military family: Means a descendant of a family of generals; Chunyu Fen calls himself a scion of a military family, reflecting his family background.

心惭覆餗："覆餗"指食物倾覆，比喻不胜其职，此处淳于棼自谦担心无法胜任太守之职，心怀愧疚。
Heart ashamed of overturning the cauldron: "Overturning the cauldron" means spilling food, metaphorically meaning being incompetent for one's post; here Chunyu Fen modestly worries about being unfit for the prefect's role, feeling guilty.

毘佐之器：指辅佐朝政的才能，"毘佐"即辅佐，形容周弁有辅佐政务的才干。
Capability of an assistant: Means the talent to assist in government; "assistant" means to assist; describes Zhou Bian as having the talent to assist in administration.

达政化之源：指通晓政治教化的根本，称赞田子华精通政务治理的本源。
Understands the source of governance and transformation: Means comprehending the fundamentals of political education; praises Tian Zihua for understanding the essence of governance.

司宪：古代掌管司法的官职，此处指周弁被任命为南柯郡负责司法的官员。
Director of Justice: An ancient official title for those in charge of justice; here it means Zhou Bian is appointed as the official responsible for justice in Nanke Prefecture.

司农：古代掌管农业、财政的官职，此处指田子华被任命为南柯郡负责农桑财政的官员。
Director of Agriculture: An ancient official title for those in charge of agriculture and finance; here it means Tian Zihua is appointed as the official responsible for agriculture and finance in Nanke Prefecture.

铨补：指选拔补充官员，淳于棼希望通过举荐贤才补充官职，使南柯郡治理完善。
Selection and supplementation: Means selecting and supplementing officials; Chunyu Fen hopes to perfect Nanke's governance by recommending worthy talent to fill posts.

蒙恩点注：指承蒙恩宠被任命官职，"点注"指任命、指派，周弁、田子华感谢国王的任命。
Favored by your grace, appointed and assigned: Means receiving the favor of appointment to office; "appointed and assigned" means appointed, assigned; Zhou Bian and Tian Zihua thank the King for their appointments.

阙下叫山呼："阙下"指宫殿之下，"山呼"指臣子对君主的叩拜礼，高呼"万岁"，形容二人在宫前谢恩的礼仪。
Below the tower, cry out 'Long Live!': "Below the tower" means below the palace tower; "cry out 'Long Live!'" refers to the ministers' kowtow ritual to the monarch, shouting "Long live!"; describes the two performing the thanksgiving ceremony before the palace.

濯龙门外主家亲："濯龙门"为汉代宫门名，代指宫廷，此处指国王、国母在宫南为淳于棼饯行，体现皇室的重视。
The master's family relatives outside Zhuolong Gate: "Zhuolong Gate" was a Han Dynasty palace gate name, here representing the palace; means the King and Queen Mother see Chunyu Fen off south of the palace, showing the royal family's regard.

二龙同汉代：化用汉代"二龙"典故，指才华出众的两人，此处喻周弁、田子华同被任用，如汉代贤才共事。
Two dragons together in the Han era: Alludes to the Han Dynasty story of "two dragons", referring to two exceptionally talented men; here it metaphorically means Zhou Bian and Tian Zihua are appointed together, like worthy Han talents working side by side.

秦地吹箫女，盈盈照紫微。可中才望见，花月倚门归：这四句诗化用"吹箫引凤"典故。相传春秋时秦穆公之女弄玉善吹笙，夜梦善吹箫的青年萧史，穆公寻得萧史许配弄玉。二人婚后月下吹箫，引来紫凤赤龙，最终萧史乘龙、弄玉跨凤升空而去。诗中"秦地吹箫女"代指公主，喻其如弄玉般美好，"盈盈照紫微"写公主光彩照人，"紫微"常指帝王居所或天空；后两句营造浪漫氛围，似盼佳人归来。
Flute-playing maiden of Qin land, Radiant, illuminates the Purple Palace. Just managed to catch sight of her, Flowers and moon, she leans by the gate returning.: These four lines allude to the story "Playing the flute attracted the phoenix".It is said that Duke Mu of Qin's daughter Nongyu was skilled in playing the sheng; she dreamed of a young man, Xiao Shi, skilled in playing the flute. Duke Mu found Xiao Shi and betrothed him to Nongyu. After marriage, they played under the moon, attracting a purple phoenix and red dragon; eventually Xiao Shi rode the dragon and Nongyu mounted the phoenix and ascended to heaven. In the poem, "flute-playing maiden of Qin land" represents the princess, comparing her beauty to Nongyu's; "radiant, illuminates the Purple Palace" describes the princess's dazzling beauty ("Purple Palace" often means the imperial dwelling or the sky); the last two lines create a romantic atmosphere, as if awaiting the beauty's return.

秦箫吹彻鸾同跨：化用"吹箫引凤"典故。萧史教弄玉吹箫，数年後弄玉能引凤凰栖息，秦穆公为他们筑凤凰台，二人终乘凤凰飞去。此处"秦箫吹彻"形容箫声悠扬至极，"鸾同跨"指淳于棼与公主如萧史弄玉般，乘鸾鸟相伴而行，象征夫妻恩爱、出行不凡如神仙眷侣。
Qin flute played through, phoenixes ride together: Alludes to the story "Playing the flute attracted the phoenix". Xiao Shi taught Nongyu to play the flute; after years, Nongyu could attract phoenixes to roost. Duke Mu of Qin built them a Phoenix Tower, and they eventually flew away on phoenixes. Here, "Qin flute played through" describes the flute music as extremely melodious; "phoenixes ride together" means Chunyu Fen and the princess, like Xiao Shi and Nongyu, ride together on phoenixes, symbolizing conjugal love and an extraordinary journey like immortal companions.

琼箫暂下钧天乐："钧天乐"出自《列子·周穆王》，传说周穆王西游昆仑山，西王母在瑶池设宴，席间演奏《钧天广乐》，此为天上仙乐，曲调绝美。句中以"琼箫"形容箫声高雅，"暂下钧天乐"意为箫声如从天而降的仙乐般动听，给人超凡脱俗之感。
Jade flute briefly descends with Jun Tian music: "Jun Tian music" comes from the "Liezi: King Mu of Zhou";It is said that King Mu of Zhou traveled west to Kunlun Mountain, the Queen Mother of the West held a feast at the Jade Pool, during which the "Vast Music of Jun Tian" was played; this is celestial music of surpassing beauty. The line uses "jade flute" to describe the flute's noble sound; "briefly descends with Jun Tian music" means the flute music is as beautiful as celestial music descending from heaven, giving a transcendent feeling.

貂蝉：古代官员帽饰。东汉以后，中常侍、侍中等官帽上插貂尾、饰金蝉，后泛指高官显爵。这里"大槐宫里着貂蝉"指在南柯郡（大槐国）担任高官。
Marten tails and cicadas (Diaochan): Decorations on ancient officials' hats. After the Eastern Han, hats of officials like Palace Attendants and Palace Stewards had marten tails and golden cicadas; later it generally meant high officials. Here, "wearing marten tails and cicadas in the Great Locust Palace" means holding high office in Nanke Prefecture (the Great Locust State).

箫史弄云烟：典出《列仙传》。箫史善吹箫，能引来凤凰，秦穆公以女弄玉妻之，后二人乘凤飞升。这里"秦楼箫史弄云烟"以箫史弄玉的典故喻指夫妻相伴的美好情境。
Xiao Shi plays amidst clouds and mist:From "Biographies of Immortals". Xiao Shi excelled at playing the flute and could attract phoenixes. Duke Mu of Qin gave him his daughter Nongyu in marriage, and later they rode phoenixes and ascended. Here, "Xiao Shi of Qin Tower plays amidst clouds and mist" uses the story of Xiao Shi and Nongyu to metaphorically describe the beautiful scene of the couple together.

竹马年：典出《后汉书·郭伋传》。郭伋任并州牧，有儿童骑竹马迎送。后以"竹马"指百姓对官吏的欢迎。这里"父老儿童竹马年"指百姓用传统方式迎接新任官员。
Year of the bamboo horse:From "Book of the Later Han: Biography of Guo Ji". When Guo Ji was Governor of Bingzhou, children rode bamboo horses to greet and see him off. Later, "bamboo horse" came to mean the common people's welcome for an official. Here, "elders and children in the year of the bamboo horse" means the people welcome the new official in the traditional way.

兰亭：东晋王羲之等文人在会稽山阴兰亭宴集，留下《兰亭集序》，后以"兰亭"指风雅幽美的胜地。这里"似兰亭景幽围翠岭"形容南柯郡景色如兰亭般清幽。
Orchid Pavilion: Where Wang Xizhi and other literati of the Eastern Jin gathered at Lanting in Shanyin, Kuaiji, leaving behind the "Preface to the Poems Composed at the Orchid Pavilion"; later "Orchid Pavilion" came to mean an elegant and serene scenic spot. Here, "scenery like Orchid Pavilion, serene, encircled by emerald hills" describes Nanke Prefecture's scenery as being as tranquil as Orchid Pavilion.

露冕新承明主恩：化用唐代钱起《送夏侯审校书东归》"露冕新承明主恩，山城别是武陵源"。原句写官员蒙受皇恩赴任，山城如世外桃源般美好。这里引用以表驸马受皇恩赴任南柯。
Dewy crown newly receives the enlightened ruler's favor: Adapts Qian Qi's (Tang) poem "Seeing Off Xiahou Shen, Collator, Returning East": "Dewy crown newly receives the enlightened ruler's favor, The mountain town is another Peach Blossom Spring." The original line describes an official receiving imperial favor to take up a post, the mountain town being like a utopia. Quoted here to express the Consort receiving royal favor to go to Nanke.

山城别是武陵源：化用唐代钱起《送夏侯审校书东归》诗句。"武陵源"典出陶渊明《桃花源记》，指理想中的世外桃源。原句赞山城如桃花源般清幽，这里形容南柯郡环境美好。
The mountain town is another Peach Blossom Spring: Adapts the line from Qian Qi's poem. "Peach Blossom Spring" alludes to Tao Yuanming's "Peach Blossom Spring", meaning an ideal utopia. The original line praises the mountain town as serene like the utopia; here it describes Nanke Prefecture's beautiful environment.

血盆经：相关典故源于佛教传说中目连救母的故事。据经文中记载，目连尊者为救母亲前往西天，途经羽州追阳县旷野，见血盆池地狱中诸多女人散发披枷，饮池中污血。狱主告知，这些妇人因生产时血污溪河、煎茶供佛时污及良善而受此果报。目连向佛祈请开示，佛言需长斋拜忏、念诵弥陀以消业障。这里指郡主为公主请《血盆经》，建议其母子长斋忏悔以灾消福长。
Blood Bowl Sutra: The related story stems from the Buddhist legend of Maudgalyayana saving his mother. According to scripture, the Venerable Maudgalyayana went to the Western Paradise to save his mother; passing through the wilderness of Zhuiyang County, Yuzhou, he saw many women in the Blood Bowl Pond Hell with disheveled hair and cangsues, drinking filthy blood from the pool. The hell warden informed him these women suffered this retribution because they polluted streams and rivers with blood during childbirth, or contaminated good things while preparing tea offerings for the Buddha. Maudgalyayana petitioned the Buddha for guidance; the Buddha said they needed prolonged fasting, repentance, and reciting Amitabha's name to eliminate karmic obstacles. Here, the Princess suggests obtaining the Blood Bowl Sutra for the princess, advising her and her child to undertake long fasting and repentance to eliminate calamity and increase blessings.

目连救母：典出佛教故事。目连尊者为救堕入地狱的母亲，遍历地狱寻母，后借佛陀之力使母亲脱离苦难。故事体现孝道与佛教的因果报应思想，常被用于劝善修行。此处借目连救母的典故解释《血盆经》的由来与作用。
Maudgalyayana saves his mother:From Buddhist story. The Venerable Maudgalyayana, to save his mother who had fallen into hell, traversed hell to find her, and with the Buddha's power, freed her from suffering. The story embodies filial piety and the Buddhist concept of karmic retribution, often used to encourage virtue and practice. Here, the story of Maudgalyayana saving his mother is used to explain the origin and purpose of the Blood Bowl Sutra.

紫衣乘传："紫衣"在古代常指高官服饰或僧道的紫色袈裟，此处指受派遣的官员；"乘传"指乘坐驿车出行，古代为传递公文或官员赴任等使用。这里指国母派遣紫衣官员乘驿车将经卷送往瑶台宫院。
Purple robes ride a relay carriage: "Purple robes" anciently often referred to high officials' garments or the purple robes of monks/priests; here it means the dispatched official; "ride a relay carriage" means traveling by post carriage, used in ancient times for delivering documents or officials taking up posts. Here it means the Queen Mother dispatches a purple-robed official by post carriage to deliver the sutra to the Jade Terrace Palace.

五伦：指儒家所倡导的五种人伦关系，即父子有亲、君臣有义、夫妇有别、长幼有序、朋友有信。这里"家尊五伦"指百姓尊崇伦理道德，社会秩序良好。
Five Cardinal Relationships: The five human relationships advocated by Confucianism: affection between father and son, righteousness between ruler and subject, distinction between husband and wife, precedence between elder and younger, and trust between friends. Here, "households honor the Five Relationships" means the people uphold ethical principles, and social order is good.

伐柯：典出《诗经·豳风·伐柯》"伐柯伐柯，匪斧不克；取妻如之何？匪媒不得"。原句以砍伐斧柄比喻娶妻需有媒人，后以"伐柯"代指婚姻之事。这里"婚姻以时歌伐柯"指婚姻依时举行，百姓传唱婚嫁相关的歌谣。
Cutting an axe handle (Fake):From "Classic of Poetry: Odes of Bin: Cutting an Axe Handle": "Cut an axe handle, cut an axe handle, Without an axe it cannot be done; How does one take a wife? Without a matchmaker it cannot be done." The original uses cutting an axe handle as a metaphor for needing a matchmaker to take a wife; later "cutting an axe handle" came to mean marriage matters. Here, "marriages in their season sing of cutting axe handles" means marriages are held at the proper time, and the people sing songs related to marriage.

夜户不闭：化用《礼记·礼运》中"谋闭而不兴，盗窃乱贼而不作，故外户而不闭"的描述。原句描绘大同社会的安宁景象，这里指南柯郡治安良好，百姓夜间不用关门。
Doors unclosed at night: Adapts the description from the "Book of Rites: Evolution of Rites": "Plots are stifled and do not arise; robbers, thieves, and rebels do not show themselves; therefore doors on the outside are not closed." The original depicts the peace of a utopian society; here it means Nanke Prefecture has good public security, and people don't need to close their doors at night.

生祠：古代百姓为纪念有功德的官员而修建的祠堂，让其在世时便受祭祀。这里"大生祠"指百姓为淳于棼修建的祠堂，以表彰其德政。
Life-time shrine: Shrines built by the common people in ancient times to commemorate virtuous officials, where they were worshipped while still alive. Here, "great life-time shrine" means the people built a shrine for Chunyu Fen to honor his benevolent governance.

温太真装砌的嵯峨：温太真即温峤，东晋大臣。据《世说新语》等记载，温峤曾以玉镜台为聘礼娶表妹刘倩之。这里以温峤的典故泛指精美建筑的营造，形容瑶台城如温峤所建般壮丽嵯峨。
Built as majestically as Wen Taizhen's constructions: Wen Taizhen is Wen Qiao, a Eastern Jin minister. According to records like "A New Account of the Tales of the World", Wen Qiao used a jade mirror stand as betrothal gift to marry his cousin Liu Qianzhi. Here, the story of Wen Qiao is used generally for the construction of exquisite buildings, describing the Jade Terrace City as majestic and lofty like something built by Wen Qiao.

秦楼双鸣玉珂：秦楼原指传说中秦穆公为女儿弄玉所建之楼，后常代指女子居所或夫妻欢聚之地。玉珂指马络头上的玉饰，行走时发声。这里"下秦楼双鸣玉珂"形容周田二人如夫妻般乘马而行，呼应其共事身份。
Descending from Qin Tower, paired jade bridle ornaments chime: Qin Tower originally referred to the tower built by Duke Mu of Qin for his daughter Nongyu; later it often represented a woman's residence or a place of conjugal joy. Jade bridle ornaments are jade decorations on horse bridles that make sound when moving. Here, "descending from Qin Tower, paired jade bridle ornaments chime" describes Zhou and Tian riding together like a married couple, echoing their collegial relationship.

明月三五：指农历十五月圆之夜。"三五"即十五，古代常用数字相乘表示日期，此处点明瑶台城竣工恰逢中秋月圆之时。
Bright moon on the fifteenth: Refers to the night of the full moon on the 15th of the lunar month. "Three fives" means fifteen, a common ancient way to denote the date by multiplication; here it specifies that the Jade Terrace City was completed just right on the Mid-Autumn full moon.

亲亲：出自儒家伦理观念，意为亲爱自己的亲人，是"仁"的重要体现。《论语》《孟子》等典籍中多有论述，强调亲属间的关爱。这里令旨中"二曰亲亲"指治国需重视亲属间的伦理情谊。
Cherishing one's relatives: Comes from Confucian ethics, meaning to love one's own relatives; it is an important aspect of "benevolence". Discussed in texts like the "Analects" and "Mencius", emphasizing care between relatives. Here, in the decree, "the second is cherishing relatives" means governing the state requires emphasizing ethical affection among kin.

姮娥窃药：典出古代神话传说。嫦娥（姮娥）偷吃西王母的不死之药后，飞升至月宫，成为月中仙子。这里"背儿夫窃药向寒宫躲"借嫦娥奔月的典故，形容瑶台清冷如月宫，公主在此似嫦娥独居。
Chang'e stealing the medicine: from ancient mythology. Chang'e (Heng'e) stole the Queen Mother of the West's elixir of immortality, flew to the moon, and became the moon goddess. Here, "behind her husband's back, stole the medicine and hid in the cold palace" borrows the story of Chang'e fleeing to the moon to describe the Jade Terrace as desolate and cold like the moon palace, with the princess there alone like Chang'e.

画卯堂：古代官署中官员每日卯时（清晨五点至七点）签到办公的场所，"画卯"即签到之意。这里"守着个闹喳喳的画卯堂"指驸马在官署忙于公务。
Morning attendance hall: The place in ancient government offices where officials signed in daily during the mao hour (5-7 am); "drawing mao" means signing in. Here, "guarding a noisy morning attendance hall" means the Consort is busy with official duties in the yamen.

画眉台：代指女子梳妆的镜台，因女子常在此画眉而得名。这里"翠臻臻画眉台脱了窝"指公主离开梳妆台所在的居所，移居瑶台城。
Eyebrow-painting terrace: Represents a woman's dressing table, named because women often painted their eyebrows there. Here, "the lush green eyebrow-painting terrace has left its nest" means the princess has left her residence with its dressing table and moved to the Jade Terrace City.

偷风斫砦："偷风"指窥探消息，"斫砦"指袭击营寨，泛指暗中探查、伺机行动。这里指探子暗中打探瑶台城情况，寻找可乘之机。
Steal wind, raid stockades: "Steal wind" means to spy out information; "raid stockades" means to attack camps; generally means secretly investigating and waiting for an opportunity to act. Here it means scouts secretly gathering information on the Jade Terrace City, looking for a vulnerable point.

撞门羊：古代出兵前宰杀羊以祭路神，后泛指出兵前的犒赏或先行试探的牺牲品。这里"先把撞门羊宰了大犒贺"指太子准备出兵前宰杀牲畜犒赏军士。
Gate-crashing ram: In ancient times, a ram was slaughtered before sending troops to sacrifice to the road god; later it generally meant a reward before battle or a sacrificial victim for a preliminary probe. Here, "first slaughter the gate-crashing ram for a great reward" means the Crown Prince prepares to slaughter animals to reward the troops before sending them out.

飞虎把河桥坐："飞虎"指勇猛的军士，"坐河桥"指占据河桥要地。这里形容军士严密守卫，准备行动。
Flying tigers guard the river bridge: "Flying tigers" means brave soldiers; "guard the river bridge" means occupying the strategic river bridge. Here it describes soldiers guarding tightly, preparing for action.

昭君出塞：典出汉代王昭君远嫁匈奴的故事，后常用来形容女子远嫁或被迫离开故土。这里"怕聒炒的昭君出塞和"借昭君出塞喻指公主可能被迫离开。
Zhaojun goes out to the frontier:From the story of Wang Zhaojun of the Han Dynasty marrying far away to the Xiongnu; later often used to describe a woman marrying far away or being forced to leave her homeland. Here, "fear the clamor of Zhaojun going out to the frontier and making peace" uses Zhaojun's story to metaphorically indicate the princess might be forced to leave.

伐柯：典出《诗经·豳风·伐柯》"伐柯伐柯，匪斧不克；取妻如之何？匪媒不得"，原指娶妻需有媒人，后代指婚姻之事。这里"咱自无媒去伐柯"指太子无需媒人，直接强抢公主成就婚姻。
Cutting an axe handle (Fake):From "Classic of Poetry: Odes of Bin: Cutting an Axe Handle" (see above). Originally meant taking a wife requires a matchmaker; later came to mean marriage matters. Here, "we ourselves, without a matchmaker, go to cut the axe handle" means the Crown Prince needs no matchmaker, he will directly seize the princess to achieve the marriage.

湘文簟：指带有湘竹纹理的竹席，湘竹即斑竹，常用来制作清凉的卧具。这里"俺汗减了湘文簟"指秋凉后不再因出汗浸湿竹席。
Xiang-patterned mat: Refers to a bamboo mat with the pattern of Xiang bamboo, often used to make cool bedding. Here, "my sweat diminishes on the Xiang-patterned mat" means after the autumn coolness, one no longer sweats enough to dampen the mat.

团扇：圆形的扇子，古代女子常用，诗词中常以团扇象征孤寂或秋凉。这里"好梦暗随团扇"指夏日的好梦随团扇收起而消逝，呼应秋凉之意。
Round fan: A round fan, commonly used by women in ancient times; in poetry, it often symbolizes loneliness or autumn coolness. Here, "good dreams secretly follow the round fan" means the good dreams of summer vanish as the round fan is put away, echoing the autumn coolness.

槐柯：指槐树的枝柯，"风动槐柯交翠舞"描绘秋风中槐树枝叶摇曳的景象，暗合南柯故事中与槐树相关的背景。
Locust branches: Refers to the branches of the locust tree. The line "wind moves locust branches, intertwining emerald dance" depicts the locust branches and leaves swaying in the autumn wind, subtly connecting to the locust tree background of the Nanke story.

秦楼通戍火："秦楼"原指女子居所，这里代指瑶台城；"戍火"指边境的烽火。全句意为瑶台城传来边境战事的警报。
Qin Tower connects to beacon fires: "Qin Tower" originally means a woman's residence, here it represents the Jade Terrace City; "beacon fires" means border beacon fires. The whole sentence means alarm of border warfare reaches the Jade Terrace City.

汉苑入边愁："汉苑"原指汉代宫苑，这里泛指宫苑；"边愁"指边境战事引发的愁绪。全句写战事阴影笼罩宫苑。
Han gardens enter border sorrow: "Han gardens" originally means Han Dynasty palace gardens, here refers to palace gardens; "border sorrow" means anxiety caused by border warfare. The whole sentence describes the shadow of war looming over the palace gardens.

娘子军：指由女子组成的军队，历史上有平阳公主组织娘子军的典故，这里指瑶台城的妇女守城队伍。
Women's army: Refers to an army composed of women; historically there is the story of Princess Pingyang organizing a women's army; here it means the women defending the Jade Terrace City.

父子兵：指父子一同参军，形容军队团结勇猛，这里指淳于棼父子率领的军队。
Father-son soldiers: Means fathers and sons serving in the army together, describing a united and brave army; here it means the army led by Chunyu Fen and his son.

马子：指马桶，旧时的便溺器具。这里"我连马子、煑粥锅都搬上城来了"写守城妇女准备用秽物防御敌人。
Horse pot (Mazi): Means chamber pot, old-fashioned toilet vessel. The line "I've even brought the horse pots and porridge cooking pots up onto the wall" describes the defending women preparing to use filth to defend against the enemy.

彩鸾双扇："彩鸾"指鸾鸟图案，古代贵官出行或居处常用绘有鸾鸟的扇子仪仗。这里"还把彩鸾双扇掌"指官员仪仗中的扇具，彰显身份。
Paired fans with colorful phoenixes: "Colorful phoenixes" refers to the phoenix pattern; fans painted with phoenixes were often used in the processions or residences of high officials in ancient times. Here, "still hold the paired fans with colorful phoenixes" refers to the fan implements in official regalia, manifesting status.

碧油幢：古代用青绿色油布制成的帐幕，常为高官出行或办公时所用。这里"老槐阴新雨碧油幢"指在槐树下的官署帐幕，点明办公环境。
Green oilcloth canopy: A canopy made of green oilcloth in ancient times, often used by high officials when traveling or conducting business. Here, "old locust shade, fresh rain, green oilcloth canopy" refers to the official canopy under the locust tree, indicating the handle official business  environment.

黄堂：古代太守、知府等地方长官的厅堂，这里"独坐黄堂"指淳于棼在南柯郡衙正堂办公。
Yellow Hall: The hall of an ancient prefect or magistrate; here "sitting alone in the Yellow Hall" means Chunyu Fen is working in the main hall of the Nanke Prefecture yamen.

素商：古代以五音配四季，商音配秋，故"素商"代指秋天。这里"偶然西风吟素商"指秋风带来秋意。
Pale Shang: Anciently, the five notes were matched with the seasons; the Shang note matched autumn, hence "pale Shang" represents autumn. Here, "occasionally the west wind intones pale Shang" means the autumn wind brings the feeling of autumn.

玉马叮当："玉马"指挂在檐下的玉制风铃，风起时发出叮当声。这里"悉阑珊玉马叮当"描绘秋风中铃响的景象。
Jade horses jingling: "Jade horses" refers to jade wind chimes hung under eaves that jingle when the wind blows. Here, "all listless, jade horses jingling" depicts the scene of chimes sounding in the autumn wind.

冰壶溜亮："冰壶"指清澈的水壶或冰制容器，"溜亮"形容水流或器物碰撞的清脆声。这里写雨声如冰壶滴水般清亮。
Ice kettle dripping clear: "Ice kettle" means a clear water pitcher or ice container; "dripping clear" describes the clear sound of dripping water or objects striking. Here it describes the sound of rain as clear as water dripping from an ice kettle.

鸳瓦：指成对的瓦，因形似鸳鸯而得名，常用于古建筑屋顶。这里"敲鸳瓦跳珠儿定荡"形容雨滴打在瓦上如珍珠跳动。
Mandarin duck tiles: Paired tiles, named for their resemblance to mandarin ducks, often used on ancient building roofs. Here, "striking mandarin duck tiles, jumping pearls, steady swaying" describes raindrops hitting the tiles like bouncing pearls.

潇湘：原指潇水、湘水，后常代指江南水乡或多雨的清幽之地。这里"长似对潇湘"形容雨声如在潇湘水乡般凄清。
XiaoXiang: Originally refers to the Xiao and Xiang rivers; later often represents the Jiangnan water country or rainy, serene places. Here, "long as if facing XiaoXiang" describes the sound of rain as mournful and clear as in the XiaoXiang region.

鹳鸣于垤，妇叹于室：出自《诗经·豳风·东山》。"鹳鸣于垤"指鹳鸟在蚁穴上鸣叫，预示天要下雨；"妇叹于室"指妻子在屋内叹息。这里大儿子诵读此句，被解读为公主有难的预兆。
The stork cries on the mound, the wife sighs in the chamber: From the "Classic of Poetry: Odes of Bin: Eastern Hills". "The stork cries on the mound" means a stork crying on an anthill foretells rain; "the wife sighs in the chamber" means the wife sighs indoors. Here, the eldest son recites this line, which is interpreted as an omen of the princess's distress.

蚁阵：比喻军队排列如蚂蚁般的阵形，这里指救堑江城的常规军阵。
Ant formation: Metaphorically means an army arrayed like ants; here it refers to the conventional military formation sent to rescue Trench River City.

老鹳阵：模仿鹳鸟习性排列的阵形，因鹳鸟喜食蚁（暗合檀萝"蚁"属），故用于对付檀萝兵。这里指救援公主的军阵。
Old stork formation: A formation arranged to mimic the behavior of storks; since storks like to eat ants (coinciding with Tanluo's "ant" nature), it is used against Tanluo troops. Here it refers to the army formation sent to rescue the princess.

泥头酒：指用泥封瓶口的酒，古代军中常以此犒赏士兵。这里"赏他五千个泥头酒"指用酒激励士兵。
Mud-headed wine: Wine with a mud-sealed bottle mouth, often used in ancient armies to reward soldiers. Here, "reward them with five thousand mud-headed wines" means using wine to motivate the soldiers.

洗兵雨：指战后降雨，古人认为可洗净兵器上的血污，象征战事平息。这里"此日相逢洗兵雨"预示战事将顺利结束。
Rain to wash weapons: Refers to rain after a battle; the ancients believed it could wash blood from weapons, symbolizing the end of hostilities. Here, "meet on this day with rain to wash weapons" predicts the battle will conclude successfully.

风马牛不相及也：出自《左传·僖公四年》，原文为"君处北海，寡人处南海，唯是风马牛不相及也"，意思是两地相距很远，即使马、牛走失，也不会跑到对方境内，比喻事物彼此毫不相干。
Horses and cattle in heat do not reach each other: From the "Zuo Zhuan: 4th Year of Duke Xi". The original text: "You dwell by the North Sea, I dwell by the South Sea; only horses and cattle in heat would not reach each other." It means two places are very far apart, even if horses or cattle stray, they won't reach the other's territory; metaphorically means things are completely unrelated.

蚁阵纷然摆：蚁阵，指蚂蚁排成的阵势，常用来比喻军队的阵势。此句形象描绘出敌军像蚂蚁排列的阵势一样纷纷摆开。
Ant formations spread out in disorder: "Ant formations" means formations arranged like ants, often used metaphorically for military formations. This line vividly depicts the enemy troops deploying like ant formations.

触槐：典故出自《左传·宣公二年》，春秋时晋国大臣鉏麑奉命刺杀忠臣赵盾，见赵盾勤政爱民，不忍下手，又怕完不成任务，于是撞槐树而死。这里"敢拚残生来触槐"意思是难道你敢不顾性命去做这种类似触槐的傻事。
Dash against the locust tree:From "Zuo Zhuan: 2nd Year of Duke Xuan". In the Spring and Autumn period, the Jin minister Chu Ni was ordered to assassinate the loyal minister Zhao Dun. Seeing Zhao Dun's diligence and care for the people, he couldn't bring himself to do it, but feared failing his mission, so he dashed against a locust tree and died. Here, "dare to stake your remaining life to dash against the locust tree" means how dare you risk your life for such a foolish act like dashing against a tree.

楚心垓：化用"垓下之围"典故，垓下是楚汉相争时项羽被围困的地方，项羽在垓下兵败，四面楚歌，最终自刎乌江。此句"怎虞姬独困在楚心垓"意思是就像虞姬被困在楚军垓下一样处境艰难。
Chu's heartland at Gaixia: Alludes to the story of the "Siege of Gaixia". Gaixia was where Xiang Yu was besieged during the Chu-Han contention; Xiang Yu was defeated at Gaixia, surrounded by Chu songs, and ultimately committed suicide at the Wu River. This line, "how can Yu Ji be trapped alone in Chu's heartland at Gaixia?" means just like Yu Ji was trapped in the Chu army's position at Gaixia, her situation is dire.

为莺莺把定了河桥外：化用《西厢记》中崔莺莺与张生在河桥分别等情节，这里以莺莺自比，表达公主被困的无奈与担忧。
For Yingying's sake, guard outside the river bridge: Alludes to scenes from the "Romance of the Western Chamber" where Cui Yingying and Zhang Sheng part at the river bridge, etc. Here, the princess compares herself to Yingying, expressing her helplessness and worry at being besieged.

望夫台：传说中妻子思念远行的丈夫，登高远望，久而久之形成望夫台。此句"咱瞭高台是做望夫台"意思是公主在高台上盼望驸马到来，如同望夫台上的妻子盼夫。
Gazing-for-Husband Terrace:It is said that a wife longing for her traveling husband climbed high to gaze afar, and over time this formed the Gazing-for-Husband Terrace. This line, "our gazing from the high terrace makes it a Gazing-for-Husband Terrace" means the princess on the high terrace longs for the Consort's arrival, like a wife on the terrace longing for her husband.

乐昌家镜儿摔：化用"破镜重圆"典故，南朝陈国乐昌公主与丈夫徐德言在战乱中分离，各执半面镜子，后两人凭借镜子重逢团圆。这里"险些儿把这座小瑶台做乐昌家镜儿摔"意思是差点像乐昌公主的镜子一样破碎，暗示局势危急。
Shatter like Princess Lechang's mirror: Alludes to the story of the "broken mirror made whole". Princess Lechang of the Chen Dynasty (Southern Dynasties) was separated from her husband Xu Deyan during war; each kept half a mirror, and later they reunited with the help of the mirrors. Here, "almost made this little Jade Terrace shatter like Princess Lechang's mirror" means almost shattered like the princess's mirror, hinting the critical situation.

南柯：出自唐李公佐的传奇小说《南柯太守传》。淳于棼在门前大槐树下饮酒后入睡，梦入大槐安国，被招为驸马，出任南柯郡太守，政绩卓著，后因战败、公主病死等原因被遣返回家。醒来后，他发现大槐安国是槐树底下的一个蚁穴，南柯郡是蚁穴旁的南枝。后用"南柯"指代梦境或虚幻的世界，也指故乡。
Nanke: From the Tang dynasty tale "The Governor of Nanke" by Li Gongzuo. Chunyu Fen drank under the large locust tree outside his gate, fell asleep, and dreamed he entered the Great State of Huai'an, was made consort and appointed Governor of Nanke Prefecture, achieved outstanding administrative success, but was later sent home due to military defeat, the princess's death, etc. Upon waking, he discovered the Great State of Huai'an was an ant nest under the locust tree, and Nanke Prefecture was the southern branch beside the nest. Later, "Nanke" came to represent dreams or an illusory world, and also one's hometown.

脸从醉后如关将，酒尚温时斩华雄：出自元末明初罗贯中所著《三国演义》中的"温酒斩华雄"情节。在十八路诸侯讨伐董卓时，董卓大将华雄连斩诸侯联军多员大将，关羽主动请缨出战。曹操为其斟了一杯热酒，关羽表示斩了华雄再饮，不多时，关羽便提着华雄的首级回到帐中，此时酒还是温的。这两句诗展现了关羽的勇猛与神速。
Face after drunk resembles General Guan, While wine was still warm, he beheaded Hua Xiong: From the "Romance of the Three Kingdoms" by Luo Guanzhong (late Yuan/early Ming), the plot "Beheading Hua Xiong while the wine is warm". When the eighteen Zhuhou were attacking Dong Zhuo, Dong Zhuo's general Hua Xiong slew several allied generals. Guan Yu volunteered to fight. Cao Cao poured him a cup of warm wine; Guan Yu said he would drink after beheading Hua Xiong. Shortly after, Guan Yu returned to the tent with Hua Xiong's head, and the wine was still warm. These two lines showcase Guan Yu's bravery and speed.

遇饮酒时须饮酒，得饶人处且饶人："遇饮酒时须饮酒"出自明代佚名的《增广贤文（三）》，意思是碰到饮酒的机会就敞开大喝一场，体现了一种及时行乐的豁达人生观。"得饶人处且饶人"是一句谚语，出自元·关汉卿《窦娥冤》第二折，意思是能宽容时就要宽容，能饶恕的地方就要饶恕。
When you meet wine, you must drink; Where you can spare people, spare them: "When you meet wine, you must drink" comes from the anonymous Ming text "Increased Verses of the Wise (III)", meaning when you encounter an opportunity to drink, drink heartily, reflecting a carpe diem philosophy. "Where you can spare people, spare them" is a proverb from the second act of Guan Hanqing's (Yuan) "The Injustice to Dou E", meaning be lenient where you can, forgive where possible.

集唐：指集合唐人诗句而成的诗。这里"纔到城门打鼔声，武陵一曲想南征。谁知一夜秦楼客，白发新添四五茎"是集合唐诗而成，分别出自不同的唐诗作品，此处为组合使用。
Assembled Tang: Means a poem assembled from lines of Tang poetry. Here, "Just reached the city gate, sound of drums, / A tune of Wuling, thoughts of southern campaign. / Who knew that overnight as a guest in Qin Tower, / Four or five new white hairs added" is assembled from different Tang poems, combined here.

黄金锁子甲：指用黄金装饰的锁子甲，是古代一种坚固的铠甲。"当初去有黄金锁子甲"中代指周弁出征时的精良装备。
Golden chainmail: Chainmail decorated with gold, a type of sturdy ancient armor. In the line "back then when leaving, had golden chainmail", it represents Zhou Bian's excellent equipment when he set out on campaign.

刘备张飞：三国时期蜀汉的重要人物，二人与关羽并称"桃园三结义"，以英勇善战、兄弟情深著称。"那些儿刘备张飞"中周弁以刘备、张飞比喻自己和同伴，暗示不应如此对待。
Liu Bei and Zhang Fei: Important figures of Shu Han during the Three Kingdoms period; along with Guan Yu, they are known as the "Oath of the Peach Garden", famed for bravery and brotherly loyalty. In the line "what kind of Liu Bei and Zhang Fei are those?", Zhou Bian compares himself and his companion to Liu Bei and Zhang Fei,hinting they should not be treated this way.

周郞：原指三国时期吴国名将周瑜，因其年轻有为且精通音律，被称为"周郎"。这里"念周郞至友同乡籍"中"周郎"代指周弁，是对他的称呼。
Zhou Lang: Originally refers to the famous Wu general Zhou Yu of the Three Kingdoms period, called "Zhou Lang" because he was young, capable, and skilled in music. Here, in the line "considering Zhou Lang, close friend and fellow townsman", "Zhou Lang" refers to Zhou Bian, it's his称呼.

暑往寒来春复秋，夕阳西下水东流。将军战马今何在，野草闲花满地愁：出自古诗，原句描绘了时光流逝、物是人非的感慨，感叹昔日将军的战马已不见踪影，只留下满地野草闲花，充满凄凉之感。周弁引用此诗来感叹兵败后的境况。
Heat goes, cold comes, spring again autumn, / Setting sun west, water flows east. / The general's warhorse, where is it now? / Wild grass, idle flowers, full of sorrow on the ground.: From an ancient poem. The original lines depict the passage of time and the change of things, lamenting that the general's warhorse of old is gone, leaving only wild grass and idle flowers everywhere, full of desolation. Zhou Bian quotes this poem to lament his situation after defeat.

天若不爱酒，天应无酒星。地若不爱酒，地应无酒泉：出自李白《月下独酌四首·其二》，原句意思是如果上天不爱酒，就不会有酒星存在；如果大地不爱酒，就不会有酒泉（传说中酒泉郡因泉水似酒而得名）。周弁引用此句为自己贪杯辩解，说天地都爱酒，自己饮酒也是合理的。
If heaven did not love wine, / There would be no Wine Star in heaven. / If earth did not love wine, / There should be no Wine Spring on earth.: From Li Bai's "Drinking Alone under the Moon IV: II". The original means if heaven didn't love wine, there would be no Wine Star; if earth didn't love wine, there would be no Wine Spring (It is said that Jiuquan Prefecture was named for its spring water resembling wine). Zhou Bian quotes this to justify his love of drink, saying heaven and earth love wine, so his drinking is reasonable.

汉樊哙：樊哙是西汉开国功臣，以勇猛著称，曾在鸿门宴上持剑盾闯入，保护刘邦，且有豪饮的典故。"汉樊哙三国周公瑾关云长都也贪杯"中周弁以樊哙为例，说明古人也有贪杯的情况。
Han's Fan Kuai: Fan Kuai was a founding meritorious official of the Western Han, known for his bravery; he famously burst into the Hongmen Banquet with sword and shield to protect Liu Bang, and there are stories of his heavy drinking. In the line "Han's Fan Kuai, Three Kingdoms' Zhou Gongjin, Guan Yunchang, all were also fond of the cup", Zhou Bian uses Fan Kuai as an example to show that ancients also loved drink.

三国周公瑾：即周瑜，三国时期吴国名将，"飮醇醪"是关于他的典故，说他为人宽宏，部下有过失，他常以醇酒款待，使其悔悟。周弁提到他贪杯，以此为自己辩解。
Three Kingdoms' Zhou Gongjin: I.e., Zhou Yu, famous Wu general of the Three Kingdoms period; the story "drinking mellow wine" is about him: he was magnanimous, and when subordinates erred, he often entertained them with fine wine to make them repent. Zhou Bian mentions his fondness for drink to justify himself.

关云长：即关羽，三国时期蜀汉名将，传说中也有饮酒的事迹。周弁以他为例，说明自己贪杯并非个例。
Guan Yunchang: I.e., Guan Yu, famous Shu Han general of the Three Kingdoms period;It is said that also had episodes involving drink. Zhou Bian uses him as an example to show his own love of drink is not unique.

于禁：三国时期魏国将领，曾在樊城之战中因水灾投降关羽，后被送回魏国，遭曹丕羞辱而死。"上丹靑于禁身牢系"中以于禁的遭遇比喻周弁被囚禁的处境。
Yu Jin: A Wei general during the Three Kingdoms period; he surrendered to Guan Yu at the Battle of Fancheng due to flooding, was later returned to Wei, and died humiliated by Cao Pi. In the line "ascend the cinnabar and azure, Yu Jin's body firmly bound", Yu Jin's fate is used as a metaphor for Zhou Bian's imprisoned situation.

周亚夫疽生背：周亚夫是西汉名将，晚年因事入狱，绝食五日，呕血而死，传说其背上生疽。"敢气的俺周亚夫疽生背"中周弁用周亚夫的典故，感叹自己因气愤可能会像周亚夫一样遭遇不幸。
Zhou Yafu's abscess growing on his back: Zhou Yafu was a famous Western Han general; in his later years he was imprisoned for reasons, fasted for five days, vomited blood and died;It is said that an abscess grew on his back. In the line "dare to anger me until Zhou Yafu's abscess grows on my back", Zhou Bian uses the story of Zhou Yafu to lament that his anger might cause him to suffer a similar misfortune.

醉卧沙场征战鬼：化用王翰《凉州词》"醉卧沙场君莫笑，古来征战几人回"，原句意思是即使醉卧在沙场上也请不要笑话，自古以来出征作战的人能有几个活着回来。周弁化用此句，表达悔不当初宁愿醉死沙场的心情。
Drunk lying on the battlefield, a ghost of war: Adapts Wang Han's "Song of Liangzhou": "Drunk lying on the battlefield, sir, do not laugh; / Since ancient times, how many return from war?" The original means even if drunk on the battlefield, don't laugh; how many who went to war since ancient times returned? Zhou Bian adapts this to express regret, wishing he had drunk himself to death on the battlefield instead.

尾大难摇：出自《左传·昭公十一年》"末大必折，尾大不掉"。原句意思是树梢太大必然折断，尾巴太大难以摆动，比喻部下势力强大，难以驾驭。这里右相用来形容驸马在南柯势力过大，难以控制。
A large tail is hard to wag: From the "Zuo Zhuan: 11th Year of Duke Zhao": "If the tip is large, it will break; if the tail is large, it won't wag." The original means if the treetop is too large it will break, if the tail is too large it's hard to wag; metaphorically means subordinates are too powerful and hard to control. Here the Right Minister uses it to describe the Consort's excessive power in Nanke, making him difficult to control.

得时而羽翼能飞，失水则蛟龙可制：古代俗语演变而来。原句意思是禽鸟得到适宜的时机就能展翅高飞，蛟龙失去水的依托就可以被制服，比喻人或事物的强弱取决于所处的环境和条件。国王用此句感叹国家气势的变化。
Gain the time, and wings can fly; Lose the water, and the flood dragon can be controlled: Evolved from an ancient saying. The original means birds given the right opportunity can soar, a flood dragon leaving water can be subdued; metaphorically means the strength of a person or thing depends on its environment and conditions.
